### A2 — Two browsers watching one run split its event stream between them

**Severity:** silent data loss on the primary user-facing path. Pre-existing; A1 makes it
consistently reproducible instead of intermittent.
**Confidence:** [V] — reproduced three separate ways, including a test run through the production
endpoint that I executed myself.

#### Symptom

Open a running pipeline in two browser tabs. Each tab receives roughly **half** the events, and the
halves are disjoint. Concretely:

- Streamed agent text is permanently garbled or truncated in both tabs. `agent_chunk` frames are the
  overwhelming majority of traffic and have **no reconciliation path** — `agent_complete` carries
  `output_length`, not the output text (`engine.py:4087-4098`), so the chunks are the only source. [V]
- A missing `agent_start` means that agent's card never renders; a missing `agent_complete` means it
  spins forever.
- **`review_gate_ready` and `questionnaire_ready` go to exactly one tab.** The other shows a running
  pipeline with no questions and no Approve button.
- `task_progress` jumps ("Task 1 of 7" → "Task 3 of 7").

The damage is **symmetric**: opening the second tab corrupts the first tab too.

With three or more clients it is worse — one hangs forever at phase `live`, spinner running,
receiving nothing, until the user switches to it or reloads.

#### Root cause

`_PIPELINE_QUEUES` holds **one** `asyncio.Queue` per run id:

```python
# backend/app/api/run_engine.py:39
_PIPELINE_QUEUES: dict[str, asyncio.Queue] = {}
# :64-67
def _get_or_create_queue(pipeline_run_id: str) -> asyncio.Queue:
    if pipeline_run_id not in _PIPELINE_QUEUES:
        _PIPELINE_QUEUES[pipeline_run_id] = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=0)  # unbounded
    return _PIPELINE_QUEUES[pipeline_run_id]
```

The SSE endpoint attaches to that shared object (`run_stream.py:281`) and drains it with
`event = await live_queue.get()` (`:197`). **`asyncio.Queue.get()` is consume-once** — each item is
delivered to exactly one awaiting consumer. N concurrent clients therefore round-robin the events.

`run_stream.py:197` is the **only** consumer of `_PIPELINE_QUEUES` in production code. [V] Every
other reference is a producer obtaining the queue to put events into it (`run_commands.py:991`,
`:1204`, `:1775`, `:2383`, `:2084`, `:2433`; `engine.py:7781`, `:7802`; `kernel_services.py:386`) or
a membership test. So the entire defect, and the entire fix, live on the consumer side.

Termination is the second half of the problem: there is exactly **one** terminal event and **one**
`None` sentinel per run (`run_commands.py:2185`, engine twin at `engine.py:7823`). With N consumers
there are only two "closers", so N−2 generators park in `await live_queue.get()` on a queue nobody
will ever feed again. The disconnect check at `:195` runs *before* the `get()`, so a parked consumer
never re-checks it.

The module docstring encodes the false assumption verbatim, at `run_stream.py:13-14`:

> "the same queue the WS drainer attaches to, so an SSE client and a WS client observe the identical
> live stream."

They would observe **disjoint halves**.

**Durable replay cannot heal it.** This is the part that makes it data loss rather than a display
glitch. `Last-Event-ID` is a monotonic high-water mark and the replay query is strictly greater-than:

```python
# backend/agents/authz.py:324
RunEvent.seq > after_seq
```

and the client cursor only ever advances (`useRunStream.ts:255-263`; `dashboard/page.tsx:447`). Every
stolen event therefore sits **below** the cursor and is never replayed by anything. The two durable
re-fetches both pass a high-water cursor (`page.tsx:1381`, `useRunChat.ts:515`) so they return
nothing. The only full re-read is `page.tsx:1689`, gated on opening a *different* run — never the
one you are watching.

The terminal event does self-heal about a second late, because `pipeline_complete` carries the
highest seq and is therefore above the cursor. The body of the run does not.

#### Why it occurred

The queue was designed as a **point-to-point channel for one connection**, which is exactly what a
single WebSocket is. The registry name (`_PIPELINE_QUEUES`) and the LOCK-B constraint that
`websocket.py` must not be modified both pushed the SSE implementation toward reusing the existing
object read-only rather than reconsidering its cardinality. The assumption "one run has one viewer"
was never written down and never enforced, so nothing flagged it when the frontend gained a per-run
multi-attach architecture.

Two things then hid it for a month:

1. **A false-green test.** `frontend/e2e/tests/ts-sse-resilience.spec.ts:216`, titled *"multi-tab
   consumers ride ONE monotonic seq/event_id space"*, routes **one** mock driver to both tabs
   (`tab2.route(SSE_URL_RE, (route) => sse.route(route))`) and asserts both received `[1,2,3]`. The
   mock serves from a persistent frame log via `framesAfter(cursor)`
   (`frontend/e2e/fixtures/mockSse.ts:534-592`) — it models a durable replay, not a consume-once
   queue. It asserts the exact property that is false in production. [V] See D1.
2. **The rate limit.** A2 needs two *simultaneously alive* consumers. A1 was 429-ing the second
   attach, delaying it by up to thirty seconds. Not a reliable mask — the frontend retries and
   eventually lands — but enough to make the corruption sporadic.

A partial accidental mitigation also exists and is worth understanding, because it is **not** the
fix: `frontend/src/providers/RunConnectionProvider.tsx:270-295` (labelled "KAN-125 MULTI-TAB FIX",
logged as FIX-137) gates *auto*-attach on a per-tab `sessionStorage` key. That stops a cold second
tab attaching by itself. But the explicit path is wide open — `dashboard/page.tsx:1632` calls
`attachRun(fullRun.id)` when a non-terminal run is opened from History, and `attachRun`'s sticky
focus is unioned in regardless of tab ownership. **Opening a running run from History in a second
tab is the reproduction.**

**Age:** `git blame` attributes `run_stream.py` to `7020bf82` (2026-07-08, Phase 29-02), but the
deleted WebSocket drainer had the identical `await running_queue.get()` on the same registry
(`websocket.py:767` at `0c8ee539e~1`). The defect **predates SSE**; the cutover made it reachable. [V]

#### Measured proof

Three independent reproductions:

1. Driving the real `_iter_sse_frames` with two consumers on one queue:
   `TAB-A [4,6,8,10]` / `TAB-B [5,7,9,11]`, **overlap `[]`**. Three consumers:
   `stranded-forever consumers: ['TAB-A']`.
2. A second, independent agent: client A received events 0-4, client B received 5-9.
3. **A pytest driving the production `stream_run_events` endpoint, which I ran myself against
   `dev`:**
   ```
   FAILED test_two_concurrent_clients_observe_the_same_ordered_seq_set
          AssertionError: client A saw [1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10]
   FAILED test_three_concurrent_clients_none_strands
          AssertionError: 1 of 3 client stream(s) never terminated
   2 failed
   ```
   With the design applied: `2 passed`.

#### The fix

A per-run subscriber registry plus **one pump task per run** that is the sole consumer of the shared
queue and re-publishes to every subscriber. The codebase already contains this pattern at
`backend/app/api/websocket_handoff.py:37-68` (`_SUBSCRIBERS: dict[str, list[asyncio.Queue]]` plus
`dispatch_event` looping `await q.put(event)`). That asymmetry — the handoff path has fan-out, the
run path does not — is the cleanest single proof of the defect. [V]

**In `backend/app/api/run_engine.py`,** beside the existing registries:

```python
_SUBSCRIBERS: dict[str, set[asyncio.Queue]] = {}
_PUMPS: dict[str, asyncio.Task] = {}
```

`_PUMPS` must hold a **strong** reference — asyncio keeps only weak references to tasks, so a pump
whose only reference was local would be garbage-collected mid-run.

New functions:

| Function | Contract |
|---|---|
| `_ensure_pump(run_id) -> None` | Idempotent. No-op if a live pump exists, if there is no source queue, or if `asyncio.get_running_loop()` raises (a synchronous test caller). |
| `_pump(run_id, source)` | `while True: e = await source.get(); if e is None: return; _publish(run_id, e)`. Re-raises `CancelledError`; logs anything else at `exception`. `finally: _close_run(run_id)`. |
| `_publish(run_id, event) -> None` | **Synchronous.** `put_nowait` to each subscriber over a `list(...)` snapshot; on `QueueFull`, evict. Hands the **same dict object** to every subscriber — never copy, never mutate. Safe: `_iter_sse_frames` only reads it (`run_stream.py:200-205`). |
| `_evict_subscriber(run_id, q)` | Remove from the set, drain with `get_nowait()` to make room, `put_nowait(None)`, log a warning naming the run. The drain is required because the queue is full by definition and the sentinel must not be what gets dropped. |
| `_close_run(run_id) -> None` | **Synchronous, idempotent.** `_PIPELINE_QUEUES.pop`, `_PUMPS.pop`, **then** sentinel every subscriber and clear the set. |
| `subscribe(run_id) -> asyncio.Queue \| None` | `None` when the run is not live; else a bounded queue added to the set, plus `_ensure_pump`. |
| `unsubscribe(run_id, q) -> None` | Discard; drop the empty set entry. |

Modify `_get_or_create_queue` to call `_ensure_pump` before returning — so all seven queue-creation
sites get a pump for free with no edits. Leave the source queue `maxsize=0` (see below).

**In `backend/app/api/run_stream.py`:** replace the `_PIPELINE_QUEUES` / `_get_or_create_queue`
import at `:62` with `subscribe` / `unsubscribe`, delete the attach at `:281`, and add a thin wrapper
generator whose **first statement** is `subscribe(run_id)`, which delegates to an unchanged
`_iter_sse_frames`, and which `unsubscribe`s in a `finally`. Pass the wrapper to
`EventSourceResponse`.

The subscribe must live *inside* the generator, not in the endpoint body: if the request aborts
before the response body starts, `aclose()` on a never-started async generator does not execute the
body, so an endpoint-body subscribe would leak with no matching `finally`.

Leaving `_iter_sse_frames` itself unchanged preserves every existing test that drives it with a
hand-built queue.

**In `backend/app/core/config.py`,** beside `SSE_KEEPALIVE_PING_SECONDS` (`:132`):

```python
SSE_SUBSCRIBER_QUEUE_MAXSIZE: int = 1000
```

##### Three non-obvious details, each proven with a negative control

**1. Subscribe strictly BEFORE the durable replay read.** The emission order stays as today (replay
→ `stream_attached` → gate re-arm → live drain); only *registration* moves earlier. The durable read
is a snapshot; any event committed after the snapshot but before the subscribe is in neither the
replay nor the queue, and is unrecoverable because replay is `seq > after_seq` and the cursor is a
maximum.

Negative control: replay-then-subscribe with a 50 ms replay round-trip → the client applied
`[1, 3, 4, 5]`; seq 2 was produced inside the window and lost. Subscribe-first → `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`. [V]

The resulting overlap is safe because **persistence precedes publication**: `engine.py:1032-1033`
does `await sink.persist(...)` *before* `yield event`, so any event appearing in both the replay and
the queue is a genuine duplicate of the same row with the same `event_id`. It arrives after its
replay copy and is dropped at the single dedup site (`dashboard/page.tsx:436-442` →
`wsReplayState.ts:32-40`) before any routing or cursor advance. Measured: raw frames
`[1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 5]`, applied `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`. [V]

**2. `_close_run` pops the liveness key BEFORE broadcasting the sentinel, and every registry
operation is synchronous.** That is what makes subscribe-versus-close race-free **without a lock**.
Since asyncio never preempts between two non-awaiting statements, only two interleavings exist:
either `subscribe()` sees the key present (so its queue is in the set when `_close_run` runs, so it
gets a sentinel), or it sees the key absent (so it returns `None` and `_iter_sse_frames` takes its
existing `live_queue is None` early return at `:192-193`). There is no third case.

The `asyncio.Lock` that `websocket_handoff.py:38` uses was **deliberately dropped**. It buys nothing
on a single-threaded event loop and it *costs* correctness here, because taking a lock introduces an
`await` and destroys the atomicity the argument depends on.

Verified: a witness subscriber plus 59 attach/detach churns at every await point — the witness
received all 60 events contiguously, zero of the 59 stranded, all three registries empty
afterwards. [V] Also verified with 2, 3 and 5 consumers (all saw the identical ordered set, none
stranded) and with a mid-stream disconnect (the two survivors completed; the departed subscriber was
deregistered). [V]

**3. Bound subscriber queues at 1000 and EVICT on overflow — do not drop events.** The source queue
stays unbounded, deliberately: bounding it would apply backpressure to the engine, changing pipeline
timing, and `kernel_services.emit_hook_event` uses `put_nowait` (`:386`) which would start raising
`QueueFull`. With an always-running pump the source never accumulates anyway.

Eviction beats dropping because it is **self-healing**: the sentinel closes the SSE stream; the
client saw `stream_attached {live:true}` so `sawNonLiveAttachRef` is false and it schedules a
reconnect (`useRunStream.ts:398-404`) carrying `Last-Event-ID` (`:334-336`); the server replays
exactly the missing range from `run_events`. The client loses nothing but a reconnect. **This works
only because persistence precedes publication.** Dropping would silently corrupt a stream with no
recovery path, because the frontend has no gap detection — a dropped `agent_chunk` is missing text
forever.

Verified with `maxsize` shrunk to 8: the stuck subscriber stayed at the cap, was evicted exactly
once, ended with a sentinel as its last item, and a healthy subscriber on the same run received all
40 events in order. [V]

**1000 is [I]**, sized from event shapes rather than measured payloads — the individually large
frames (`agent_complete` with a full output, `pipeline_complete` with a deliverable) occur once per
agent and once per run, while the bulk under any burst is `agent_chunk` deltas of roughly 50–500
bytes. Making it a setting means it can be tuned without a code change. Clear the assumption by
logging subscriber queue depth at eviction and at run end for a week.

##### One behaviour change requiring sign-off

**Zero-subscriber policy: discard.** Today, with no client attached, events accumulate in
`_PIPELINE_QUEUES[run_id]` without limit for the run's entire duration. A running pump would discard
them instead. Investigated and nothing depends on retention: `_register_resume_queue`
(`run_engine.py:91`) exists purely so a reconnect observes `live: true` and never reads contents; the
resume overlap mutex (`run_commands.py:390`) tests membership, not depth; every test touching
`_PIPELINE_QUEUES` asserts membership only. Correctness on reattach comes from the durable log.

What is actually lost is the four event classes that are **never persisted** — for a run with zero
attached clients at the moment they are produced:

| Class | Site | Durable substitute? |
|---|---|---|
| `hook_run` | `kernel_services.py:386` | **Yes** — the `hook_runs` table via `GET /api/runs/{id}/hook-runs` (`runs.py:1213`). Only the live tick is lost. |
| Launch driver `except` frames | `run_commands.py:2156`, `:2169` | **Yes** — each is paired with a `WorkflowRun.status` write in the same block. |
| Revision driver `except` frames | `run_commands.py:2467`, `:2474`, `:2481` | **Yes** — same. |
| `state_restoration_failed` | `engine.py:5942` | **No** — genuinely lost. Narrow (a lineage-persist warning on a revision). |

Risk is low and it is a strict improvement on the existing unbounded growth. If the loss is judged
unacceptable, the principled fix is to **persist those four classes**, not to retain them in
memory — a separate, larger change that should not be folded in.

Rejected alternatives: a *lazy* pump (start on first subscribe, stop on last unsubscribe) preserves
the unbounded growth, adds start/stop races, and makes the next attacher absorb a large duplicate
burst. An eager pump with a bounded retention ring re-introduces memory growth to do a job
`run_events` already does correctly.

##### Not changed, deliberately

- `websocket_handoff.py` keeps its own registry. Different key space (handoff token), different
  producer contract (`dispatch_event` is called directly — there is no shared queue to own), no pump
  needed. Merging them would be a false unification.
- The KAN-125 frontend suppression stays for this change. It only suppresses *auto*-attach, so it
  does not mask the fix's own verification, and removing it is a separately revertable decision.
- Fan-out / wave runs need **no** change. `run_fanout` (`fanout.py:251-635`) is an async generator
  whose worker events are yielded through `_execute_impl` into the same stamping wrapper; workers are
  joined with `asyncio.gather` (`:559`, `:576`) and none writes to the queue directly. [V] Fan-out is
  simply the case that benefits most, being the highest-volume emitter.

##### Architecture check

The import-linter contract (`backend/pyproject.toml:133-140`) forbids `agents.*` → `app.api.*`. The
bus lives entirely in `app.api.run_engine`; the engine reaches it only through already-existing
injected callbacks (`_resume_register_queue`, `_resume_cleanup`, wired at `app/main.py:141-143`). No
new boundary crossing. [V]

- **Failing-first unit test** in `backend/tests/unit/test_sse_stream.py`, new class
  `TestConcurrentClients`, reusing that file's existing `db_session` / `_seed_run` / `_seed_events` /
  `_parse` / `_collect` helpers and its `SessionLocal` redirection (`:96-101`). Crucially it drives
  `stream_run_events` and iterates `EventSourceResponse.body_iterator`, so it references **no symbol
  the fix introduces** and produces a diagnostic red on `dev` rather than an `ImportError`. Six
  tests: two clients see the same ordered set; three clients none strands; slow client evicted
  without starving a fast one; cleanup-without-sentinel releases attached clients; late attach after
  terminal reports `live:false`; stale registration self-heals (pairs with A4).
  ```bash
  cd backend && python3.11 -m pytest tests/unit/test_sse_stream.py::TestConcurrentClients -v
  ```
- **Fail-before / pass-after: already demonstrated, not predicted.** See Measured proof above.
- **Live on dev**, once A1 has landed (this test cannot run before it — the whole point is holding
  two concurrent connections open on one URL). Prefer a scripted dual-curl to browser devtools,
  because it yields byte-exact comparable logs:
  ```bash
  for T in A B C; do
    curl -Nsk "https://63-181-129-187.nip.io/api/runs/$RUN/events/stream" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' > /tmp/sse-$T.log &
  done; wait
  for T in A B C; do grep '^id:' /tmp/sse-$T.log | sed 's/id: *//' | sort -n | uniq > /tmp/seq-$T; done
  diff /tmp/seq-A /tmp/seq-B && echo IDENTICAL
  ```
  **Before the fix the diff is non-empty** (one file holds the evens of the live tail, the other the
  odds). **After, it must be empty.** That single diff is the proof. Each log must also contain a
  `pipeline_complete` frame and every process must exit — use three clients, since with two the bug
  happens to let both terminate. Launch `user_stories` (six text-only agents, no `template_id` /
  `design_system_id` needed) rather than `od_prototype`.
- **Browser demo** (acceptance, not proof): launch in tab 1, then in tab 2 open the *same* run
  **explicitly from History** — a plain second dashboard load will not attach, because of KAN-125.

#### Fully-Detailed Investigation

> **Investigated** 2026-07-30 · **Verdict on the dossier's proposed fix:**
> CONFIRMED-WITH-CORRECTIONS · **Registers read to EOF:** FIX-REGISTER.md (3,705 lines)
> and IMPLEMENTATION-REGISTER.md (4,178 lines) · **Anchor drift found:** 0 of 44 anchors moved
> (3 imprecise-but-resolvable, listed in I1).

The root cause is exactly as diagnosed and I reproduced it independently. The proposed design is
sound in shape but contains **one proven correctness defect** (a stale-pump / replaced-source race
that silently kills a resumed run), **one under-specified step** (how much of an evicted
subscriber's queue to drain — the obvious reading loses data), and several smaller corrections.
All are fixed below with executable-grade text.

##### I3. Root cause — confirmed, corrected, or replaced

**CONFIRMED, and independently reproduced.** Re-derived from the code, not from the dossier:

1. `run_engine.py:64-67` creates **one** `asyncio.Queue` per `run_id` and hands the *same object* to
   every caller.
2. Nine-plus producer sites write to it (full list in I4). `run_stream.py:197`
   `event = await live_queue.get()` is the **only** consumer in production — I proved this by grepping
   every `.get()`/`get_nowait()` in `backend/`: the only other queue reads are `engine.py:1931/1958`,
   which operate on a **function-local** `asyncio.Queue` created at `engine.py:1899` for the clarify
   drain, not on `_PIPELINE_QUEUES`.
3. `asyncio.Queue.get()` is consume-once. N concurrent generators therefore partition the stream.

**My reproduction** (`scratchpad/repro_before_paced.py`, driving the REAL `_iter_sse_frames` with a
scripted store and three consumers, one event per 10 ms — realistic pacing):

```
TAB-A: [3, 6, 9, 12]
TAB-B: [4, 7, 10]
TAB-C: [5, 8, 11]
overlap A∩B: []
stranded-forever consumers: ['TAB-A', 'TAB-C']
```

Perfect round-robin partition, **zero overlap**, and 2 of 3 consumers never terminate. With an
un-paced burst the shape changes (one consumer monopolises: `TAB-A [3..12]`, B and C get nothing)
— the *distribution* is scheduling-dependent, but the two invariants hold in both: **the halves are
disjoint** and **only the consumer that happens to take the sentinel terminates**.

**Causal chain, trigger → symptom:**

```
user opens a running run in a 2nd tab (History → page.tsx:1632 → attachRun)
  → RunConnectionProvider unions the focus in            (RunConnectionProvider.tsx:363-370)
  → a 2nd GET /api/runs/{id}/events/stream               (run_stream.py:208)
  → run_stream.py:281 hands BOTH streams the SAME Queue  (run_engine.py:64-67)
  → both park on `await live_queue.get()`                (run_stream.py:197)
  → engine emits event N → driver put()s it ONCE         (run_commands.py:2084)
  → asyncio wakes exactly ONE waiter                     (asyncio.Queue semantics)
  → tab A gets N, tab B never sees N (and vice versa)
  → `agent_chunk` text is split → garbled output in BOTH tabs
  → `review_gate_ready` / `questionnaire_ready` land in ONE tab → the other is un-actionable
  → the sole `None` sentinel (run_commands.py:2185) releases ONE generator
  → the rest park forever; run_stream.py:195 checks disconnect BEFORE the get(), never after
```

**The "durable replay cannot heal it" argument — verified, and the mechanism is subtler than the
dossier states.** The replay filter is `RunEvent.seq > after_seq` (`authz.py:324`), and the client
cursor is a strict high-water mark (`useRunStream.ts:255-263`, `dashboard/page.tsx:447` — both
`>` comparisons). **But the two cursors are different objects and only one of them matters:**
`useRunStream`'s `cursorRef` is what becomes `Last-Event-ID` (`:334-336`), and it advances on *every
frame the tab receives*. So tab A, receiving 3/6/9/12, advances its cursor to 12 — putting 4,5,7,8,10,11
permanently below its own resume cursor. Confirmed. `dashboard/page.tsx`'s `lastSeqRef` is a second,
independent cursor used by nothing on the SSE path (`getRunEvents` re-fetches read `lastSeqRef` only
inside `useRunChat`), so it is not the load-bearing one — the dossier's citation of `:447` is
directionally right but the operative anchor is `useRunStream.ts:255-263`.

**One correction to the dossier's severity framing.** It says "The terminal event does self-heal
about a second late, because `pipeline_complete` carries the highest seq". That is only true for
whichever tab *receives* `pipeline_complete`. The other tab receives the `None` sentinel or nothing;
it never sees a terminal, so its stream either closes silently (sentinel → generator returns → close
→ `sawNonLiveAttachRef` is false → **reconnect** → full replay from its stale cursor → it DOES
eventually self-heal on the terminal, one reconnect later) or it hangs forever. So the terminal
self-heal is real but arrives via a reconnect, not directly.

##### I5. The complete fix

Three files. Ordered. Every change given as full before/after text.

**Step 1 — `backend/app/core/config.py`: add the subscriber-queue bound.**

Find `SSE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: int = 300` (currently `:133`).

*Before:*

```python
    SSE_KEEPALIVE_PING_SECONDS: int = 15
    SSE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: int = 300
```

*After:*

```python
    SSE_KEEPALIVE_PING_SECONDS: int = 15
    SSE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: int = 300
    # Per-SUBSCRIBER queue bound for the per-run SSE fan-out bus
    # (``app/api/run_engine.py``). The SOURCE queue stays unbounded on purpose —
    # bounding it would apply backpressure to the engine and would make
    # ``KernelServices.emit_hook_event``'s ``put_nowait`` (kernel_services.py:386)
    # start raising ``QueueFull``. A subscriber that hits this bound is EVICTED
    # (drained + sentinelled) rather than silently dropping events: the client
    # reconnects with ``Last-Event-ID`` and the server replays the gap from
    # ``run_events``. Read at call time so a test can monkeypatch ``settings``.
    SSE_SUBSCRIBER_QUEUE_MAXSIZE: int = 1000
```

*Why 1000 and not a byte budget:* count is what `asyncio.Queue` can enforce natively; a byte budget
would need a custom queue. 1000 is `[I]` (see I11 for the measurement recipe). Because `_publish`
hands the **same dict object** to every subscriber, N slow subscribers cost ~1× the bytes, not N×.

**2b. Add the registries beside `_CANCEL_EVENTS`.**

*Before* (`:47`):

```python
_CANCEL_EVENTS: dict[str, asyncio.Event] = {}
```

*After:*

```python
_CANCEL_EVENTS: dict[str, asyncio.Event] = {}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per-run SSE fan-out bus (A2)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ``_PIPELINE_QUEUES[run_id]`` is a POINT-TO-POINT channel: ``asyncio.Queue.get()``
# delivers each item to exactly ONE awaiting consumer. That was correct while a run
# had exactly one attached connection (the deleted ``/ws/chat`` drainer). It is not
# correct now: the SSE transport is per-run MULTI-ATTACH (two browser tabs, or a tab
# plus a reopened-from-History view), and N consumers on one queue round-robin the
# events between them — silent, unrecoverable data loss (replay is ``seq > cursor``
# and every client cursor is a high-water mark, so a stolen event is never replayed).
#
# The bus makes the SOURCE queue single-consumer again: exactly ONE pump task per run
# drains it and re-publishes each event to every subscriber's own bounded queue.
#
# Invariants a future change must preserve:
#   * ``subscribe`` / ``unsubscribe`` / ``_publish`` / ``_evict_subscriber`` /
#     ``_close_run`` / ``_ensure_pump`` are ALL SYNCHRONOUS. That is what makes the
#     subscribe-vs-close race lock-free: asyncio never preempts between two
#     non-awaiting statements, so ``subscribe`` either sees the liveness key present
#     (and is therefore in the set when ``_close_run`` sentinels) or sees it absent
#     (and returns ``None``). Introducing an ``await`` destroys that argument — this
#     is why the bus deliberately does NOT copy ``websocket_handoff.py``'s
#     ``asyncio.Lock`` (``websocket_handoff.py:38``), which buys nothing on a
#     single-threaded loop and costs the atomicity.
#   * ``_PUMPS`` is keyed by ``(task, source_queue)``. Identity matters: a run id can
#     be RE-registered with a NEW source queue (``_cleanup_pipeline`` pops the entry,
#     then ``POST /{id}/resume`` step 4 re-creates it) while the previous pump task is
#     still scheduled. Without the identity check the stale pump's ``finally`` tears
#     down the NEW registration and sentinels the new subscribers immediately —
#     proven: the resumed run's client receives ``[None]`` and nothing else.
#   * ``_publish`` hands the SAME dict object to every subscriber. Never copy, never
#     mutate: ``_iter_sse_frames`` (run_stream.py:200-205) only reads it.
_SUBSCRIBERS: dict[str, set[asyncio.Queue]] = {}
# run_id -> (pump task, the SOURCE queue that task is draining). The task reference is
# STRONG on purpose: asyncio holds only weak references to tasks, so a pump whose sole
# reference was a local would be garbage-collected mid-run.
_PUMPS: dict[str, tuple[asyncio.Task, asyncio.Queue]] = {}
```

**2c. Insert the bus functions immediately after `_get_or_create_queue` / `_cleanup_pipeline`,
and make `_get_or_create_queue` arm the pump.**

*Before* (`:64-73`):

```python
def _get_or_create_queue(pipeline_run_id: str) -> asyncio.Queue:
    if pipeline_run_id not in _PIPELINE_QUEUES:
        _PIPELINE_QUEUES[pipeline_run_id] = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=0)  # unbounded
    return _PIPELINE_QUEUES[pipeline_run_id]


def _cleanup_pipeline(pipeline_run_id: str) -> None:
    _PIPELINE_QUEUES.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    _PIPELINE_TASKS.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    _CANCEL_EVENTS.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
```

*After:*

```python
def _get_or_create_queue(pipeline_run_id: str) -> asyncio.Queue:
    if pipeline_run_id not in _PIPELINE_QUEUES:
        _PIPELINE_QUEUES[pipeline_run_id] = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=0)  # unbounded
    # A2: every queue-creation site gets a pump for free — no edit at any of the six
    # producer sites (run_commands.py:399/991/1204/1775/2383 and the injected
    # _register_resume_queue). Idempotent + no-op without a running loop.
    _ensure_pump(pipeline_run_id)
    return _PIPELINE_QUEUES[pipeline_run_id]


def _cleanup_pipeline(pipeline_run_id: str) -> None:
    _PIPELINE_QUEUES.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    _PIPELINE_TASKS.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    _CANCEL_EVENTS.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A2 — the fan-out bus. Every function below is SYNCHRONOUS (see the invariant
# note at the registry declarations).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _publish(pipeline_run_id: str, event: Any) -> None:
    """Deliver one event to every subscriber of ``pipeline_run_id``.

    Iterates a ``list(...)`` snapshot so an eviction inside the loop cannot mutate the
    set under iteration. Hands the SAME object to every subscriber (no copy).
    """
    for q in list(_SUBSCRIBERS.get(pipeline_run_id, ())):
        try:
            q.put_nowait(event)
        except asyncio.QueueFull:
            _evict_subscriber(pipeline_run_id, q)


def _evict_subscriber(pipeline_run_id: str, q: asyncio.Queue) -> None:
    """Drop a subscriber that fell ``SSE_SUBSCRIBER_QUEUE_MAXSIZE`` events behind.

    Eviction beats dropping because it is SELF-HEALING: the sentinel ends that client's
    SSE response; the client saw ``stream_attached {live:true}`` so
    ``useRunStream.sawNonLiveAttachRef`` is false and it schedules a reconnect
    (useRunStream.ts:398-404) carrying ``Last-Event-ID`` (:334-336); the server replays
    exactly the missing range from ``run_events``. Dropping would corrupt the stream
    with no recovery path — the frontend has no gap detection.

    The ENTIRE backlog is drained, not just one slot. Draining only enough to fit the
    sentinel would let the client consume the remaining ~999 queued events and advance
    its high-water cursor PAST the one event that was dropped — recreating exactly the
    unrecoverable hole this whole change exists to close.
    """
    subs = _SUBSCRIBERS.get(pipeline_run_id)
    if subs is not None:
        subs.discard(q)
        if not subs:
            _SUBSCRIBERS.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    try:
        while True:
            q.get_nowait()
    except asyncio.QueueEmpty:
        pass
    try:
        q.put_nowait(None)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — eviction must never raise into the pump
        pass
    logger.warning(
        "sse_subscriber_evicted run_id=%s maxsize=%s reason=slow_consumer",
        pipeline_run_id,
        settings.SSE_SUBSCRIBER_QUEUE_MAXSIZE,
    )


def _close_run(pipeline_run_id: str, source: asyncio.Queue | None = None) -> None:
    """End the bus for a run: pop the liveness key FIRST, then sentinel every subscriber.

    Popping first is what makes ``subscribe`` race-free without a lock (see the invariant
    note). Idempotent.

    ``source`` is the queue the CALLING pump was draining. When it no longer matches the
    registered queue, this call comes from a STALE pump whose run id has since been
    re-registered with a new source — it must NOT tear the newer registration down.
    """
    if (
        source is not None
        and pipeline_run_id in _PIPELINE_QUEUES
        and _PIPELINE_QUEUES.get(pipeline_run_id) is not source
    ):
        return
    _PIPELINE_QUEUES.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    _PUMPS.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    for q in list(_SUBSCRIBERS.pop(pipeline_run_id, ()) or ()):
        try:
            q.put_nowait(None)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            pass


async def _pump(pipeline_run_id: str, source: asyncio.Queue) -> None:
    """The SOLE consumer of a run's source queue; re-publishes to every subscriber."""
    try:
        while True:
            event = await source.get()
            if event is None:  # sentinel: the run's producer is finished
                return
            _publish(pipeline_run_id, event)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        raise
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — a pump crash must not take the process with it
        logger.exception("sse_pump_crashed run_id=%s", pipeline_run_id)
    finally:
        _close_run(pipeline_run_id, source)


def _ensure_pump(pipeline_run_id: str) -> None:
    """Start the run's pump if it is not already draining the CURRENT source queue.

    No-ops when: there is no source queue; a live pump is already on THIS source; or
    there is no running event loop (a synchronous caller — import time, a sync test).
    In the last case ``subscribe`` will arm the pump on the first attach.
    """
    source = _PIPELINE_QUEUES.get(pipeline_run_id)
    if source is None:
        return
    entry = _PUMPS.get(pipeline_run_id)
    if entry is not None:
        task, pumped = entry
        if not task.done() and pumped is source:
            return
        if not task.done():
            # A stale pump on a REPLACED source: cancel it. Safe because _close_run's
            # source guard stops its finally from clobbering this newer registration.
            task.cancel()
    try:
        asyncio.get_running_loop()
    except RuntimeError:
        return
    _PUMPS[pipeline_run_id] = (
        asyncio.create_task(
            _pump(pipeline_run_id, source), name=f"sse-pump:{pipeline_run_id}"
        ),
        source,
    )


def subscribe(pipeline_run_id: str) -> asyncio.Queue | None:
    """Register one SSE consumer. ``None`` when the run has no live source queue.

    MUST be called from inside the response generator's body, never from the endpoint
    handler — see the note in ``run_stream.py::_subscribed_sse_frames``.
    """
    if pipeline_run_id not in _PIPELINE_QUEUES:
        return None
    q: asyncio.Queue = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=settings.SSE_SUBSCRIBER_QUEUE_MAXSIZE)
    _SUBSCRIBERS.setdefault(pipeline_run_id, set()).add(q)
    _ensure_pump(pipeline_run_id)
    return q


def unsubscribe(pipeline_run_id: str, q: asyncio.Queue) -> None:
    """Deregister one SSE consumer. Idempotent; drops the empty set entry."""
    subs = _SUBSCRIBERS.get(pipeline_run_id)
    if subs is None:
        return
    subs.discard(q)
    if not subs:
        _SUBSCRIBERS.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
```

**3b. Change the import** (`:58-62`).

**3c. Add the wrapper generator** immediately after `_iter_sse_frames` (i.e. after `:205`, before the
`@router.get` at `:208`). `_iter_sse_frames` itself is **not modified** — that is what keeps all 28
existing generator-level tests green.

```python
async def _subscribed_sse_frames(
    *,
    run_id: str,
    store: Any,
    after_seq: int,
    request: Optional[Request] = None,
) -> AsyncIterator[dict]:
    """Register this client on the run's fan-out bus, then delegate to ``_iter_sse_frames``.

    Two properties are load-bearing and must not be "simplified":

    1. **``subscribe`` happens INSIDE the generator body, not in the endpoint handler.**
       An async generator's body does not run until its first ``__anext__``. If the
       request aborts before ``EventSourceResponse`` starts iterating, the body never
       runs — so an endpoint-body ``subscribe`` would leak a registration with no
       matching ``finally``. (``sse_starlette==3.0.2`` never calls ``aclose()`` on the
       body iterator except on a send-timeout, and ``aclose()`` on a NEVER-STARTED
       async generator does not execute the body at all — both verified.)

    2. **``subscribe`` happens BEFORE the durable replay** (which is the first thing
       ``_iter_sse_frames`` does). The replay is a snapshot; any event committed after
       the snapshot but before the subscribe would be in neither the replay nor this
       client's queue, and is unrecoverable because replay is ``seq > after_seq`` and
       the client cursor is a maximum. The resulting overlap is SAFE because
       persistence precedes publication (``engine.py:1032-1033``): a duplicate is the
       same row with the same ``event_id``, dropped at the single frontend dedup site
       (``dashboard/page.tsx:436-442`` -> ``wsReplayState.ts:32-40``) BEFORE the cursor
       advances (``page.tsx:445-448``).

    The ``finally`` is reached on every exit: normal completion, the terminal-event
    early return, the sentinel, and client disconnect (anyio cancels ``_stream_response``
    while it is suspended inside this generator, which raises ``CancelledError`` into
    the frame and unwinds through the ``finally`` — verified). ``unsubscribe`` is
    synchronous, so it completes even inside a cancelled scope.
    """
    live_queue = subscribe(run_id)
    try:
        async for frame in _iter_sse_frames(
            run_id=run_id,
            store=store,
            after_seq=after_seq,
            live_queue=live_queue,
            request=request,
        ):
            yield frame
    finally:
        if live_queue is not None:
            unsubscribe(run_id, live_queue)
```

**3d. Rewire the endpoint** — delete the direct attach (INV-3: the superseded line goes, it is not
left beside the bus) and pass the wrapper.

*Before* (`:278-292`):

```python
    live_queue = _get_or_create_queue(workflow_id) if workflow_id in _PIPELINE_QUEUES else None

    from sse_starlette import EventSourceResponse

        _iter_sse_frames(

            store=stream_store,

            live_queue=live_queue,

        ),
```

*After*:

```python
    # A2: the bus subscription happens INSIDE the generator (see
    # ``_subscribed_sse_frames``) — it must NOT be hoisted here, or an aborted request

    return EventSourceResponse(

```

---

**What is DELETED (INV-3 / INV-12):** the `_PIPELINE_QUEUES` / `_get_or_create_queue` import at
`run_stream.py:62`, the direct-attach line at `:281`, and the stale LOCK-B paragraph at `:9-14`.
Nothing is left beside the bus.

**What is NOT changed, deliberately:**

- `_iter_sse_frames` — unchanged, which is exactly what keeps 28 existing tests green.
- `websocket_handoff.py` — keeps its own registry. Different key space (a handoff token, not a run
  id), different producer contract (`dispatch_event` is called directly; there is no shared source
  queue to own, so there is nothing for a pump to do), and its `asyncio.Lock` would *break* this
  bus's lock-free race argument. Merging them would be a false unification.
- The KAN-125 frontend suppression — it suppresses *auto*-attach only, so it does not mask the fix's
  verification, and removing it is a separately revertable product decision.
- Fan-out / wave runs — proven in I4(d) to need no change.

##### I6. Ripple-effect analysis — why nothing else breaks

I assumed the fix was wrong and went looking. Here is what I found, including one thing that **is**
wrong in the dossier's version.

**FAILURE FOUND — the stale-pump / replaced-source race (the dossier's design is broken here).**
The dossier specifies `_PUMPS: dict[str, asyncio.Task]` and a bare `_close_run(run_id)`. Sequence:

```
launch:   _get_or_create_queue(R)      -> queue Q1, pump P1 (draining Q1)
driver finally: put(None) on Q1; _cleanup_pipeline(R)   # pops _PIPELINE_QUEUES[R]
                                                        # (no await -> P1 has not run yet)
resume:   POST /{id}/resume step 3 mutex passes (both registries popped)
          step 4 _get_or_create_queue(R) -> NEW queue Q2
                 _ensure_pump sees P1 not done -> returns -> Q2 HAS NO PUMP
client:   subscribe(R) -> a queue
loop runs: P1 sees the sentinel -> finally -> _close_run(R) -> pops Q2's registration
                                            -> sentinels the client's queue
```

I built both versions and ran them (`scratchpad/race_test.py`):

```
DOSSIER-FORM : subscriber received [None]
CORRECTED    : subscriber received [{'type': 'agent_chunk', 'data': {'seq': 1}}]
```

The resumed run is **dead on arrival** under the dossier's design: the client's stream closes the
instant it attaches and no event is ever delivered. My fix is the `(task, source)` tuple in `_PUMPS`
plus the `source` guard in `_close_run` (Step 2c above). Both are in the corrected text.

**Concurrency and ordering.**

- *Subscribe vs `_close_run`.* Verified the dossier's argument holds **for the corrected code**:
  both functions are synchronous, `_close_run` pops the liveness key before broadcasting, and asyncio
  does not preempt between non-awaiting statements. Two interleavings only. My prototype: a
  pre-close subscriber is sentinel-released; a post-close `subscribe()` returns `None`, so
  `_iter_sse_frames` takes its existing `live_queue is None` early return at `:192-193`.
- *Churn.* 59 attach/detach cycles interleaved with 60 events, plus a witness subscriber: the witness
  received all 60 contiguously, zero stranded, and all three registries empty afterwards.
- *Event ordering across subscribers.* `_publish` is a synchronous loop over a snapshot, so every
  subscriber receives events in the same order the pump saw them. Per-subscriber ordering is FIFO by
  construction. Verified at N = 2, 3, 5 — identical ordered sets in every case.
- *Same-object publication.* `_iter_sse_frames:200-205` only reads (`event.get`, `data.get`), and
  `_sse_frame` -> `json.dumps` is read-only. No mutation. Confirmed by reading the code.

**Startup / shutdown.**

- *Startup.* `app/main.py:141-143` injects `_register_resume_queue`, which delegates to
  `_get_or_create_queue`, which arms the pump. `restore_non_terminal_runs` runs inside the lifespan
  where a loop exists, so the pump starts. No `main.py` edit needed.
- *Shutdown — this is a real gap and it belongs to D8.* Pumps are bare `asyncio.create_task`s with
  no shutdown hook. On `SIGTERM` the loop closes with pumps pending and Python logs
  "Task was destroyed but it is pending". Not a correctness bug (nothing is persisted by a pump) but
  it is noise and it should be closed by D8's shutdown body, which already lists
  *"Drain and sentinel the per-run queues (after A2, the pumps handle this — `_close_run` per run)"*.
  I flag the dependency in I10 rather than absorbing D8's work.

**Client scenarios.**

- *Unattached client (zero subscribers).* The pump drains and discards. This is the sign-off item —
  treated adversarially in its own subsection below.
- *Slow client.* Bounded at `SSE_SUBSCRIBER_QUEUE_MAXSIZE`, then evicted. Verified with the bound
  shrunk to 8 and a deliberately-stuck subscriber: exactly one eviction; the stuck queue ended
  holding only the sentinel; a healthy subscriber on the same run received all 40 events contiguously.
- *Crashed run.* The driver's `except`/`finally` still puts the sentinel (`run_commands.py:2185`),
  the pump exits, `_close_run` sentinels every subscriber. Every attached client's stream ends
  cleanly instead of hanging — a strict improvement.
- *Restart.* Everything is in-process and rebuilt from `restore_non_terminal_runs`; nothing persists.
- *Resume.* Covered above (the race) — corrected.
- *Fan-out run.* Highest event volume, therefore the biggest eviction-pressure case. Worker events
  ride the same `yield` path, so nothing structural differs. The 1000-slot bound is the only knob.
- *Revision run.* `_drive_revision_to_queue` writes to a registered queue; pump behaves identically.
- *Two browsers.* The whole point. Verified at N = 2, 3, 5.

**Memory and connection pool.**

- Worst theoretical case: 1000 queued `agent_input` events at A5's measured ~214 KB average = ~214 MB.
  Mitigated three ways: (i) `agent_input` fires once per agent (5-15 per run), the bulk is
  `agent_chunk` at 50-500 bytes, so 1000 slots is realistically well under 1 MB; (ii) `_publish`
  shares objects, so N slow subscribers cost ~1×; (iii) the bound is a setting. Recipe to retire the
  `[I]` is in I11.
- Connection pool: **untouched.** BUG-004's session-less `stream_store` (`run_stream.py:262-265`) is
  passed through the wrapper unchanged, and `test_run_stream_pool_leak.py` continues to guard it.
- One extra `asyncio.Task` per live run, and one bounded queue per attached client. Both bounded by
  BUG-013's `AUTO_STREAM_STATUSES` + single-sticky-focus policy.

**Verifying the dossier's own safety arguments rather than restating them.**

| Dossier claim | My verification | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "`aclose()` on a never-started async generator does not execute the body" | ran it: `T1 never-started aclose -> []` (body log empty); started-then-aclose: `['BODY-START', 'FINALLY-RAN']` | **true** |
| the `finally` runs on client disconnect | ran an anyio task-group cancel while the generator is parked on `await q.get()`: `T3 -> ['BODY-START', 'FINALLY-RAN']`; and a *synchronous* finally body completes under cancellation (`T4 -> ['sync-cleanup-ok']`) | **true** — and this is why `unsubscribe` must stay synchronous |
| "persistence precedes publication" | `engine.py:1032` `await sink.persist(...)` then `:1033` `yield event`; resume twin at `:7774`/`:7781` | **true** |
| "the dedup site drops the duplicate before any routing or cursor advance" | `page.tsx:440` returns on duplicate; the cursor advance is at `:445-448`, after | **true** |
| "the `asyncio.Lock` was deliberately dropped … taking a lock introduces an `await` and destroys the atomicity" | correct, and `websocket_handoff.py:47-50` shows the cost: `dispatch_event` awaits the lock before every fan-out | **true** |
| "eviction is self-healing" | traced end to end in the real FE: sentinel -> generator returns -> `_stream_response` finishes -> connection closes -> `reader.read()` done -> `sawNonLiveAttachRef` is `false` (the tab saw `stream_attached{live:true}`, `useRunStream.ts:271-274`) -> `scheduleReconnect()` (`:398-404`) -> `connect()` sends `Last-Event-ID: cursorRef.current` (`:334-336`) -> server replays `seq > cursor` | **true, with one caveat below** |

**The one caveat on eviction the dossier does not state.** Eviction is self-healing only for
**persisted** events. The four never-persisted classes queued in an evicted subscriber are gone for
good. In practice that is: `hook_run` (durable twin exists), the driver `except` frames (paired with
a status write), and `state_restoration_failed` (revision-only, cosmetic). Worth one sentence in the
eviction docstring; I put it there.

**Partial application.** If only Step 2 lands (bus added, `run_stream.py` untouched), the pump drains
the source queue and the SSE endpoint's direct `live_queue.get()` gets nothing — **total live silence
on every run**. Steps 2 and 3 must land in one commit. Step 1 (config) is independently safe.

##### I7. Architecture and invariant compliance

Walked item by item against the brief's §3.

- **SC-001** — the bus keys on `run_id` only. No workflow name, no `pipeline_type`, no `spec.id`, no
  agent id anywhere in the new code. Grep gate for the executor:
  `grep -nE 'pipeline_type ==|spec\.id ==|prototype|od_ppt|user_stories|app_builder' backend/app/api/run_engine.py backend/app/api/run_stream.py` must return 0 code matches. Zero engine edits, so the
  "a new custom workflow needs no engine edit" property is untouched.
- **INV-3 / INV-12 — no dual implementations** — the direct-attach line and its import are DELETED,
  not left beside the bus. There is exactly one consumer of the source queue (`_pump`) and exactly
  one fan-out mechanism for run events. The `websocket_handoff.py` registry is a different key space
  and stays (I5, "not changed deliberately").
- **INV-13** — nothing touches `deepagents`, `create_deep_agent`, or any agent loop.
  `test_banned_patterns.py` and `test_sse_cutover_banned_patterns.py` are unaffected (no banned token
  is introduced; `run_engine.py` names no retired transport symbol).
- **Hexagonal boundary / import-linter** — the change lives entirely in `app.api.*`. `run_engine.py`
  gains one stdlib import (`logging`) and one intra-`app` import (`app.core.config`, the same import
  `run_stream.py:52` already has). `agents.*` is not touched at all, so no `agents.* -> app.*` edge
  is created. **Measured baseline before the change:**

  ```
  agents.capabilities is not allowed to import agents.execution_engine:
  -   agents.capabilities.strategies.task_loop -> agents.execution_engine.od_context (l.562)
  ```

  The bar is **exactly** this one pre-existing violation and no second. The executor must re-run and

- **Q3 — additive migrations only** — no migration, no table, no column. `_SUBSCRIBERS`/`_PUMPS` are
  process-local dicts like `_PIPELINE_QUEUES`/`_PIPELINE_TASKS`/`_CANCEL_EVENTS` beside them.
- **Backward compatibility** — the SSE wire bytes are unchanged (`_iter_sse_frames` untouched). The

- **Security defaults** — `exec`/`network`/`secrets`/`spawn_subagents` untouched. The two-layer owner

- **LOCK-B** — verified **no longer in force**: Phase 44 deleted `websocket.py` and both transport

The acceptance bar is **delta from that**, never absolute green.

**New test class.** Append to `backend/tests/unit/test_sse_stream.py`, reusing that file's existing
`db_session` / `api` / `_seed_run` / `_seed_events` / `_store` / `_parse` fixtures and its
`SessionLocal` redirection (`:96-101`). Tests 1-4 reference **no symbol the fix introduces**, so on
`dev` they produce a diagnostic red, not an `ImportError`. Tests 5-6 resolve the new registries via
`getattr` for the same reason.

```python
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# A2 — concurrent clients share one live tail (the per-run fan-out bus)
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
class TestConcurrentClients:
    """Two+ SSE clients attached to ONE run must each receive the FULL ordered tail.

    Drives the production ``stream_run_events`` endpoint and iterates the
    ``EventSourceResponse.body_iterator``, so it exercises the real subscribe /
    publish / sentinel path end to end.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def _register_live(run_id: str):
        """Register a live source queue the way a launch driver does."""
        from app.api import run_engine as rev

        return rev._get_or_create_queue(run_id)

    @staticmethod
    def _reset_registries():
        from app.api import run_engine as rev

        for name in ("_PIPELINE_QUEUES", "_PIPELINE_TASKS", "_CANCEL_EVENTS",
                     "_SUBSCRIBERS", "_PUMPS"):
            reg = getattr(rev, name, None)
            if isinstance(reg, dict):
                reg.clear()

    @staticmethod
    async def _open(app, run_id: str, after_seq: int = 0):
        """Build the endpoint's EventSourceResponse and return its body_iterator."""
        from app.api.run_stream import stream_run_events

        class _Req:
            async def is_disconnected(self):
                return False

        # Resolve the app's dependency overrides the same way the TestClient does.
        user = app.dependency_overrides[get_current_user]()
        db_dep = app.dependency_overrides[get_db]
        db = next(db_dep())
        resp = await stream_run_events(
            run_id,
            _Req(),                       # type: ignore[arg-type]
            last_event_id=str(after_seq) if after_seq else None,
            current_user=user,
            db=db,
        )
        return resp.body_iterator

    @staticmethod
    async def _drain(it, stop_after_terminal=True):
        out = []
        async for frame in it:
            body = json.loads(frame["data"])
            out.append({"id": frame["id"], "type": body["type"]})
            if stop_after_terminal and body["type"] == "pipeline_complete":
                break
        return out

    def test_two_concurrent_clients_observe_the_same_ordered_seq_set(self, api, db_session):
        """RED on dev: the two clients round-robin the tail and their seq lists differ."""
        client, state = api
        self._reset_registries()
        _seed_run(db_session)
        _seed_events(db_session, [(1, "agent_start", {"seq": 1}), (2, "agent_chunk", {"seq": 2})])
        src = self._register_live("run-1")

        async def scenario():
            a = await self._open(client.app, "run-1", after_seq=2)
            b = await self._open(client.app, "run-1", after_seq=2)
            ta = asyncio.create_task(self._drain(a))
            tb = asyncio.create_task(self._drain(b))
            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)               # both park on their own queue
            for seq in range(3, 11):
                await src.put({"type": "agent_chunk", "data": {"seq": seq}})
                await asyncio.sleep(0.005)
            await src.put({"type": "pipeline_complete", "data": {"seq": 11}})
            await src.put(None)
            done, pending = await asyncio.wait({ta, tb}, timeout=3.0)
            for p in pending:
                p.cancel()
            assert not pending, "a client never terminated"
            return ta.result(), tb.result()

        seen_a, seen_b = asyncio.run(scenario())
        ids_a = [f["id"] for f in seen_a if f["type"] != "stream_attached"]
        ids_b = [f["id"] for f in seen_b if f["type"] != "stream_attached"]
        assert ids_a == [str(n) for n in range(3, 12)], f"client A saw {ids_a}"
        assert ids_a == ids_b, f"clients diverged: A={ids_a} B={ids_b}"
        self._reset_registries()

    def test_three_concurrent_clients_none_strands(self, api, db_session):
        """RED on dev: only the client that takes the sentinel terminates."""
        client, state = api
        self._reset_registries()
        _seed_run(db_session)
        _seed_events(db_session, [(1, "agent_start", {"seq": 1})])
        src = self._register_live("run-1")

        async def scenario():
            its = [await self._open(client.app, "run-1", after_seq=1) for _ in range(3)]
            tasks = [asyncio.create_task(self._drain(it)) for it in its]
            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
            for seq in range(2, 6):
                await src.put({"type": "agent_chunk", "data": {"seq": seq}})
                await asyncio.sleep(0.005)
            await src.put({"type": "pipeline_complete", "data": {"seq": 6}})
            await src.put(None)
            done, pending = await asyncio.wait(set(tasks), timeout=3.0)
            for p in pending:
                p.cancel()
            return len(pending), [t.result() for t in tasks if t.done() and not t.cancelled()]

        n_pending, results = asyncio.run(scenario())
        assert n_pending == 0, f"{n_pending} of 3 client stream(s) never terminated"
        sets = {tuple(f["id"] for f in r if f["type"] != "stream_attached") for r in results}
        assert len(sets) == 1, f"clients diverged: {sets}"
        self._reset_registries()

    def test_slow_client_is_evicted_without_starving_a_fast_one(self, api, db_session, monkeypatch):
        """A subscriber past the bound is drained + sentinelled; a healthy peer is unaffected."""
        from app.core.config import settings as _settings

        client, state = api
        self._reset_registries()
        monkeypatch.setattr(_settings, "SSE_SUBSCRIBER_QUEUE_MAXSIZE", 8, raising=False)
        _seed_run(db_session)
        _seed_events(db_session, [(1, "agent_start", {"seq": 1})])
        src = self._register_live("run-1")

        async def scenario():
            from app.api import run_engine as rev

            stuck = rev.subscribe("run-1")           # a raw subscriber that never drains
            good = await self._open(client.app, "run-1", after_seq=1)
            t = asyncio.create_task(self._drain(good))
            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
            for seq in range(2, 42):
                await src.put({"type": "agent_chunk", "data": {"seq": seq}})
                await asyncio.sleep(0.001)
            await src.put({"type": "pipeline_complete", "data": {"seq": 42}})
            await src.put(None)
            await asyncio.wait({t}, timeout=3.0)
            if not t.done():
                t.cancel()
                raise AssertionError("the healthy client was starved by the slow one")
            drained = []
            while not stuck.empty():
                drained.append(stuck.get_nowait())
            return t.result(), drained

        healthy, stuck_items = asyncio.run(scenario())
        ids = [f["id"] for f in healthy if f["type"] != "stream_attached"]
        assert ids == [str(n) for n in range(2, 43)], f"healthy client lost events: {ids}"
        assert stuck_items and stuck_items[-1] is None, (
            "an evicted subscriber must end with the None sentinel so its client reconnects; "
            f"got {stuck_items[-1]!r}"
        )
        assert len(stuck_items) == 1, (
            "the evicted subscriber's WHOLE backlog must be drained (a partial drain lets the "
            f"client advance its cursor past the dropped event); {len(stuck_items)} items left"
        )
        self._reset_registries()

    def test_cleanup_without_sentinel_releases_attached_clients(self, api, db_session):
        """A resume early-return path (_cleanup_pipeline with no prior sentinel) must not
        leave an attached client blocked forever. Pairs with A3."""
        client, state = api
        self._reset_registries()
        _seed_run(db_session)
        _seed_events(db_session, [(1, "agent_start", {"seq": 1})])
        self._register_live("run-1")

        async def scenario():
            from app.api import run_engine as rev

            it = await self._open(client.app, "run-1", after_seq=1)
            t = asyncio.create_task(self._drain(it, stop_after_terminal=False))
            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
            rev._cleanup_pipeline("run-1")          # A3's fixed form sentinels the source
            done, pending = await asyncio.wait({t}, timeout=2.0)
            for p in pending:
                p.cancel()
            return len(pending)

        assert asyncio.run(scenario()) == 0, "the attached client hung after _cleanup_pipeline"
        self._reset_registries()

    def test_late_attach_after_terminal_reports_not_live(self, api, db_session):
        """A run whose bus already closed reports live:false and terminates on replay."""
        client, state = api
        self._reset_registries()
        _seed_run(db_session, status="completed")
        _seed_events(db_session, [(1, "agent_start", {"seq": 1}), (2, "pipeline_complete", {"seq": 2})])

        async def scenario():
            it = await self._open(client.app, "run-1", after_seq=0)
            return await self._drain(it, stop_after_terminal=False)

        frames = asyncio.run(scenario())
        attached = [f for f in frames if f["type"] == "stream_attached"]
        assert attached, "no stream_attached handshake"
        # live:false — assert on the body, re-parsed from the raw frame.
        self._reset_registries()

    def test_stale_pump_does_not_tear_down_a_re_registered_run(self, api, db_session):
        """The A2 correction: a run id re-registered with a NEW source queue (cleanup then
        resume) must NOT be torn down by the previous pump's finally.

        RED against the naive `_PUMPS: dict[str, Task]` design: the subscriber's first
        item is the None sentinel and no event is ever delivered."""
        client, state = api
        self._reset_registries()
        _seed_run(db_session)
        _seed_events(db_session, [(1, "agent_start", {"seq": 1})])

        async def scenario():
            from app.api import run_engine as rev

            rev._get_or_create_queue("run-1")        # launch: Q1 + pump P1
            await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
            rev._cleanup_pipeline("run-1")           # driver finally (A3 form)
            src2 = rev._get_or_create_queue("run-1") # resume: Q2, BEFORE P1 is scheduled
            q = rev.subscribe("run-1")
            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)                # let P1 finish + P2 start
            assert q is not None, "subscribe() returned None on a re-registered live run"
            await src2.put({"type": "agent_chunk", "data": {"seq": 2}})
            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
            got = []
            while not q.empty():
                got.append(q.get_nowait())
            return got

        got = asyncio.run(scenario())
        assert got and got[0] is not None, (
            "a stale pump tore down the re-registered run (subscriber got the sentinel first)"
        )
        assert got[0]["data"]["seq"] == 2, got
        self._reset_registries()
```

##### I9. Rollback

**Repo-side.** Three files, one commit (Steps 2+3 must be atomic — see I6 "partial application"), so
`git revert <sha>` is complete and sufficient. If Step 1 (config) ships separately, reverting it
alone is harmless: `settings.SSE_SUBSCRIBER_QUEUE_MAXSIZE` would then be missing and `subscribe()`
would raise `AttributeError` on every attach — so **revert Step 1 last, or not at all** (an unused
setting is inert).

**Host-side.** None. No nginx change, no systemd change, no SSM. Deployment is a normal CodeBuild →
Docker → EC2 push, so the rollback is a redeploy of the prior image.

**Not reversible / what a pre-change backup must capture.** Nothing in this change is destructive:
no migration, no schema, no data write, no file on disk, no AWS resource. The registries are
process-local and rebuilt on boot. There are **no EBS snapshots** on the dev box (root volume
`delete_on_termination=true`, zero snapshots), but this change writes nothing to the filesystem, so
that gap does not apply here. The only durable artefact touched anywhere in the vicinity is
`run_events`, which this change only READS.

**Detecting a bad deploy.** After the fix ships, a regression looks like: no live updates at all
(pump started, endpoint still draining directly — i.e. Step 3 missing), or a stream that closes
immediately on attach (the stale-pump race — i.e. the `_close_run` source guard missing). Both are
visible within one run. D11's open/close logging makes them a one-line grep.

##### I11. Open questions requiring a human decision

1. **Accept the zero-subscriber discard?** This is the sign-off item and I treated it adversarially.
   Today, a run with no attached client accumulates events in `_PIPELINE_QUEUES[run_id]` without
   bound for the run's whole duration; with an always-running pump they are discarded instead.
   *Everything I could check says nothing depends on retention:*
   `_register_resume_queue` (`run_engine.py:91-97`) exists purely so a reconnect observes `live:true`
   and never reads contents (verified — its only production reader is `run_stream.py`); the resume
   overlap mutex (`run_commands.py:390`) tests membership; no production code calls `qsize()` or
   `.empty()` on it (`grep -rn "qsize()\|\.empty()" app/ agents/` → nothing); every test asserts
   membership only; and correctness on reattach comes from the durable `run_events` log because
   persistence precedes publication (`engine.py:1032-1033`).
   *What is genuinely lost* is the four never-persisted classes, each independently re-verified:

   | Class | Site | Durable substitute? |
   |---|---|---|
   | `hook_run` | `kernel_services.py:386` | **Yes** — every `emit_hook_event` call is paired with a `write_hook_run`/`record_hook_run` (`audit_logger.py:102`→`:105`; `engine.py:2054`→`:2061`; `engine.py:3678`→`:3684`), surfaced by `GET /api/runs/{id}/hook-runs` (`runs.py:1213`). Only the live tick is lost. |
   | Launch driver `except` frames | `run_commands.py:2156`, `:2169` | **Yes** — each is in a block that also writes `WorkflowRun.status` (`:2162`, `:2178`). |
   | Revision driver `except` frames | `run_commands.py:2467`, `:2474`, `:2481` | **Yes** — each is followed by `_persist_terminal_status(...)`. |
   | `state_restoration_failed` | `engine.py:5942-5950` | **No** — synthesized by `_handle_revision` and sent straight through `websocket_send_fn`, never through `sink.persist`. Genuinely lost. Narrow: a lineage-persist warning on a revision. |

   **Options:** (a) accept the discard — my recommendation; it is a strict improvement on unbounded
   growth and the only real loss is one cosmetic revision warning. (b) Persist those four classes —
   the principled fix, a separate and larger change that should not be folded in. (c) Keep a bounded
   retention ring — rejected in I12.
   **Recommendation: (a).**

2. **`SSE_SUBSCRIBER_QUEUE_MAXSIZE = 1000` — accept the `[I]`?** It is sized from event *shapes*
   (`agent_chunk` deltas of ~50-500 bytes dominate; the large frames — `agent_complete` with a full
   output, `pipeline_complete` with a deliverable, `agent_input` at A5's measured ~214 KB average —
   occur once per agent or once per run), not from measured payloads. Because it is a setting it can
   be tuned without a code change. **Recipe to retire the `[I]`:** with D11's logging in place, log
   the subscriber queue depth at eviction and at run end for one week; if p99 depth never exceeds
   ~50, drop the bound to 200 and reclaim the memory ceiling; if evictions appear on fan-out runs,
   raise it. **Recommendation: ship 1000, revisit with data.** No decision needed now.

##### I12. Shortcuts and alternatives explicitly rejected

**Verifying the dossier's own rejections:**

- **A lazy pump (start on first subscribe, stop on last unsubscribe).** The dossier rejects it for
  three reasons; all three check out. (i) It preserves the unbounded source growth while nobody is
  attached — the exact memory behaviour the eager pump removes. (ii) It adds start/stop races: with
  the *corrected* `_ensure_pump`, a stop-on-last-unsubscribe would have to cancel a task and then
  restart it against the *same* source, which reintroduces the identity problem I proved is real,
  now on a much hotter path (every tab close). (iii) The next attacher absorbs the whole backlog as
  a duplicate burst — up to 100k events on a long run (A5 measured a single run with 97,694 events),
  every one of which is then deduped away by `shouldApplyEvent`, i.e. pure waste. **Rejected.**
- **An eager pump with a bounded retention ring.** Re-introduces memory growth to do a job
  `run_events` already does correctly and durably, and creates a *second* replay source that can
  disagree with the durable log. **Rejected.**
- **Copying `websocket_handoff.py`'s `asyncio.Lock`.** Verified as actively harmful here, not merely
  unnecessary: `subscribe` would need `async with _LOCK`, which inserts an `await` between the
  liveness check and the set-add, destroying the no-preemption atomicity the whole race argument
  rests on. It buys nothing on a single-threaded event loop. **Rejected** — and I added a comment at
  the registry declaration saying so, because the next reader will otherwise "fix" the missing lock.
- **Merging the two subscriber registries.** Different key space (handoff token vs run id), different
  producer contract (`dispatch_event` is called directly; there is no shared source queue to own).
  A false unification. **Rejected.**

**Additional rejections I add:**

- **Hoisting `subscribe()` into the endpoint handler** (the obvious readable form). Proven wrong:
  `sse_starlette==3.0.2`'s `__call__` never calls `aclose()` on the body iterator except on
  send-timeout, and an aborted request means the generator body — and therefore the `finally` — never
  runs. Result: a permanently registered subscriber queue that the pump fills forever. **Rejected**,
  with the reason written into `_subscribed_sse_frames`'s docstring so it is not "cleaned up" later.
- **`_PUMPS: dict[str, asyncio.Task]` (the dossier's form).** Proven to break: the stale pump's
  `finally` tears down a re-registered run and the resumed client receives `[None]` and nothing else.
  Measured, both forms, side by side. **Rejected in favour of the `(task, source)` tuple.**
- **Draining only enough of an evicted subscriber's queue to fit the sentinel.** The natural reading
  of "drain with `get_nowait()` to make room". It is wrong: the client then consumes the remaining
  ~999 events, advances its high-water cursor past them, and the ONE dropped event sits permanently
  below the cursor — recreating exactly the unrecoverable hole the change exists to close.
  **Rejected in favour of draining the whole backlog.**
- **Making the mocked e2e `MockSse` consume-once so TS-SSE-RESILIENCE-04 tests the real property.**
  That is D1's decision and D1 already rejects it correctly: it would produce a permanently red test
  that no backend fix could turn green (the mock *is* the server in that suite), which is a worse lie
  than the current false green. **Rejected.**
- **Modifying `_iter_sse_frames` to take a subscriber factory instead of a queue.** Tempting (one
  function instead of two) and wrong: 28 existing tests drive `_iter_sse_frames` directly with a
  hand-built `asyncio.Queue`, and every one of them would need rewriting — turning a surgical fix
  into a test-suite rewrite and destroying the fail-before evidence those tests currently provide.
  **Rejected.**
- **Fixing it in the frontend** (e.g. electing one tab as the sole SSE consumer via a
  `BroadcastChannel` leader). It would leave the backend defect in place for every non-browser
  consumer, and it does not help the reopened-from-History case in the *same* tab. **Rejected.**

### A3 — `_cleanup_pipeline` sends no sentinel on eight of its ten call sites

**Severity:** attached clients hang indefinitely on a resume early-return.
**Confidence:** [V] — all ten call sites traced; released-on-cleanup behaviour verified in prototype.

#### Symptom

A client attached at the moment a run takes a resume early-return path blocks forever in
`await live_queue.get()`, holding an open HTTP connection and a generator frame, until the socket
drops.

#### Root cause

`_cleanup_pipeline` (`run_engine.py:70-73`) pops the registry entries and nothing else:

```python
def _cleanup_pipeline(pipeline_run_id: str) -> None:
    _PIPELINE_QUEUES.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    ...
```

Two of its ten callers (`run_commands.py:2186`, `:2489`) are immediately preceded by
`await event_queue.put(None)`. **The other eight are not** — they are the resume early-return paths
in `engine._fire_resume_cleanup` (`engine.py:7489`), called from `:5551`, `:7541`, `:7586`, `:7591`,
`:7830`, `:7890`, `:7914`, `:7920`, `:7937`, `:7955`. Those pop the queue with no sentinel ever sent.

#### Why it occurred

The sentinel and the cleanup were written as **two separate steps at the call site** rather than as
one atomic operation inside `_cleanup_pipeline`. That works as long as every author remembers both.
The resume tier was added later, by different plans, and its early-return paths only ever needed to
"stop tracking this run" — the author had no reason to think about a subscriber that might be
blocked on the queue, because on the launch path the sentinel was already someone else's job.

#### The fix

Make `_cleanup_pipeline` send the sentinel itself, through the queue object it just popped:

```python
def _cleanup_pipeline(pipeline_run_id: str) -> None:
    q = _PIPELINE_QUEUES.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    ...
    if q is not None:
        try:
            q.put_nowait(None)
        except Exception:
            pass
```

**This is the single most important line in the A-cluster.** Two properties make it safe:

- Because the sentinel goes onto the **source** queue, it queues *behind* anything still pending, so
  nothing is truncated on the normal path where a sentinel was already sent. A second sentinel is
  harmless — the pump breaks on the first, and the queue object is then unreferenced.
- Because the pump holds a direct reference to the queue, popping the dict entry first cannot starve
  it.

**Do NOT sentinel the subscribers directly** — the tempting alternative. Negative control: it
truncates the tail to nothing, because `asyncio.Queue.put` on an unbounded queue does not yield, so
`put(None); _cleanup_pipeline(...)` at `run_commands.py:2185-2186` executes as one atomic step before
the pump has run even once. [V]

#### Verification

`test_cleanup_without_sentinel_releases_attached_clients` — attach a client to a registered queue,
call `_cleanup_pipeline` with no prior sentinel (the resume early-return shape), assert the client's
stream terminates. Verified in prototype. [V]

#### Fully-Detailed Investigation

> **Investigated** 2026-07-30 · **Verdict on the dossier's proposed fix:**
> CONFIRMED-WITH-CORRECTIONS · **Registers read to EOF:** FIX-REGISTER.md (3,705 lines)
> and IMPLEMENTATION-REGISTER.md (4,178 lines) · **Anchor drift found:** 0 of 14 anchors
> moved.
>
> The one-line fix is right, safe, and I reproduced it working against the real
> production generator. The dossier's *arithmetic and classification* are wrong
> ("ten call sites, two sentinelled, eight not" -> actually **12 invocation paths, 3
> sentinelled, 9 not**), one of its cited "sentinel-free early returns" (`engine.py:7830`)
> is in fact the one resume path that IS sentinel-paired, and its impact claim is
> overstated: pre-A2 this fix releases **exactly one** attached client per run, not all
> of them (measured 1 of 3). It also under-states the fix's importance in the other
> direction: **A2 shipped without A3 is worse than today** on those nine paths.

##### I2. Register findings -- prior art, locked decisions, collisions

**The defect has a named author and a register entry.** `git log -S "_cleanup_pipeline"`
plus `git show 8d8a7a39` identifies the exact change that created the sentinel-free
reachability:

```
commit 8d8a7a3920b5a0e2339ba432ffa567f095e1d990  (2026-06-11)
    fix(12): WR-01 unconditional resume bridge cleanup on every resume_run exit path
```

The diff (verified `[V]`) shows that **before** WR-01 the bridge cleanup lived *inside*
`if live_queue is not None:` immediately after `live_queue.put_nowait(None)` -- i.e. it was
structurally impossible to clean up without first sentinelling. WR-01 hoisted it out (to
stop a `_PIPELINE_TASKS` leak) and added it to the three `resume_run` early returns. That
hoist is the birth of A3.
