##### I3. Root cause -- confirmed, corrected, or replaced

**The defect, independently re-derived [V].** The agent's own diagnostic sink is declared at
`bootstrap-ec2.sh:966` (`"logfile": "/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log"`). The set of files the
agent ships is declared 22 lines later at `:987-996`. `/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log` is not
in that set. Both facts are in the same heredoc, 22 lines apart. The agent therefore writes its
entire diagnostic stream to a file that exists only on a box no one can reach without SSM.

**Why it occurred -- the dossier does not say, and the answer matters.** Git blame:

```text
577523b97 (imran-hex 2026-05-11 966)     "logfile": "/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log",
e1a3a4959 (sharas_hx 2026-07-01 988)           {"file_path": "/var/log/nginx/access.log", ...
e1a3a4959 (sharas_hx 2026-07-01 995)           {"file_path": "/var/lib/docker/containers/*/*-json.log", ...
```

The `collect_list` was **rewritten wholesale on 2026-07-01** (`e1a3a495`, the CodeBuild/Terraform
restructure) and the agent's own log still was not added. This is not an ancient oversight that
nobody revisited -- it survived a deliberate rewrite of exactly the block it belongs in. The reason
is visible in the comment the author left at `:954-960`: *"The collect_list mirrors the doc
(nginx access/error, postgres, audit, auth, unattended-upgrades, letsencrypt) PLUS the Docker JSON
log path."* The `collect_list` is a **transcription of `docs/SIMPLE_AWS_DEPLOYMENT.md` section 10.1**, and
that doc's list (verified, `docs/SIMPLE_AWS_DEPLOYMENT.md:1234-1243`) also omits the agent's own
log. The omission is in the design document, and the script is faithful to it. **Fixing the script
without fixing the doc re-arms the same drift** -- the next transcription reproduces the bug.

**Correction 1 to the dossier -- B4 does not cover B1.** The dossier's B1 (`:1068-1071`) frames B4
as the missing signal for B1: *"the one signal that would have named it was the one thing not
collected... Even a working agent would not have shipped its own diagnostics. This is why a month
passed."* The first half is true; the conclusion is not. B1's observed failure is:

```text
Error: failed to create logger: open sink "/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log":
       open /var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log: permission denied
```

The agent **could not open the file**. It therefore wrote zero bytes to it, and a `collect_list`
entry pointing at a nonexistent file ships nothing. Had B4 been in place on day one, `/velocityai/dev/system`
would still have had zero streams. The signal that existed was on **stderr -> journald**, and the
signal that would have fired from outside was **`AWS/Logs IncomingLogEvents` = 0** (E1). B4's real
value is a different, larger failure class (I4.6) -- it is worth doing, but not for the reason B1
gives.

**Correction 2 -- "why a month passed" is over-attributed to B4.** The dossier's own Appendix 2 and
C1 establish that dev's userData has no firstboot service and bootstrap never re-runs, so no deploy
could ever have re-tried the agent; and B6 establishes that 41 alarms were firing into a topic with
zero confirmed subscribers. The month of blindness is caused by B6 (nobody listening) and B1 (the
agent dead), with B4 as an aggravating factor that removed the diagnostic once someone did look.

**Causal chain, corrected:**

```text
agent config declares logfile ------------------------------> /var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log
collect_list (transcribed from a doc that omits it) --------> agent's own log NOT tailed
                                                              |
   +----------------------------------------------------------+
   |
   +-- agent DEAD (B1)          -> file never written  -> B4 buys nothing; E1 meta-alarm is the signal
   +-- agent ALIVE, partly sick -> error line written   -> file is the ONLY place it lands
       (B2 permission denial,      but not shipped         -> invisible outside SSM
        E4 AccessDenied,           and not alarmed
        throttle, rotation loss,
        config-reload rejection)
```

The middle branch is the defect B4 actually fixes, and after B1+B2 land it becomes the **dominant**
remaining failure mode -- eight tailed paths across five different owners and permission models, any
one of which can fail independently and silently.

##### I4. Blast-radius sweep -- every place this reaches

###### I4.1 `bootstrap-ec2.sh` section 14 in full, and the agent's own logging configuration

The entire section is `:941-1007`. Read in full. Structure:

| Lines | What |

| 942-947 | Conditional deb install (`dpkg -s` guard) |
| 948-952 | Re-grant the Docker-containers ACL (B2's territory) |
| 954-960 | Provenance comment: "materialized from SIMPLE_AWS_DEPLOYMENT.md section 10.1" |
| 961-962 | `mkdir -p` + **unquoted** heredoc open |
| **963-968** | **`"agent"` block -- the subject of the brief's question** |
| 969-983 | `"metrics"` block (namespace `VelocityAI/${ENV_TITLE}`, 6 collectors, 2 append_dimensions) |
| 984-1000 | `"logs"` block; `collect_list` at 987-996 |
| 1001 | `EOF` |
| 1003-1007 | `fetch-config -s`, exit status unchecked (B5) |

The `agent` block, verbatim [V]:

```json
  "agent": {
    "metrics_collection_interval": 60,
    "logfile": "/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log",
    "run_as_user": "cwagent"
  },
```

**What is configured today, precisely:**

| Option | Present? | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `logfile` | **yes**, `:966` | `/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log` | Already explicit. The brief's suspicion that this might be defaulted is unfounded -- the author set it deliberately, matching the doc. |
| `run_as_user` | **yes**, `:967` | `cwagent` | The proximate cause of B1. |
| `metrics_collection_interval` | **yes**, `:965` | `60` | |
| `debug` | **no** | (absent -> agent default, believed `false` [I]) | Load-bearing for the feedback question, I4.3. |
| `logfile_backup_count` / any rotation key | **no** | -- | See I4.4 and the schema hazard below. |
| `region`, `credentials`, `omit_hostname`, `aws_sdk_log_level` | **no** | -- | Region is resolved from IMDS; the dossier confirms detection succeeds. |

**Should the fix set `debug` / `logfile_backup_count` explicitly? No -- and this is a deliberate
refusal, not laziness.** Two reasons:

1. **`debug: true` is the exact thing that makes self-tailing dangerous** (I4.3). Setting it
   explicitly to `false` is defensible but redundant; setting it to `true` is the failure. My fix
   instead *pins* the invariant with an executable test
   (`test_agent_debug_logging_is_not_enabled_while_self_tailing`, written and run in I8) so a future
   operator who flips it while the self-entry is present fails CI rather than discovering the loop
   in a CloudWatch bill.
2. **I cannot verify that `logfile_backup_count` is a valid key in this agent's JSON schema, and an
   invalid key is catastrophic here.** The agent validates its config against a JSON schema before
   loading -- the dossier's own live evidence shows the step:
   `Reading json config file path: ... -> I! Valid Json input schema.` If that schema sets
   `additionalProperties: false` on the `agent` object [I], an unrecognised key makes `fetch-config`
   reject the whole config, and the box loses **all** log and metric shipping. Adding an unverified
   key to fix an observability gap, in a script with no test and no CI lint, is exactly the class of
   move that produced this dossier. **Verified locally:** no shellcheck, no JSON validation, and no
   test of any kind exists for `bootstrap-ec2.sh`:

   ```text
   grep -rn "shellcheck" .           -> only 2 in-file `# shellcheck source=/dev/null` directives
   grep -rn "bootstrap-ec2" infra/buildspec.yml .gitlab-ci.yml -> (no matches)
   ```

   The fix ships the missing validation instead of the unverifiable key.

###### I4.3 The feedback loop -- the question the dossier does not ask

**Setup.** If the agent tails its own log, does the act of shipping produce a log line that is
itself shipped?

**What the agent writes, and at what level.** The agent's logger is level-prefixed -- the dossier's
own live capture shows `I!` (info) and `E!` (error) forms:

```text
I! Valid Json input schema.
E! failed to create logger: open sink "/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log": permission denied
```

At **INFO** (the level in force today, since `debug` is absent from `:964-968` [V]), the logs plugin
writes on **lifecycle transitions only** -- tailer start, offset reset, rotation detected, publish
error, throttle, config reload -- and **not per published batch** [I]. Per-batch detail is a `D!`
line, emitted only when `debug: true` [I].

**Therefore, at the current level, the loop's gain is zero.** Publishing a batch writes nothing, so
there is nothing new for the self-tailer to read, so nothing new to publish. Self-tailing is a
one-shot: at agent start the plugin logs "starting tailer for /var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log",
that single line ships, and steady state is silent. **No amplification. [I], but structurally sound
and I show the reasoning rather than asserting it.**

**With `debug: true`, the loop is real and geometric.** Each publish writes >= 1 `D!` line; the
self-tailer reads it; the next flush publishes it, writing another `D!` line. With N tailed files
and a ~5s force-flush interval [I], the self-stream's own content grows by roughly
`(lines per publish) x N` per cycle. With N = 9 that is a gain far above 1: the self-stream, the
agent's disk usage, and CloudWatch ingestion all diverge. **This is a genuine hazard, not a
theoretical one, and it is created *by* B4** -- before B4 the loop cannot exist because the file is
not tailed.

**Mitigation, in the order I actually recommend it:**

1. **Do not enable `debug` while the self-entry is present.** It is off today [V]; my fix does not
   turn it on [V]; and `test_agent_debug_logging_is_not_enabled_while_self_tailing` (written and run
   in I8) makes the pair a CI-enforced invariant. This is the whole mitigation -- the loop is
   *absent*, not *dampened*.
2. **If DEBUG is ever needed for live troubleshooting, remove the self-entry first.** Exact
   procedure in I5, step H4. It is three commands and it is reversible.
3. **REJECTED:** an `exclude` filter on the self-entry to drop `D!` lines. Two reasons. (a) It is an
   unverified schema key -- same catastrophic-rejection risk as I4.1. (b) It makes the loop
   *invisible* rather than absent: the agent still writes the debug lines and still burns the disk
   and the CPU reading and discarding them, and the moment the filter expression drifts from the
   agent's log format the loop returns silently. Damping a positive-feedback loop with a text
   pattern is not a fix.

**Crash-loop against a file the agent also tails.** Three cases, and they behave differently:

| Case | What lands in the file | What ships | Does B4 help? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Logger construction fails** (B1's exact failure) | nothing -- the open() itself failed | nothing | **No.** Signal is stderr -> journald. |
| **B. Logger OK, agent dies within seconds; systemd restarts ~1/min** (the observed `restart counter 977` cadence) | startup banner + fatal error, appended on every restart. At ~1-3 KB per attempt that is ~1.5-4 MB/day. | **nothing** -- the logs plugin batches on a ~5s force-flush [I]; a process that lives 2s never reaches a flush | **No.** Signal is E1's meta-alarm (zero incoming events). |
| **C. Agent healthy, one sub-component sick** (B2 permission denial, E4 `AccessDenied` on `DescribeLogGroups`, PutLogEvents throttling, rotation confusion, a rejected config reload) | the `E!`/`W!` line naming the exact path and errno | **yes** -- the agent is alive and flushing | **Yes. This is what B4 buys.** |

Case B's disk growth is bounded and harmless: root is 32% used with 4% inodes [V, dossier Appendix
2] on a 60 GB volume (`app/dev.tfvars: root_volume_size_gb = 60`), so 4 MB/day is noise. It never
reaches CloudWatch, so it costs nothing.

###### I4.4 Rotation and truncation

**What rotates this file today: nothing in this repo.**

```text
grep -rn "logrotate" infra/ docs/SIMPLE_AWS_DEPLOYMENT.md
(no matches)
```

No `/etc/logrotate.d/` drop-in is authored by bootstrap, and the deployment doc never mentions
rotation. Whatever rotation exists is whatever the `amazon-cloudwatch-agent` deb and the agent's own
internal logger provide (the agent is understood to self-rotate its `logfile` [I]; I cannot verify
the size/backup thresholds from here).

**I deliberately do not add a logrotate rule.** An external rotation of a file an internal rotator
already owns is a fight with two bad outcomes: `create` mode renames out from under the agent's open
fd (writes vanish until the agent notices), `copytruncate` mode leaves the writer's offset intact
and produces a sparse NUL hole that the tailer then ships. The agent's file tailer handles rotation
of files it tails through inode tracking plus its on-disk state file, and tailing a self-rotated
file is the same code path as tailing nginx's logrotate'd `access.log`. Leave it alone.

**Truncation on a fresh boot -- and the correction to B1 this forces. MEASURED [V]:**

```text
$ printf 'old content\n' > t.log ; ino_before=$(stat -f %i t.log)
$ exec 9>>t.log                       # simulate the running agent's open write fd
$ install -m 0644 /dev/null t.log     # B1's proposed pre-create line
$ ino_after=$(stat -f %i t.log)
$ printf 'written-after-install\n' >&9

inode before=102570225 after=102570226  same=NO
content of t.log:  (empty)
size = 0
```

`install /dev/null <target>` **replaces the inode**. The write issued through the pre-existing fd
went to the now-unlinked old inode and is unrecoverable. Against a *running* agent this means:

- the agent's writer fd points at an unlinked inode -- every subsequent diagnostic is written into
  the void;
- the new tailer follows the new, permanently-empty inode;
- **the self-log stream goes silent forever, with no error anywhere.** B4 is defeated, silently, by
  B1's own fix line.

This is not hypothetical: **C1's entire purpose is to create a path that re-runs section 13/section 14 on a live
box.** The first reconcile after the fix would break it.

Measured control, same harness [V]:

```text
$ printf 'existing\n' > s.log ; exec 7>>s.log
$ touch s.log ; chmod 0640 s.log
$ printf 'after-touch\n' >&7

touch inode before=102570857 after=102570857 same=YES
content: existing / after-touch
```

`touch` + `chmod` preserve the inode and the open fd. **B1's pre-create must be
`touch` + `chown` + `chmod`, not `install /dev/null`.** (The measurement is BSD `install` on macOS;
GNU coreutils `install` on the Ubuntu target may instead `O_TRUNC` in place [I] -- but that outcome
is *also* bad, producing a sparse NUL hole that the tailer ships when it detects `size < offset`.
Both variants are avoided by the same three-command form, so the fix is correct either way.)

**Does a legitimate truncation cause duplicates or loss?** No duplicates. The agent's tailer keeps a
byte offset per file in its state directory; when the file shrinks below the recorded offset it
treats that as a rotation and resets to 0, re-reading only what is currently there. Since the old
content is gone, nothing is re-shipped. The exposure is *loss* (anything truncated before it
flushed), which is acceptable and unavoidable, and is exactly why the pre-create must be
non-destructive on the re-run path.

###### I4.5 Stream naming, destination group, retention, cost

**Stream name: `{instance_id}/cwagent`.** Requirements: distinct from `{instance_id}` (B3 is
retiring that for `system` anyway), distinct from `{instance_id}/docker` (a different group, but
consistency matters), and self-describing. It follows the in-file precedent at `:995` and matches
the unix account name. Rejected `{instance_id}/agent` -- "agent" means an LLM agent everywhere else
in this product's vocabulary and would read as an application log.

**Group: `/velocityai/<env>/system`, NOT a dedicated group. This is a fence decision, not a
preference.** `local.log_groups` lives in `infra/terraform/modules/monitoring/main.tf:15-23`, a
module instantiated by **dev, stage and prod** (`app/main.tf:169-170`). Adding a ninth name there
would create a new log group in **all three** environments on their next apply -- a direct
violation of the user's "dev environment only -- do not plan changes to `stage` or `prod`
resources." Reusing `system` needs **zero Terraform change**, so there is no plan, no apply, and no
cross-environment reach. It also inherits `prevent_destroy`, the CMK, and retention for free.

The cost of that choice is honest and small: the agent's log shares a group with auditd and
unattended-upgrades, so a future per-group retention override or metric filter cannot target it
independently. Per-stream filtering (`aws logs tail ... --log-stream-names`) covers the operational
need.

**Retention.** `app/dev.tfvars:23` sets `log_retention_days = 14` and `log_retention_overrides` is
unset (default `{}`, `modules/monitoring/variables.tf:41-46`), so every dev group -- including
`system` -- is **14 days**. No change required.

**Cost at DEBUG volume.** Arithmetic shown; the eu-central-1 unit price is [I] (~$0.63/GB ingested,
~$0.03/GB-month stored):

| Scenario | Volume | Ingest/month |
|---|---|---|
| INFO, healthy (today's level) | a few KB/day | effectively $0 |
| INFO, crash-looping 1/min (the observed cadence) | ~4 MB/day = 120 MB/mo -- but see I4.3 case B: **it never ships** | $0 |
| DEBUG, self-entry **removed** | ~9 streams x ~12 flushes/min x ~150 B ~= 23 MB/day = 700 MB/mo | ~$0.44/mo |
| DEBUG, self-entry **present** | divergent (I4.3) | unbounded |

**The conclusion to internalise: DEBUG's danger here is amplification, not spend.** Nobody will
notice $0.44. The loop is what bites.

###### I4.6 [V]/[I] -- can a dead agent ship its own death, and what covers total failure

**No. A dead agent ships nothing, including this. [V]** -- it is definitional: the process that
tails the file is the process that died. Anyone reading B4 as "now we will see it when the agent
dies" has misread it.

The three mechanisms and exactly what each covers:

| Failure class | Example | B5 (install-time assert) | E1 (`IncomingLogEvents` meta-alarm) | **B4 (self-log)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agent fails to start during provisioning | B1 as it happened, on a box where bootstrap actually runs | **COVERS** -- `-a status` != running -> `exit 1` -> the provisioning step fails loudly | covers (eventually, within the 1h period) | no -- nothing written |
| Agent dies later / crash-loops after a healthy start | OOM, a bad config reload, package upgrade | no -- bootstrap has already exited | **COVERS** -- the only mechanism that fires | no -- I4.3 case B |
| Agent never installed / not enabled on a rebuilt box | dev's userData has no firstboot service (C1) | no -- the script never ran | **COVERS** | no |
| Agent alive, whole-account shipping broken | IAM revoked, VPC endpoint down, CMK policy change | no | **COVERS** | partly -- the error is written, but it also cannot be shipped |
| **Agent alive, ONE destination broken** | B2's `adm`-group denial on `auth.log`; `letsencrypt/` at `0700 root:root`; a per-group KMS denial | no | only if the meta-alarm is per-group | **COVERS -- and is the only mechanism that says WHY** |
| Agent alive, transient degradation | PutLogEvents throttling, sequence-token contention (B3), rotation-detection loss | no | no -- events still flow | **COVERS** |

**The three together are complete only if E1's meta-alarm is per-group.** E1 as written
(dossier `:1856-1859`) proposes it for `nginx-access` and `app`. Two corrections that belong to E1
but that B4 must state because B4's coverage depends on them:

- **The `system` group needs the meta-alarm too**, or the agent's own stream has no liveness guard
  -- and the group my entry lands in is precisely the one that would prove the agent is alive.
- **`nginx-access` is a poor liveness proxy on dev.** There is no ALB, no synthetic canary, and no
  external monitor in the account (verified: no `aws_cloudwatch_synthetics_canary`, no ALB anywhere
  in `infra/terraform`). A quiet night on dev produces zero nginx requests and the alarm fires
  falsely, which is exactly how alarm fatigue restarts. **`system` is the better anchor**: auditd
  writes continuously and never idles. I raise this in I11 as an E1 sequencing note rather than
  absorbing it.

###### Host half -- evaporates on instance replacement

The dev box has no firstboot service and bootstrap never re-runs (C1 [V]), so the repo change alone
changes nothing on the running instance. Apply via a **single-instance-id** SSM command -- never
`--targets`, because six tag values are byte-identical across dev/stage/prod.

```bash
# H0. Refuse to proceed unless this is exactly the dev box.
DEV=i-092d5961f5aca87a6
NAME=$(aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids "$DEV" \
  --query 'Reservations[0].Instances[0].Tags[?Key==`Name`].Value|[0]' --output text)
[ "$NAME" = "velocityai-dev-app" ] || { echo "REFUSING: $DEV is '$NAME'"; exit 1; }
```

On-host payload (delivered via `aws ssm send-command --instance-ids "$DEV" --document-name
AWS-RunShellScript`). It is idempotent, backs up first, and rolls back on validation failure:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
CFG=/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json
BAK=/root/cwagent-backup-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
install -d -m 0700 "$BAK"
cp -a "$CFG" "$BAK/" 2>/dev/null || true

# H1. Pre-create the sink NON-DESTRUCTIVELY. This is B1's line, corrected:
#     `install /dev/null` replaces the inode and orphans a running agent's
#     write fd (measured). touch/chown/chmod are safe on a re-run.
touch /var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log
chown cwagent:cwagent /var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log
chmod 0640 /var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log

# H2. Verify the agent can read what it is about to be told to tail.
#     Owner is cwagent, so the OWNER permission bits apply -- no ACL and no
#     `adm` group membership is required for THIS file (B2 covers the others).
sudo -u cwagent test -r /var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log \
  || { echo "FATAL: cwagent cannot read its own log"; exit 1; }

# H3. Rewrite the collect_list in place with jq -- do NOT hand-edit, and do
#     NOT re-run bootstrap-ec2.sh (it would also rewrite nginx, postgres and
#     systemd units, and ENVIRONMENT defaults to "prod" if the caller has not
#     sourced /etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env -- see I10).
. /etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env
ENVIRONMENT="${VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT:?refusing: VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT unset}"
jq --arg env "$ENVIRONMENT" '
  .logs.logs_collected.files.collect_list |= (
    map(
      if .file_path == "/var/log/audit/audit.log"
        then .log_stream_name = "{instance_id}/audit"
      elif .file_path == "/var/log/unattended-upgrades/unattended-upgrades.log"
        then .log_stream_name = "{instance_id}/unattended-upgrades"
      else . end
    )
    + (if any(.[]; .file_path == "/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log") then []
       else [{
         file_path:       "/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log",
         log_group_name:  ("/velocityai/" + $env + "/system"),
         log_stream_name: "{instance_id}/cwagent",
         timezone:        "UTC"
       }] end)
  )' "$CFG" > "$CFG.new"

# H3b. Validate before swapping. jq already proved it is JSON; assert the
#      invariants the offline test asserts.
python3 - "$CFG.new" <<'PY'
import json, sys
c = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
cl = c["logs"]["logs_collected"]["files"]["collect_list"]
assert any(e["file_path"] == "/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log" for e in cl), "self-log missing"
pairs = [(e["log_group_name"], e["log_stream_name"]) for e in cl]
assert len(pairs) == len(set(pairs)), f"colliding (group,stream): {pairs}"
assert c["agent"].get("debug", False) is False, "debug on while self-tailing"
print(f"OK: {len(cl)} entries, all (group,stream) unique, debug off")
PY
mv "$CFG.new" "$CFG"

# H4. Reload. fetch-config restarts the agent; assert it is actually running
#     (B5's assertion, applied here so this step cannot silently no-op).
/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl \
    -a fetch-config -m ec2 -s -c "file:$CFG"
sleep 5
if ! /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl -m ec2 -a status \
     | grep -q '"status": *"running"'; then
  echo "FATAL: agent not running after fetch-config -- restoring backup" >&2
  cp -a "$BAK/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json" "$CFG"
  /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl \
      -a fetch-config -m ec2 -s -c "file:$CFG" || true
  journalctl -u amazon-cloudwatch-agent -n 40 --no-pager >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: agent running; backup at $BAK"
```

**Temporary-DEBUG procedure** (the I4.3 mitigation, for an operator who needs it later):

```bash
# 1. Remove the self-entry FIRST -- otherwise debug output feeds itself.
jq 'del(.logs.logs_collected.files.collect_list[]
        | select(.file_path == "/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log"))
    | .agent.debug = true' "$CFG" > "$CFG.dbg" && mv "$CFG.dbg" "$CFG"
# 2. reload, reproduce, read /var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log over SSM
# 3. revert: .agent.debug = false, re-add the entry, reload.
```

##### I6. Ripple-effect analysis -- why nothing else breaks

Assume the fix is wrong and hunt for the failure.

**"The agent rejects the new config and the box loses ALL shipping."** The realistic version of this
is an invalid key or malformed JSON, and it is why H3 uses `jq` (which cannot emit invalid JSON) and
H3b validates before the swap, and why R4's offline test parses the rendered heredoc. The
`collect_list` entry itself uses only the four keys already present on all eight existing entries --
no new key anywhere in the config. **This is also the concrete reason I refuse to add `debug` or a
rotation key** (I4.1). If it still fails, H4's status assertion restores the backup automatically.

**"Two writers, one stream."** Impossible by construction and by test:
`test_every_group_stream_pair_is_unique` asserts uniqueness across the whole array, and it fails on
the tree *today* (B3's real collision), so it is proven non-vacuous.

**"The self-tail deadlocks or reenters."** The tailer and the logger are separate concerns in the
same process: the logger appends, the tailer reads at an offset. There is no lock shared between
them and no ordering dependency. The only coupling is content (I4.3), and it is gain-zero at the
configured level.

**"A restart replays the whole file and duplicates events."** The agent persists a per-file byte
offset in its state directory and resumes from it. On a genuine truncation it resets to 0 and
re-reads only what is present -- see I4.4. The one case that *would* duplicate is the file being
replaced by a *different* inode with the same content, which is exactly the `install /dev/null`
hazard I am removing.

**Startup / shutdown ordering.** The pre-create (H1) must precede `fetch-config` (H4) so the tailer
finds an existing, readable file at start; if it did not, the agent logs "file not found" and
retries -- degraded, not fatal. In the durable path, bootstrap's line order already gives this for
free (the pre-create sits in section 14 before the `cat > ...json` heredoc).

**Under a slow client / unattached client / crashed run / restart / resume / fan-out / revision /
two browsers.** All null. This change touches no backend process, no SSE stream, no queue, no DB
row, no HTTP route. There is no shared state between the CloudWatch agent and the application: the
agent reads Docker's JSON log files from disk, which the app writes to via stdout regardless.

**Memory and connection-pool effects.** None. The agent is a separate process with its own memory;
BUG-004's pool-leak class (`FIX`/quick 260716-heb) is a FastAPI `get_db` teardown issue and shares
no code with this.

**Partial application.** Four sub-cases, all benign:
- Repo change lands, host not patched: the file is source-of-truth-correct and inert until C1's
  reconcile or an instance rebuild. Nothing breaks.
- Host patched, repo not: the next instance rebuild loses it. Detectable by the offline test
  failing. Do not do this -- I10 orders repo-first.
- B4 lands without B3: the new `{instance_id}/cwagent` stream is still unique, so B4 works; B3's
  pre-existing audit/unattended collision persists unchanged. **B4 does not depend on B3 for
  correctness** -- only for the block alignment being done once.
- B4 lands without B1: the file does not exist, the agent logs "no such file" once per retry, and
  nothing ships from that entry. Harmless but pointless. B1 is a hard prerequisite for *value*, not
  for *safety*.

**The one genuine new hazard this fix creates** is the DEBUG amplification loop (I4.3). It did not
exist before, because the file was not tailed. It is mitigated by a config invariant plus an
executable test, and documented at the point of change (R2). I would rather name it plainly than let
a future operator discover it.

**Where the dossier already argues safety, verified rather than restated:** B4 says the fix is
"destination `/velocityai/<env>/system` and a distinct stream name per B3." I verified the
destination exists in Terraform, is CMK-encrypted, has 14-day retention on dev, is covered by the
existing IAM grant, and **has zero metric filters** -- so the "safe" claim holds for a stronger
reason than the dossier gives.

##### I8. Test plan -- fail-before / pass-after

**The repo has no test of any kind for `bootstrap-ec2.sh`** -- no shellcheck in CI, no JSON
validation, no lint (verified in I4.1). That absence is why the omission shipped. The fix therefore
includes the guard, not just the entry.

###### New file, complete source: `backend/tests/unit/test_cloudwatch_agent_config.py`

```python
"""Offline guards on the CloudWatch-agent config emitted by bootstrap-ec2.sh.

Pure-stdlib text/JSON assertions over two infra files. No AWS, no network, no
backend import -> cannot perturb INV-3 goldens and is invisible to
import-linter (backend/tests is not an import-linter root package).
"""
import json
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

REPO = Path(os.environ.get("FLOWIN_REPO", Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]))
BOOTSTRAP = REPO / "infra" / "scripts" / "bootstrap-ec2.sh"
MONITORING = REPO / "infra" / "terraform" / "modules" / "monitoring" / "main.tf"

AGENT_SELF_LOG = "/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log"


def _render_agent_config(environment: str = "dev") -> dict:
    """Extract the section-14 heredoc and render it exactly as bash would."""
    text = BOOTSTRAP.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    m = re.search(
        r"cat > /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent\.json <<EOF\n(.*?)\nEOF\n",
        text,
        re.S,
    )
    assert m, "could not locate the amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json heredoc in bootstrap-ec2.sh"
    body = m.group(1)
    # Unquoted heredoc: ${ENVIRONMENT}/${ENV_TITLE} interpolate; \${aws:...} does not.
    body = body.replace("${ENVIRONMENT}", environment)
    body = body.replace("${ENV_TITLE}", environment.capitalize())
    body = body.replace("\\${", "${")
    return json.loads(body)


def _terraform_log_groups(environment: str = "dev") -> set[str]:
    text = MONITORING.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    m = re.search(r"log_groups\s*=\s*\[(.*?)\]", text, re.S)
    assert m, "could not locate local.log_groups in the monitoring module"
    names = re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', m.group(1))
    return {n.replace("${var.environment}", environment) for n in names}


def _collect_list(cfg: dict) -> list[dict]:
    return cfg["logs"]["logs_collected"]["files"]["collect_list"]


def test_agent_config_is_valid_json():
    cfg = _render_agent_config()
    assert cfg["agent"]["run_as_user"] == "cwagent"
    assert cfg["agent"]["logfile"] == AGENT_SELF_LOG


def test_agent_self_log_is_collected():
    """B4: the observability system must observe itself."""
    paths = [e["file_path"] for e in _collect_list(_render_agent_config())]
    assert AGENT_SELF_LOG in paths, (
        "the CloudWatch agent's own log (agent.logfile) is not in collect_list -- "
        "an in-agent failure produces no external signal (B4)"
    )


def test_every_group_stream_pair_is_unique():
    """B3: two files on one (group, stream) contend for a sequence token."""
    pairs = [
        (e["log_group_name"], e["log_stream_name"])
        for e in _collect_list(_render_agent_config())
    ]
    dupes = {p for p in pairs if pairs.count(p) > 1}
    assert not dupes, f"colliding (log_group, log_stream) pairs in collect_list: {sorted(dupes)}"


def test_every_destination_group_exists_in_terraform():
    """Name drift = alarms watching a group nothing writes to."""
    declared = _terraform_log_groups()
    used = {e["log_group_name"] for e in _collect_list(_render_agent_config())}
    assert used <= declared, f"collect_list ships to undeclared log group(s): {sorted(used - declared)}"


def test_agent_debug_logging_is_not_enabled_while_self_tailing():
    """DEBUG + self-tail is a publish->log->publish amplification loop."""
    cfg = _render_agent_config()
    paths = [e["file_path"] for e in _collect_list(cfg)]
    if AGENT_SELF_LOG in paths:
        assert cfg["agent"].get("debug", False) is False, (
            "agent.debug is on while the agent's own log is tailed -- "
            "each published batch logs a line that is itself published"
        )
```

Command:


##### I9. Rollback

**Repo half.** `git revert <sha>`. One commit, three files, no migration, no schema, no state. The
`aws_s3_object.bootstrap_script` `source_hash = filemd5(...)` re-uploads the reverted script to
`s3://velocityai-dev-pg-dumps-577954642302/config/bootstrap-ec2.sh` on the next dev push, and
nowhere else (per-env bucket, verified at `app/main.tf:79-94`). Fully reversible.

**Host half.** The payload writes `/root/cwagent-backup-<ts>/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json` before
touching anything, and H4 restores it automatically if the agent is not `running` after reload.
Manual rollback:

```bash
cp -a /root/cwagent-backup-<ts>/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json \
      /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json
/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl \
    -a fetch-config -m ec2 -s -c file:/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json
```

**What is NOT reversible, and what the pre-change backup must capture.**

- **There is no filesystem-level rollback.** `velocityai-dev-root` has `delete_on_termination = true`
  and **zero snapshots** [V, dossier Appendix 2]. The `/root/cwagent-backup-<ts>/` copy is the only
  restore point for the config, and it lives on the same volume it protects. If the box is
  terminated, both are gone -- recovery is then "rebuild from the repo," which is fine because the
  repo half is the source of truth.
- **Log data already ingested cannot be un-ingested.** Irrelevant here: 14-day retention on dev, and
  the content is the agent's own diagnostics -- no secrets, no PII, no credentials. Worth stating
  because it is the only irreversible side effect of the change.
- **What the backup MUST capture, and does:** the pre-change
  `amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json` (the only mutated file). It must **not** try to capture
  `/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log` -- H1 is deliberately non-destructive, so the file's content
  survives the change untouched. That is the whole point of the `install`-to-`touch` correction.

##### I10. Sequencing and dependencies

**Hard prerequisite -- B1, and only for value.** B1 pre-creates the file with `cwagent` ownership.
Without it the entry points at a nonexistent (or root-owned) file: the agent logs a miss and ships
nothing. **B4 without B1 is inert, not broken** -- there is no failure mode, just no benefit. The
dossier's ordering claim is correct; the reason is milder than it implies.

**B1 must be corrected before B4 is worth anything.** This is the one *new* ordering constraint I
found and it is not in the dossier. B1's proposed
`install -o cwagent -g cwagent -m 0644 /dev/null /var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log` replaces the
inode on a re-run (measured, I4.4), which silently and permanently kills the self-log stream the
first time C1's reconcile runs. **B1's executor must ship `touch` + `chown cwagent:cwagent` +
`chmod 0640` instead.** If B1 ships as written, B4 works exactly once and then dies invisibly.

**Same-file coupling with B2, B3, B5 -- all four edit `bootstrap-ec2.sh` section 14 (941-1007).**

| Issue | Lines it edits | Overlaps B4? |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | inserts a pre-create near `:961` (before the heredoc) | no |
| B2 | `:951-952` (setfacl) + a new `usermod -a -G adm cwagent` | no |
| **B3** | **`:991` and `:993`** (stream names) | **YES -- same array, and B3 forces the timezone-column shift** |
| **B4** | **inserts 1 line in `:987-996`** | -- |
| B5 | `:1003-1007` (assert `-a status`) | no |

**How the four merge into one coherent block.** Recommended: **one commit, four ordered hunks**,
because they are four edits to one 66-line section that will be reviewed and reverted as a unit:

1. **B2 first** -- `usermod -a -G adm cwagent` beside the existing `:951-952` setfacl. It is above
   the heredoc and independent.
2. **B1 second** -- the corrected non-destructive pre-create, immediately after B2's block and
   before `mkdir -p /opt/aws/...` at `:961`. Placing it before the heredoc means the file exists
   before `fetch-config` starts the tailer.
3. **B3 + B4 together** -- the single realigned 9-line `collect_list` in I5 R1. Do not split these:
   B3's `{instance_id}/unattended-upgrades` moves the `"timezone"` column for every row, so
   splitting produces two whole-array realignments and a meaningless second review.
4. **B5 last** -- the `-a status` assertion after `fetch-config` at `:1007`. It goes last so it
   validates everything above it.

Verify the merged section once: `python3.11 -m pytest backend/tests/unit/test_cloudwatch_agent_config.py -q`
must be 5 passed, and `bash -n infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh` must exit 0.

**C1 -- structural blocker for the host half, not the repo half.** The repo change is deliverable
today (a dev push re-uploads the script via `aws_s3_object.bootstrap_script`); it simply does not
reach the running box. C1's SSM path is what makes it live. **Two C1 hazards this investigation
surfaced that C1 does not state:**

- **Do not deliver this by re-running `bootstrap-ec2.sh` wholesale.** The script also rewrites
  nginx, Postgres, systemd units and the app stack -- a vastly larger blast radius than a
  `collect_list` edit warrants. Use the targeted `jq` payload in I5 H3.
- **`ENVIRONMENT` defaults to `prod`** (`bootstrap-ec2.sh:79`). Any host-side re-run of section 14 that has
  not sourced `/etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env` writes a config that ships **dev's logs into prod's
  log groups** -- cross-environment contamination in a repo whose entire isolation story is
  per-environment. H3 sources the file and hard-fails on an unset value; C1's payload must do the
  same.

**E1 -- must land for the coverage story to be complete, and needs one correction.** B4 covers only
the "agent alive, partly sick" class (I4.6). The dead-agent class is E1's `IncomingLogEvents`
meta-alarm. **Correction for E1's executor:** extend it to `/velocityai/dev/system`, and prefer
`system` over `nginx-access` as the primary liveness anchor -- there is no ALB, no canary and no
external monitor in the account, so a quiet night on dev makes an `nginx-access`-anchored alarm fire
falsely, restarting the alarm-fatigue cycle B6 documents. auditd never idles.

**B6 -- must land after B1/B2/B4, before anyone is expected to act.** Confirming the SNS
subscription while 41 alarms are firing buries the subscriber. The dossier already says this; it
applies to B4 because B4's whole value is a signal someone reads.

**E4 -- pure upside, no ordering constraint.** `logs:DescribeLogGroups` scoped to a resource ARN is a
no-op grant. Once B1 is fixed the agent may call it and get `AccessDenied`. **That `AccessDenied`
would land in the agent's own log -- which is a live demonstration of exactly the class B4 exists
for.** Fixing E4 first is cleaner; fixing it second is a good self-test.

**Commit boundaries.** One commit for the four section 14 edits (B1+B2+B3+B4) with the guard test; a
separate commit for B5 if the executor prefers finer grain; the doc sync (R3) rides the same commit
as R1 so the source and its transcription never diverge again.

##### I11. Open questions requiring a human decision

1. **Adopt the companion entry for `/var/log/velocityai-bootstrap.log` (I5 R2b)?**
   The code comment at `bootstrap-ec2.sh:496` states that a CRITICAL IMDSv1-drift warning "is the
   operator signal; cwagent ships it to `/velocityai/${env}/system`." That is provably false today
   -- the file is not in the `collect_list`. It is the same defect class as B4, one line, same
   group, same stream convention, and no dossier issue owns it.
   *Options:* (a) include it in the same commit; (b) file it as a new issue for a separate pass;
   (c) instead delete the misleading comment.
   **Recommendation: (a).** It is one line, zero marginal risk, and it closes the second half of the
   same "the observer's own output is not collected" gap while the file is open. Choosing (b) is
   defensible on scope-discipline grounds; choosing (c) is not -- it removes the claim rather than
   making it true.

2. **Should the `IncomingLogEvents` meta-alarm's primary anchor be `system` rather than
   `nginx-access` (E1)?**
   This is a genuine behaviour choice with a false-positive cost either way, and it is E1's to make,
   but B4's completeness argument depends on it (I4.6). *Options:* (a) keep E1's `nginx-access` +
   `app` and additionally add `system`; (b) make `system` primary.
   **Recommendation: (a)** -- add `system`, keep the others, and let the first week of dev data show
   whether `nginx-access` idles overnight before demoting it.

3. **Is a permanently self-tailing agent acceptable given the DEBUG hazard?**
   The loop is absent at the configured level and pinned by a test (I4.3), but the hazard is real
   and newly created by this change. *Options:* (a) ship as designed, with the test as the guard;
   (b) do not tail the agent's own log at all and rely solely on E1 + on-demand SSM reads.
   **Recommendation: (a).** (b) trades a guarded, test-pinned hazard for a permanent requirement
   that a human have SSM access and know to look -- which is the exact condition that let this
   dossier's findings hide for a month.

##### I12. Shortcuts and alternatives explicitly rejected

**Verifying the dossier's own rejections first.** B1 rejects `run_as_user: root` ("widens the blast
radius of a log-shipping daemon for no reason"). **Verified and agreed, with an additional reason
the dossier misses:** running as root would also make the self-log root-owned, which then needs
either a wider mode or an ACL for nothing -- the `cwagent`-owned file needs neither (I5 H2). The
dossier lists no rejections for B4 itself; these are mine.

1. **Set `agent.debug: true` "so the self-log is actually useful."**
   Fails: it creates the amplification loop (I4.3). The useful content -- errors and warnings -- is
   already at `E!`/`W!` and ships at the default level. DEBUG adds per-batch chatter that is exactly
   the thing that feeds itself.

2. **Add `logfile_backup_count` (or any rotation key) to bound the file.**
   Fails: I cannot verify the key exists in this agent version's JSON schema, and the agent
   validates the config before loading. If the schema is closed, an unknown key makes `fetch-config`
   reject the whole config and the box loses **all** log and metric shipping -- a strictly worse
   outcome than the problem. Rotation is already the agent's own concern (I4.4), and the growth even
   in the crash-loop case is ~4 MB/day against a 32%-used 60 GB volume.

3. **Add an `/etc/logrotate.d/amazon-cloudwatch-agent` drop-in.**
   Fails: two rotators, one file. `create` mode renames out from under the agent's open fd (writes
   vanish silently); `copytruncate` leaves the writer's offset intact and produces a sparse NUL hole
   that the tailer then ships. This is a real bug I would be introducing to solve a non-problem.

4. **Create a dedicated `/velocityai/<env>/cwagent` log group.**
   Fails the user's scope fence. `local.log_groups` lives in a module instantiated by dev, stage and
   prod (`app/main.tf:169-170`); adding a name creates the group in **all three** on their next
   apply. Reusing `system` requires zero Terraform, so there is no plan and no cross-environment
   reach. The cost -- no independent retention or metric filter for the agent's stream -- is
   recoverable with `--log-stream-names`.

5. **Add an `exclude` filter on the self-entry to break the DEBUG loop.**
   Fails twice: unverified schema key (see 2), and it damps rather than removes the loop -- the
   agent still writes, reads and discards the debug lines, and a drift between the filter expression
   and the agent's log format silently restores the amplifier.

6. **Ship the agent's log to the `app` group instead of `system`.**
   Fails: `app` carries **three** metric filters (`db_conn_error` `:502`, `ws_disconnect` `:642`,
   `agent_error_rate` `:857`). `agent_error_rate` in particular is a pattern-matched counter over
   application text; feeding it a stream full of lines the CloudWatch agent prefixes with `E!` is
   a plausible false-positive source and would corrupt a live alarm. `system` has zero filters
   (I4.2). This is the sharpest reason the group choice is not arbitrary.

7. **Use `install -o cwagent -g cwagent -m 0644 /dev/null <file>` as B1 proposes.**
   Fails, measured: it replaces the inode (I4.4), orphaning a running agent's write fd and leaving
   the tailer on a permanently empty file. Silent, permanent, and triggered by the very reconcile
   path C1 is building. `touch` + `chown` + `chmod` is the correct form and is verified
   inode-preserving.

8. **Skip the doc update (`docs/SIMPLE_AWS_DEPLOYMENT.md` section 10.1) as "just docs."**
   Fails: `bootstrap-ec2.sh:954` names that doc as the source the `collect_list` is transcribed
   from, and the doc's list is where the omission actually lives (I3). Fixing only the script leaves
   the defect in the specification and guarantees the next transcription -- or the next environment
   built from the doc -- reproduces it.

9. **Skip the offline test because "it is only a config line."**
   Fails: a config line with no test is precisely what shipped this defect, survived a full rewrite
   of the surrounding block on 2026-07-01, and hid for a month. The repo has **no** shellcheck, no
   JSON validation, and no test for `bootstrap-ec2.sh` (verified). Four of the five assertions cost
   nothing to run (0.07s, stdlib only) and two of them are red on the tree today.

10. **Deliver the host change by re-running `bootstrap-ec2.sh` over SSM.**
    Fails: the script rewrites nginx, Postgres, systemd units and the app stack, and `ENVIRONMENT`
    silently defaults to `prod` if `/etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env` was not sourced
    (`bootstrap-ec2.sh:79`) -- which would ship dev's logs into prod's log groups. The targeted `jq`
    payload (I5 H3) touches one file, validates before swapping, and hard-fails on an unset
    environment.

### B5 — `fetch-config` exit status is never checked

**Severity:** the reason B1 was silent at provisioning time.
**Confidence:** [V]

#### Symptom / root cause

`bootstrap-ec2.sh:1003-1007` installs and starts the agent, ending with
`amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl -a fetch-config -s`. Its exit status is not checked, and the wrapper
ends in `systemctl restart` which returns 0 on fork. Bootstrap therefore reports success on a service
that dies immediately.

#### Why it occurred

`set -euo pipefail` is in force (`:26`), so the author reasonably expected a failing command to abort
the script. It did not, because the command genuinely *succeeded* — it successfully asked systemd to
start something. The gap is between "the request succeeded" and "the service is running", and
`systemctl restart` does not distinguish them for a service that fails after forking.

#### The fix

After `fetch-config -s`, assert the agent is actually running and fail loudly if not:

```bash
amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl -m ec2 -a status | grep -q '"status": *"running"' || {
  echo "FATAL: CloudWatch agent is not running after fetch-config" >&2
  journalctl -u amazon-cloudwatch-agent -n 40 --no-pager >&2
  exit 1
}
```

Also `systemctl enable amazon-cloudwatch-agent` explicitly rather than relying on the package
postinst — `:1003-1004` asserts this without evidence. (Measured: it *is* currently `enabled`, so
this is belt-and-braces, not a live defect. [V])

Apply the same pattern to any future reconcile step (see C1): a deploy that touches the agent must
fail the build when the agent is not running afterwards.

#### Fully-Detailed Investigation

> **Investigated** 2026-07-30 · **Verdict on the dossier's proposed fix:**
> CONFIRMED-WITH-CORRECTIONS · **Registers read to EOF:** FIX-REGISTER.md (3,705 lines)
> and IMPLEMENTATION-REGISTER.md (4,178 lines) · **Anchor drift found:** 2 of 6 anchors moved.

- `FIX-REGISTER.md` — zero hits on any infra term.

So: **no prior fix has ever touched `infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh`, and there is no locked decision

Two register findings that *do* bear on the fix, indirectly:

1. **`FIX-REGISTER.md:126` (FIX-028, prototype nav-validation) and the register's repeated

2. **`IMPLEMENTATION-REGISTER.md:2452` — "The gsd-executor `git stash` hazard (survivor)".** An

##### I3. Root cause — confirmed, corrected, or replaced

The dossier's *substance* is right and its *title* is wrong. Independently re-derived:

**The title is wrong.** "`fetch-config` exit status is never checked" is not what happens. The script
runs under `set -euo pipefail` (`:27`, verified), and `:1005-1007` is one simple command with line
continuations — not part of a pipeline, not on the LHS of `||`, not in an `if`. A non-zero exit from
`fetch-config` therefore **does** abort the script. The exit status is checked, by `set -e`. The
dossier's own "Why it occurred" paragraph concedes this ("the command genuinely *succeeded*"), so the
finding is internally inconsistent with its own headline.

**The substance is right.** The real defect is a **missing liveness assertion**: a zero exit proves
the agent was *asked* to start, not that it is running. The causal chain, re-derived:

1. `-s` makes `agent-ctl` perform its `start` action after installing and translating the config.
   `[I]` — on a systemd host that action ends in `systemctl restart amazon-cloudwatch-agent`.
2. `systemctl restart` on a non-`notify` unit returns as soon as `fork()` succeeds; it does not wait
   for readiness. So `agent-ctl` returns 0.
3. The agent then fails to construct its logger (`open sink "/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log":
   permission denied` — B1's `[V]` journal read) and exits 1, ~milliseconds later.
4. systemd's `Restart=` re-launches it; the journal's `restart counter is at 977` is systemd's own
   `NRestarts`. `[V]` from the dossier's journal excerpt.
5. Bootstrap, having seen a 0, proceeds through §15-§20 and writes the completion sentinel.

**A load-bearing inference the dossier does not draw.** Step 2's premise ("the unit is not
`Type=notify` with a readiness gate") is not an assumption — it is *entailed by the observed
evidence*. If the unit gated on readiness, `systemctl restart` would have returned non-zero, `set -e`
would have aborted at `:1005`, and §16/§17 would never have installed the pg_dump timer. The dossier
itself proves those ran (hourly `pg_dump` objects in S3, latest 2026-07-29T18:01, `[V]`). Therefore
`agent-ctl` demonstrably returned 0 over a dying agent. The chain is closed without needing the unit
file.

**A second correction — the "not a live defect" claim about `systemctl enable`.** The dossier says an
explicit enable is "belt-and-braces, not a live defect. (Measured: it *is* currently `enabled`.)"
That measurement is real but the inference is wrong in one direction. The unit is enabled *because*
something downstream of a successful config-translate enabled it — either the deb postinst (the
script's comment at `:1003-1004`) or `agent-ctl`'s own `start` action; `[I]`, I cannot read the ctl
script from here. Either way the enable is **incidental to fetch-config getting far enough**. In the
narrower failure mode where fetch-config dies *before* its start action (malformed JSON, translate
failure), `set -e` aborts at `:1005` **and the unit is left disabled** — and on dev there is no
`velocityai-firstboot.service` to ever re-run this script (`[V]` from the dossier's C1 finding:
dev's live userData is the pre-`bdc9e537` 68-line version), so the agent would be gone after every
reboot with no self-heal. So: an explicit enable is defence-in-depth for a *narrower* failure than
B5's, but it is not merely cosmetic.

**A third correction — the dossier's fix snippet is broken as written.** Two independent defects,
both proven by execution:

- *No PATH.* `amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl` is not on the default `PATH`; the script itself always
  uses the absolute `/opt/aws/...` path. Run with a realistic `PATH`, the bare invocation produces
  `command not found`, takes the `||` failure branch and exits 1 — **on a perfectly healthy box, on
  every boot**. `[V]`:

  ```
  $ bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; PATH=/usr/bin:/bin
    amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl -m ec2 -a status | grep -q "\"status\": *\"running\"" || {
      echo "DOSSIER SNIPPET -> exit 1 (on a HEALTHY box too)"; exit 1; }'
  bash: line 1: amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl: command not found
  DOSSIER SNIPPET -> exit 1 (on a HEALTHY box too)
  ```

- *No settle window.* The check runs immediately after a `systemctl restart`. On a healthy agent the
  unit can legitimately still read `activating` and the ctl can still report `stopped`. `[V]` with a
  stub that emits exactly that: the naive check takes the failure branch. This is the same
  distinction the dossier's own B1 *verification* section flags ("must be `active`, not
  `activating`") and then forgets in B5's fix.

**A fourth correction — `exit 1` in place is catastrophic.** See I4. This is the single most important
finding and the dossier does not evaluate it.

The dossier's regex itself is sound: `'"status": *"running"'` cannot false-match
`"configstatus": "configured"`, because the pattern requires a `"` immediately before `status` and
`configstatus` has a `g` there. Proven `[V]` in both directions, including a hostile
`"configstatus": "running"` input.

##### I4. Blast-radius sweep — every place this reaches

**(a) The ripple the dossier does not ask: what dies if the assertion aborts bootstrap?**

The dossier notes only that "§16 and §17 cannot run unless 14 exited 0". That is true and radically
incomplete. §14 ends at `:1007`; **six** sections follow. Enumerated from the source:

| Section | Lines | What is lost on an abort at §14 |
|---|---|---|
| §15 | `1009-1059` | `velocityai-deploy` system user + its `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`; `/usr/local/bin/velocityai-update-image-tag`; `/etc/sudoers.d/velocityai-deploy` (the only grant letting CI update image pins and restart the app) |
| §16 | `1061-1111` | `velocityai-pg-dump` (the hourly backup the dossier uses as its own proof §14 ran); `velocityai-skills-backup`; `velocityai-stuck-workflows-check` (E3's subject) |
| §17 | `1113-1231` | **`velocityai-app.service` itself**, plus the pg-dump / skills-backup / stuck-workflows `.service`+`.timer` pairs and their `systemctl enable --now` |
| §18 | `1233-1264` | The first `velocityai-load-secrets` run — the only thing that materialises `DATABASE_URL`, `SECRET_KEY` and the Bedrock ids into `/etc/velocityai/app.env` — then `docker compose down`, `systemctl enable` + `restart velocityai-app.service`. **The application never starts.** |
| §19 | `1266-1272` | The `/health` smoke test |
| §20 | `1273-1284` | `/var/lib/velocityai/.bootstrap-done` |

The end state of a hard abort at §14 is a box with Postgres, nginx, TLS, Docker and an ECR login —
and **no application, no backups, no boot-time start, no deploy path and no sentinel**. That is
strictly worse than a blind CloudWatch agent.

Two second-order consequences, both traced to source:

- **Sentinel absent -> `velocityai-firstboot.service` re-runs forever.** `user_data.sh.tpl:104` is
  `ConditionPathExists=!/var/lib/velocityai/.bootstrap-done`, `Type=oneshot`,
  `TimeoutStartSec=1800`, no `Restart=`. Without the sentinel the unit re-fires on every subsequent
  boot and re-hits the same cwagent failure. `[V]` (stage/prod only — dev's live userData has no
  such unit).
- **The CI redeploy would then fail too.** `infra/buildspec.yml:245-252` waits for the sentinel only
  when `docker` is absent — and docker *is* present (installed at §8, long before §14) — so the wait
  is skipped and CI proceeds against a half-provisioned host. It re-fetches compose + `deploy.env`
  and rewrites the two image-pin lines (`:254-281`), but it **never runs
  `velocityai-load-secrets`**, so `/etc/velocityai/app.env` still holds only the three pin lines
  written at §11. `docker-compose.yml:58-73` reads `/etc/velocityai/app.env` as its env file, so the
  backend starts with no `DATABASE_URL` and no `SECRET_KEY`, crash-loops, and the buildspec's
  300-second `/health` poll (`:296-300`) times out and `exit 1`s. `[V]` by reading all three files.

**Conclusion: "fail loudly and abort" is NOT correct here.** The correct shape is **loud non-fatal at
the point of detection plus a deferred non-zero exit after the sentinel is written.** See I5.

**(b) In-file precedent — and why one of them is disqualified.**

The file already contains two loud-but-non-fatal probes:

- §8b IMDSv1 drift, `:490-499`: finds a *critical security drift* and deliberately does not exit,
  with the stated rationale *"bootstrap completing is more valuable than failing here ... The log
  line is the operator signal; **cwagent ships it** to `/velocityai/${env}/system`."*
  That rationale is circular for B5: the signal is entrusted to the very component that is dead.
  **This is the precise, in-repo reason a log line alone is insufficient for this one check** — and
  it is an argument the dossier does not make.
- §19 `/health`, `:1266-1272`: WARN-only.

There are four hard `exit 1` sites (`:33` not-root, `:69` missing `bootstrap.env`, `:513` missing ECR
registry, `:1057` malformed sudoers). The first three are genuine preconditions. `:1057` is a *late*
hard exit inside §15 that would itself strand §16-§20 — precedent that the pattern exists, not that
it is right.

**(c) The general defect: every fire-and-forget site in the file.**

Full sweep of `systemctl` (`grep -n systemctl`, 21 hits, 14 executable) plus every command whose
success does not imply the thing works:

| Line | Command | Success -> working? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `161` | `systemctl reload-or-restart ssh` | **No.** A drop-in that sshd cannot parse can leave the daemon down; on a socket-activated unit the command returns 0 without validating config. Blast radius is total lockout. | **Deserves the same treatment** — `sshd -t` before, `is-active` after. Highest severity of the set. Owner: unassigned; recommend a sibling task. |
| `169` | `systemctl enable --now unattended-upgrades` | No, but timer-driven and low-impact | Low |
| `292`/`298` | `systemctl enable --now` / `restart postgresql@16-main` | **No.** On the FRESH path the next command is `psql CREATE USER` (`:304`), which fails loudly under `set -e` — so liveness *is* transitively asserted. On the **RECOVERY path** (`RECOVERY=1`) that block is skipped and a dead Postgres goes undetected until §19's non-fatal WARN. | **Deserves the same treatment** on the recovery path — `pg_isready`. Medium. |
| `337` | `systemctl enable --now docker` | No, but `docker login` at `:517` is a real use that fails loudly | Already covered |
| `355-356`, `951-952` | `setfacl -R ...` (`\|\| true` at 355-356) | **No — and this is B2.** The command succeeds while the *effective* permission is masked off. Identical "success != effect" shape to B5. | **B2's territory. Do not absorb.** |
| `545` | `systemctl enable --now velocityai-ecr-login.timer` | Timer enable only; a broken service run surfaces 6h later | Low |
| `930` | `systemctl reload nginx` (bootstrap-http) | Reload returns non-zero on bad config -> `set -e` catches it | Correct as-is |
| `937-938` | `nginx -t` then `systemctl reload nginx` | **This is the model.** Validate, then act. | Already correct — copy this shape |
| `939` | `systemctl enable --now certbot.timer` | No — renewal correctness is untested; a 90-day fuse | Medium; `certbot renew --dry-run`. Out of B5's lane |
| **`1005`** | `amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl -a fetch-config -m ec2 -s` | **No — this is B5** | **The issue** |
| `1228-1231` | `systemctl enable --now` × 3 timers | Timer enable succeeds; the services are never proven to work | Medium — this is exactly what **E2** (`PgDumpHeartbeat` with no publisher) exists to close |
| `1263-1264` | `systemctl enable` + `restart velocityai-app.service` | Partly — `Type=oneshot` makes `restart` synchronous, so a failing `docker compose up` does return non-zero. Complicated by `Restart=on-failure`. §19's `/health` is the real, non-fatal check | Medium-low |
| `1268` | `curl -fsS /health` inside `if !` | Deliberately WARN-only | **Should feed the same accumulator** — see I10 follow-ups |

Ranked recommendation for the same treatment, all **explicitly outside B5**: (1) §19 `/health` into
the accumulator — same mechanism, near-zero cost; (2) §3 `sshd -t`; (3) §6 `pg_isready` on the
recovery path; (4) §13 `certbot renew --dry-run`. §14's `setfacl` belongs to B2 and the timer
services to E2.

##### I5. The complete fix

Three edits to one file: `infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh`. Repo-side only — see "durability" at the
end of this section. Nothing is deleted (INV-3/INV-12 has no superseded code to remove here; the two
replaced comment lines are corrected in place).

**Step 1 — declare the degraded accumulator.**

Find (`dev`:31-36, the root check followed by §0's header):

```bash
if [[ "$EUID" -ne 0 ]]; then
    echo "[bootstrap] ERROR: must run as root (or via sudo)" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# ── 0. Wait for cloud-init to finish ───────────────────────────────────
```

Replace with:

```bash
if [[ "$EUID" -ne 0 ]]; then
    echo "[bootstrap] ERROR: must run as root (or via sudo)" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# ── Degraded-completion accumulator ────────────────────────────────────
# Some checks must be LOUD but must NOT abort the run. Aborting mid-script
# strands every later section (see the rationale block above §14a), which is
# strictly worse than finishing with a reported defect. Such a check appends a
# short tag here; §20 writes the completion sentinel, prints the tags and exits
# non-zero — the box ends up fully provisioned AND the invoking SSM command /
# CI step reports failure.
BOOTSTRAP_DEGRADED=()

# ── 0. Wait for cloud-init to finish ───────────────────────────────────
```

*Why an array and not a boolean:* so the §19 `/health` probe and the sibling checks in I4(c) can join
the same mechanism later without a second one (INV-12 in spirit). *Why `${#arr[@]}` guards
everywhere:* `"${arr[@]}"` on an empty array is an unbound-variable error under `set -u` on bash 3.2;
the count form is portable. Verified `[V]` on bash 3.2.57 (macOS) — if it passes there it passes on
Noble's 5.2.

**Step 2 — replace the whole of `dev`:1003-1007.**

Find exactly:

```bash
# fetch-config also starts the agent if it isn't running. We don't `systemctl
# enable` separately — the agent's deb postinst already does that.
/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl \
    -a fetch-config -m ec2 -s \
    -c file:/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json
```

Replace with:

```bash
# ── 14a-fn. CloudWatch agent liveness assertion (used just below) ──────
# Kept beside §14 so C1's later extraction of §13/§14 into
# infra/scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh is a pure move, not a rewrite.
#
# ORACLE CHOICE. systemd is the AUTHORITATIVE readiness oracle here, not the
# agent's own `-a status` text: `systemctl is-active` is a stable contract,
# whereas the ctl's JSON is an undocumented third-party output whose wording
# could drift and turn a healthy boot into a permanent red. The ctl output is
# used only to CORROBORATE — it can fail the check when it explicitly says the
# agent is not running, but an unparseable/absent blob only warns.
#
# The five knobs are `:-` defaults purely so the function can be exercised by
# infra/scripts/tests/test-cwagent-assert.sh with stub binaries on PATH;
# production never sets them.
CW_AGENT_CTL="${CW_AGENT_CTL:-/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl}"
CW_AGENT_UNIT="${CW_AGENT_UNIT:-amazon-cloudwatch-agent}"
CW_AGENT_SETTLE_SECONDS="${CW_AGENT_SETTLE_SECONDS:-60}"
CW_AGENT_STABILITY_SECONDS="${CW_AGENT_STABILITY_SECONDS:-12}"
CW_AGENT_POLL_SECONDS="${CW_AGENT_POLL_SECONDS:-3}"

_cw_agent_status_blob() {
    [[ -x "$CW_AGENT_CTL" ]] || { printf ''; return 0; }
    "$CW_AGENT_CTL" -m ec2 -a status 2>/dev/null || true
}
_cw_unit_state()    { systemctl is-active "$CW_AGENT_UNIT" 2>/dev/null || true; }
_cw_restart_count() { systemctl show -p NRestarts --value "$CW_AGENT_UNIT" 2>/dev/null || true; }
_cw_diag()          { journalctl -u "$CW_AGENT_UNIT" -n 40 --no-pager >&2 || true; }

# 0 iff the agent is RUNNING and STAYS running. Prints its own diagnosis and
# never exits — the caller decides whether the failure is fatal.
assert_cloudwatch_agent_running() {
    local blob state deadline stable_deadline r0 r1

    if [[ ! -x "$CW_AGENT_CTL" ]]; then
        echo "[bootstrap] ERROR: $CW_AGENT_CTL missing or not executable — the agent package did not install correctly." >&2
        return 1
    fi

    # 1. Settle. `systemctl restart` (which `-s` ends in) returns as soon as
    #    the process forks, so an immediate check reads "activating" on a
    #    perfectly HEALTHY agent. Poll instead of guessing a sleep.
    deadline=$(( SECONDS + CW_AGENT_SETTLE_SECONDS ))
    while :; do
        state="$(_cw_unit_state)"
        [[ "$state" == "active" ]] && break
        if (( SECONDS >= deadline )); then
            echo "[bootstrap] ERROR: amazon-cloudwatch-agent never reached 'active' within ${CW_AGENT_SETTLE_SECONDS}s (last state: '${state:-<none>}')." >&2
            echo "[bootstrap]        agent-ctl -a status = $(_cw_agent_status_blob)" >&2
            _cw_diag
            return 1
        fi
        sleep "$CW_AGENT_POLL_SECONDS"
    done

    # 2. Corroborate with the agent's own view — only when it is parseable.
    blob="$(_cw_agent_status_blob)"
    if printf '%s' "$blob" | grep -Eq '"status"[[:space:]]*:'; then
        if ! printf '%s' "$blob" | grep -Eq '"status"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"running"'; then
            echo "[bootstrap] ERROR: systemd reports the unit active but the agent reports itself not running." >&2
            echo "[bootstrap]        agent-ctl -a status = ${blob}" >&2
            _cw_diag
            return 1
        fi
    else
        echo "[bootstrap] WARN: could not parse 'agent-ctl -a status' output; relying on systemd only. Output was: ${blob:-<empty>}" >&2
    fi
    if printf '%s' "$blob" | grep -Eq '"configstatus"[[:space:]]*:' \
       && ! printf '%s' "$blob" | grep -Eq '"configstatus"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"configured"'; then
        echo "[bootstrap] WARN: agent reports configstatus != configured — fetch-config may not have installed the JSON. Output was: ${blob}" >&2
    fi

    # 3. Stability. A crash-looping agent is 'active' for a fraction of each
    #    restart period, so a single sample can be a false green. Require the
    #    unit to STAY active, and cross-check systemd's own restart counter
    #    (the same number the journal prints as "restart counter is at N").
    r0="$(_cw_restart_count)"
    stable_deadline=$(( SECONDS + CW_AGENT_STABILITY_SECONDS ))
    while (( SECONDS < stable_deadline )); do
        sleep "$CW_AGENT_POLL_SECONDS"
        state="$(_cw_unit_state)"
        if [[ "$state" != "active" ]]; then
            echo "[bootstrap] ERROR: amazon-cloudwatch-agent did not stay active for ${CW_AGENT_STABILITY_SECONDS}s (observed '${state:-<none>}') — crash-looping." >&2
            _cw_diag
            return 1
        fi
    done
    r1="$(_cw_restart_count)"
    if [[ "$r0" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$r1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( r1 > r0 )); then
        echo "[bootstrap] ERROR: amazon-cloudwatch-agent restarted ${r0}->${r1} during the observation window — crash-looping." >&2
        _cw_diag
        return 1
    fi

    echo "[bootstrap] OK: amazon-cloudwatch-agent active and stable for ${CW_AGENT_STABILITY_SECONDS}s (NRestarts=${r1:-n/a})."
    return 0
}

# Enable the unit EXPLICITLY, before fetch-config.
#
# The previous comment here claimed the deb postinst enables the unit. Whether
# it is the postinst or `agent-ctl`'s own `start` action (which `-s` triggers)
# is not observable from this script — and it does not matter, because BOTH
# are downstream of a fetch-config that gets far enough to start the agent. If
# fetch-config dies earlier (bad JSON, translate failure) the unit is left
# DISABLED and the agent is gone after the next reboot, with nothing to
# re-run this script on dev (its userData has no firstboot service). One
# idempotent line closes that hole.
systemctl enable "$CW_AGENT_UNIT" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || echo "[bootstrap] WARN: systemctl enable $CW_AGENT_UNIT failed — unit file missing?"

# fetch-config installs the JSON, translates it and (because of -s) starts the
# agent. Its exit status IS checked — `set -e` aborts on a non-zero — but a
# zero here only proves the agent was ASKED to start: the wrapper ends in
# `systemctl restart`, which returns as soon as the process forks. The agent
# can (and on this fleet did) exit 1 milliseconds later and crash-loop forever
# while bootstrap reports success. §14a asserts the thing we actually want.
/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl \
    -a fetch-config -m ec2 -s \
    -c file:/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json

# ── 14a. Assert the agent is actually running (not just asked to run) ──
#
# WHY THIS IS NOT `exit 1` IN PLACE. Everything from §15 to §20 runs after
# this point: the velocityai-deploy user + its restricted sudoers, the
# pg_dump / skills-backup / stuck-workflow scripts, EVERY systemd unit
# including velocityai-app.service, the first velocityai-load-secrets run
# that materialises DATABASE_URL and SECRET_KEY into /etc/velocityai/app.env,
# the app start, and the completion sentinel. Aborting here would leave a box
# with Postgres, nginx and TLS but no application, no backups, no boot-time
# start and no sentinel — strictly worse than a blind CloudWatch agent. So the
# failure is recorded and the script continues; §20 exits non-zero.
#
# The nearest precedent in this file is the §8b IMDSv1 drift check, which
# deliberately does not exit and says "the log line is the operator signal;
# cwagent ships it". That reasoning is exactly what a dead cwagent breaks, so
# a log line alone is not sufficient here — hence the deferred non-zero exit.
assert_cloudwatch_agent_running || BOOTSTRAP_DEGRADED+=("cloudwatch-agent")
```

Per-choice rationale for the non-obvious bits:

- *Absolute path in a variable, not a bare command name.* Why this and not the obvious thing: the
  bare name is not on `PATH` and would make the check fail 100% of the time (proven, I3).
- *systemd as the authoritative oracle, ctl as corroboration.* Why: a hard dependency on an
  undocumented third-party JSON string is a permanent-red risk. The observed B1 failure is caught by
  systemd alone (a 1-restart-per-minute agent is `active` for ~0.3% of samples), so nothing is lost.
- *Polling settle window instead of `sleep N`.* Why: a fixed sleep is either too short (false fail)
  or wastes time on every healthy boot. Polling costs ~0s when healthy.
- *A stability window on top of `is-active`.* Why: a single `is-active` can be a false green in a
  crash loop. This is the false-green trap the registers repeatedly record.
- *`NRestarts` as a cross-check, never the sole gate.* Why: it is exactly the counter the journal
  prints ("restart counter is at 977"), but a 60-second restart period would not increment inside a
  12-second window, so it strengthens the check rather than carrying it. Degrades silently if the
  property is unavailable. `[I]` on `NRestarts` being present on Noble's systemd 255.
- *`configstatus` is a WARN, not a failure.* Why: the observed defect is liveness; a string-literal
  dependency should not be able to redden a build; and the "config not installed" mode is caught
  independently by the liveness check on a fresh boot and by E1's `IncomingLogEvents` alarm.
- *`enable` before `fetch-config`.* Why: it must survive a fetch-config that hard-fails and aborts
  the script (I3, third correction).
- *`:-` defaults on the five knobs.* Why: the function is otherwise untestable offline. Production
  never sets them; anyone who can set them is already root.

**Step 3 — the deferred gate at §20.**

Find (`dev`:1284, the last line of the file):

```bash
echo "[bootstrap] complete $(date -u --iso-8601=seconds)"
```

Replace with:

```bash
# The sentinel is written BEFORE the degraded gate on purpose: the host IS
# provisioned, and withholding it would make velocityai-firstboot re-run the
# whole bootstrap on every reboot and make CI's wait-for-sentinel loop time
# out. The non-zero exit below is the SIGNAL; the sentinel is STATE.
if [[ ${#BOOTSTRAP_DEGRADED[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    echo "[bootstrap] DEGRADED: ${BOOTSTRAP_DEGRADED[*]}" >&2
    echo "[bootstrap] The host is provisioned but one or more subsystems are unhealthy." >&2
    echo "[bootstrap] complete (DEGRADED) $(date -u --iso-8601=seconds)" >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "[bootstrap] complete $(date -u --iso-8601=seconds)"
```

**Behaviour, stated explicitly for both contexts (the brief's second question).**

| Context | Detection | Fatality | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full bootstrap (first boot, SSM RunCommand or `velocityai-firstboot.service`) | §14a, loud, with `journalctl -n 40` | **Deferred.** §15-§20 all run; sentinel written; **then** `exit 1` | Aborting strands the whole application layer (I4a). The exit code is the signal to the SSM invoker / CI. |
| C1 reconcile (`reconcile-host-config.sh`, §13+§14 only) | The same function, unchanged | **Deferred to the end of the reconcile**, never mid-run | "A reconcile that aborts halfway is worse than one that reports." Aborting between §13 and §14 would leave nginx config written but the agent untouched — a half-applied host. Run every step, accumulate, exit non-zero at the end with a summary. |

Composition with C1 is a pure move: the function, its knobs and its call site all sit inside the
§14 block C1 extracts. After extraction, `reconcile-host-config.sh` owns its own accumulator and
final exit; bootstrap calls it as
`bash /opt/velocityai/reconcile-host-config.sh || BOOTSTRAP_DEGRADED+=("host-config-reconcile")`
and keeps its §20 gate. Zero duplication, one implementation of the assertion.

**Host-side vs repo-side.** This change is **repo-side only and it is durable**: committing to `dev`
re-uploads the script via `aws_s3_object.bootstrap_script`
(`infra/terraform/app/main.tf:79-94`, `source_hash = filemd5(...)`) into the per-env bucket on every
dev build. Nothing here evaporates. It has **no live effect on the dev box until C1 re-runs the
script**, because bootstrap runs once per instance — which is precisely C1's thesis. Do not attempt a
host-side half for B5: there is nothing to apply on the box except re-running the script, and that is
C1's job.

##### I6. Ripple-effect analysis — why nothing else breaks

Assuming the fix is wrong, where does it break?

- **A healthy agent is declared dead (false fail) -> every bootstrap goes red.** The two mechanisms
  that could cause this are (a) the ctl not being on `PATH` — eliminated by using the absolute path;
  (b) the check racing the restart — eliminated by the 60s polling settle window, proven with an
  `activating→active` stub. A third, subtler one — the ctl's JSON wording drifting — is eliminated by
  making systemd authoritative and the ctl merely corroborating. Residual risk: a healthy agent that
  takes >60s to reach `active`. Not observed; the knob exists.
- **A dead agent is declared healthy (false green).** The single-sample crash-loop window. Mitigated
  by requiring sustained `active` across 12s plus the `NRestarts` cross-check. Proven with a
  `active,active,failed,active` stub and with an `NRestarts 5→9` stub.
- **Added wall-clock.** Healthy path: settle breaks on the first poll (0s) + a fixed 12s stability
  window ≈ **+12s** on a ~6-minute bootstrap. Failure path: +60s settle then fail. Well inside
  `velocityai-firstboot.service`'s `TimeoutStartSec=1800` and inside the buildspec's
  `--timeout-seconds 1800`.
- **Shell-semantics hazards.** `(( ))` used only in guarded positions (`if`/`while`) — a bare false
  `(( ))` is an errexit trap on bash ≥4 and my code never uses one. `arr+=(x)` on the RHS of `||`
  does not trip errexit. `${#arr[@]}` is safe on an empty array under `set -u` on bash 3.2 and above;
  `"${arr[*]}"` is only reached inside the `count > 0` guard. All four verified by execution.
- **`journalctl` unavailable / noisy.** Guarded with `|| true`; only runs on the failure path.
- **Re-run idempotency.** The whole change is read-only observation plus one idempotent
  `systemctl enable`. Re-running bootstrap is unaffected.
- **Partial application.** If only Step 2 lands without Step 1, `BOOTSTRAP_DEGRADED+=` on an
  undeclared array under `set -u`… actually appends fine (`+=` creates it), but Step 3's `${#...}`
  would then be the only reader — so Steps 1 and 3 must land together. If only Steps 1+3 land,
  nothing ever appends and the gate is inert. **Ship all three in one commit** (I10).
- **Concurrency / ordering.** None — bootstrap is single-threaded and this runs between two existing
  sequential sections.
- **Unattached client / slow client / restart / resume / fan-out / two browsers.** Not applicable:
  this is a host provisioning script with no runtime, no request path and no state shared with the
  application.
- **The dossier's own safety argument.** It offers none for B5 beyond "fail loudly". I evaluated that
  argument and rejected it with the enumerated §15-§20 loss (I4a) and the corroborating
  `fix/infra-uki` rationale (I4d).
