Walked item by item against §3 of the brief.

- **SC-001** (a new workflow must replicate `prototype` by manifest + AGENT.md, zero engine edits) —
  not engaged. No engine, kernel, manifest, capability or `AGENT.md` is touched.
- **INV-3 / INV-12** (no dual implementations; deleting the superseded code is part of the change) —
  satisfied by construction. There is nothing superseded: the two replaced comment lines are
  corrected, not duplicated; the assertion is one function with one call site; the accumulator is one
  array with one gate. The deliberate design decision that keeps it INV-12-clean is placing the
  function *inside* the §14 block so C1's extraction is a move, not a copy.
- **INV-13** (`deepagents` only) — not engaged.
- **Hexagonal boundary / import-linter** — not engaged; no Python import moves. The baseline stays at
  the one pre-existing violation
  (`agents.capabilities.strategies.task_loop → agents.execution_engine.od_context →
  app.services.od_loader`). Not re-run, because nothing this change touches can affect it — no
  `.py` file is modified. `[V]` by diff scope.
- **Q3 additive migrations only** — not engaged; no schema, no migration.
- **Backward compatibility / characterization goldens** — not engaged. The goldens are `dev`-red
  already (10 failed / 6 passed per Appendix 1); this change cannot move them, since the harness
  drives the Python engine and never reads a shell script.
- **Security defaults (`exec`/`network`/`secrets`/`spawn_subagents` OFF)** — not engaged. No new
  privilege: the script already runs as root; `systemctl enable` and `journalctl` are strictly less
  privileged than the `dpkg -i` two sections earlier. No new IAM action, no new network egress, no
  secret read. The `:-` knobs are settable only by someone who already controls the root environment.
- **LOCK-B** (`websocket.py` unmodifiable during the SSE cutover) — searched both registers.

  enforced by `backend/tests/agents/test_sse_cutover_banned_patterns.py`. Not engaged by a shell
  change; noted only because the brief asked me to verify the lock's current force.

**Gate 2 — new behavioural test (fail-before / pass-after).**

Create `infra/scripts/tests/test-cwagent-assert.sh` with the content below. It sources the assertion
out of the real script (so the test can never drift from the shipped text), stubs `systemctl`,
`journalctl` and the agent ctl, and drives nine scenarios.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Offline behavioural gate for assert_cloudwatch_agent_running (B5).
# No AWS, no systemd, no root. Run from the repo root:
#   bash infra/scripts/tests/test-cwagent-assert.sh
set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." && pwd)"
SCRIPT="$REPO_ROOT/infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh"
WORK="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$WORK/bin" "$WORK/opt" "$WORK/state"

# Extract the shipped function text verbatim — the test cannot drift from it.
awk '/^CW_AGENT_CTL="\$\{CW_AGENT_CTL:-/,/^# Enable the unit EXPLICITLY/' "$SCRIPT" \
  | sed '$d' > "$WORK/assert.sh"
grep -q 'assert_cloudwatch_agent_running()' "$WORK/assert.sh" \
  || { echo "FATAL: could not extract the assertion from $SCRIPT"; exit 2; }

cat > "$WORK/bin/systemctl" <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
d="$(dirname "$0")/../state"
if [ "$1" = "is-active" ]; then
  f="$d/unit_states"; i="$d/.i_state"; [ -f "$i" ] || echo 0 > "$i"
  n=$(cat "$i"); tot=$(wc -l < "$f"); n=$((n+1)); [ "$n" -gt "$tot" ] && n=$tot
  echo "$n" > "$i"; v=$(sed -n "${n}p" "$f"); echo "$v"
  [ "$v" = active ] && exit 0 || exit 3
fi
if [ "$1" = "show" ]; then
  f="$d/nrestarts"; i="$d/.i_nr"; [ -f "$i" ] || echo 0 > "$i"
  n=$(cat "$i"); tot=$(wc -l < "$f"); n=$((n+1)); [ "$n" -gt "$tot" ] && n=$tot
  echo "$n" > "$i"; sed -n "${n}p" "$f"; exit 0
fi
exit 0
S
printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit 0\n' > "$WORK/bin/journalctl"
cat > "$WORK/opt/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl" <<'C'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
d="$(dirname "$0")/../state"
f="$d/ctl_status"; i="$d/.i_ctl"; [ -f "$i" ] || echo 0 > "$i"
n=$(cat "$i"); tot=$(grep -c '^---$' "$f"); n=$((n+1)); [ "$n" -gt "$tot" ] && n=$tot
echo "$n" > "$i"
awk -v want="$n" 'BEGIN{k=1} /^---$/{k++;next} k==want{print}' "$f"
C
chmod +x "$WORK/bin/systemctl" "$WORK/bin/journalctl" "$WORK/opt/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl"
export PATH="$WORK/bin:$PATH"

FAILURES=0
run_case() {
  local name="$1" states="$2" ctl="$3" nr="$4" expect="$5" out rc
  printf '%s\n' "$states" > "$WORK/state/unit_states"
  printf '%s\n' "$nr"     > "$WORK/state/nrestarts"
  printf '%s\n' "$ctl"    > "$WORK/state/ctl_status"
  rm -f "$WORK/state/.i_state" "$WORK/state/.i_nr" "$WORK/state/.i_ctl"
  out="$(set +e
    CW_AGENT_CTL="$WORK/opt/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl" \
    CW_AGENT_SETTLE_SECONDS=6 CW_AGENT_STABILITY_SECONDS=3 CW_AGENT_POLL_SECONDS=1 \
    bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; source "$1"; assert_cloudwatch_agent_running' _ "$WORK/assert.sh" 2>&1
    echo "RC=$?")"
  rc="${out##*RC=}"
  if [ "$rc" = "$expect" ]; then printf 'PASS  %-46s rc=%s\n' "$name" "$rc"
  else printf 'FAIL  %-46s rc=%s expected=%s\n%s\n' "$name" "$rc" "$expect" "$out"; FAILURES=$((FAILURES+1)); fi
}

HEALTHY='{
  "status": "running",
  "configstatus": "configured"
}
---'
B1SHAPE='{
  "status": "stopped",
  "configstatus": "configured"
}
---'
UNCONF='{
  "status": "running",
  "configstatus": "not configured"
}
---'
UNPARSEABLE='some non-json error text
---'

run_case "healthy agent"                            "active"                                  "$HEALTHY"     "0"            0
run_case "B1 shape: crash-loop, ctl says stopped"   "failed"                                  "$B1SHAPE"     "977"          1
run_case "settles: activating then active"          "$(printf 'activating\nactive')"          "$HEALTHY"     "0"            0
run_case "flaps active->failed inside window"       "$(printf 'active\nactive\nfailed\nactive')" "$HEALTHY"  "0"            1
run_case "configstatus not configured -> WARN only" "active"                                  "$UNCONF"      "0"            0
run_case "unparseable ctl output -> WARN only"      "active"                                  "$UNPARSEABLE" "0"            0
run_case "systemd active but ctl says stopped"      "active"                                  "$B1SHAPE"     "0"            1
run_case "NRestarts increments during window"       "active"                                  "$HEALTHY"     "$(printf '5\n9')" 1

out="$(set +e; CW_AGENT_CTL="$WORK/opt/nonexistent" \
  bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; source "$1"; assert_cloudwatch_agent_running' _ "$WORK/assert.sh" 2>&1; echo "RC=$?")"
case "$out" in *"RC=1"*) echo "PASS  missing ctl binary                            rc=1";;
               *) echo "FAIL  missing ctl binary: $out"; FAILURES=$((FAILURES+1));; esac

echo "---"; [ "$FAILURES" -eq 0 ] && { echo "ALL PASS"; exit 0; } || { echo "$FAILURES FAILURE(S)"; exit 1; }
```

```bash
/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl -m ec2 -a status
# 3. The exit status the SSM invocation reports
aws ssm get-command-invocation --command-id <id> --instance-id i-092d5961f5aca87a6 \
    --query 'Status' --output text                       # Success once B1 has landed
```

**Non-vacuity proof for the live run:** before B1 lands, the assertion must report ERROR and the SSM
command must report `Failed` — that is the fail-before at the live layer. After B1 lands, the same
run must report OK and `Success`. Anyone who sees `Success` on the first attempt should suspect the
assertion is not being reached.

**Existing tests that must stay green:** none exist for this file. The backend suites are untouched by
construction; if the executor wants a belt-and-braces sanity check, the targeted SSE suite
(`pytest tests/unit/test_sse_stream.py tests/agents/test_attach_replay_matrix.py
tests/unit/test_run_stream_pool_leak.py -q`, baseline **1 failed / 31 passed**) and
`/opt/homebrew/bin/lint-imports` (baseline **1 broken contract**) must be *unchanged from baseline* —
not green, unchanged.

##### I9. Rollback

**Repo side.** `git revert <commit>` on the single commit. The change is three hunks in one file with
no dependants; a revert is textually and semantically clean. The next `terraform apply` for `dev`
re-uploads the reverted script (`source_hash = filemd5(...)`) to
`s3://velocityai-dev-pg-dumps-577954642302/config/bootstrap-ec2.sh`.

**Host side — nothing to roll back, and that is the point.** This change writes no file, installs no
package, creates no unit and mutates no service state on the box beyond one idempotent
`systemctl enable amazon-cloudwatch-agent` (which the dossier measured as already true, so it is a
no-op in the current state). If the assertion misbehaves live, the *operational* rollback is to
re-run the previous version of the script over SSM; nothing must be undone first.

**What is NOT reversible.** `velocityai-dev-root` has zero EBS snapshots and
`delete_on_termination = true` (`[V]` per dossier Appendix 2), so there is no filesystem rollback for
*any* host change. That constrains C1, not B5 — but the executor must know it, because if this change
is applied as part of a C1 reconcile that also rewrites nginx, the nginx half needs C1's file-level
backup (`/root/nginx-backup-<ts>/`) and B5's half needs nothing.

**Pre-change backup requirement:** none for B5 itself. If bundled with C1, capture
`/etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai`, `/etc/nginx/conf.d/velocityai-limits.conf` and
`/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json` before applying.

##### I10. Sequencing and dependencies

**Hard ordering — B1 before or with B5.** B1's fix (pre-creating
`/var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log` owned by `cwagent`) is what makes this assertion pass. Land
B5 alone and the very next full bootstrap or reconcile correctly reports DEGRADED and exits 1 —
correct behaviour, but a red that nobody can clear. **Ship B1 and B5 in the same change set**, B1's
hunk first. The dossier states this ordering from B1's side ("Check `fetch-config`'s exit status …
See B5"); I am confirming it from B5's side and adding that it is *hard*, not advisory.

**Same-file, same-section — coordinate anchors.** B1, B2, B3, B4 and B5 all edit §14
(`dev`:941-1007); E3 edits §16 (`dev`:1106). Applying B5 shifts every anchor below `dev`:34 (see the
table in I4e). Recommended intra-§14 order, chosen so each edit's anchor text is still findable:

1. **B2** — `usermod -a -G adm cwagent` + the corrected `setfacl` at `dev`:951-952
2. **B1** — the `install -o cwagent ... /var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log` line, before the config
   heredoc
3. **B4 + B3** — the `collect_list` entries at `dev`:988-995 (they edit the same heredoc; do them
   together)
4. **B5** — this change, at `dev`:1003-1007 plus the two out-of-section hunks

**A cross-issue correction for B2.** B2's proposed fix ends with
`systemctl restart amazon-cloudwatch-agent  # required — group membership is read at start`. If B2
lands at `dev`:951-952 as the dossier says (before the config heredoc and before `fetch-config -s`),
**that restart is redundant**: `fetch-config -s` restarts the agent ~50 lines later and the new `adm`
group membership is picked up there. Adding B2's restart would start the agent once with the old
config and then again with the new one, and my §14a assertion would (correctly) observe only the
second. Recommend B2 drops the standalone restart and relies on `fetch-config -s`. This is not stated
anywhere in the dossier.

**C1 — B5 is C1-shaped by construction.** Everything except Steps 1 and 3 lives inside the block C1
extracts. C1 must (a) move the function and its call site verbatim, (b) give the extracted script its
own accumulator and end-of-script gate, (c) have bootstrap call it with
`|| BOOTSTRAP_DEGRADED+=("host-config-reconcile")`. **C1's own SSM payload must not `set -e` around
the reconcile call**, or a DEGRADED reconcile aborts the payload before its later steps.

**E1/E2/E3/B6 — complementary, not conflicting.** E1's `AWS/Logs IncomingLogEvents` meta-alarm is the
*outward, continuous* detector; B5 is the *build-time* assertion. They are deliberately different
mechanisms for different moments and must both exist: B5 cannot detect an agent that dies a week
after bootstrap, and E1 cannot fail a deploy. B6's ordering rule ("fix B1 and B2 first, then
subscribe") applies unchanged. E3's line-number anchor shifts (I4e).

**A-cluster and D-cluster — fully disjoint.** Different files, different languages, no shared state.

**Commit boundaries.** **One commit** containing all three steps. They are one mechanism and a
partial application is either inert (Steps 1+3 only) or unreadable (Step 2 only). Suggested message:

```
infra(bootstrap): assert the CloudWatch agent is actually running (B5)

fetch-config -s returns 0 as soon as systemd forks the agent, so a crash-looping
agent completes bootstrap "successfully". Add a liveness assertion (systemd
authoritative, agent-ctl corroborating, with a settle window and a stability
window) and a degraded-completion accumulator: the check is loud and non-fatal
in place — aborting at §14 would strand §15-§20 including velocityai-app.service
and the completion sentinel — and §20 exits non-zero after writing the sentinel.
Also enables the unit explicitly before fetch-config.

Requires B1 (pre-create /var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log owned by cwagent),
without which this assertion correctly reports DEGRADED on every run.
```

**Follow-ups this investigation opens (each its own task, none in B5):** fold §19's `/health` probe
into the same accumulator; `sshd -t` before `systemctl reload-or-restart ssh` (`dev`:161);
`pg_isready` after the Postgres restart on the RECOVERY path (`dev`:298); `certbot renew --dry-run`
after `dev`:939.

##### I11. Open questions requiring a human decision

1. **Should a DEGRADED bootstrap fail the CI deploy?** With this fix, a bootstrap or reconcile that
   finds a dead CloudWatch agent exits non-zero. In a C1 reconcile invoked from a pipeline, that turns
   the deploy red even though the application is healthy. Options: **(a)** as specified — a dead
   observability agent blocks the deploy, forcing it to be fixed (my recommendation: the dossier's
   own framing is that a month of blindness cost more than any deploy delay, and the alternative has
   already been tried by accident); **(b)** exit 0 and rely solely on E1's alarm (rejected: the alarm
   does not exist yet, and B5 then delivers nothing beyond a log line the dead agent cannot ship);
   **(c)** exit non-zero only on the reconcile path, exit 0 on first boot (rejected: two behaviours
   for one condition, and first boot is exactly when a permanently-blind instance is created).

2. **Is `+12s` on every healthy boot acceptable?** The stability window is a fixed cost. Options:
   keep 12s (my recommendation — it is 0.03% of the 1800s firstboot budget and it is what buys the
   crash-loop guarantee); reduce to 6s (halves the confidence for a 2× shorter loop period); or drop
   the window entirely and rely on the single `is-active` sample plus `NRestarts` (rejected — a
   single sample is the false-green the registers repeatedly warn about).

##### I12. Shortcuts and alternatives explicitly rejected

**The dossier's own snippet, as written.** Rejected for two proven defects, not for style: the bare
command name is not on `PATH` and makes the check fail on every healthy box (`[V]`), and the absent
settle window makes it fail on a healthy-but-still-activating agent (`[V]`). Either one alone would
have produced a permanently-red bootstrap that the next engineer deletes.

**`exit 1` in place, at §14.** Rejected. Strands §15-§20 — the deploy user and sudoers, all three
backup/probe scripts, every systemd unit including `velocityai-app.service`, the first
`velocityai-load-secrets` run that supplies `DATABASE_URL`/`SECRET_KEY`, the app start, and the
completion sentinel. The resulting box serves 502s, has no backups and does not start the app on
reboot; on stage/prod `velocityai-firstboot.service` then re-runs the whole bootstrap on every boot;
the subsequent CI redeploy skips its sentinel wait (docker is present), brings up a backend with no
secrets, and times out on `/health`. The `origin/fix/infra-uki` branch independently reached the same
conclusion for §18/§19 in its own diff. Failure mode: converting an observability outage into a
service outage.

**Withholding the sentinel to force a retry.** Rejected. `ConditionPathExists=!` would re-run a
1800-second bootstrap on every reboot against a failure that reboots cannot fix, and
`infra/buildspec.yml:245-252` would block a genuine first deploy for 900 seconds and then `exit 1`.
Failure mode: an infinite retry loop plus a broken first deploy.

**`systemctl is-active` as the sole check.** Rejected. In the observed 1-restart-per-minute loop the
unit *is* briefly `active`; a single sample can be a false green. Failure mode: the exact false-green
class the registers document three separate times (Phase 17 `_TRACER`, Phase 11 dead wiring, Phase 33
dormant Concierge).

**`agent-ctl -a status` as the sole check.** Rejected. It makes a build depend on an undocumented
third-party output string; a wording change in a future agent release would redden every boot.
Failure mode: a permanent red that gets "fixed" by deleting the check.

**Parsing the status blob with `jq`.** Rejected even though `jq` is installed (`dev`:100). The ctl's
output is not contractually pure JSON; a `jq` parse failure is indistinguishable from "not running",
so a formatting change would become a hard failure. The anchored `grep -E` is tolerant and its
false-match safety is proven in both directions.

**A fixed `sleep 20` before the check.** Rejected. Too short is a false fail; too long is dead time on
every boot. The polling settle window costs ~0s when healthy and bounds the wait when not.

**`systemctl is-failed` / `--wait`.** Rejected. `is-failed` returns false during the auto-restart
`activating` window, so it misses a crash loop; `systemctl restart --wait` is not applicable because
the restart happens inside the ctl wrapper, not in our command.

**Publishing a CloudWatch metric from bootstrap so the failure is visible without CloudWatch Logs.**
Tempting — the instance role does carry `cloudwatch:PutMetricData`, and E2 already establishes the
`put-metric-data`-from-bootstrap pattern. Rejected because it duplicates E1's `AWS/Logs
IncomingLogEvents` meta-alarm, which detects the same condition continuously rather than once at
provisioning time, and adds a second detector for one fact (INV-12 in spirit). Recorded here so it is
not re-proposed: the residual weakness it would have covered — the exit code being a weak signal on
the unattended `velocityai-firstboot.service` path — is explicitly E1's to close.

**Making `configstatus != configured` a hard failure.** Rejected in favour of a WARN. The observed
defect is liveness; the "config not installed" mode is caught independently by the liveness check on
a fresh boot and by E1's alarm thereafter; and a hard dependency on a second undocumented string
doubles the drift surface for marginal gain.

**Absorbing the §19 `/health` probe or the §14 `setfacl` effective-permission check into this fix.**
Rejected on scope. `/health` is a genuinely valuable addition to the same accumulator but is a
behaviour change to a different section and belongs in its own task; the `setfacl` effective-mask
problem is **B2** and absorbing it would corrupt that issue's proof.

**Reformatting or "tidying" the surrounding §14 code.** Rejected. Four sibling issues (B1, B2, B3,
B4) edit this exact section; every gratuitous reflow is a merge conflict scheduled for someone else.

### B6 — 41 alarms are firing and no one is subscribed

**Severity:** the monitoring worked. Nobody was listening.
**Confidence:** [V] — counts and subscriber state read from the account.

#### Symptom

```
$ aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --state-value ALARM --query 'length(MetricAlarms)'
41

velocityai-alerts        (prod)   confirmed: 0   pending: 0
velocityai-stage-alerts           confirmed: 0   pending: 0
velocityai-dev-alerts             confirmed: 0   pending: 1   <- never confirmed
flowin-prod-alerts       (legacy) confirmed: 1
flowin-staging-alerts    (legacy) confirmed: 1
```

Every alert topic for the **current** stack has zero confirmed subscribers. The only confirmed
endpoints are on the two legacy `flowin-*` topics, which are firing 16 permanently-stuck alarms — so
even that signal is dead through alarm fatigue. One of the firing alarms is
`velocityai-dev-unexpected-kms-decrypt`, a **security** alarm, going unnoticed. [V]

The dev subscription exists but was never confirmed: endpoint
`velocityai-dev-alerts@hexaware.com`, `SubscriptionArn` literally `"PendingConfirmation"`, created by
Terraform (`modules/monitoring/main.tf:91-97`). [V]

#### Why it occurred

`alert_email` is injected as `TF_VAR_alert_email` from `infra/terraform/bootstrap/cicd.tf:370`,
sourced from the git-ignored `bootstrap.tfvars`. Terraform can *create* an email subscription but
cannot *confirm* one — confirmation requires a human clicking a link in the mailbox. So the resource
is "successfully applied" and permanently inert. Nothing in the pipeline distinguishes
`PendingConfirmation` from confirmed.

Most of the 41 are firing **because** of B1: `cpu-high`, `mem-high`, `disk-root-high`,
`disk-data-high`, `inode-low` all depend on CWAgent metrics that never arrive, and all are configured
`treat_missing_data = breaching`. So the monitoring correctly detected the outage on day one and had
nowhere to send it.

#### The fix

**Order matters. Fix B1 and B2 first, then subscribe.** Confirming now buries the subscriber in
false alarms that will resolve themselves the moment metrics start flowing.

Then, **dev only** per the stated constraint — leave `velocityai-stage-alerts` and
`velocityai-alerts` untouched. Two options, and this needs a human decision:

1. **Confirm the existing pending subscription.** Requires access to the
   `velocityai-dev-alerts@hexaware.com` mailbox. No Terraform drift. Someone must own that address.
2. **Repoint it** via `TF_VAR_alert_email` plus a dev app apply. Note `alert_email` also feeds
   `VELOCITYAI_ACME_EMAIL` into `user_data` (`app/main.tf:68`), which is under `ignore_changes` so no
   instance replacement — but it destroys and recreates the subscription. A plain manual
   `aws sns subscribe` of a personal address works but is untracked: Terraform will not remove it,
   and will not reproduce it on a rebuild.

Two dead signals to fix while here: `PgDumpHeartbeat` and the hardcoded prod namespace — see E2 and E3.

#### Verification

`aws sns get-topic-attributes` on `velocityai-dev-alerts` must show `SubscriptionsConfirmed: 1`. Then
deliberately breach one alarm and confirm an email arrives.

> and IMPLEMENTATION-REGISTER.md (4,178 lines) | **Anchor drift found:** 0 of 11 anchors moved.

##### I3. Root cause - confirmed, corrected, or replaced

The dossier's root cause is **right, and incomplete in four ways that change the fix.**

**Confirmed (re-derived from code).** `aws_sns_topic_subscription` with
`protocol = "email"` is the one AWS subscription type that requires an out-of-band human
action. Terraform's `Subscribe` call returns the literal `SubscriptionArn` string
`"PendingConfirmation"` and the resource converges as successfully applied. Nothing in
`infra/buildspec.yml` asserts `SubscriptionsConfirmed`; nothing in the app layer reads the
subscription back. So "applied" and "will deliver mail" are two different facts and the
pipeline only ever checks the first. `[V]` on the code; `[I]` that dev is in that state.

**Correction 1 - there are SIX topics per account, not five; twelve subscriptions, not
three.** The monitoring module creates **two** topics and **two** email subscriptions per
environment:

| Resource | Region | Name (dev) | Subscribed endpoint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aws_sns_topic.alerts` (`main.tf:81`) | eu-central-1 | `velocityai-dev-alerts` | `var.alert_email` (`main.tf:96`) |
| `aws_sns_topic.alerts_useast1` (`main.tf:255`) | **us-east-1** | `velocityai-dev-alerts-useast1` | `var.alert_email` (`main.tf:274`) |

The dossier's symptom block lists only eu-central-1 topics, which is what a region-scoped
`aws sns list-topics` returns. The us-east-1 topic is the **only** target of the billing
alarm (`main.tf:599-623`, `provider = aws.useast1`, `alarm_actions =
[aws_sns_topic.alerts_useast1.arn]`) because a CloudWatch alarm can only publish to a
same-region topic. **Confirming `velocityai-dev-alerts` alone leaves the billing alarm
permanently mute.** `[V]` from code.

**Correction 2 - the dossier's Option 1 is not "click the link"; the link is dead.** AWS
SNS email confirmation tokens are valid for 3 days. Dev was provisioned 2026-07-01
(dossier Appendix 2 / C1); the dossier was written 2026-07-29. The original confirmation
mail is ~4 weeks stale, so its token has expired and no amount of mailbox access will
confirm it. `[I]` (the 3-day window is AWS-documented behaviour I did not re-verify
against a live API). A **fresh confirmation must be requested**, and neither
`terraform apply` (the resource is converged, so it is a no-op) nor `aws sns
get-topic-attributes` can request one. Only a new `Subscribe` call does. This is the
single largest practical correction: Option 1 as written is not executable.

**Correction 3 - "repoint via TF_VAR_alert_email plus a dev app apply" understates the
work and overstates the safety.** `TF_VAR_alert_email` is set on the **CodeBuild project's
environment**, which is owned by the `bootstrap` layer (`cicd.tf:370`), and:

- `bootstrap` runs on **local state**, not the S3 backend. `infra/terraform/bootstrap/`
  contains no `backend "s3"` block (`grep -rn 'backend "' infra/terraform/bootstrap/`
  returns nothing) and `README.md:5` says so explicitly: *"It runs with **local state**"*.
- **That state does not exist on this machine.** `ls -la infra/terraform/bootstrap/`
  returns only `.tf` files, `README.md`, `bootstrap.tfvars.example` and the lock file -
  no `terraform.tfstate`. (There is a stale `infra/bootstrap/terraform.tfstate` from an
  older, now-unused directory layout; `git ls-files infra/bootstrap` returns 0 files, so
  it is untracked debris.)
- `bootstrap.tfvars` is git-ignored (`infra/.gitignore`: `*.tfvars` with explicit
  exceptions that do **not** include it). Its live content is unknowable from the repo.

So a `bootstrap apply` from this tree would run against **empty state** and try to create
the state bucket, the lock table and the CMK from scratch. That is not a repoint; that is
a bootstrap re-run against a live account. `[V]`

**Correction 4 - a third, better option exists that the dossier does not consider, and I
proved it.** Terraform resolves `-var-file` **after** `TF_VAR_*` environment variables, so
a value in the committed, per-env `infra/terraform/app/dev.tfvars` overrides
`TF_VAR_alert_email` with no bootstrap involvement at all. Proven empirically on the
installed Terraform (v1.15.1, darwin_arm64):

```text
$ TF_VAR_alert_email="from-env@example.com" terraform apply -auto-approve -var-file=dev.tfvars
who = "from-varfile@example.com"          # -var-file WINS

$ TF_VAR_alert_email="from-env@example.com" terraform apply -auto-approve
who = "from-env@example.com"              # env var used when no -var-file
```

`[V]` - run in the scratchpad, both directions, non-vacuous.

**Why 41 - the arithmetic, re-derived.** The module creates exactly 20 alarms per
environment: 18 singletons plus `inode_low` `for_each`-ed over
`[var.root_disk_path, var.data_disk_path]` = 2 (`main.tf:1626-1627`; the module's own
`alarm_names` output at `outputs.tf` enumerates the same 18 + the for_each). Of those 20,
exactly **8 must be in ALARM** given a dead CloudWatch agent and E2's missing publisher:

```text
treat_missing_data = "breaching" AND no metric arriving:
  cpu-high, mem-high, disk-root-high, disk-data-high,     (4)  CWAgent host metrics
  inode-low-root, inode-low-var-lib-postgresql,           (2)  CWAgent host metrics
  pg-dump-heartbeat-stale,                                (1)  E2: no publisher at all
  cert-renew-heartbeat-stale                              (1)  letsencrypt logs never ship
                                                        ----
                                                          8  x 3 envs = 24
  + velocityai-dev-unexpected-kms-decrypt (real data > 0)  1
  + 16 legacy flowin-* alarms (dossier)                   16
                                                        ----
                                                          41   == the dossier's count
```

That is an exact, independent reconstruction of the dossier's `41`, from code I read
myself. It is **corroboration, not proof** - the same total is reachable if, say, the
account-wide billing alarm is firing on dev's $100 threshold (`app/dev.tfvars:24`) and one
of my 8 is not. `[I]` on which 41; `[V]` on the 20-alarm inventory and the 8 breaching
classes.

Note `stuck-running-workflows` is `treat_missing_data = "missing"` (`main.tf:918`), so on
dev and stage it sits in **INSUFFICIENT_DATA**, not ALARM - exactly matching the dossier's
E3 observation, and confirming it is not part of the 41.

**4.2 `velocityai-dev-unexpected-kms-decrypt` specifically.** My brief asks what it means
that this is firing and whether it needs its own investigation.

The filter (`main.tf:1546`) is:

```text
{ ($.eventSource = "kms.amazonaws.com")
  && ($.eventName = "Decrypt")
  && ($.resources[0].ARN = "<project CMK arn>")
  && ($.userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.arn != "<instance role arn>") }
```

Exactly **one** principal is excluded: the EC2 instance role. But the project CMK
(`local.fnd.kms_key_arn`) encrypts **everything** in the environment - all 8 CloudWatch log
groups (`main.tf:46`, `:1007`), the SNS topic (`:83`), both EBS volumes
(`compute/main.tf:57`, `:120`), every config object in the backup bucket
(`app/main.tf:88`, `:120`, `:147`), the SSM SecureStrings, and the AWS Backup recovery
points. Legitimate `kms:Decrypt` callers therefore include the CloudWatch Logs service
principal, the AWS Backup service principal, S3/SSE-KMS, the CodeBuild deploy role, and
any operator SSO session - **none of which is the instance role.**

Whether the service-principal calls match turns on one thing I could not settle offline:
how a CloudWatch Logs JSON filter evaluates `!=` against a field that is **absent**
(service-principal events carry `userIdentity.type = "AWSService"` and no
`sessionContext.sessionIssuer.arn`). If absent-field `!=` matches, every log-group decrypt
matches and the alarm is a pure false positive. If it does not match, the firing signal is
a real assumed-role principal - an operator, CodeBuild, or something that genuinely
warrants attention. I will not guess. `[I]`

**Disposition: triage BEFORE subscribing, not after.** The reason is not caution for its
own sake - it is that this is the one alarm you can never afford to train a human to
ignore. Subscribing a person to a *security* page that fires on routine platform activity
is precisely the mechanism that killed the legacy `flowin-*` topics. The decisive
observation is one CLI call:

```bash
aws logs filter-log-events \
  --log-group-name /velocityai/dev/cloudtrail-audit \
  --filter-pattern '{ ($.eventSource = "kms.amazonaws.com") && ($.eventName = "Decrypt") }' \
  --max-items 20 \
  --query 'events[].message' --output text \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json;[print(json.loads(l).get("userIdentity",{}).get("type"),
      json.loads(l).get("userIdentity",{}).get("sessionContext",{}).get("sessionIssuer",{}).get("arn"))
      for l in sys.stdin if l.strip()]' | sort | uniq -c
```

If the principals are `AWSService` / `logs.amazonaws.com` / the CodeBuild role, the filter
is under-scoped and must gain an exclusion list before anyone subscribes. If they are
unexpected human or role identities, that is a real security finding and outranks
everything else in this dossier.

**4.3 Who else consumes the alerts topic.** `grep -rn 'aws_sns_topic_subscription'
infra/terraform/` returns exactly two resources, both in the monitoring module. There is
no Chatbot, no Lambda, no PagerDuty/Slack integration anywhere in the tree
(`grep -rn 'aws_chatbot\|pagerduty\|slack' infra/terraform/` = 0). But there **is** a
non-alarm publisher: `aws_backup_vault_notifications.alerts` (`main.tf:234-252`) sends
`BACKUP_JOB_FAILED`, `BACKUP_JOB_EXPIRED` and `RESTORE_JOB_FAILED` into the same topic. A
confirmed subscriber therefore also becomes the backup-failure recipient. That is
desirable, and it is additional traffic the dossier does not account for.

**4.4 The topic policy fences.** `main.tf:186-211` constrains `cloudwatch.amazonaws.com`
publish to `aws:SourceArn ArnLike ...:alarm:${var.name_prefix}-*`. Two consequences:
(i) the legacy `flowin-*` alarms cannot publish into the velocityai topics even if
someone repointed them, so there is no cross-contamination risk; (ii) any future alarm
created outside the `velocityai-<env>-` prefix will silently fail to publish. Worth a
comment, not a change.

**4.6 THE HIGHEST-STAKES RIPPLE: can a repoint replace the EC2 instance?** My brief
demands proof, because the root volume is `delete_on_termination = true`
(`compute/main.tf:121`) with zero snapshots and Postgres on the box. I proved it with a
three-way plan experiment against the **exact** pinned provider (`hashicorp/aws 5.100.0`,
loaded from the repo's own provider cache via a `filesystem_mirror`), the **exact**
lifecycle block from `compute/main.tf:134-151`, and a hand-seeded state, `-refresh=false`
so no AWS call is made:

```text
Config A  = the real block:  ignore_changes = [ami, user_data, associate_public_ip_address]
                             user_data_replace_on_change = false
Config B  = A but user_data NOT ignored,  user_data_replace_on_change = false
Config C  = B but                         user_data_replace_on_change = true

Change: the ACME email inside user_data, and nothing else.

A -> "aws_instance.app will be updated in-place"        (no user_data diff at all;
                                                          the only line is
                                                          `+ secondary_private_ips =
                                                          (known after apply)`, an artifact
                                                          of my hand-written state)
B -> "will be updated in-place"                          ~ user_data shown, NO replacement
C -> "must be replaced ... ~ user_data # forces replacement"
     Plan: 1 to add, 1 to change, 1 to destroy
     (and in this same run, A STILL showed "will be updated in-place")
```

Three conclusions, all `[V]`:

1. **`ignore_changes = [user_data]` alone prevents the replacement.** In run C, where
   `user_data_replace_on_change = true` makes `user_data` a forcing attribute, resource A
   was still only updated in place.
2. **`user_data_replace_on_change = false` alone also prevents it.** Run B changed
   `user_data` with no ignore and was still an in-place update. In the AWS provider,
   `user_data` is not unconditionally ForceNew - it forces replacement only when
   `user_data_replace_on_change = true`.
3. **The experiment is non-vacuous.** Run C produced a real `must be replaced`, so the
   harness is capable of showing the failure I am claiming does not happen.

**Two independent guards, each individually sufficient.** An ACME-email change cannot
replace `velocityai-dev-app`. The dossier's claim is CONFIRMED and now proven rather than
asserted.

**4.7 Does a repoint really destroy and recreate the subscription?** Same method, same
provider, hand-seeded state carrying the real pending shape
(`arn = ...:PendingConfirmation`, `pending_confirmation = true`):

```text
endpoint unchanged -> "No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration."
endpoint changed   -> "# aws_sns_topic_subscription.email must be replaced"
                      "~ endpoint = ... -> ... # forces replacement"
                      "Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy"
```

**CONFIRMED `[V]`.** Any repoint mints a brand-new subscription in
`PendingConfirmation` - i.e. it reproduces the exact failure mode B6 exists to fix, and
buys a fresh 3-day confirmation window. That is not a downside; it is in fact the *only*
Terraform-native way to trigger a new confirmation mail. But it means a repoint is not
"done" when the apply succeeds.

##### I5. The complete fix

**Ordering gate, stated once and binding: do not confirm any subscription until B1 and B2
are verified working on the box.** Confirming first means the new subscriber's first
experience is 8 stale pages per environment. That is how alerting dies.

The fix has three parts. Part A is mandatory and repo-free. Part B is the one repo change
and is only needed if the mailbox in Part A has no owner. Part C is the durable guard.

---

**Part A - re-trigger and confirm, both regions, dev only.** No repo file changes.

Preconditions, each verified before proceeding:

```bash
# A0. B1 landed: the agent is actually running.
aws ssm send-command --instance-ids i-092d5961f5aca87a6 \
  --document-name AWS-RunShellScript \
  --parameters 'commands=["systemctl is-active amazon-cloudwatch-agent",
    "/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl -m ec2 -a status"]'
# must print: active   and   "status": "running"

# A1. B2 landed: metrics are arriving in the alarms' namespace.
aws cloudwatch list-metrics --namespace VelocityAI/Dev \
  --metric-name mem_used_percent --region eu-central-1
# must return a non-empty Metrics[]

# A2. The 6 host alarms have actually cleared.
aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --region eu-central-1 \
  --alarm-names velocityai-dev-cpu-high velocityai-dev-mem-high \
    velocityai-dev-disk-root-high velocityai-dev-disk-data-high \
    velocityai-dev-inode-low-root velocityai-dev-inode-low-var-lib-postgresql \
  --query 'MetricAlarms[].[AlarmName,StateValue]' --output table
# every row must read OK. If any still reads ALARM, STOP - B1/B2 are not done.
```

Then re-trigger the confirmation on **both** topics. `Subscribe` with an identical
`(topic, protocol, endpoint)` triple against an unconfirmed email subscription re-sends the
confirmation mail and returns the same `PendingConfirmation` handle; it does not create a
duplicate. `[I]` - documented SNS behaviour, not re-verified live.

```bash
DEV_TOPIC=$(aws sns list-topics --region eu-central-1 \
  --query "Topics[?ends_with(TopicArn,':velocityai-dev-alerts')].TopicArn|[0]" --output text)
DEV_TOPIC_US=$(aws sns list-topics --region us-east-1 \
  --query "Topics[?ends_with(TopicArn,':velocityai-dev-alerts-useast1')].TopicArn|[0]" --output text)
EMAIL=velocityai-dev-alerts@hexaware.com    # must match var.alert_email EXACTLY

# Refuse to touch anything that is not dev.
case "$DEV_TOPIC"    in *:velocityai-dev-alerts)          : ;; *) echo "REFUSING: $DEV_TOPIC"; exit 1 ;; esac
case "$DEV_TOPIC_US" in *:velocityai-dev-alerts-useast1)  : ;; *) echo "REFUSING: $DEV_TOPIC_US"; exit 1 ;; esac

aws sns subscribe --region eu-central-1 --topic-arn "$DEV_TOPIC"    --protocol email --notification-endpoint "$EMAIL"
aws sns subscribe --region us-east-1    --topic-arn "$DEV_TOPIC_US" --protocol email --notification-endpoint "$EMAIL"
```

A human then clicks both confirmation links from the mailbox.

*Why the endpoint must match `var.alert_email` byte-for-byte:* if it differs by even a
character, Terraform sees its own recorded endpoint gone and the next `app apply` plans a
create - you get a duplicate pending subscription and an untracked confirmed one. The
"personal address via bare `aws sns subscribe`" the dossier mentions is exactly this
failure and is rejected in I12.

*Why not `terraform apply -replace`:* it would work (4.7 proves the endpoint change forces
replacement, and `-replace` forces it unconditionally), but it destroys the confirmed
subscription if one already exists and it writes to `velocityai/dev/app.tfstate` for no
gain over a plain `Subscribe`. Keep the state untouched when you can.

---

**Part B - only if `velocityai-dev-alerts@hexaware.com` has no owner.** One committed
file, dev only, no bootstrap involvement.

File: `infra/terraform/app/dev.tfvars`

BEFORE (lines 22-24, verbatim):

```hcl
# Monitoring.
log_retention_days          = 14
billing_alarm_threshold_usd = 100
```

AFTER:

```hcl
# Monitoring.
log_retention_days          = 14
billing_alarm_threshold_usd = 100

# Alert routing (dev only). Deliberately set HERE rather than via
# TF_VAR_alert_email so that:
#   (a) it is reviewable in git instead of living in a git-ignored
#       bootstrap.tfvars whose local state does not exist in this repo, and
#   (b) it survives the pending migration off CodeBuild, which deletes
#       infra/terraform/bootstrap/cicd.tf (the only TF_VAR_alert_email source)
#       without replacing it in .github/workflows/deploy.yml.
# Terraform resolves -var-file AFTER TF_VAR_*, so this wins over the CI value
# while CodeBuild still exists. Not a secret: the same class of address is
# already published in infra/terraform/RUNBOOK.md:44-46 and
# infra/terraform/bootstrap/bootstrap.tfvars.example:96.
# Changing this value DESTROYS and RECREATES both SNS email subscriptions
# (eu-central-1 and us-east-1) as PendingConfirmation - a human must click
# both links. It cannot touch the EC2 instance: user_data is in
# ignore_changes and user_data_replace_on_change is false
# (infra/terraform/modules/compute/main.tf:81,141).
alert_email = "<OWNED-MAILBOX@hexaware.com>"
```

`<OWNED-MAILBOX@hexaware.com>` is the human decision in I11. Do not invent one.

Then land it the normal way (push to `dev`), or, if applying by hand, mirror CI exactly:

```bash
cd infra/terraform/app
terraform init -reconfigure \
  -backend-config="bucket=$TF_STATE_BUCKET" \
  -backend-config="key=velocityai/dev/app.tfstate" \
  -backend-config="region=eu-central-1" \
  -backend-config="dynamodb_table=$TF_STATE_LOCK_TABLE" \
  -backend-config="encrypt=true"
terraform plan -no-color -var-file=dev.tfvars \
  -var="expected_account_id=577954642302" -var="aws_region=eu-central-1" \
  -var="state_bucket=$TF_STATE_BUCKET" -var="image_tag=<current tag>"
```

**The plan MUST read exactly:**

```text
Plan: 2 to add, 0 to change, 2 to destroy.
```

and the only two resources named must be
`module.monitoring.aws_sns_topic_subscription.email[0]` and
`module.monitoring.aws_sns_topic_subscription.email_useast1[0]`. **If `aws_instance.app`,
`aws_ebs_volume.data` or `aws_eip.this` appears anywhere in that plan, abort.** That

**Part C - the standing guard (do this in the same change, not later).**

The reason dev sat unsubscribed for a month is that nothing distinguishes
`PendingConfirmation` from confirmed. Add that check to the CI path that already runs on
every dev push.

File: `infra/buildspec.yml`, `post_build` phase - append after the SSM redeploy poll
loop ends (currently the file's last statement, `:314-324`).

AFTER (append):

```yaml
      # --- Alert-delivery guard --------------------------------------------
      # Terraform can CREATE an email subscription but cannot CONFIRM one, so
      # "apply succeeded" says nothing about whether an alarm can reach a human.
      # dev sat with SubscriptionsConfirmed=0 for a month because nothing checked.
      # WARN-only on purpose: a stale mailbox must not fail a deploy.
      - |
        set -euo pipefail
        for pair in "eu-central-1:velocityai-${ENVIRONMENT}-alerts" \
                    "us-east-1:velocityai-${ENVIRONMENT}-alerts-useast1"; do
          rgn="${pair%%:*}"; nm="${pair#*:}"
          arn="$(aws sns list-topics --region "$rgn" \
                  --query "Topics[?ends_with(TopicArn,':${nm}')].TopicArn|[0]" \
                  --output text 2>/dev/null || echo None)"
          if [ "$arn" = "None" ] || [ -z "$arn" ]; then
            echo "WARNING: SNS topic ${nm} not found in ${rgn}." >&2; continue
          fi
          n="$(aws sns get-topic-attributes --region "$rgn" --topic-arn "$arn" \
                --query 'Attributes.SubscriptionsConfirmed' --output text)"
          if [ "${n:-0}" -lt 1 ]; then
            echo "WARNING: ${nm} has ${n} CONFIRMED subscriber(s) - alarms fire into the void." >&2
          else
            echo "OK: ${nm} has ${n} confirmed subscriber(s)."
          fi
        done
```

*Why WARN and not fail:* a deploy blocked because someone left the company and their
mailbox bounced is a worse outage than a missing alert. The warning is loud, appears in
every build log, and is the thing whose absence caused this issue.

*Why in `buildspec.yml` despite C1's advice:* C1 correctly says work written into the
buildspec is thrown away by `origin/fix/infra-uki`. That is true, and this snippet is 20
lines that cost nothing to re-port. The alternative - waiting for the migration - leaves
the gap open indefinitely. **Port it into `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` when that branch
lands**; note it in the migration checklist.

**Nothing to delete (INV-3/INV-12).** B6 supersedes no code path. The two subscription
resources remain the single mechanism; Part A adds no second mechanism (it re-drives the
same SNS `Subscribe` Terraform already owns); Part B changes a value, not a mechanism;
Part C adds a read-only assertion. There is no shadow implementation to remove.

##### I6. Ripple-effect analysis - why nothing else breaks

Assuming my fix is wrong, here is where it would show.

**"The apply replaces the instance and I lose Postgres."** The catastrophic case. Ruled out
by two independent guards, each proven sufficient in isolation (4.6). Additionally fenced
by the mandatory plan assertion in Part B, and by `disable_api_termination` /
`disable_api_stop` (`compute/main.tf:111-112`) which would make a destroy fail loudly
rather than silently. Residual risk: an executor who runs `apply` without reading the plan.
Mitigation: the plan assertion is written as a stop-loss with an explicit abort condition.

**"Confirming makes the new subscriber's inbox unusable."** Real, and the entire reason for
the ordering gate. Post-B1/B2/E2/E3 the expected steady state is **0 firing velocityai-dev
alarms** - unless `unexpected-kms-decrypt` (4.2) or `billing-monthly` (#20) is a true
positive, which is exactly why both are triaged before subscription rather than after.

**"The `-var-file` override silently stops working."** It would take someone converting the
CI call from `-var-file` to `-var` for the same variable, or removing `-var-file` entirely.
Both are visible one-line diffs in `buildspec.yml:198`. And after the infra-uki migration
`-var-file` becomes the *only* source, so the risk decays to zero.

**"Two subscriptions to the same mailbox means duplicate mail."** Yes - by design. The
eu-central-1 topic carries 19 alarms plus backup-job events; us-east-1 carries the billing
alarm only. They never carry the same event. No duplication.

**Concurrency / ordering.** SNS `Subscribe` is idempotent for an identical
`(topic, protocol, endpoint)` triple `[I]`; two operators running Part A concurrently
produce one pending subscription and two confirmation mails, either of which works. There
is no lock to contend and no queue to drain.

**Startup / shutdown, unattached clients, slow clients, crashed runs, restarts, resumes,
fan-out runs, revision runs, two browsers.** All null. B6 changes no runtime code path.
The application does not read the SNS topic, does not read `alert_email`, and does not know
alarms exist. The only in-application coupling is `VELOCITYAI_ACME_EMAIL`, which is read
once at first boot by `bootstrap-ec2.sh:83` and passed to `certbot --email` at `:932` - and
that script does not re-run (C1's finding: dev's userData has no firstboot service and
`/var/lib/velocityai/.bootstrap-done` does not exist).

**The ACME side effect, examined properly.** Changing `alert_email` changes the ACME
registration address baked into the *S3-hosted* bootstrap script's environment. Three
reasons this is inert on dev: (i) `user_data` is in `ignore_changes`, so the on-box
`/etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env` is not rewritten; (ii) even if it were, bootstrap does not
re-run; (iii) certbot's registered ACME account is already created and renewal does not
re-register. The only visible effect would be on a **future rebuilt** instance, where the
new address would receive Let's Encrypt expiry notices - which is arguably an improvement.
`[V]` on (i) and (ii); `[I]` on (iii).

**Memory / connection-pool effects.** None. No process changes.

**Partial application.** Part A is two independent CLI calls; if the second fails you have
a confirmed eu-central-1 topic and a still-pending us-east-1 one - degraded, not broken
(you lose only the billing alarm). Part B is a single Terraform apply of two resources; if
it fails after destroying and before creating, re-running converges (the resource is
`count`-gated on a non-empty string that is still non-empty). Part C is read-only and
cannot fail the build (`|| echo None`, and WARN-only).

**Where the dossier already argues safety, I verified rather than restated:** the
`ignore_changes` claim (4.6, proven with a non-vacuous control), the destroy/recreate claim
(4.7, proven), the per-env isolation claim (4.5, read from the buildspec state keys), and
the "16 stuck legacy alarms cannot reach us" implication (4.4, read from the topic policy).

```bash
for pair in "eu-central-1:velocityai-dev-alerts" "us-east-1:velocityai-dev-alerts-useast1"; do
  rgn="${pair%%:*}"; nm="${pair#*:}"
  arn=$(aws sns list-topics --region "$rgn" \
```

- **Before: `Confirmed: "0"`, `Pending: "1"`** on eu-central-1 (dossier `[I]`), and an

**T4 - end-to-end delivery, per topic.** A confirmed subscription that never delivers is
the same failure one layer down. Drive each topic separately, because they have different
publishers and different policies:

```bash
# eu-central-1 path: force one real alarm through the alarm -> topic -> mailbox chain.
aws cloudwatch set-alarm-state --region eu-central-1 \
  --alarm-name velocityai-dev-mem-high --state-value ALARM \
  --state-reason "B6 delivery test $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
```

##### I9. Rollback

**Part A (confirmation).** Reversible: `aws sns unsubscribe --subscription-arn <arn>`. Note
the consequence - Terraform's state still holds the pre-confirmation
`...:PendingConfirmation` handle, so after unsubscribing, the next `app apply` will plan a
create and mint a fresh pending subscription. That is convergent, not broken.

**Part B (`dev.tfvars`).** `git revert` the commit and let the next dev push apply, or
apply by hand. The revert destroys and recreates the subscriptions back to the CI-supplied
address, in `PendingConfirmation` - i.e. a revert returns you to the *current* broken state
rather than to a working one. Say that out loud before reverting.

**Part C (buildspec guard).** `git revert`; it is read-only and WARN-only, so reverting has
no side effect beyond losing the warning.

**Not reversible, and the reason the plan assertion in T2 is non-negotiable:** an EC2
instance replacement. `velocityai-dev-root` has `delete_on_termination = true`
(`compute/main.tf:121`) and **zero snapshots** (dossier Appendix 2). Postgres lives on that
volume. There is no filesystem-level rollback for the dev box. The data EBS
(`aws_ebs_volume.data`) survives with `prevent_destroy = true` (`compute/main.tf:66`) and
the EIP survives with `prevent_destroy = true` (`:189`) - but the root volume, and with it
every host-level fix B1/B2/B3/B4/B5 and A1 apply, does not.

**What a pre-change backup must capture.** Under my recommended path, nothing on the host
is touched, so no host backup is required for B6 itself. But if this change is executed in
the same window as A1/B1/B2 (which do touch the host), the shared prerequisite is theirs:
`/root/nginx-backup-<ts>/` for the nginx config (C1's requirement) and a copy of
`/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json` before B1 rewrites it.
For B6 specifically the only "backup" worth taking is a record of the current state, so a
revert is informed rather than guessed:

```bash
aws sns list-subscriptions-by-topic --region eu-central-1 --topic-arn "$DEV_TOPIC"    > /tmp/b6-subs-eu.json
aws sns list-subscriptions-by-topic --region us-east-1    --topic-arn "$DEV_TOPIC_US" > /tmp/b6-subs-us.json
terraform -chdir=infra/terraform/app state show \
  'module.monitoring.aws_sns_topic_subscription.email[0]' > /tmp/b6-tfstate-sub.txt
```

##### I10. Sequencing and dependencies

**Hard prerequisites (blocking).**

- **B1 must land first.** Six of the eight firing dev alarms are CloudWatch-agent metrics.
  Confirming before B1 subscribes a human to a false-alarm storm.
- **B2 must land with B1.** B1 alone yields a running agent that ships nothing (B2's own
  framing, and I agree: the alarms key on metrics, and metrics need the agent alive, but
  `cert-renew-heartbeat-stale` additionally needs the *letsencrypt log* readable). **A
  correction for B2's author:** `usermod -a -G adm cwagent` does not cover
  `/var/log/letsencrypt/` (mode `0700 root:root` - B2 says so itself), so alarm #8 stays in
  ALARM after B1+B2 unless B2 also grants that ACL or drops the path from the
  `collect_list`. B6's ordering gate will catch it, but B2 should own the fix.

**Strongly recommended before subscribing (non-blocking but noisy if skipped).**

- **E2** removes `pg-dump-heartbeat-stale` from the firing set - it is the one alarm
  B1+B2 provably cannot clear, because its namespace `VelocityAI/Backups`
  (`main.tf:733`) has no publisher anywhere in the tree (verified: the sole
  `put-metric-data` call in `bootstrap-ec2.sh` is `StuckRunningWorkflows` at `:1105`).
- **E3** takes `stuck-running-workflows` out of INSUFFICIENT_DATA and stops dev's data
  corrupting prod's series. Not in the 41 (it is `tmd = "missing"`), but it is a dead
  signal the new subscriber would otherwise never receive.
- **Triage #19 (`unexpected-kms-decrypt`) and #20 (`billing-monthly`)** - see 4.2 and I11.

**Follows B6 (do not fold in).**

- **E1** adds the `AWS/Logs IncomingLogEvents` meta-alarm that would have caught B1 on day
  one. It belongs *after* B6, because the meta-alarm is only useful once someone is
  subscribed; and it must ship with its own metric-filter rewrites because the JSON log
  format breaks alarm #10's positional pattern.
- **D11** adds SSE-stream logging, which is the natural replacement signal for the dead
  alarm #12. Retuning #12 should wait for it.

**File-level collisions across the 27 issues.**

| File | Issues that edit it | Collision with B6? |
|---|---|---|
| `infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh` | A1, B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, E1, E2, E3, C1 | **None.** B6 does not edit it. |
| `infra/terraform/modules/monitoring/main.tf` | E1 (filters/alarms `:466-497`, plus new alarms), E2 (may delete `:727-748`) | **None on the same hunk.** B6 does not edit this file at all under either Part A or Part B. |
| `infra/terraform/app/dev.tfvars` | **B6 only** (Part B) | None. |
| `infra/buildspec.yml` | **B6 only** (Part C); C1 says do not invest here | Advisory conflict with C1, addressed in I5 Part C. |

**Recommended global order:** `B1 -> B2 -> (E2, E3) -> [triage #19, #20] -> B6 -> E1 -> D11`.
The dossier asserts "B1 and B2 first, then subscribe"; I verified that ordering is
necessary and found it **insufficient** without E2 (alarm #7 survives B1+B2) and without
the letsencrypt ACL (alarm #8 survives B1+B2).

**Commit boundaries.** Part A is not a commit (AWS action only). Part B is one commit
touching one file. Part C is one commit touching one file. **Keep them separate** so Part C
- which is the durable value and carries no risk - can land and stay landed even if the
mailbox decision in I11 stalls Part B indefinitely.

##### I11. Open questions requiring a human decision

**Q1 - Who owns `velocityai-dev-alerts@hexaware.com`?** This is the whole issue. Terraform
subscribed it on 2026-07-01 and nobody confirmed it, which is at least consistent with
nobody reading it. Three outcomes:

- **(a) It exists and someone reads it.** Best case. Execute Part A only; no repo change,
  no Terraform state write, no drift. **Recommended if true.**
- **(b) It exists as a distribution list but nobody is on it.** Add the on-call engineer to
  the list, then Part A. Still no repo change.
- **(c) It does not exist / has no owner.** Execute Part B with a real, owned address.
  **My recommendation for the address in that case: reuse
  `velocityai-oncall@hexaware.com`,** which the RUNBOOK already names as the intended
  operational mailbox for all three environments (`RUNBOOK.md:44-46`). Reusing it means dev
  alerts land in the same place stage/prod alerts eventually will, which is the correct
  end state, and it avoids minting a fourth address nobody owns either.

I cannot resolve this from the repo: `bootstrap.tfvars` is git-ignored, so the live value
is only knowable from AWS, and no AWS profile authenticates here.

**Q2 - Is `velocityai-dev-unexpected-kms-decrypt` a true positive?** A security alarm is
firing and nobody has looked. Two dispositions, and the decision belongs to whoever owns
security for this account:

- **If the contributing events are service principals / CodeBuild / routine platform
  activity:** the filter is under-scoped (4.2) and must gain an exclusion list **before**
  anyone subscribes. Subscribing first teaches the recipient that the security page is
  noise.
- **If they are unexpected human or role identities:** this outranks every other item in
  the dossier and should be escalated immediately, not sequenced behind B1.

**My recommendation:** run the one `filter-log-events` command in 4.2 before doing anything
else in this issue. It is read-only, costs nothing, and its answer changes the priority
order of the whole dossier.

**Q3 - Should the dev billing alarm stay at $100 on an account-wide metric?** Three alarms
(dev $100, stage $250, prod $500) watch the identical `AWS/Billing::EstimatedCharges`
account total. The dev one fires first and attributes the whole account's spend to dev.
Options: (a) raise dev's threshold above the account's steady-state run rate; (b) delete
the dev and stage billing alarms and keep only prod's, since the metric is not per-env;
(c) leave it and accept a monthly false page. **I recommend (b)** - one account-wide metric
deserves exactly one alarm - but it changes stage and prod behaviour, so it is outside
B6's dev-only fence and needs an explicit decision.

**Q4 - Is silencing the legacy `flowin-prod-alerts` / `flowin-staging-alerts` fatigue in
scope?** **My answer: no, and deliberately so.** Reasoning, from evidence:

- Those topics are **not in this repository**. The only trace is a documentation sentence
  (`docs/SIMPLE_AWS_DEPLOYMENT.md:1315`) describing an SNS topic `flowin-prod-alerts` that
  "fans out to PagerDuty / Slack / email per the on-call setup". No Terraform resource
  anywhere in `infra/` creates them (`grep -rn 'flowin-.*-alerts' infra/` = 0 hits). They
  predate the `velocityai-*` stack and are unmanaged by this codebase.
- They carry the account's **only two confirmed subscribers** (dossier `[I]`), and 16
  permanently-stuck alarms.
- The brief's scope fence is **dev only**. `flowin-prod-alerts` is, by name, a production
  topic with a real human on the other end, owned by whoever set up the original on-call.

Touching them would be an unmanaged, cross-environment, human-facing change made by an
agent with no AWS credentials and no owner list. **It is a separate decision, and it needs
the same person who answers Q1.** What B6 *should* do is hand over the finding: the 16
stuck alarms are the reason the one working alert channel in the account is already
ignored, and confirming a velocityai subscriber does not fix that.

##### I12. Shortcuts and alternatives explicitly rejected

**1. "Just click the link in the original confirmation email."** The dossier's Option 1 as
literally written. **Rejected: the token expired ~4 weeks ago** (I3, Correction 2). Nothing
about the pending subscription is clickable any more. This is the single most likely way an
executor wastes a day.

**2. `aws sns subscribe` a personal address, untracked.** The dossier flags it; I reject it
harder, on INV-12 grounds. It creates a **second, parallel delivery mechanism** alongside
the Terraform-managed one: Terraform will not remove it, will not reproduce it on a
rebuild, and the next `app apply` will still show one pending subscription forever. Worse,
it makes the Part-C guard lie - `SubscriptionsConfirmed` becomes 1 while the
Terraform-managed subscription is still dead, so the check that exists to catch this exact
failure now reports OK.

**3. Repoint via `TF_VAR_alert_email` (the dossier's Option 2).** **Rejected as written.**
It requires a `bootstrap apply`, and the bootstrap layer runs on local state that does not
exist in this repository or on this machine (I3, Correction 3). An apply from here would
run against empty state and attempt to create the state bucket, lock table and CMK against
a live account. Even with the correct state in hand, the channel it edits is deleted by
`origin/fix/infra-uki` (4.8). `-var-file` achieves the same result with one reviewable file
and no bootstrap involvement, and is proven to take precedence (I3, Correction 4).

**4. `terraform apply -replace` on the subscription to force a fresh confirmation mail.**
Works (4.7 proves the mechanism), but writes to `velocityai/dev/app.tfstate` and, if a
confirmed subscription ever exists, destroys it to create a pending one. A plain
`Subscribe` call achieves the same re-send with zero state mutation. Rejected as a
strictly worse instrument for the same job.

**5. Set `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"` on the six host alarms so they stop firing.**
The tempting one-line "fix" for the symptom. **Rejected:** the module's own comment
(`main.tf:355-361`) explains why `breaching` is correct - *"With `notBreaching`, a dead
agent leaves every host alarm in OK state while the disk fills, OOM-killer fires, etc."*
Flipping it converts a loud, correct alert into permanent silence and would have made B1
undetectable forever. The alarms are not wrong; the agent is dead. Fix B1.

**6. Delete the alarms that are currently firing.** Same class of error. Two of them
(#7 `pg-dump-heartbeat-stale`, #17 `stuck-running-workflows`) genuinely have no working
publisher - but the correct fix is E2's and E3's *publisher*, not the alarm. Deleting
`pg-dump-heartbeat-stale` in particular would remove the only backstop on the documented
RPO of 1 hour. E2 already argues this and I agree.

**7. Confirm only the eu-central-1 topic.** The obvious reading of the dossier, and it
leaves the billing alarm mute because it is the sole publisher to the us-east-1 topic
(4.1 #20, I3 Correction 1). Rejected.

**8. Add the `SubscriptionsConfirmed` check as a hard build gate.** Rejected in favour of
WARN-only: a bounced or decommissioned mailbox would then block every deploy, trading a
monitoring gap for an availability gap. The warning is loud and appears in every build log.

**9. Fold E2/E3 into B6 because "we're in the area".** Rejected. They edit
`infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh`, which C1 has established cannot reach a running instance
without an SSM push - a fundamentally different delivery mechanism with a different risk
profile and a different verification. Folding them in would put a host-mutating change
inside a change whose entire safety argument is "this touches no host". Keep the blast
radii separate.

**10. Fix alarm #12 (`ws-disconnect-spike`) here, since I found it dead.** Rejected as
scope creep, and recorded instead: its replacement signal does not exist yet. D11 adds
`run_stream.py` logging with a closed vocabulary of close reasons
(`client_disconnect | terminal_event | sentinel | no_live_queue | evicted`); retuning #12
to that vocabulary should be D11's follow-up or E1's, not B6's. The finding is the
contribution; the fix has a better owner.

## Cluster C — Delivery

---

### C1 — No host-configuration change can reach a running instance

**Severity:** the structural blocker. Without this, A1, B1, B2, B3, B4 and B5 are all unshippable.
**Confidence:** [V] — the gating condition, the Terraform lifecycle, and the live userData all read
directly.

#### Symptom

Editing `infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh` and pushing to `dev` changes nothing on the dev box. The
build succeeds, the deploy succeeds, and the host configuration is byte-identical afterwards.

#### Root cause

Three independent mechanisms, all deliberate, combining to a dead end:

1. `velocityai-firstboot.service` is gated by
   `ConditionPathExists=!/var/lib/velocityai/.bootstrap-done` (`user_data.sh.tpl:104`). [V]
2. `user_data_replace_on_change = false` and `user_data` is in `ignore_changes`
   (`modules/compute/main.tf:81`, `:134-151`). [V]
3. The CI deploy's on-host script only does `docker compose pull && up -d`
   (`infra/buildspec.yml:225-311`). It says so itself at `:286-287`: *"steady-state CI/CD deploys do
   NOT re-run bootstrap."* [V]

There is **no `aws_ssm_association`, no `aws_ssm_document`, and no agent-config SSM parameter
anywhere in the repo.** [V]

**A dev-specific finding makes this worse.** The live dev userData is **68 lines with no
`velocityai-firstboot.service` and no sentinel logic at all**, ending at *"awaiting SSM RunCommand
for full install"*. Dev launched 2026-07-01T03:59Z, before commit `bdc9e537` added self-bootstrap;
stage (07:10Z) and prod (10:55Z) have it. Confirmed on-box: `/var/lib/velocityai/.bootstrap-done`
**does not exist**. [V] So on dev, **nothing will ever regenerate the nginx or agent config** unless
a human deliberately re-runs the script.

#### Why it occurred

Every one of the three mechanisms is individually correct. Gating on a sentinel makes first-boot
idempotent. `ignore_changes` on `user_data` prevents Terraform from replacing a stateful instance —
which matters enormously here, because Postgres runs on the box and the root volume has
`delete_on_termination = true` with **zero snapshots**. And keeping the steady-state deploy to a
container pull is fast and safe.

What is missing is the fourth thing: a **reconcile** step. The design implicitly assumed host
configuration is immutable after provisioning, which was true until the application's transport
changed underneath it. The buildspec even demonstrates the author understood the general problem —
`chown 10001:10001` on the data directories is re-asserted on *every* deploy, with a comment
explaining that bootstrap does not re-run. The precedent existed; it just was not extended to nginx
or the agent.

#### The fix

**Two halves, both required. They are complements, not alternatives.**

**Now — apply to the running box, scoped to one instance id.**

```bash
DEV=i-092d5961f5aca87a6
NAME=$(aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids "$DEV" \
  --query 'Reservations[0].Instances[0].Tags[?Key==`Name`].Value|[0]' --output text)
[ "$NAME" = "velocityai-dev-app" ] || { echo "REFUSING: $DEV is '$NAME'"; exit 1; }

aws ssm send-command --instance-ids "$DEV" --document-name AWS-RunShellScript ...
```

**Never use `--targets`.** Six tag values — `Project`, `Owner`, `CostCenter`, `Repo`, `ManagedBy`,
`Component` — are **byte-identical across dev, stage and prod**. Only `Environment` and `Name`
discriminate, and an instance id is safer than either. [V]

The patch script must be idempotent (`grep -q` before appending), must back up to
`/root/nginx-backup-<ts>/` first, must gate on `nginx -t` before `systemctl reload`, and must restore
the backup and exit non-zero if validation fails. There is **no filesystem-level rollback available**
— `velocityai-dev-root` has zero snapshots — so the file-level backup is the only restore point. [V]

**Durable — the same day, commit to the repo.** Edit `bootstrap-ec2.sh` §13 (nginx) and §14
(CloudWatch agent) with the identical changes. This needs **no new pipeline step**:
`infra/terraform/app/main.tf:79-94` declares `aws_s3_object.bootstrap_script` with
`source_hash = filemd5(...)` into the **per-env** bucket, and every dev push already runs
`$TF/app apply` for `ENVIRONMENT=dev`. So committing to `dev` re-uploads the script to
`s3://velocityai-dev-pg-dumps-577954642302/config/bootstrap-ec2.sh` **and nowhere else**. [V]

**Later — a real reconcile step.** Extract §13/§14 *out* of `bootstrap-ec2.sh` into
`infra/scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh` and have bootstrap call it — one implementation, no shadow
copy. Then the pipeline change is **one line** (`bash infra/scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh` inside
the existing SSM payload), which is cheap to port later.

**Put that line in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, not `infra/buildspec.yml`.** The unmerged
`origin/fix/infra-uki` branch **deletes `buildspec.yml` entirely** (−324 lines) along with
`bootstrap/cicd.tf`, migrating to GitHub Actions. Work written into the buildspec is thrown away.
That branch keeps `bootstrap-ec2.sh` and modifies it only at lines 544-573, 1239-1244 and 1261-1274 —
**zero overlap** with §13 (703-938) and §14 (941-1007), so those edits are provably conflict-free. [V]

#### Verification

- The nginx probe pair from A1, run from outside.
- `aws s3api head-object --bucket velocityai-dev-pg-dumps-577954642302 --key config/bootstrap-ec2.sh`
  must show a fresh `LastModified` and the new `ContentLength`.
- **Survival matrix** [V]:

| Event | nginx change survives? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `docker compose pull && up -d` | **Yes** | nginx is host-installed; compose has only `backend` + `frontend` |
| Reboot | **Yes** | files on root EBS, `nginx.service` enabled, and the IP is a real Elastic IP (`eipalloc-0098c8fa703931a5e`) so the FQDN and TLS cert survive a stop/start |
| `certbot.timer` renewal | **Yes** | no renewal hook rewrites the site file |
| Instance replacement | **No** | root volume `delete_on_termination=true`, zero snapshots — hence the durable half |
| Someone re-runs `bootstrap-ec2.sh` | **No** — overwritten wholesale | hence the durable half |
| Auto-regeneration | **Cannot happen** on dev | its userData has no firstboot service |

##### I2. Register findings -- prior art, locked decisions, collisions

**The registers say nothing about this issue. That is itself the finding.**

I searched both registers (and `ISSUES-REGISTER.md`, `FIX-TEST-REGISTER.md`) for every term that could
touch host provisioning:

```bash
grep -rniE "\binfra\b|terraform|nginx|cloudwatch agent|cwagent|ec2|codebuild|systemd|certbot|\
bootstrap-ec2|reconcile|user_data|buildspec|ssm send-command|firstboot" \
  .planning/IMPLEMENTATION-REGISTER.md .planning/FIX-REGISTER.md \
  .planning/ISSUES-REGISTER.md .planning/FIX-TEST-REGISTER.md
```

Every hit is a false positive:
- `test-infra` (an ISSUES-REGISTER **tag**, ~14 rows: ISS-002/003/010/011/022/025/026/049 ...);
- `app-infra-generator` (an app_builder **agent name**, Phase 13/15/19, ISS-005);
- `"pure infra/refactor phase"` prose (IMPL `:301`), `"backend infra"` UAT prose (`:570`),
  `"test infra"` in per-phase `VALIDATION.md` descriptions (`:888`, `:972`, `:1092`, `:1188`);
- `reconcile` used for **event/register/terminal-status** reconciliation (IMPL `:73`, `:1704`,
  `:1850`, `:2255`, `:4076`; FIX `:3654`, `:3675`), never host config.

Literal `bootstrap-ec2.sh` / `buildspec` / `user_data` / `firstboot` / `terraform` / `cwagent`:
**zero occurrences** in either register. [V]

**What follows from that:**

1. **No prior fix touches these files.** `FIX-001..FIX-143` are 100% application-layer (backend
   Python / frontend TS / AGENT.md prompts / Alembic). The single infra-adjacent entry, **FIX-040**
   (IMPL `:2848`, FIX `:152`), edits `backend/Dockerfile` -- the container build, not the host. So
   **no shipped fix can be regressed by this change**, and there is no established anchor to
   contradict.
2. **No locked decision governs the host layer.** The full locked-decision corpus (Overview §4/§8,
   INV-1/2/3/5/7/8/12/13, SC-001, Q3, LOCK-A..G, ND-1..ND-13, D-01..D-24 per phase) is about the
   *engine kernel, capability registry, transport, migrations and UI*. None of them reach
   `infra/`. The only ones that touch this change at all are the *general* ones -- INV-12
   (no dual implementation) and Q3 (additive migrations) -- and I honour both in I7.
3. **The one adjacent precedent is a warning, not a constraint.** IMPL Phase 23 §7 records the
   `gsd-executor git stash` hazard: an executor's verification stash swept an uncommitted
   `app/core/config.py` boot fix and crashed the live backend (restored as `3f2645a1`). The same
   class applies here: this change is *entirely* uncommitted-shell-until-pushed, and an executor
   running a verification stash mid-flight would silently revert it. Commit before verifying.
4. **The nearest structural analogue in the registers is P43's injected-callback discipline**
   (IMPL `:3658`): "narrator persist, the live-ectx registry, and cached-invoke all reach the kernel
   as INJECTED callbacks ... no engine->app import". The C1 analogue is: the reconcile logic must
   have exactly **one** home, and every caller (bootstrap, pipeline, one-shot) must *invoke* it
   rather than carry a copy. I design to that in I5.
5. **`.planning/DEV-SSE-INFRA-ISSUES-260729.md` is untracked** (`git status --short` ->
   `?? .planning/DEV-SSE-INFRA-ISSUES-260729.md`) and has no register row. Nothing to reconcile.

##### I3. Root cause -- confirmed, corrected, or replaced

**The dossier's causal chain is correct.** I re-derived it independently.

**The chain, verified end to end:**

1. A host-config value lives only in `infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh` (nginx site :731-915, agent
   config :962-1001). [V]
2. That script is *executed* on the box by exactly two things:
   (a) `velocityai-firstboot.service`, written by `user_data.sh.tpl:99-114`, which runs
   `/opt/velocityai/run-firstboot-bootstrap.sh` (`:76-96`) -- which `aws s3 cp`s the script from
   `s3://$VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET/config/bootstrap-ec2.sh` (`:86-87`) and `bash`es it (`:95`);
   (b) a human, per `infra/terraform/RUNBOOK.md:125` ("Run `infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh` on the
   new instance via SSM RunCommand"). [V]
3. (a) is gated `ConditionPathExists=!/var/lib/velocityai/.bootstrap-done`
   (`user_data.sh.tpl:104`), and the script's own last act is to write that sentinel
   (`bootstrap-ec2.sh:1281-1282`). So the unit is a strict once-per-instance latch. [V]
4. Terraform cannot re-deliver a changed `user_data`: `user_data_replace_on_change = false`
   (`compute/main.tf:81`) plus `user_data` inside `ignore_changes` (`:140`). [V]
5. The steady-state deploy never re-runs bootstrap and says so:
   `buildspec.yml:286-287`, and the on-host script (`:232-301`) does only
   `aws s3 cp` of two config objects, an app.env pin rewrite, `chown`, ECR login,
   `docker compose pull` (:293) and `up -d` (:294). [V]
6. Therefore a repo edit to `bootstrap-ec2.sh` changes the S3 object and nothing else.

**Three corrections / additions to the dossier's root-cause section:**

**C1-a. There is no fourth path, and I proved the negative.** `aws_ssm_association`,
`aws_ssm_document` and any CloudWatch-agent SSM parameter are absent from `infra/` (grep exit 1).
`aws ssm send-command` occurs once in executable code (`buildspec.yml:304`) and twice in comments
(`bootstrap-ec2.sh:19`, `:60`). [V]

**C1-b. The "someone re-runs bootstrap" escape hatch is worse than the dossier implies -- it is
destructive on a live box.** Re-running the whole script does far more than rewrite nginx: it
`apt-get -y full-upgrade`s (:93), `systemctl restart postgresql@16-main` (:298),
`docker compose down --remove-orphans` (:1240) and `systemctl restart velocityai-app.service`
(:1264). On a box serving traffic with runs in flight that is an outage plus abandoned runs
(compounding D8/D9). "A human re-runs the script" is therefore **not** an acceptable fallback for a
config change, which strengthens the case for extraction rather than weakening it.

**C1-c. Root cause of the root cause: `bootstrap-ec2.sh` conflates two lifecycles.** The file mixes
genuinely once-per-instance provisioning (partition + mkfs the data EBS, `initdb`, issue the TLS
cert, create the `velocityai-deploy` user, install the sudoers stanza) with *pure declarative
host configuration* (nginx site, agent config, ACLs) that is idempotent and safe to re-apply on any
schedule. Because the two share one file, the once-only latch that the first correctly needs is
inherited by the second, which does not. That -- not any of the three gates -- is the defect.
Every gate is right for provisioning; none is right for configuration. The fix is to separate the
lifecycles, not to weaken a gate.

**Where the dossier is right for a slightly wrong reason:** it frames the fix as "extract §13/§14".
§13 as written is *not* wholly re-runnable: lines 919-935 issue a TLS certificate. That block is
provisioning, must stay behind the latch, and must be carved out of the extraction (see I5 step 2).
The dossier does not mention this and an executor following it literally would move
`certbot certonly` into a script the pipeline runs on every deploy.
