##### I4. Blast-radius sweep -- every place this reaches

###### I4.1 The three blocking mechanisms, quoted

**(1) The sentinel gate.** `infra/terraform/modules/compute/user_data.sh.tpl:99-114`:

```ini
cat >/etc/systemd/system/velocityai-firstboot.service <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=VelocityAI first-boot full host bootstrap (Postgres, nginx, Docker, app)
After=cloud-init.target network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target
ConditionPathExists=!/var/lib/velocityai/.bootstrap-done

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
TimeoutStartSec=1800
ExecStart=/opt/velocityai/run-firstboot-bootstrap.sh

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT
```

and its writer, `bootstrap-ec2.sh:1281-1282`:

```bash
install -d -m 0755 /var/lib/velocityai
date -u --iso-8601=seconds > /var/lib/velocityai/.bootstrap-done
```

**(2) The Terraform lifecycle.** `infra/terraform/modules/compute/main.tf:80-81` and `:134-151`:

```hcl
  user_data                   = base64encode(local.user_data)
  user_data_replace_on_change = false
...
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [
      # AMI rolls forward as Canonical publishes new images; we want to
      # control instance refresh through a deliberate `terraform taint`,
      # not on every plan.
      ami,
      user_data,
      # AWS provider drift: after `aws_eip_association` attaches an EIP, the
      # describe-instances API starts reporting `associate_public_ip_address`
      # as `true` regardless of the launch-time setting. Without this ignore,
      # every subsequent `terraform plan` marks the instance for replacement
      # (true -> false # forces replacement) -- which then cascades into
      # destroying the data EBS volume_attachment, which requires stopping
      # the instance, which is blocked by `disable_api_stop = true`. See
      # hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws#14149 for the upstream issue.
      associate_public_ip_address,
    ]
  }
```

Note what else is in that `lifecycle`: **nothing.** No `prevent_destroy`, no `create_before_destroy`,
no `replace_triggered_by`. The instance's siblings do carry protection --
`aws_ebs_volume.data` has `prevent_destroy = true` (`:65-67`) and `aws_eip.this` has
`prevent_destroy = true` (`:176-190`) -- and `disable_api_termination` / `disable_api_stop`
(`:111-112`) are variable-driven. So the *instance* is the only unprotected member of the trio, and
`ignore_changes` on `user_data` is the only thing standing between a template edit and a rebuild.
That is exactly why it is correct and must not be removed. [V]

**(3) The CI deploy.** `infra/buildspec.yml:282-294` (the whole on-host mutation surface):

```bash
        # Bind-mounted data dirs MUST be owned by the container uid:gid (10001).
        # Backend + frontend run as non-root 10001 (see backend/frontend
        # Dockerfile); the backend creates <user>/<run> subdirs under /app/runs
        # and writes /app/skills. bootstrap-ec2.sh sets this ownership on FIRST
        # BOOT only -- steady-state CI/CD deploys do NOT re-run bootstrap, so we
        # re-assert it here on every deploy. Without it every pipeline run aborts
        # with EACCES ([Errno 13] Permission denied: '/app/runs/<user>'). Keeps
        # dev/stage/prod consistent regardless of when each host was provisioned.
        mkdir -p /opt/velocityai/data/runs /opt/velocityai/data/skills
        chown -R 10001:10001 /opt/velocityai/data/runs /opt/velocityai/data/skills
        aws ecr get-login-password --region "${REGION}" | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "${REGISTRY}"
        docker compose pull
        docker compose up -d --remove-orphans
```

That comment is the precedent the dossier cites, and it is exact: the author already recognised the
class of problem and solved it for **one** value (`chown`). My fix generalises the same slot.

###### I4.2 Is SSM usable on the dev box? -- yes, and it is already proven in production

The brief asks me to verify this before building on it. I can, without AWS credentials, to a much
higher standard than "the endpoints exist".

**The decisive evidence: the current pipeline already SSM-RunCommands this exact instance on every
deploy, and the build fails if it does not succeed.** `infra/buildspec.yml:304-324`:

```bash
        CMD_ID="$(aws ssm send-command \
          --instance-ids "${INSTANCE_ID}" \
          --document-name AWS-RunShellScript \
          --comment "velocityai deploy ${IMAGE_TAG}" \
          --timeout-seconds 1800 \
          --parameters file:///tmp/ssm-params.json \
          --region "${AWS_REGION}" \
          --query Command.CommandId --output text)"
        echo "SSM command: ${CMD_ID}"
        # Poll until the on-host script finishes.
        while true; do
          STATUS="$(aws ssm get-command-invocation --command-id "${CMD_ID}" --instance-id "${INSTANCE_ID}" --region "${AWS_REGION}" --query Status --output text 2>/dev/null || echo Pending)"
          case "${STATUS}" in
            Success) echo "Redeploy succeeded."; break ;;
            Failed|Cancelled|TimedOut)
              echo "Redeploy ${STATUS}:";
              aws ssm get-command-invocation ... --query StandardErrorContent --output text || true;
              exit 1 ;;
            *) sleep 10 ;;
          esac
        done
```

`INSTANCE_ID` comes from `terraform -chdir=infra/terraform/app output -raw instance_id` (`:222`) --
i.e. `i-092d5961f5aca87a6` for `ENVIRONMENT=dev`. [V] The dossier's own Appendix 2 records
`[V]` that **CodeBuild `velocityai-gitlab-runner-dev` succeeded 2026-07-29T16:27Z**. A build cannot
succeed unless this poll reached `Success`. **Therefore SSM RunCommand demonstrably works on
`i-092d5961f5aca87a6` as of 2026-07-29.** [I, but one inferential step from two `[V]` facts]

The supporting conditions all check out in the repo too:

| Requirement | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Instance role carries `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` | `foundation/main.tf:95` `attach_ssm_managed_policy = true`; `modules/iam/main.tf:184-188` attaches `arn:${partition}:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore`; `variables.tf:47-51` default `true`; `aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive` (`main.tf:240-248`) keeps exactly that one managed policy | [V] repo |
| `ssm` / `ssmmessages` / `ec2messages` interface endpoints, private DNS | `network/main.tf:3-10` service list; `:352-361` `aws_vpc_endpoint "interface"` with `private_dns_enabled = true` (:360) | [V] repo |
| App SG can reach the endpoint SG on 443 | `network/main.tf:301` `"VPC-internal egress to interface endpoints (HTTPS)"`; `:312-316` dedicated endpoint SG "only the app SG may reach 443/tcp" | [V] repo |
| Endpoint policy does not block RunCommand | `network/main.tf:18-29`: `Action = "*"`, `Resource = "*"`, only condition `aws:PrincipalAccount == var.account_id` | [V] repo |
| SSM agent present on the box | Ubuntu Noble ships `amazon-ssm-agent` as a preinstalled snap; nothing in `bootstrap-ec2.sh` installs, removes or masks it (`grep -c "amazon-ssm-agent" infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh` -> 0) | [I] |

**Conclusion: SSM is usable and no fallback path is needed.** The dossier is right to use it; it
simply understates how firmly that is already established.

**If an executor still wants a pre-flight** (cheap, read-only, ~5s):

```bash
aws ssm describe-instance-information \
  --filters "Key=InstanceIds,Values=i-092d5961f5aca87a6" \
  --region eu-central-1 \
  --query 'InstanceInformationList[0].{Ping:PingStatus,Agent:AgentVersion,Platform:PlatformName}'
# expect: Ping == "Online"
```

**If -- against this evidence -- SSM were unavailable, the fallback is EC2 Instance Connect /
Session Manager is also SSM, so the only genuine fallback is `ssh`**, and there is none: no port
22 ingress is opened for operators and `ssh_key_name` is optional
(`compute/main.tf:78`, `key_name = var.ssh_key_name != "" ? var.ssh_key_name : null`). The honest
fallback is therefore *"fix SSM first"*, which is why proving it up front matters.

**The instance-id guard and the tag footgun, in my own words.** `aws ssm send-command` accepts
either `--instance-ids` or `--targets Key=tag:...`. Tag targeting resolves at send time to *every*
instance matching the tag, and the resolution is invisible in the command you typed. In this account
six of the eight tags on the dev, stage and prod instances -- `Project`, `Owner`, `CostCenter`,
`Repo`, `ManagedBy`, `Component` -- are byte-identical across all three environments (dossier
Appendix 2, `[V]`). `Component = "compute"` is set literally in `compute/main.tf:131` with no
environment interpolation, so it is provably identical by construction [V]. Only `Environment` and
`Name` differ. A `--targets Key=tag:Component,Values=compute` therefore fans a *dev* config change
out to *prod* -- silently, with a single `Success`, and with no filesystem rollback anywhere
because no root volume in any environment has ever been snapshotted. `--instance-ids` names one
opaque, unforgeable identifier and cannot fan out. The `Name`-tag assertion the dossier prepends is
belt-and-braces on top of that: it converts a mistyped instance id from "silently reconfigure the
wrong host" into "refuse and exit 1".

###### I4.3 The durable half -- per-env bucket, and who actually reads the object

**Per-env bucket: CONFIRMED.** The chain is:
`app/main.tf:80` `bucket = local.fnd.backup_bucket_name` ->
`app/locals.tf:11` `fnd = data.terraform_remote_state.foundation.outputs` (state key
`velocityai/${ENVIRONMENT}/foundation.tfstate`, `buildspec.yml:155`) ->
`foundation/outputs.tf:74-77` `backup_bucket_name = module.backups.backup_bucket_name` ->
`foundation/main.tf:44` `bucket_name = "${local.name_prefix}-pg-dumps-${module.account_guard.account_id}"`,
with `name_prefix = "velocityai-dev"` for dev (`app/locals.tf:5-7`, same convention in foundation).
So dev's object key is
`s3://velocityai-dev-pg-dumps-577954642302/config/bootstrap-ec2.sh` and **a dev push touches only
dev's copy** -- `buildspec.yml:189-203` runs `$TF/app apply -var-file="${ENVIRONMENT}.tfvars"` with
`ENVIRONMENT` fixed per CodeBuild project (`buildspec.yml:6-10`). [V]

**`filemd5` behaviour: CONFIRMED and correctly understood.** `app/main.tf:83-84` pairs
`source` with `source_hash = filemd5(...)`. `source_hash` is what makes Terraform compare the
*local file content* rather than the (unreliable) S3 ETag, so an edit to `bootstrap-ec2.sh`
produces a plan diff and a re-upload on the very next `app apply`. No pipeline change needed for
the upload itself. [V]

**Who reads it? Exactly one consumer, and on the running dev box it is not present.**

```bash
$ grep -rn "config/bootstrap-ec2" . --include='*' | grep -v '^./.git/'
infra/terraform/app/main.tf:81:  key    = "config/bootstrap-ec2.sh"
infra/terraform/modules/compute/user_data.sh.tpl:86:  if aws s3 cp "s3://$${VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET}/config/bootstrap-ec2.sh" \
```

One writer, one reader. The reader is `user_data.sh.tpl:80-95`:

```bash
echo "[firstboot] $(date -u +%FT%TZ) fetching bootstrap-ec2.sh from S3"
. /etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env
: "$${VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET:?VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET missing}"
REGION="$${VELOCITYAI_REGION:-eu-central-1}"
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if aws s3 cp "s3://$${VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET}/config/bootstrap-ec2.sh" \
       /opt/velocityai/bootstrap-ec2.sh --region "$${REGION}"; then
    break
  fi
  ...
done
chmod 0755 /opt/velocityai/bootstrap-ec2.sh
echo "[firstboot] running bootstrap-ec2.sh"
bash /opt/velocityai/bootstrap-ec2.sh
```

and that wrapper is only ever executed by `velocityai-firstboot.service`, which
(i) does not exist in the *live* dev userData (dossier `[V]`, read on-box: 68 lines, no firstboot
unit, ends at *"awaiting SSM RunCommand for full install"*), and
(ii) even if it did, is latched off by `ConditionPathExists`.

**So, plainly: on the running dev instance, nothing fetches that S3 object -- ever.** The durable
half is *not* delivery for the current box. It is a record for the next rebuild.

**But it *is* real for a rebuild, which the dossier does not spell out.** `ignore_changes` suppresses
*drift detection on an existing resource*; it does not pin the value for a *newly created* one. A
replaced dev instance is created with `user_data = base64encode(local.user_data)`
(`compute/main.tf:80`) rendered from the **current** `user_data.sh.tpl`, which does contain the
firstboot unit. So `dev instance replaced -> firstboot runs -> fetches the current S3 object ->
current config`. The durable half therefore closes the "instance replacement" row of the survival
matrix, which is exactly the row the host-side half cannot. Both halves are needed, as the dossier
says -- I am adding the mechanism by which the durable half actually pays off.

**Ownership/permissions check for the reader:** `policies/s3-config-read.json` grants
`s3:GetObject` on `${bucket_arn}/config/*` and `s3:ListBucket` scoped to `s3:prefix = config/*`;
attached as `${name_prefix}-s3-config-read` (`modules/iam/main.tf:122-125`). The object is
`server_side_encryption = "aws:kms"` with `kms_id = local.fnd.kms_key_arn`
(`app/main.tf:87-88`), and `policies/kms-decrypt.json` grants `kms:Decrypt` via
`kms:ViaService = s3.${region}.amazonaws.com`. So any *new* file placed under the same `config/`
prefix with the same KMS key is readable with **zero IAM change**. [V] That is a load-bearing
property of my fix.

**The extracted body depends on exactly three variables, and I measured that rather than assuming
it** (full `awk` + `grep -oE` count in I6): `${ENVIRONMENT}` x8 real uses (the `log_group_name`
fields at `:988-995`), `${DOMAIN}`/`$DOMAIN` x12, `${ENV_TITLE}` x1 (the metric `namespace` at
`:970`). `$ACME_EMAIL` appears once, at `:932`, **inside the cert block that stays in bootstrap**.
`REGION`, `PARAM_PREFIX`, `BACKUP_BUCKET`, `APP_USER` and `IMAGE_TAG` are **not referenced at all**
in 703-1007. [V]

All three are re-derivable on the box from `/etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env` (written by
`user_data.sh.tpl:52-62`, persists on the root volume): `DOMAIN <- VELOCITYAI_FQDN`,
`ENVIRONMENT <- VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT`, `ENV_TITLE <- ${ENVIRONMENT^}`. Precedent:
`velocityai-load-secrets` (`bootstrap-ec2.sh:604-701`) is a standalone script emitted by bootstrap
that does exactly this re-sourcing at `:614`. [V]

**But two of those three carry a silent default in bootstrap that must NOT be carried across.**
`bootstrap-ec2.sh:78-79` reads `PARAM_PREFIX="${VELOCITYAI_PARAM_PREFIX:-/velocityai/prod}"` and
`ENVIRONMENT="${VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT:-prod}"`. `PARAM_PREFIX` is irrelevant here (not used in
§13/§14), but `ENVIRONMENT` **is** -- it renders nine environment-scoped identifiers. A reconcile
that inherits the `:-prod` default and runs with an unset variable writes dev's logs and metrics
into prod's namespaces, silently and irreversibly. The reconcile script must therefore be
**fail-closed** on `VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT`, not defaulted. This is implemented in I5 step 1,
guarded again in the SSM payload (I5 step 5b), gated by an operator pre-flight (I5 step 5a), and
analysed in full in I6.

The dossier's conflict claim is **exactly right**, and I verified it rather than trusting it:

```
@@ -544,30 +544,47 @@ TIMER
@@ -1239,6 +1256,9 @@ systemctl enable --now \
@@ -1261,14 +1281,32 @@ systemctl enable --now \
```

Old-side ranges: **544-573**, **1239-1244**, **1261-1274**. §13 is **703-939**, §14 is **941-1007**.
`max(573) < min(703)` and `max(1007) < min(1239)`. **Zero overlap. Provably conflict-free.** [V]

What the three hunks do (I read the full diff): §10 stops downloading `docker-compose.yml` /
`deploy.env` from S3 (decision "D-2, inline delivery"), and §18/§19 become conditional on a compose
file existing. Nothing in §13/§14 territory.

**Two things the dossier missed on that branch, both good news:**

1. **`aws_s3_object.bootstrap_script` SURVIVES**, and the branch says why in its own words
   (`git show origin/fix/infra-uki:infra/terraform/app/main.tf:130-132`):
   ```
   # `aws_s3_object.bootstrap_script` above intentionally STAYS Terraform-managed:
   # it must exist before any CI run has ever happened, so it is infrastructure,
   # not deploy output.
   ```
   with `key = "config/bootstrap-ec2.sh"` at `:85` and `source_hash = filemd5(...)` at `:88`, and
   `module "compute"` still `depends_on = [aws_s3_object.bootstrap_script]` at `:40-41`.
   The branch *deletes* `aws_s3_object.compose_yaml` and `aws_s3_object.deploy_env` but keeps this
   one. **So the durable half's mechanism -- an S3 `config/` object with `filemd5` -- is exactly the
   category that branch preserves.** A second object of the same category is aligned with its own
   stated rule, not fighting it.
2. **`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` has a clean, specific insertion point.** The SSM payload is
   built at branch lines 349-418 (`cat > remote.sh <<EOF` ... `EOF`), sent at 425-431, polled at
   438-470. The relevant slot:

   ```
   367-372   # PRE-CONDITION guard: $APP_ENV must exist
   373-379   grep-check BACKEND_IMAGE / FRONTEND_IMAGE lines exist
   373       echo '${COMPOSE_CONTENT}' | base64 -d > /opt/velocityai/docker-compose.yml
   376       chown -R 10001:10001 /opt/velocityai/data/skills /opt/velocityai/data/runs
   378-379   sed -i image pins
   384-392   POST-CONDITION: grep -qxF the pins
   393-407   pre-deploy pg_dump (stage/prod only)
   409       systemctl restart velocityai-app.service      <-- reconcile goes IMMEDIATELY BEFORE
   410-417   health poll
   ```

   line 349), deliberately, so runner-side `${COMPOSE_CONTENT}` / `${ECR_REGISTRY}` / `${IMAGE_TAG}`
   interpolate. Every box-side `$` in the branch's script is escaped `\$`. Any line I add must obey
   the same rule or the GitHub runner's `set -u` shell will evaluate it and fail with
   *unbound variable*. The branch's own header comment (352-357) documents this exact trap.

   `${{ vars.AWS_REGION || env.AWS_REGION }}` override at the send-command -- so the branch is not
   drop-in for the current `eu-central-1` dev environment. Not my problem to fix, but the executor
   should not assume that branch is turnkey.

###### I4.9 The survival matrix, row by row

| Event | Dossier | My verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docker compose pull && up -d` | Yes | **CONFIRMED [V]** | `docker-compose.yml` has exactly two services, `backend:` (:43) and `frontend:` (:140). nginx is host-installed via `apt-get install -y nginx` (`bootstrap-ec2.sh:99`). A container lifecycle operation cannot touch `/etc/nginx/`. |
| Reboot | Yes, "`nginx.service` enabled" | **CONFIRMED, wrong reason [V]** | `grep "systemctl enable" bootstrap-ec2.sh` shows nginx is **never** explicitly enabled -- only `systemctl reload nginx` (:930, :938). It is enabled because Debian/Ubuntu package postinst enables+starts a service on install (`apt-get install -y nginx`, :99). Same outcome; the stated justification is wrong and would mislead someone auditing the script. Config files live on the root EBS, which is not wiped by a reboot. |
| Elastic IP survives stop/start | Yes | **CONFIRMED [V]** | `compute/main.tf:168-191` `aws_eip "this"` with `domain = "vpc"` and a hard-coded `prevent_destroy = true` plus a long comment on why the address is identity; `:193-196` `aws_eip_association`. A VPC-domain EIP association survives stop/start. FQDN is `<dashed-eip>.nip.io` (`modules/dns`), so the hostname and hence the TLS cert survive. |
| `certbot.timer` renewal | Yes, `[V]` | **CONFIRMED as a conclusion, but the evidence is `[I]` not `[V]`** | Two corrections. (a) `grep -n "certbot\|renew" bootstrap-ec2.sh` -> only `apt-get install ... certbot python3-certbot-nginx` (:101), `certbot certonly --webroot ...` (:931-932), `systemctl enable --now certbot.timer` (:939). **No `--deploy-hook`, no `--renew-hook`, nothing written under `/etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/`.** `certonly --webroot` stores `authenticator = webroot` with no installer, so `certbot renew` re-authenticates and re-writes only `/etc/letsencrypt/`. The conclusion holds. (b) **It cannot have been *observed*.** Dev launched 2026-07-01; a Let's Encrypt cert is 90 days and certbot renews at 30 days remaining, i.e. ~day 60. At 29 days of uptime **no renewal has yet occurred on this box.** Mark the row `[I]`, well-founded. |
| Instance replacement | No | **CONFIRMED [V]** | `compute/main.tf:121` `delete_on_termination = true` on `root_block_device`. And the "zero snapshots" claim is structurally provable: `aws_backup_selection.by_tag` (`modules/backups/main.tf:278-295`) selects on `Backup = "true"` (defaults, `variables.tf:59-69`); that tag is set on `aws_ebs_volume.data` (`compute/main.tf:62`) and **not** in `root_block_device.tags` (`:123-126`, only `Name` + `Component`). So the root volume is outside the backup plan by construction. |
| Someone re-runs `bootstrap-ec2.sh` | No -- overwritten wholesale | **CONFIRMED [V]** | `cat > /etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai <<EOF` (:731) is a truncating write. See also I3 C1-b: re-running is destructive well beyond nginx. |
| Auto-regeneration | Cannot happen on dev | **CONFIRMED for the running instance, INCOMPLETE as stated [I]** | Correct that the live userData has no firstboot unit (dossier `[V]`, on-box). But a **replaced** dev instance renders `user_data` fresh from the current `user_data.sh.tpl`, which does have the unit -- so on a rebuild, auto-regeneration *does* happen and *is* the mechanism the durable half relies on. The row should read "Cannot happen on the **current** dev instance." |

---

##### I5. The complete fix

**Design principle.** Ship the *mechanism* first, provably inert; let the sibling issues' *content*
ride it afterwards. That gives a falsifiable gate for C1 alone
(`sha256sum /etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai` unchanged after reconcile) which is impossible if
mechanism and content land together.

**Delivery decision (this replaces the dossier's proposal, which cannot run).**

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| (a) `bash infra/scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh` inside the SSM payload | **impossible** -- no repo on the box (I4.5) |
| (b) inline base64 the script into every SSM payload | works, but the script then exists in two shapes (repo file + pipeline-embedded copy), and *two* pipelines must each carry the embedding -- an INV-12 smell and double the port cost |
| (c) emit the script from a heredoc inside `bootstrap-ec2.sh` to `/usr/local/bin/` | matches 5 in-file precedents (`velocityai-load-secrets` :604-701, `velocityai-pg-dump` :1062-1078, `velocityai-skills-backup` :1080-1092, `velocityai-stuck-workflows-check` :1094-1111, `velocityai-update-image-tag` :1017-1040) -- but the body becomes opaque to `bash -n`, and on the dev box (bootstrap never re-runs) the file would never appear |
| **(d) a repo file uploaded to S3 as a 4th `config/` object with `filemd5`, fetched by both bootstrap and the pipeline** | **CHOSEN** |

Why (d): it is *the exact mechanism already proven for `bootstrap-ec2.sh` itself*; the instance role
already has `s3:GetObject` on `config/*` and `kms:Decrypt` via S3 (I4.3) so **zero IAM change**;
`filemd5` gives free change-detection with no pipeline edit for the upload; the script is a
standalone file so CI can `bash -n` it; there is exactly **one** copy of the logic in the repo and
one on the box; and it is the same category `origin/fix/infra-uki` explicitly preserves
("infrastructure, not deploy output", I4.8).

**Ordering decision.** Land the durable half **first**, then run one SSM command that carries **no
logic at all** -- only fetch-and-run. That means there is never, at any instant, a second copy of
the reconcile logic anywhere. It also means the dev push that lands the change *already uploads the
object* (`$TF/app apply` runs on every dev build, `buildspec.yml:189-203`), so the operator step is
three lines.

**Step 1 -- NEW FILE `infra/scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh`** (mode 0755).

This is a *faithful* extraction of §13 (minus cert issuance) and §14 as they exist today. It must be
byte-equivalent in output so that C1 alone is a provable no-op.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# VelocityAI host-configuration reconcile.
#
# The DECLARATIVE half of infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh: nginx site + limits +
# proxy-header snippet, and the CloudWatch agent config + ACLs. Everything here
# is idempotent and safe to re-apply on a running host at any time.
#
# It exists because bootstrap-ec2.sh runs exactly ONCE per instance
# (velocityai-firstboot.service is gated by ConditionPathExists on
# /var/lib/velocityai/.bootstrap-done), while these values legitimately change
# with the application. Provisioning that is genuinely once-per-instance --
# partitioning the data EBS, initdb, ISSUING the TLS certificate, creating the
# deploy user + sudoers -- deliberately stays in bootstrap-ec2.sh.
#
# Callers (all three run the SAME file -- there is no second copy):
#   1. bootstrap-ec2.sh  -- first boot, after the cert block
#   2. the CI deploy     -- every deploy, via SSM RunCommand
#   3. an operator       -- ad hoc, same SSM one-liner
#
# Contract: FAIL-CLOSED. A bad nginx template must fail the caller loudly, not
# be reloaded. `nginx -t` parses the on-disk config in a throwaway process; the
# running master keeps its in-memory config until a SUCCESSFUL reload, so a
# validation failure costs zero downtime. On failure we restore the backup and
# exit non-zero.
set -euo pipefail

# --- context ---------------------------------------------------------------
# bootstrap.env is written by Terraform's compute user_data and persists on the
# root volume. Re-sourcing it here (rather than inheriting exported vars) is
# what makes this script runnable standalone. Same idiom as
# /usr/local/bin/velocityai-load-secrets.
if [[ ! -f /etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env ]]; then
    echo "[reconcile] FATAL: /etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env missing -- this box is not bootstrapped." >&2
    echo "[reconcile]        Refusing to render host config from defaults." >&2
    exit 1
fi
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
. /etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env

# FAIL-CLOSED on ENVIRONMENT -- deliberately NOT `${VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT:-prod}`.
#
# bootstrap-ec2.sh:79 defaults this to "prod" because on first boot a missing
# value could only mean the earliest single-environment deployment. Here that
# default is a LIVE HAZARD: this script renders
#   metrics.namespace          -> "VelocityAI/${ENV_TITLE}"        (agent JSON)
#   logs.*.log_group_name      -> "/velocityai/${ENVIRONMENT}/..." (8 entries)
# so an unset value would silently ship DEV logs into the PROD log groups and
# DEV metrics into the PROD namespace -- cross-environment data contamination
# with no error, no alarm, and no way to un-publish. A hard failure is the only
# safe behaviour: it costs a re-run, the default costs prod's data integrity.
#
# Same reasoning for FQDN: a wrong DOMAIN writes an nginx site pointing at a
# certificate path that does not exist, which `nginx -t` would then reject.
DOMAIN="${VELOCITYAI_FQDN:?FATAL: VELOCITYAI_FQDN unset in /etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env}"
ENVIRONMENT="${VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT:?FATAL: VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT unset in /etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env -- refusing to default to prod and poison prod log groups}"
[[ "$ENVIRONMENT" =~ ^(dev|stage|prod)$ ]] || {
    echo "[reconcile] FATAL: VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT='${ENVIRONMENT}' is not dev|stage|prod" >&2
    exit 1
}
ENV_TITLE="${ENVIRONMENT^}"
echo "[reconcile] environment=${ENVIRONMENT} -> log groups /velocityai/${ENVIRONMENT}/*, namespace VelocityAI/${ENV_TITLE}"

TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
BACKUP_DIR="/root/host-config-backup-${TS}"

echo "[reconcile] $(date -u --iso-8601=seconds) start env=${ENVIRONMENT} domain=${DOMAIN}"

# --- backup (the ONLY restore point -- the root volume has no snapshots) ----
install -d -m 0700 "$BACKUP_DIR"
for f in /etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai \
         /etc/nginx/conf.d/velocityai-limits.conf \
         /etc/nginx/snippets/velocityai-proxy-headers.conf \
         /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json; do
    [[ -f "$f" ]] && cp -a "$f" "$BACKUP_DIR/$(basename "$f")"
done
getfacl -pR /var/lib/docker/containers > "$BACKUP_DIR/docker-containers.acl" 2>/dev/null || true
id cwagent > "$BACKUP_DIR/cwagent.id" 2>&1 || true
echo "[reconcile] backup -> $BACKUP_DIR"

restore_and_die() {
    echo "[reconcile] FAILED -- restoring from $BACKUP_DIR" >&2
    [[ -f "$BACKUP_DIR/velocityai" ]]                        && cp -a "$BACKUP_DIR/velocityai"                        /etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai
    [[ -f "$BACKUP_DIR/velocityai-limits.conf" ]]            && cp -a "$BACKUP_DIR/velocityai-limits.conf"            /etc/nginx/conf.d/velocityai-limits.conf
    [[ -f "$BACKUP_DIR/velocityai-proxy-headers.conf" ]]     && cp -a "$BACKUP_DIR/velocityai-proxy-headers.conf"     /etc/nginx/snippets/velocityai-proxy-headers.conf
    [[ -f "$BACKUP_DIR/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json" ]]      && cp -a "$BACKUP_DIR/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json"      /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json
    echo "[reconcile] restored; nginx was NOT reloaded, the running config is unchanged" >&2
    exit 1
}

# ============================================================================
# nginx  (was bootstrap-ec2.sh section 13, lines 703-939)
# ============================================================================
mkdir -p /var/www/letsencrypt /etc/nginx/snippets

cat > /etc/nginx/conf.d/velocityai-limits.conf <<'EOF'
<<< VERBATIM lines 707-715 of bootstrap-ec2.sh -- see step 1b >>>
EOF

cat > /etc/nginx/snippets/velocityai-proxy-headers.conf <<'EOF'
<<< VERBATIM lines 719-726 of bootstrap-ec2.sh >>>
EOF

# The full nginx site is written with $DOMAIN interpolated. Keeping the
# heredoc unquoted because we WANT shell expansion of $DOMAIN; nginx vars
# (like $host, $request_uri) are escaped with \ to survive bash.
cat > /etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai <<EOF
<<< VERBATIM lines 732-914 of bootstrap-ec2.sh >>>
EOF
ln -sfn /etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/velocityai
rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default

# Validate BEFORE reload. Skip the reload (not the write) when no certificate
# exists yet: on a brand-new box this script runs before certbot has issued,
# and `ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/$DOMAIN/fullchain.pem` would make
# `nginx -t` fail on a file the caller is about to create.
if [[ -d "/etc/letsencrypt/live/${DOMAIN}" ]]; then
    nginx -t || restore_and_die
    systemctl reload nginx
    echo "[reconcile] nginx validated and reloaded"
else
    echo "[reconcile] NOTE: no cert at /etc/letsencrypt/live/${DOMAIN} yet -- config written, reload deferred to the caller"
fi
systemctl enable --now certbot.timer

# ============================================================================
# CloudWatch agent  (was bootstrap-ec2.sh section 14, lines 941-1007)
# ============================================================================
if ! dpkg -s amazon-cloudwatch-agent >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    wget -q https://s3.amazonaws.com/amazoncloudwatch-agent/ubuntu/amd64/latest/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.deb \
        -O /tmp/cw-agent.deb
    dpkg -i /tmp/cw-agent.deb
    rm /tmp/cw-agent.deb
fi
# Re-grant ACL now that cwagent user exists. See bootstrap section 8 for why
# o::r is load-bearing (preserves world-read on per-container /etc/hosts so
# non-root containers can do DNS).
setfacl -R -m u:cwagent:rX,o::r /var/lib/docker/containers
setfacl -R -d -m u:cwagent:rX,o::r /var/lib/docker/containers

mkdir -p /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc
cat > /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json <<EOF
<<< VERBATIM lines 963-1000 of bootstrap-ec2.sh >>>
EOF

/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl \
    -a fetch-config -m ec2 -s \
    -c file:/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json

echo "[reconcile] $(date -u --iso-8601=seconds) complete"
```

**Step 1b -- how the executor produces the `<<< VERBATIM >>>` bodies.** Do **not** retype them. Cut
them mechanically so the extraction is provably faithful:

```bash
cd /Users/1000060523/Documents/Work/UKI/Flowin/flowin
sed -n '707,715p' infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh   # limits.conf body
sed -n '719,726p' infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh   # proxy-headers body
sed -n '732,914p' infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh   # nginx site body (NOT 915 -- that is the EOF)
sed -n '963,1000p' infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh  # agent JSON body (NOT 1001 -- that is the EOF)
```

The escaping in the two unquoted heredocs (`\$host`, `\$request_uri`, `\${aws:InstanceId}` ...) is
already correct for an unquoted heredoc and must be carried across **byte for byte**. Both new
heredocs use the same quoting as their originals -- quoted `<<'EOF'` for limits/proxy-headers,
unquoted `<<EOF` for the site and the agent JSON.

*Before* (lines 703-1007, abbreviated -- 305 lines):

```bash

mkdir -p /var/www/letsencrypt /etc/nginx/snippets
cat > /etc/nginx/conf.d/velocityai-limits.conf <<'EOF'
...
cat > /etc/nginx/snippets/velocityai-proxy-headers.conf <<'EOF'
...
cat > /etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai <<EOF
...

rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default

# Initial cert (HTTP-01 webroot) — only if no cert exists yet for this domain

    ...
fi

# ── 14. CloudWatch agent ───────────────────────────────────────────────
...
/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl \
    -a fetch-config -m ec2 -s \
```

*After* (replaces exactly lines 703-1007):

```bash
# ── 13/14. Host configuration (nginx + CloudWatch agent) ───────────────
#
# The declarative half of this script now lives in
# infra/scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh, uploaded by the app layer to
# s3://$BACKUP_BUCKET/config/reconcile-host-config.sh (aws_s3_object
# .reconcile_script, source_hash = filemd5). Same delivery mechanism as this
# script itself.
#
# WHY: bootstrap runs exactly once per instance (velocityai-firstboot.service
# is gated on /var/lib/velocityai/.bootstrap-done), but nginx and the agent
# config legitimately change with the application. The reconcile script is
# idempotent and is re-run by CI on every deploy, so a repo edit reaches a
# LIVE host. Genuinely once-per-instance provisioning -- including ISSUING the
# TLS cert below -- stays here.
mkdir -p /var/www/letsencrypt /etc/nginx/snippets

# Retry the fetch. Under `set -e` (line 27) a single transient S3 failure would
# abort provisioning; the firstboot wrapper already retries the bootstrap-script
# fetch 30x for exactly this reason (user_data.sh.tpl:85-92) and this inherits
# the same posture.
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
    if aws s3 cp "s3://${BACKUP_BUCKET}/config/reconcile-host-config.sh" \
         /opt/velocityai/reconcile-host-config.sh --region "$REGION"; then
        break
    fi
    echo "[bootstrap] reconcile-host-config.sh not available yet (attempt $i) — retrying"
    sleep 10
done
[[ -s /opt/velocityai/reconcile-host-config.sh ]] || {
    echo "[bootstrap] ERROR: could not fetch reconcile-host-config.sh from S3" >&2; exit 1; }
chmod 0755 /opt/velocityai/reconcile-host-config.sh

# Initial cert (HTTP-01 webroot) — only if no cert exists yet for this domain.
# Runs BEFORE the reconcile so the reconcile's `nginx -t` has a certificate to
# validate against. The temporary bootstrap-http site below only needs the
# webroot, not the real site file.
if [[ ! -d /etc/letsencrypt/live/$DOMAIN ]]; then
    cat > /etc/nginx/sites-available/bootstrap-http <<EOF2
server {
    listen 80 default_server;
    location /.well-known/acme-challenge/ { root /var/www/letsencrypt; }
    location / { return 200 'bootstrap'; add_header Content-Type text/plain; }
}
EOF2
    ln -sfn /etc/nginx/sites-available/bootstrap-http /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/bootstrap-http
    rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/velocityai
    systemctl reload nginx
    certbot certonly --webroot -w /var/www/letsencrypt \
        --non-interactive --agree-tos --email "$ACME_EMAIL" -d "$DOMAIN"
    rm /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/bootstrap-http
fi

# Writes nginx + agent config, validates, reloads, restarts the agent.
# Fail-closed: a bad template aborts bootstrap here rather than shipping.
bash /opt/velocityai/reconcile-host-config.sh
```

Three non-obvious choices, each with its reason:

- **The cert block moves *above* the reconcile call, not into it.** `certbot certonly` calls a
  rate-limited external CA and mutates `sites-enabled`; running it on every deploy is wrong.
  Putting it first also means the reconcile's `nginx -t` always has a cert to validate.
  (I still keep the cert-absent guard inside the reconcile script for the pathological case where
  issuance fails -- belt and braces, and it keeps the script standalone-safe.)
- **`ln -sfn .../velocityai` moved into the reconcile script, so the cert block only needs
  `rm /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/bootstrap-http`** -- the original `:934` re-link is now redundant
  because reconcile runs immediately after and re-links unconditionally. One link site, not two
  (INV-12).
- **`nginx -t` and `systemctl reload nginx` are deleted from bootstrap entirely.** They now exist
  once, inside the reconcile script. If they were left in both places a future edit would drift.

**Step 3 -- EDIT `infra/terraform/app/main.tf`: add the 4th `config/` object.**

*After* the existing `aws_s3_object.bootstrap_script` block (i.e. insert at line 95, immediately
after its closing `}` at `:94`):

```hcl
# --- Host-config reconcile script hosted in S3 ------------------------------
# The declarative half of bootstrap-ec2.sh (nginx site + limits + proxy-header
# snippet, CloudWatch agent config + ACLs), extracted so it can be re-applied
# to a RUNNING host. bootstrap-ec2.sh fetches and runs it on first boot; the CI
# deploy fetches and runs it on every deploy. `source_hash` re-uploads whenever
# the local script changes, so a repo edit reaches a live host on the next
# deploy without any pipeline change.
#
# Same category as bootstrap_script: infrastructure that must exist before any
# CI run, not deploy output. Same bucket/prefix/KMS key, so the instance role's
# existing s3-config-read + kms-decrypt grants already cover it.
resource "aws_s3_object" "reconcile_script" {
  bucket = local.fnd.backup_bucket_name
  key    = "config/reconcile-host-config.sh"

  source      = "${path.root}/../../scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh"
  source_hash = filemd5("${path.root}/../../scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh")

  content_type           = "text/x-shellscript"
  server_side_encryption = "aws:kms"
  kms_key_id             = local.fnd.kms_key_arn

  tags = {
    Name      = "${local.name_prefix}-reconcile-script"
    Component = "compute"
  }
}
```

and extend the compute `depends_on` (`app/main.tf:34-38`):

```hcl
  depends_on = [
    aws_s3_object.compose_yaml,
    aws_s3_object.deploy_env,
    aws_s3_object.bootstrap_script,
    aws_s3_object.reconcile_script,
  ]
```

Run `terraform fmt infra/terraform/app` afterwards -- `pre_build` hard-gates on
`terraform fmt -check -recursive` (`buildspec.yml:97`).

**Step 5 -- the one-shot, to reach the dev box NOW.**

Run only **after** step 1-4 are committed and the dev push has completed (so the S3 object exists
and carries the current content). The payload carries **no logic** -- that is the point.

**Step 5b -- the reconcile itself.**

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

DEV=i-092d5961f5aca87a6
REGION=eu-central-1

# Instance-id guard. NEVER --targets: Project/Owner/CostCenter/Repo/ManagedBy/
# Component are byte-identical on dev, stage and prod, so a tag target would
# fan a dev change out to prod with no filesystem rollback anywhere.
NAME=$(aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids "$DEV" --region "$REGION" \
  --query 'Reservations[0].Instances[0].Tags[?Key==`Name`].Value|[0]' --output text)
[ "$NAME" = "velocityai-dev-app" ] || { echo "REFUSING: $DEV is '$NAME'"; exit 1; }

# Confirm the object we are about to run is the one we just pushed.
aws s3api head-object --region "$REGION" \
  --bucket velocityai-dev-pg-dumps-577954642302 \
  --key config/reconcile-host-config.sh \
  --query '{LastModified:LastModified,ContentLength:ContentLength,ETag:ETag}'

cat > /tmp/reconcile.sh <<'SCRIPT'
# SSM AWS-RunShellScript runs this under /bin/sh (dash on Ubuntu), which lacks
# `set -o pipefail`. Re-exec under bash on the first line -- same idiom as
# infra/buildspec.yml:236.
if [ -z "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then exec bash "$0" "$@"; fi
set -euo pipefail
[ -f /etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env ] || { echo "FATAL: bootstrap.env missing"; exit 1; }
. /etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env
# Same fail-closed guard as the reconcile script. Repeated HERE deliberately:
# this payload must refuse BEFORE it fetches and runs anything, so a box with a
# missing/garbled bootstrap.env never even reaches the script. Never default
# ENVIRONMENT to prod -- that renders dev config into prod's log groups and
# metric namespace.
: "${VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT:?FATAL: VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT unset -- refusing to reconcile}"
[ "$VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT" = "dev" ] || {
  echo "FATAL: VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT='$VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT', expected 'dev'"; exit 1; }
REGION="${VELOCITYAI_REGION:-eu-central-1}"
: "${VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET:?VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET missing}"
sha256sum /etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai || true
aws s3 cp "s3://${VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET}/config/reconcile-host-config.sh" \
    /opt/velocityai/reconcile-host-config.sh --region "$REGION"
chmod 0755 /opt/velocityai/reconcile-host-config.sh
bash /opt/velocityai/reconcile-host-config.sh
sha256sum /etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai
systemctl is-active nginx
SCRIPT

jq -Rs '{commands: [.]}' /tmp/reconcile.sh > /tmp/ssm-params.json

CMD_ID=$(aws ssm send-command \
  --instance-ids "$DEV" \
  --document-name AWS-RunShellScript \
  --comment "velocityai dev host-config reconcile" \
  --timeout-seconds 600 \
  --parameters file:///tmp/ssm-params.json \
  --region "$REGION" \
  --query Command.CommandId --output text)
echo "SSM command: $CMD_ID"

while true; do
  STATUS=$(aws ssm get-command-invocation --command-id "$CMD_ID" --instance-id "$DEV" \
            --region "$REGION" --query Status --output text 2>/dev/null || echo Pending)
  case "$STATUS" in
    Success) aws ssm get-command-invocation --command-id "$CMD_ID" --instance-id "$DEV" \
               --region "$REGION" --query StandardOutputContent --output text; break ;;
    Failed|Cancelled|TimedOut)
      aws ssm get-command-invocation --command-id "$CMD_ID" --instance-id "$DEV" \
        --region "$REGION" --query StandardErrorContent --output text; exit 1 ;;
    *) sleep 5 ;;
  esac
done
```

**Which half is durable and which evaporates.** Steps 1-4 are durable (repo + S3 + pipeline). Step 5
is a one-shot operational action; it leaves no artefact except the backup directory and the applied
config. If the instance is replaced, steps 1-4 reproduce everything and step 5 is unnecessary.

##### I6. Ripple-effect analysis -- assume this is wrong, and hunt

**Assumption under attack: "the extraction is faithful."** It is the single point of failure. If a
byte of the nginx site changes, `nginx -t` may still pass while behaviour shifts (a dropped
`include`, a lost `\$` escape). Mitigations, in order of strength: (a) the executor cuts the bodies
with `sed`, never by hand (step 1b); (b) the acceptance gate is a **sha256 comparison of the
rendered output before and after**, not a visual diff (I8 T1); (c) the live box's current hash is
already known and independently reproduced (`5f090af1...4083d`), so the post-reconcile hash on the
box must equal it exactly.

**`nginx -t` passes but the reload breaks live traffic.** Not possible for a config error --
`nginx -t` parses the same files the master would load. It *is* possible for a *semantic* error
(e.g. a location that matches too broadly). But C1 alone changes no semantics; the sha256 gate
catches any accidental change. When A1/D3/E1 add semantics, each brings its own probe (A1's
probe pair, D3's header count, E1's `aws logs test-metric-filter`).

**Reload during an in-flight SSE stream.** `systemctl reload nginx` sends `SIGHUP`: the master forks
new workers with the new config and asks old workers to **finish their current connections** before
exiting (graceful shutdown). An open `/api/runs/{id}/events/stream` connection is served to
completion by its old worker. It does *not* drop. There is a bounded window in which two worker
generations coexist -- irrelevant here since C1 changes nothing. Note `worker_shutdown_timeout`
defaults to 4 hours on nginx and is not set in this config, so even a multi-hour run's stream
survives.

**The agent restart drops in-flight log lines.** `fetch-config -s` ends in `systemctl restart`. The
agent restarts and resumes tailing from its stored file position (`/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/logs/state`).
Today the agent is dead anyway (B1), so there is nothing to drop. After B1 lands, a restart per
deploy is a sub-second gap and the file positions are persisted -- no loss. Worth stating because
"we restart the log shipper on every deploy" sounds alarming and is not.

**Concurrency: two deploys at once.** `buildspec.yml` has no concurrency control on the SSM step;
two overlapping dev builds could both `aws s3 cp` and both run the reconcile. Every operation is a
truncating write followed by `nginx -t` + reload -- the outcome is the same file either way, and the
worst case is two reloads. Not a corruption risk. The `fix/infra-uki` deploy.yml does add
`concurrency` on the `deploy` job (its comment at lines 58-65), which is strictly better.

**Interleaving with the app restart.** In buildspec I place the reconcile *before* ECR login and
`docker compose up -d`. So the order is: host config -> containers. If reconcile fails, the
containers are untouched and the previously-deployed image keeps serving behind the previous nginx
config -- a clean, fully-consistent abort. If I had put it after, a green build could ship a broken
proxy. In `deploy.yml` I place it before `systemctl restart velocityai-app.service` for the same
reason.

**Partial application.** The script is a linear sequence of truncating writes. If it dies midway
(SSM timeout, instance reboot), the possible states are: nginx files written but not validated
(previous config still running -- nginx has not been reloaded); or nginx done and the agent
half-done (agent config written, `fetch-config` not run -- the agent keeps its previous config).
Neither state is corrupt, and re-running the script converges. `restore_and_die` covers the one
state that matters (invalid nginx template).

**Crashed run / restart / resume / fan-out / revision / two browsers.** None of these touch host
config. The only interaction is the nginx reload, addressed above. Specifically: a run parked at a
human review gate holds an SSE connection open on the *old* worker across the reload and is
unaffected; `restore_non_terminal_runs` is a backend-process concern and no container is restarted
by the reconcile.

**Memory / connection pool.** No process is added. The agent's own memory is unchanged (same
config). nginx briefly runs two worker generations during a graceful reload; `worker_processes auto`
on a 4-vCPU box means a few extra processes for the duration of the longest in-flight request.

**The bootstrap script gets longer to reason about, not shorter.** It loses 305 lines and gains ~35.
`bash -n` must still pass (I8 T0). The removed §14 was *after* §13 and *before* §15; nothing between
them reads a variable set by them, so removing both leaves no dangling reference. I checked: the
only downstream reference to anything §13/§14 sets is
`bootstrap-ec2.sh:1271` (a log line naming `/opt/velocityai/docker-compose.yml`) -- unrelated.

**The `set -euo pipefail` interaction.** `bootstrap-ec2.sh:27` sets it. The new
`bash /opt/velocityai/reconcile-host-config.sh` is a plain command; a non-zero exit aborts bootstrap.
That is intended (fail-closed) but it means a transient S3 failure on first boot now aborts
provisioning, where previously §13 would have run from the inline body. Mitigation: the firstboot
wrapper already retries the S3 fetch 30x for `bootstrap-ec2.sh` (`user_data.sh.tpl:85-92`); this
`aws s3 cp` has no retry. **Add one** -- the executor should wrap step 2's `aws s3 cp` in the same
`for i in $(seq 1 30)` loop the wrapper uses. I call this out rather than leaving it: it is the one
new failure mode the change introduces.

**The worst plausible failure of this change, and why it is now impossible.** The reconcile script
renders **environment-scoped identifiers** into two places:

```
bootstrap-ec2.sh:970   "namespace": "VelocityAI/${ENV_TITLE}",
bootstrap-ec2.sh:988-995  "log_group_name": "/velocityai/${ENVIRONMENT}/{nginx-access|nginx-error|
                          postgres|system|auth|system|letsencrypt|app}"
```

I measured the full variable surface of the extracted range:

```bash
$ awk 'NR>=703 && NR<=1007' infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh \
    | grep -oE '\$\{?(DOMAIN|ENVIRONMENT|ENV_TITLE|REGION|PARAM_PREFIX|ACME_EMAIL|BACKUP_BUCKET|APP_USER|IMAGE_TAG)\}?' \
    | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
   9 ${ENVIRONMENT}      # 8 real (log_group_name x8) + 1 in a comment at :955
   8 ${DOMAIN}
   4 $DOMAIN
   2 ${ENV_TITLE}        # 1 real (:970 namespace) + 1 in the same comment
   1 $ACME_EMAIL         # :932 -- inside the cert block, which STAYS in bootstrap
```

So the extraction depends on exactly **three** values: `DOMAIN`, `ENVIRONMENT`, and `ENV_TITLE`
(derived from `ENVIRONMENT`). `REGION`, `PARAM_PREFIX`, `BACKUP_BUCKET`, `APP_USER` and `IMAGE_TAG`
are **not** referenced anywhere in §13/§14. [V]

`bootstrap-ec2.sh:79` reads `ENVIRONMENT="${VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT:-prod}"` -- a **silent default to
prod**. Carrying that default into a script that (a) runs on every deploy and (b) renders prod's
log-group names and prod's metric namespace would mean: one box with a missing or truncated
`/etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env` starts shipping **dev's nginx access log, auth log, audit log and
container stdout into `/velocityai/prod/*`**, and **dev's CPU/memory/disk metrics into
`VelocityAI/Prod`**. There is no error, no alarm, and no un-publish -- CloudWatch Logs has no
delete-by-content and the prod alarms would then be evaluating a mixture of two hosts. It would also
be *invisible*: `[reconcile] complete`, exit 0.

This is a plausible failure on **this** box, not a theoretical one. Dev's
`/var/lib/velocityai/.bootstrap-done` does not exist (dossier `[V]`), so nothing attests that the
full bootstrap ever ran there, and dev's userData is the pre-firstboot 64-line template -- the one
piece of state the reconcile trusts has an unusual provenance.

Three independent guards now make it impossible:
1. **The script refuses to start** on an unset `VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT` (`:?` not `:-`) and on any
   value outside `dev|stage|prod` (step 1). Fail-closed beats a wrong default: the cost of the
   guard is a re-run, the cost of the default is prod's data integrity.
2. **The SSM payload refuses to fetch** unless `VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT = dev` (step 5b) -- so a
   mis-typed instance id that somehow passed the `Name`-tag check still cannot reconcile.
3. **The operator sees the value before anything runs** (step 5a pre-flight), including the
   *current* on-box agent config, which already reads `VelocityAI/Dev`.

The script also echoes its resolved environment on every run
(`[reconcile] environment=dev -> log groups /velocityai/dev/*, namespace VelocityAI/Dev`), so the
SSM output and the CodeBuild log both carry the proof.

**Nested-script contexts are preserved -- verified, not assumed.** `bootstrap-ec2.sh` emits 15
nested files, six of which are shell scripts carrying their **own** `set -euo pipefail`:

```bash
$ grep -n "set -euo pipefail" infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh
27:   set -euo pipefail          # top level
608:  set -euo pipefail          # inside velocityai-load-secrets      (emitted at :606)
1021: set -euo pipefail          # inside velocityai-update-image-tag  (emitted at :1017)
1064: set -euo pipefail          # inside velocityai-pg-dump           (emitted at :1062)
1082: set -euo pipefail          # inside velocityai-skills-backup     (emitted at :1080)
1097: set -euo pipefail          # inside velocityai-stuck-workflows   (emitted at :1094)

$ awk 'NR>=703 && NR<=1007 && /set -euo pipefail/ {print NR}' infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh
(no output)
```

**Zero occurrences inside 703-1007.** Every command in §13 and §14 therefore executes in the
*top-level* `:27` context -- none of it lives inside an emitted script, and none of it is a nested
expansion. The extraction is context-preserving by construction: moving that body into a standalone
file whose own first lines are `set -euo pipefail` reproduces the same `-e`/`-u`/`pipefail`
semantics, and the caller (`bash /opt/velocityai/reconcile-host-config.sh` under bootstrap's own
`set -e`) propagates a non-zero exit exactly as an inline command would have.

The one semantic difference the executor must hold in mind: **`-u` now bites earlier and harder.**
Inside bootstrap, `DOMAIN`/`ENVIRONMENT` were already bound at `:77`/`:79` before §13 ran; in the
standalone script they are bound at the top from `bootstrap.env`, and I have deliberately made two
of them `:?`-fatal. That is the intended behaviour change, and it is the only one.

**Where the dossier already argues safety, verified rather than restated:**
- *"`nginx -t` gating means downtime on a failed validation is zero."* Verified: `nginx -t` runs a
  throwaway process; the running master's in-memory config is only replaced on a successful reload.
  True.
- *"The file-level backup is the only restore point."* Verified structurally: root volume
  `delete_on_termination = true` (`compute/main.tf:121`) and outside the AWS Backup tag selection
  (I4.9). True.

##### I7. Architecture and invariant compliance

Walked item by item against the brief's §3.

| Invariant | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **SC-001** (a new workflow replicates `prototype` by manifest + AGENT.md, zero engine edits) | **Not engaged.** Zero files under `backend/agents/` or `backend/app/`. The kernel is not read, written, imported or configured by this change. |
| **INV-3 / INV-12** (no dual implementation; deleting the superseded code is part of the change) | **The central constraint here, and satisfied by construction.** Exactly one copy of the reconcile logic exists: `infra/scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh`. Bootstrap, CI and the operator all *invoke* it. §13/§14 bodies are **deleted** from `bootstrap-ec2.sh` in the same commit (explicit delete list in I5, with three grep gates). The one-shot (step 5) carries no logic. I explicitly rejected the inline-base64 delivery (I5 option b) precisely because it would create a second shape of the same script. |
| **INV-13** (`deepagents` only) | Not engaged -- no Python touched, no agent loop, no `create_deep_agent`. |
| **Hexagonal boundary / import-linter** | Not engaged. No Python import moves. `lint-imports` is unchanged: the pre-existing single broken contract (`agents.capabilities.strategies.task_loop -> agents.execution_engine.od_context -> app.services.od_loader`) stays the bar, and this change cannot add a second. |
| **Q3 -- additive migrations only, every new table carries `owner_id` + `workspace_id`** | **Zero migrations.** `git diff --stat -- backend/alembic` must be empty. No table. |
| **Backward compatibility (`prototype` / `od_*` / PPT / code-gen byte-identical, characterization-proven)** | Untouched by construction. No engine, no event, no deliverable, no prompt. The goldens' known-red baseline (10 failed / 6 passed) is unaffected and this change must not be gated on it. |
| **Security defaults (`exec` / `network` / `secrets` / `spawn_subagents` OFF)** | Unchanged -- no capability, no manifest, no compiler trust flag. |
| **LOCK-B** (`websocket.py` unmodifiable during the SSE cutover) | **Superseded, verified.** `backend/app/api/websocket.py` was **deleted in full** by Phase 44 plan 44-07 (IMPL `:3683`: "DELETED (44-07, whole file, 2316 lines)"), and the CI banned-pattern ratchet `backend/tests/agents/test_sse_cutover_banned_patterns.py` now forbids `/ws/chat`, `useWebSocket`, `routeWebSocket`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_TRANSPORT`, `SSE_TRANSPORT_ENABLED` (IMPL `:3693`, `:3696`). LOCK-B's *additive-only* clause no longer binds; its *successor* rule does -- **do not reintroduce any WS run frame**. My change touches no transport at all, and I deliberately do **not** delete the now-dead `location /ws/chat` nginx block (`bootstrap-ec2.sh:843-856`) even though it is dead config: removing it would be a semantic change riding a mechanism-only commit, and `/ws/handoff/` (`:862-875`) is a live survivor sitting three lines away. |
| **Scope fence: dev only; do not touch `infra/terraform/shared/`** | Honoured. Files touched: `infra/scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh` (new), `infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh`, `infra/terraform/app/main.tf`, `infra/buildspec.yml`. `infra/terraform/shared/` untouched -- important, because `buildspec.yml:143-150` runs `$TF/shared apply` on **every** build and it is a no-op only while that directory is unchanged. The one-shot targets `--instance-ids i-092d5961f5aca87a6` only. |

**One honest caveat on the dev-only fence.** `infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh` and
`infra/terraform/app/main.tf` are shared *sources* across environments. Committing this to `dev`
changes the source that stage and prod will also use **when their own pipelines next run**. It does
not change stage or prod now (their CodeBuild projects are triggered by pushes to their own
branches, `buildspec.yml:6-10`), and the change is behaviour-preserving by construction (the sha256
gate). But an executor must not describe this as "dev-only files" -- it is "dev-only *effect*, on a
shared source". That is unavoidable for any host-config fix in this repo and is the same posture
the dossier takes for E2/E3.

**There is no existing test over `infra/`.** Verified:
`grep -rln "bootstrap-ec2\|buildspec\|nginx" backend/tests frontend/e2e` returns only
`test_api_prefix_validator.py` and `test_prompt_contracts.py`, both matching on the string `nginx`
inside the `api_prefix` validator's infra-file glob -- neither reads `infra/`. So there is no suite
to keep green and no suite to extend; the gates below are new and are static + on-box.

**No baseline measurement is required for this plan.** The change touches zero Python and zero
TypeScript, so the known-red backend goldens (10 failed / 6 passed) and the 1 broken import contract
are unaffected *by construction*, not by measurement. I did not re-run them; re-running them would
prove nothing about an infra-only diff. I did run the one gate that is genuinely relevant:

```
$ bash -n infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh
$ echo $?
0
```

**T-pre -- environment-identity gate (ON-BOX, read-only, blocks everything else).** The full
pre-flight is I5 step 5a. Its four assertions are the gate:
`VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT=dev` (not `<UNSET>`, not `prod`), `VELOCITYAI_FQDN=63-181-129-187.nip.io`,
`VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET=velocityai-dev-pg-dumps-577954642302`, and the existing on-box agent
config already reading `"namespace": "VelocityAI/Dev"` + `/velocityai/dev/nginx-access`.
*Fail-before is real and testable offline:* run the reconcile script locally with
`VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT` unset and it must exit non-zero with
`FATAL: VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT unset ... refusing to default to prod`, **not** render
`VelocityAI/Prod`:
```bash
env -u VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT VELOCITYAI_FQDN=x bash -c \
  'set -euo pipefail; ENVIRONMENT="${VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT:?FATAL}"; echo "$ENVIRONMENT"'
# expect: exit 1, "VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT: FATAL"
```
This is the one test whose *failure mode* is unrecoverable (published CloudWatch data cannot be
withdrawn), so it runs first and blocks T5/T6.

**T0 -- syntax (offline, both files).**
```bash
bash -n infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh
bash -n infra/scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh
```
*Fail-before:* n/a (the new file does not exist). *Pass-after:* both exit 0.
This is the gate that a heredoc-in-bootstrap design would have lost (I5 option c).

**T1 -- extraction fidelity (offline, THE acceptance gate).** Render the site from both the
pre-change and post-change sources and compare hashes.

```bash
# BEFORE (from git, so it works after the edit is applied)
git show HEAD:infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh > /tmp/boot-before.sh
DOMAIN='63-181-129-187.nip.io' bash -c \
  '{ echo "cat <<EOF"; sed -n "732,915p" /tmp/boot-before.sh; } | bash' > /tmp/site-before

# AFTER (from the new reconcile script; adjust the range to its own heredoc)
RECON_START=$(grep -n 'cat > /etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai <<EOF' \
                infra/scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh | cut -d: -f1)
RECON_END=$(awk -v s="$RECON_START" 'NR>s && /^EOF$/ {print NR; exit}' \
                infra/scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh)
DOMAIN='63-181-129-187.nip.io' bash -c \
  "{ echo 'cat <<EOF'; sed -n \"$((RECON_START+1)),${RECON_END}p\" \
     infra/scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh; } | bash" > /tmp/site-after

diff /tmp/site-before /tmp/site-after && echo "SITE IDENTICAL"
shasum -a 256 /tmp/site-before /tmp/site-after
```
*Expected:* `SITE IDENTICAL`, and both hashes equal
`5f090af17801bcf6d11c7964f3fe80cc58bbe4ed5bb4a031d365875bc474083d`.
*Fail-before is predictable and meaningful:* if the executor retypes rather than `sed`-cuts a body,
this diff is non-empty. I have already run the "before" side of this today and it produced exactly
that hash, so the expected value is measured, not guessed.

Repeat the same before/after render for the agent JSON (`ENVIRONMENT=dev ENV_TITLE=Dev`, ranges
`963,1001` vs the reconcile script's own), and a plain `diff` for the two quoted heredocs
(`sed -n '707,715p'` and `sed -n '719,726p'` vs the new file).

**T2 -- deletion gates (offline).**

```bash
grep -c 'amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json <<EOF' infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh   # 0

grep -c 'reconcile-host-config.sh'           infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh   # 1
grep -c 'reconcile-host-config.sh'           infra/buildspec.yml              # 1
grep -c 'reconcile_script'                   infra/terraform/app/main.tf      # 3  (resource, source, source_hash) + depends_on
```
*Fail-before:* the first three are 1, 1, 1 today. *Pass-after:* 0, 0, 0. This is the INV-12 proof.

**T3 -- Terraform gates (offline; mirrors the CI pre_build).**
```bash
terraform fmt -check -recursive infra/terraform
terraform -chdir=infra/terraform/app init -backend=false -no-color
terraform -chdir=infra/terraform/app validate -no-color
```
*Fail-before:* `validate` errors if the new resource references a file that does not exist --
`filemd5` on a missing path is a **plan-time** error, so this catches a forgotten `git add`.
*Pass-after:* both exit 0.

**T4 -- gitleaks (offline; the only whole-repo CI gate that sees the new file).**
```bash
gitleaks detect --no-git --redact --no-banner -v --config .gitleaks.toml --source .
```
*Expected:* exit 0. The reconcile script contains no secret-shaped literals (paths, nginx
directives, JSON keys). Running this locally is worth the 20s -- a gitleaks trip fails the whole
dev build at `pre_build`, before anything is deployed.

**T5 -- on-box no-op proof (the live gate; run as part of step 5).** The one-shot payload already
prints `sha256sum /etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai` before and after.
*Expected:* **the two hashes are identical**, and both equal `5f090af1...4083d`.
*Interpretation:* C1 has replaced the delivery mechanism and changed nothing else. That is the whole
claim, tested directly.
Then:
```bash
systemctl is-active nginx                     # active
nginx -t                                      # syntax is ok / test is successful
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://63-181-129-187.nip.io/login   # 200
```

**T6 -- durable-half proof (post-push).**
```bash
aws s3api head-object --bucket velocityai-dev-pg-dumps-577954642302 \
  --key config/reconcile-host-config.sh \
  --query '{LastModified:LastModified,ContentLength:ContentLength}'
aws s3api head-object --bucket velocityai-dev-pg-dumps-577954642302 \
  --key config/bootstrap-ec2.sh \
  --query '{LastModified:LastModified,ContentLength:ContentLength}'
```
*Expected:* both `LastModified` within minutes of the build, and `bootstrap-ec2.sh`'s
`ContentLength` **smaller** than before (it lost ~270 net lines). A stale `LastModified` on
`bootstrap-ec2.sh` would mean `filemd5` did not fire -- i.e. the app apply did not run -- and is the
one silent failure mode of the durable half.

**T7 -- the mechanism actually re-runs (the C1 acceptance criterion, one deploy later).** Push a
one-character, semantically-null change to the reconcile script (e.g. a comment). Confirm the next
dev build's SSM output contains `[reconcile] ... start` and `[reconcile] ... complete`, and that
`aws s3api head-object` shows a fresh `LastModified`.
*Fail-before:* today, a change to `bootstrap-ec2.sh` produces **no** on-box effect -- that is the
bug. *Pass-after:* the change reaches the box automatically. This is the only test that proves C1
rather than proving the extraction.

**No golden/characterization snapshot changes**, because no engine byte or event can move. If any
golden diff appears, the change has escaped its blast radius and must be reverted.

##### I9. Rollback

**What is NOT reversible.** There are no EBS snapshots of the root volume, in any environment, ever
(`delete_on_termination = true`, `compute/main.tf:121`; the volume is outside the `Backup = "true"`
selection, `modules/backups/main.tf:278-295` vs `compute/main.tf:123-126`). So there is **no
filesystem-level rollback for any host change.** The file-level backup the reconcile script writes
is the only restore point that exists.

**What the pre-change backup must capture** (this is what `restore_and_die` in step 1 backs up, and
it is exactly the set of paths the script writes):

| Path | Why |
|---|---|
| `/etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai` | the site |
| `/etc/nginx/conf.d/velocityai-limits.conf` | zones + `log_format` |
| `/etc/nginx/snippets/velocityai-proxy-headers.conf` | the `include`d snippet |
| `/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json` | agent config |
| `getfacl -pR /var/lib/docker/containers` | the ACL state B2 will change |
| `id cwagent` | the group membership B2 will change |

Backups go to `/root/host-config-backup-<UTC-timestamp>/`, mode 0700, one directory per run, never
overwritten. Sizing: the four files total ~14 KB; the ACL dump grows with container count but is
kilobytes. Root is 32% used (dossier `[V]`), so unbounded accumulation is not a near-term risk, but
the executor should note that nothing prunes them.

**Rollback by change class:**

| Change | Reverse | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **Repo (steps 1-4)** | `git revert <sha>` on `dev`, push | one build; the app layer re-uploads the old `bootstrap-ec2.sh` and *leaves* `config/reconcile-host-config.sh` behind as an orphan (Terraform destroys the object because the resource is gone -- verify with `head-object` -> 404). The reverted buildspec no longer calls it. |
| **nginx config on the box** | `cp -a /root/host-config-backup-<ts>/velocityai /etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai && nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx` | seconds, zero downtime |
| **limits / proxy-headers** | same `cp -a` + `nginx -t` + reload | seconds |
| **agent config** | `cp -a .../amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json /opt/aws/.../etc/ && amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl -a fetch-config -m ec2 -s -c file:...` | seconds |
| **ACL / group changes (B2's payload, not C1's)** | `setfacl --restore=/root/host-config-backup-<ts>/docker-containers.acl`; `gpasswd -d cwagent adm` | seconds. **`--restore` is the only reliable inverse** -- there is no "undo" for a mask recomputation. |
| **A failed `nginx -t`** | nothing to roll back -- the reload never happened, the running config is untouched, and `restore_and_die` puts the files back too | zero |
| **The instance itself** | **NO ROLLBACK.** Root volume is `delete_on_termination`, unsnapshotted. If the box is destroyed, Postgres data survives only on the separate data EBS (`prevent_destroy = true`) and would have to be re-attached by hand (`compute/main.tf:106-110` says exactly this). | catastrophic; never touch `disable_api_termination` |

**One rollback trap.** If step 5 is run and *then* the repo change is reverted, the box keeps the
reconciled config (identical to before, by T5) but the pipeline stops re-applying it. That is the
pre-C1 state -- safe. The reverse order (revert first, then run the one-shot) would fetch a
404 for the S3 object and fail loudly. Either way, no half state.

##### I10. Sequencing and dependencies

**C1 must land FIRST.** A1, B1, B2, B3, B4 and B5 all edit host configuration that only C1 can
deliver. Landing any of them before C1 produces a repo change with no on-box effect -- and a false
sense of completion, which is exactly the failure the dossier documents for the last month.

**Which siblings ride this mechanism, and where each lands:**

| Issue | Rides C1? | Exact seam in `infra/scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh` |
|---|---|---|
| **A1** SSE `limit_conn` exemption | **yes** | two edits: `limit_conn_zone velocityai_stream:10m;` appended to the limits heredoc (was `bootstrap-ec2.sh:706-716`); the `location ~ ^/api/runs/[^/]+/events/stream/?$` block inserted into the site heredoc immediately before `location /api/ {` (was `:822`) |
| **B1** agent crash-loop | **yes** | `install -o cwagent -g cwagent -m 0644 /dev/null /var/log/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log` before the `fetch-config` call; plus the new `collect_list` entry (see B4) |
| **B2** `cwagent` cannot read the logs | **yes** | `usermod -a -G adm cwagent` + the two `setfacl` lines rewritten with an explicit `m::rx`; note `systemctl restart amazon-cloudwatch-agent` is already implied by `fetch-config -s`, so B2 needs no separate restart |
| **B3** two files, one stream | **yes** | `log_stream_name` on the `audit.log` and `unattended-upgrades.log` entries in the agent JSON |
| **B4** agent's own log not collected | **yes** | one more `collect_list` entry; **ordered after B1**, which creates the file |
| **B5** `fetch-config` exit status unchecked | **yes** | the assertion block goes immediately after the `fetch-config` call. **This is the same region C1 creates**, so B5 is a direct edit to my new file -- see the conflict note below |
| **D3** `/_next/static/` security headers | **yes** | the `location /_next/static/` block inside the site heredoc |
| **E1** nginx JSON log format | **yes for the nginx half** | `log_format velocityai escape=json ...` in the limits heredoc. **But E1's metric filters live in `modules/monitoring/main.tf:469`** and are applied by `$TF/app apply`, not by the reconcile. E1 is therefore a *split* change and both halves must land in the same commit or the filters break. |
| **E2** `PgDumpHeartbeat` has no publisher | **NO** | `velocityai-pg-dump` is `bootstrap-ec2.sh:1062-1078`, in **§16** -- outside the extracted range |
| **E3** stuck-workflows hardcodes `VelocityAI/Prod` | **NO** | `velocityai-stuck-workflows-check` is `bootstrap-ec2.sh:1094-1111`, also **§16** |
| **E4** `logs:DescribeLogGroups` resource-scoped | **NO** | `policies/cloudwatch-write.json` -- pure Terraform, applied by the pipeline |
| **B6** SNS subscription unconfirmed | **NO** | Terraform + a human clicking a link |
| **A2-A5, D1-D2, D4-D11** | **NO** | application code; ship on the normal container deploy |

**The E2/E3 gap is a real finding the dossier does not state.** Both fixes edit §16, which my
extraction does not cover. Three options:
1. **Widen the reconcile scope to §16** -- the three emitted scripts (`velocityai-pg-dump`,
   `velocityai-skills-backup`, `velocityai-stuck-workflows-check`) are pure `cat >` + `chmod`, fully
   idempotent, and would fit. But §16 also has systemd timer wiring in §17 that is not obviously
   safe to re-run on every deploy.
2. **Ship E2/E3 as their own one-shot SSM** (the same three-line fetch-and-run pattern, different
   payload).
3. **Leave them for the next rebuild.**

My recommendation: **(1), as a follow-up commit after C1 lands and is proven**, scoped to the three
`cat >`+`chmod` script emissions only, not the systemd units. Do not widen the scope in the C1
commit -- that would break the "provable no-op" acceptance gate.

**Conflict on the same lines.** C1, A1, B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, D3 and E1 all edit the *same new file*.
That is the intended outcome (one file, one place) but it means:
- they cannot be parallel-executed;
- each must rebase on the last;
- the T1 sha256 gate is C1's alone -- once A1 lands, the hash legitimately changes and each
  subsequent issue owns its own probe.

**Commit boundaries.** Four commits, in order:

1. `infra: extract host config into reconcile-host-config.sh (no behaviour change)` --
   the new file + the `bootstrap-ec2.sh` edit. Gated on T0, T1, T2.
2. `infra: upload reconcile-host-config.sh from the app layer` --
   `app/main.tf`. Gated on T3.
3. `infra: run the host-config reconcile on every deploy` --
   `buildspec.yml`. Gated on T4.
4. *(operational, no commit)* the one-shot SSM. Gated on T5, T6.

Splitting 1 from 2/3 matters: commit 1 is the reviewable one (a 305-line move), and if commit 1's
diff is anything other than a move plus ~35 lines of glue, the review should stop.

**Explicit orderings the dossier asserts, verified:**
- *"Fix B1 and B2 first, then subscribe [B6]"* -- correct, and both now depend on C1, so the real
  chain is **C1 -> B1 -> B2 -> B4 -> B3 -> B5 -> B6**. (B4 after B1 because B4 collects the file B1
  creates; B5 last in the agent group because it asserts the end state.)
- *"A2 cannot be live-tested before A1"* -- correct, and A1 cannot reach the box before C1. So the
  full A-cluster live proof is gated on C1.
- *"C1's later half is one line in the pipeline"* -- **corrected**: it is a three-line fetch-and-run,
  because there is no repo on the box (I4.5).

##### I11. Open questions requiring a human decision

**Q1. Does the reconcile run on every deploy, or only when the script changes?**
Every deploy (my recommendation, and what step 4 implements). *Options:* (a) unconditional -- ~2s
per deploy, self-healing against manual drift, and the failure mode is loud; (b) conditional on an
S3 ETag/hash compare -- saves ~2s, but adds state to reason about and lets manual drift persist
silently. **Recommend (a).** The `chown` precedent at `buildspec.yml:291` is unconditional for the
same reason.

**Q2. Fail-closed or fail-open when the reconcile fails?**
Fail-closed (my recommendation, and what step 1's contract implements). *Options:* (a) fail-closed --
a bad nginx template or a dead agent aborts the deploy; the app keeps running the previous
image behind the previous, still-valid config, so downtime is zero, but an unrelated app deploy is
blocked by a config bug; (b) fail-open with a warning -- app deploys never blocked, but a broken
proxy or a dead log shipper ships green, which is precisely the B1/B5 failure this whole cluster
exists to end. **Recommend (a).** This is genuinely a product/ops judgement, not a technical one,
which is why it is here.

**Q3. Should the now-dead `location /ws/chat` block be removed while the file is open?**
It is dead config -- Phase 44 deleted `/ws/chat` from the backend (IMPL `:3683`) and the CI ratchet
`test_sse_cutover_banned_patterns.py` bans the token in `backend/app`, `backend/agents` and
`frontend/src` -- but `infra/` is **not** in that ratchet's scan set, so nothing forces it.
*Options:* (a) leave it -- C1 stays a provable no-op (my strong preference for this commit);
(b) remove it in a follow-up, alongside A1, with its own probe. **Recommend (a) now, (b) later.**
Note the block sits three lines from the live `/ws/handoff/` survivor, so this is a
read-carefully edit, not a delete-the-block edit.

**Q4. Who owns the backup directories under `/root/`?**
Nothing prunes `/root/host-config-backup-*`. At one per deploy and ~14 KB each this is negligible
for a year, but it is unbounded. *Options:* (a) accept; (b) keep the last N in the script;
(c) a `tmpfiles.d` rule. **Recommend (a)** and revisit if root usage moves off 32%.
