### D3 — `/_next/static/` returns none of the five security headers

**Confidence:** [V] — measured live against dev.

**Symptom.**
```
/login                                 -> 5 of 5 security headers
/_next/static/chunks/...css            -> 0 of 5
```
HSTS, CSP, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options` and `Referrer-Policy` are all absent on every
static asset.

**Root cause.** nginx inherits `add_header` directives from an outer level **if and only if** no
`add_header` is defined at the current level. `location /_next/static/`
(`bootstrap-ec2.sh:908-913`) defines its own `add_header Cache-Control ...`, which discards all five
server-level headers declared at `:791-799`.

**Why it occurred.** This is one of nginx's genuinely counter-intuitive rules — `add_header` is
replace-not-merge across levels. The location was added to set a long immutable cache lifetime for
hashed assets, a correct and unrelated goal, and the side effect is invisible unless you specifically
curl that path and compare.

**The fix.** Either re-declare the five headers inside the static location, or better, add `always`
and move the shared set into a snippet included by both — a single source, so a future location
cannot silently drop them again. Note `proxy_cache_valid 200 1y` in that block is also a no-op
without a `proxy_cache` zone; worth removing or wiring while in the file.

**Verification.** The measurement above, expecting 5 and 5.

#### Fully-Detailed Investigation

> **Investigated** 2026-07-30 | **Verdict on the dossier's proposed fix:**
> CONFIRMED-WITH-CORRECTIONS | **Registers read to EOF:** FIX-REGISTER.md (3,705 lines) and
> IMPLEMENTATION-REGISTER.md (4,178 lines) | **Anchor drift found:** 0 of 4 anchors moved (one is
> imprecise rather than wrong).

The dossier's diagnosis is exactly right and the mechanism is now measured, not asserted. Three
material additions: (1) the `add_header Cache-Control` that causes the bug is **redundant** — the
Next.js upstream already emits the byte-identical value, and the live response carries
`Cache-Control` **twice** today; so the correct fix is to **delete** the directive, not to
re-declare the five headers beside it; (2) the loss is not limited to 200s — it also drops on 304
and on 404; (3) A1's proposed block is safe **as written** but one tempting extra line
(`add_header X-Accel-Buffering no;`) would silently reproduce D3 on the SSE stream.

##### I3. Root cause — confirmed, corrected, or replaced

**The dossier's mechanism is correct.** nginx's `add_header` is inherited from an outer configuration
level **if and only if** no `add_header` is declared at the current level — replace, not merge.
`location /_next/static/` declares `add_header Cache-Control` at `:912`, which discards all five
server-level `add_header` directives from `:791/792/797/798/799`.

I did not take that on faith. **Reproduced on nginx 1.24.0** — the exact version on the dev box —
in a throwaway container (`nginx:1.24-alpine`, already cached locally), with a fake Next.js upstream
that sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and `X-Powered-By: Next.js` just as
the real one does. Full matrix [V]:

| Location shape | Status | security headers | `Cache-Control` count |
|---|---|---|---|
| no `add_header` (models `location /`) | 200 | **5 / 5** | 1 |
| `add_header Cache-Control` (models `/_next/static/` verbatim) | 200 | **0 / 5** | **2** |
| same, upstream 404 | 404 | **0 / 5** | 1 (only the upstream's) |
| same, 304 via `If-None-Match` | 304 | **0 / 5** | **2** |
| `add_header` deleted | 200 | **5 / 5** | 1 |
| `add_header` deleted, upstream 404 | 404 | **5 / 5** | - |
| `add_header` deleted, 304 | 304 | **5 / 5** | 1 |
| `add_header` kept **plus** `include` of a security-header snippet | 200 | **5 / 5** | **2** |
| server-level `return 404` (models `location = /docs`) | 404 | **5 / 5** | - |
| **regex** location, no `add_header` (models A1) | 200 | **5 / 5** | 1 |
| **regex** location, with `add_header X-Accel-Buffering` | 200 | **0 / 5** | 1 |
| server-level directives replaced by an `include` of a snippet | 200 | **5 / 5** | 1 |

And re-measured **live against dev** (2026-07-29 22:22-22:30Z) [V]:

| Path | Status | security headers | `Cache-Control` count |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | 307 | **5 / 5** | 1 |
| `/login` | 200 | **5 / 5** | 1 |
| `/_next/image?url=...` | 400 | **5 / 5** | 0 |
| `/hexaware-logo.png` (public asset, via `location /`) | 200 | **5 / 5** | 1 |
| `/_next/static/chunks/turbopack-0t4ed0dgspv5m.js` | 200 | **0 / 5** | **2** |
| `/_next/static/chunks/00tv7qdafdv01.css` | 200 | **0 / 5** | **2** |
| `/_next/static/chunks/__does_not_exist__.js` | 404 | **0 / 5** | 1 |

**Correction 1 (material) — the offending directive is redundant, and the live response carries a
duplicate `Cache-Control` today.** The dossier does not mention this. Next.js 16.2.4 sets the header
itself. Proof, from the installed dependency
(`frontend/node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/router-server.js:394-400`) [V]:

```js
if (!res.getHeader('cache-control') && matchedOutput.type === 'nextStaticFolder') {
    if (opts.dev && !isNextFont(parsedUrl.pathname)) {
        res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'no-cache, must-revalidate');
    } else {
        res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable');
    }
}
```

`nextStaticFolder` is everything under `/_next/static/`, and prod is not `dev`
(`frontend/next.config.ts` sets `output: "standalone"`; CodeBuild ships a production build). The
value is **byte-identical** to the nginx one. `add_header` *appends* — it never replaces an upstream
header — so today every `/_next/static/` 200 carries the header twice. That is measured live and
reproduced locally. Consequence: **deleting `:912` costs nothing** and is strictly better than the
dossier's two suggestions.

**Correction 2 — the loss is not confined to 200s.** Measured: the drop also applies to **304 Not
Modified** (the common repeat-visit path, which the browser hits for every hashed asset it already
has) and to an upstream **404**. The dossier's one-line symptom understates the reach.

**Correction 3 — `always` is not what is broken.** The location's `add_header Cache-Control` has no
`always`, so it does not even *fire* on a 404 (measured: the 404 carries exactly one
`Cache-Control`, from the upstream) — yet inheritance is still killed on that 404. Presence of an
`add_header` at the level, not whether it fires, is what disables inheritance. This kills a
plausible-looking "fix" (adding `always` to `:912`) before anyone tries it.

**Causal chain, end to end.**

1. `27483e6a` (2026-05-11) adds a security-header block at server level and, in the same commit, a
   `/_next/static/` block whose only purpose is a long immutable cache lifetime.
2. nginx's replace-not-merge rule means the second silently voids the first for that prefix.
3. The effect is invisible from the app: the page itself (`/login`) carries all five, so any
   browser-based or page-level check passes. Only a direct `curl` of an asset URL shows it.
4. It has never been observable from inside either, because nginx access logs are not shipped (B1)
   and the log format carries no response headers anyway (E1).
5. It survived `0e9c410e` and `e1a3a495` because neither author had reason to look at the other block.

**(c) Is it safe to apply these five to the actual asset types Next.js serves?** The brief asks this
explicitly because applying a header where it was previously absent is a real behaviour change.
Asset inventory taken from the live `/login` HTML [V]: 36 `.js`, 8 `.css`, 4 `.woff2` under
`/_next/static/`, plus `.js.map` on demand.

| Header | Effect on a subresource | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| `Strict-Transport-Security` | HSTS is a host-scoped policy already set by the document. Redundant on a subresource. | none |
| `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` | Governs whether a **document** may be framed. A `.js`/`.css`/`.woff2` is never a frame document, and Next serves no HTML under `/_next/static/`. | none |
| `Referrer-Policy` | Governs the referrer a **document** sends. Ignored when delivered with a subresource. | none |
| `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` | The one with a real failure mode: a stylesheet whose `Content-Type` is not `text/css`, or a script whose type is not a JS MIME, is **blocked**. Measured live: `.css -> text/css; charset=UTF-8`, `.js -> application/javascript; charset=UTF-8` [V]. Both correct. Fonts and source maps are not `script`/`style` fetch destinations, so the blocking rule does not apply to them. | none for js/css [V]; `font/woff2` correctness is [I] (see caveat) |
| `Content-Security-Policy` | **CSP is enforced against a protected resource - a Document or a Worker.** A CSP delivered with a script/style/font/image response is not enforced against the page that loaded it. The only path by which a `/_next/static/` response's own CSP becomes enforced is if it is loaded as a Worker / SharedWorker / ServiceWorker script. | none, proven absent (below) |

Worker check [V]: `grep -rn "new Worker\|SharedWorker\|serviceWorker"` over `frontend/src` returns
**zero** matches (the single hit is `new URL('./src', import.meta.url)` inside a vendored data blob
in `frontend/src/data/skills.ts`, an alias string, not a worker construction).
`frontend/public/` contains five SVGs and one PNG — **no `sw.js`, no worker bundle** [V]. Next.js 16
App Router registers no service worker of its own. So nothing consumes a `/_next/static/` script as
a worker, and the CSP is inert there. Even if one appeared, this policy's `default-src 'self'` and
`connect-src 'self' https://<domain> wss://<domain>` are what a same-origin worker would need, and
with `worker-src` absent it falls back to `script-src`, which permits `'self'`.

Specific concerns the brief named:

- **Fonts.** `font-src 'self' data:` is enforced by the **document's** CSP, which already carries
  this exact value today and already loads `/_next/static/media/*.woff2` successfully. Putting the
  same string on the font response changes nothing.
- **Source maps.** `.js.map` is fetched out-of-band by devtools and is not subject to page CSP. (The
  live probe for a `.map` returned 404, i.e. maps are not shipped in this build [V].)
- **`worker-src`.** Absent from the policy; falls back to `script-src`. Moot given no workers.
- **Inline styles in Next chunks.** `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` is already granted by the document
  CSP. A chunk's own CSP does not gate the document's style application.

nginx reproduction exactly, so the other measurements stand. The font's `Content-Type` is `[I]`.

##### I5. The complete fix

Three ordered steps. Steps 1 and 2 are the repo (durable); step 3 is the running box (evaporates on
instance replacement or a bootstrap re-run — see I9).

###### Step 1 (commit 1) — delete the redundant directive. This alone closes D3.

File: `infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh`. Anchor: the `location /_next/static/` block, currently
lines 908-913.

**BEFORE**

```nginx
    location /_next/static/ {
        proxy_pass         http://velocityai_frontend;
        include            /etc/nginx/snippets/velocityai-proxy-headers.conf;
        proxy_cache_valid  200 1y;
        add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable";
    }
```

**AFTER**

```nginx
    # Hashed, content-addressed assets. Deliberately declares NO add_header:
    # nginx's add_header is REPLACE-NOT-MERGE across levels, so a single
    # add_header here silently discards every security header inherited from
    # the server block (measured 2026-07-30: 0 of 5 on every .js/.css, on 200,
    # 304 and 404 alike). The immutable Cache-Control this block used to set is
    # already emitted by the upstream itself - Next.js
    # router-server.js sets "public, max-age=31536000, immutable" for every
    # nextStaticFolder output - so nginx was only ever duplicating it.
    # proxy_cache_valid was inert: no proxy_cache zone exists anywhere.
    # If this block ever genuinely needs an add_header, it MUST also carry
    #   include /etc/nginx/snippets/velocityai-security-headers.conf;
    location /_next/static/ {
        proxy_pass         http://velocityai_frontend;
        include            /etc/nginx/snippets/velocityai-proxy-headers.conf;
    }
```

Why delete rather than re-declare: measured, the upstream already sends the byte-identical
`Cache-Control`, so the directive adds nothing and currently produces a duplicate header. Why also
drop `proxy_cache_valid`: it is provably inert (no `proxy_cache` zone in the repo) and wiring one
would be actively harmful — see I11/I12.

###### Step 2 (commit 2) — move the five headers into a snippet. One source, no second copy.

This is a **move**, not an addition (INV-3/INV-12): the inline directives are deleted in the same
change. Proven byte-equivalent — a server-level `include` of the snippet yields the identical 5/5
[V].

**2a.** Insert a new heredoc immediately after the existing proxy-headers heredoc (after `:726`,
before the comment at `:728`):

```bash
# Response security headers, in a snippet so there is exactly ONE copy.
# nginx's add_header is REPLACE-NOT-MERGE across configuration levels: any
# location that declares its own add_header silently discards every add_header
# inherited from the server block. Keeping the set in one file means such a
# location can restore them with a single include line instead of a divergent
# copy of a 400-character CSP.
#
# NOTE the heredoc is UNQUOTED on purpose - ${DOMAIN} must expand at install
# time. There are deliberately NO nginx variables in this file; a $host or
# $scheme here would be eaten by bash. (Contrast the proxy-headers snippet
# above, which is QUOTED precisely because it is full of nginx variables.)
cat > /etc/nginx/snippets/velocityai-security-headers.conf <<EOF
add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;
add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
# SAMEORIGIN (not DENY): the prototype/ppt template + design-system galleries
# embed their own /api/.../preview endpoints in same-origin <iframe>s. DENY
# blocks all framing (incl. same-origin), which renders the previews blank.
# SAMEORIGIN keeps cross-origin clickjacking protection (CSP frame-src is 'self').
add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;
add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always;
add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com; connect-src 'self' https://\${DOMAIN} wss://\${DOMAIN}; frame-src 'self' blob:" always;
EOF
```

The `\${DOMAIN}` escaping is deliberate and load-bearing. This new heredoc is nested inside no other
heredoc, so `${DOMAIN}` would expand unescaped — which is what we want. **Verify after editing that
the rendered snippet on disk contains the literal FQDN and not the string `${DOMAIN}`**; that is the
single thing most likely to be got wrong here, and it is the exact quoted-heredoc trap E3 documents
at `:1105-1106`. (If the executor writes the heredoc without any backslash, `${DOMAIN}` expands at
`cat` time — correct. The backslash form above is for the case where this text is itself pasted
inside another expanding context; pick one and check the rendered file.)

**2b.** Replace lines `791-799` of the site heredoc:

**BEFORE**

```nginx
    add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;
    add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
    # SAMEORIGIN (not DENY): the prototype/ppt template + design-system galleries
    # embed their own /api/.../preview endpoints in same-origin <iframe>s. DENY
    # blocks all framing (incl. same-origin), which renders the previews blank.
    # SAMEORIGIN keeps cross-origin clickjacking protection (CSP frame-src is 'self').
    add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;
    add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always;
    add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com; connect-src 'self' https://${DOMAIN} wss://${DOMAIN}; frame-src 'self' blob:" always;
```

**AFTER**

```nginx
    # The five response security headers. Single source: snippets/velocityai-security-headers.conf.
    # Any location that declares its own add_header MUST re-include this file
    # or it silently ships with zero security headers (nginx add_header is
    # replace-not-merge across levels).
    include /etc/nginx/snippets/velocityai-security-headers.conf;
```

Nothing else in the site file changes.

###### Step 3 (commit 3, or fold into A1's) — the standing guard.

The snippet makes the remedy one line; it does **not** make the mistake impossible, because an
`include` is opt-in. What makes it *detectable* is an assertion. Add this to the same place A1's
apply script lives (and, per C1's "later" half, to `infra/scripts/reconcile-host-config.sh` once it
exists):

```bash
# Header-parity ratchet. A location that declares its own add_header silently
# drops every inherited security header (D3). Assert the invariant instead of
# trusting the convention. Run AFTER `systemctl reload nginx`.
assert_security_headers() {
  local base="$1" path="$2" n
  n=$(curl -sSk -o /dev/null -D - --max-time 10 "$base$path" \
      | tr -d '\r' \
      | grep -icE '^(strict-transport-security|x-content-type-options|x-frame-options|referrer-policy|content-security-policy):')
  if [ "$n" -ne 5 ]; then
    echo "FATAL: $path returned $n/5 security headers (expected 5)" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "OK: $path 5/5 security headers"
}

BASE="https://${DOMAIN}"
ASSET=$(curl -sSk --max-time 10 "$BASE/login" \
        | grep -oE '"/_next/static/[^"]+\.(js|css)"' | tr -d '"' | head -1)
[ -n "$ASSET" ] || { echo "FATAL: could not discover a /_next/static asset" >&2; exit 1; }
assert_security_headers "$BASE" /login   || exit 1
assert_security_headers "$BASE" "$ASSET" || exit 1
```

###### Step 4 — apply to the running box (host-side, transient)

Per C1, no deploy reaches the dev instance, so the repo edit alone changes nothing live. **Fold this
into A1's single SSM payload** — same file, one `nginx -t`, one reload, one backup. Two idempotent
range-restricted deletes, safe to run twice:

```bash
# inside A1's SSM patch script, AFTER its backup to /root/nginx-backup-<ts>/
# and BEFORE its `nginx -t` gate.
SITE=/etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai

# D3: drop the two directives inside the /_next/static/ block only.
sed -i '\|^    location /_next/static/ {$|,\|^    }$|{ /add_header Cache-Control/d; /proxy_cache_valid/d; }' "$SITE"

# Assert the block is now add_header-free (idempotent + non-vacuous).
awk '/^    location \/_next\/static\/ \{$/,/^    \}$/' "$SITE" | grep -q 'add_header' \
  && { echo "FATAL: /_next/static/ still declares add_header"; exit 1; }
awk '/^    location \/_next\/static\/ \{$/,/^    \}$/' "$SITE" | grep -q 'proxy_pass' \
  || { echo "FATAL: /_next/static/ block not found - sed address did not match"; exit 1; }
```

The second `grep -q proxy_pass` check is the non-vacuity guard: if the `sed` address never matched
(because the live file differs from the repo render), the first assertion would pass trivially. The
dossier measured the live file byte-identical to the repo render
(`sha256 5f090af1...`, A1 pre-flight) [V by dossier], so the address will match — but assert it
anyway.

If step 2 (the snippet) is also applied to the host, it needs the snippet file written **before**
the `include` line is added to the site file, or `nginx -t` fails. Given the host change is
transient and the box will be rebuilt from `bootstrap-ec2.sh` eventually, the simpler and safer
host-side action is **step 4 only** (the two deletes). The snippet extraction is a repo-only
improvement that lands on the next real provision. State that choice explicitly in the runbook.

##### I6. Ripple-effect analysis — why nothing else breaks

Assume the fix is wrong. Where would it show?

- **A browser rejects an asset it used to accept.** The only header with a blocking mode is
  `nosniff`, and it blocks only on a wrong `Content-Type` for a script or stylesheet destination.
  Measured: `.js -> application/javascript`, `.css -> text/css` [V]. Correct. Fonts and maps are not
  nosniff-blocked destinations.
- **The CSP breaks something.** It cannot: a CSP on a subresource is not enforced against the
  loading document, and the only enforcing consumer (a worker) is proven absent [V]. The document's
  CSP is unchanged — this fix does not touch the policy string, only where it is *also* emitted.
- **Caching regresses and every page load re-downloads the bundle.** The single most important
  ripple, and it is measured away: the upstream sets the identical `Cache-Control` unconditionally
  for `nextStaticFolder` (`router-server.js:394-400` [V]), and the live response proves it arrives
  (the duplicate is *both* copies). After the fix the client sees exactly one
  `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Same value, same semantics, one fewer header. Verify with
  the `cc=1` assertion in I8.
- **`proxy_cache_valid` removal changes caching.** It cannot: there is no `proxy_cache` zone
  anywhere in the repo [V], so nginx has been ignoring the directive since 2026-05-11.
- **Concurrency / ordering.** None. `add_header` is evaluated per-response in the header filter
  chain; there is no shared state, no queue, no task.
- **Startup / shutdown.** `nginx -t` runs in a throwaway process against the on-disk config; a
  failed validation leaves the running master's in-memory config untouched, so downtime on a bad
  edit is zero (A1 establishes this and it applies unchanged here). A successful `reload` forks new
  workers and drains the old ones — **in-flight SSE streams on the old workers are not cut**; nginx
  keeps old workers alive until their connections close (`worker_shutdown_timeout` default is
  unlimited). So a reload during an active run does not kill the stream. [I] on the exact drain
  semantics for this box's `worker_shutdown_timeout` (not set in the repo, so the default applies).
- **Unattached client / slow client / crashed run / restart / resume / fan-out / revision / two
  browsers.** All of these are A2/A3/A4/A5 territory on `/api/runs/*/events/stream`. This change
  touches only `/_next/static/`, which serves static files from the Next.js process and participates
  in no run lifecycle. Zero interaction.
- **Memory / connection pool.** None. No upstream behaviour changes; the same `keepalive 32` pool to
  `velocityai_frontend` is used identically.
- **Partial application.** The two `sed` deletes are independent and each idempotent. If only the
  `add_header` delete lands, D3 is fixed and an inert `proxy_cache_valid` survives — harmless. If
  only the `proxy_cache_valid` delete lands, nothing changes at all (still 0/5). If step 2 lands
  without step 1, the location still declares `add_header` and is still 0/5 — the snippet does not
  fix it on its own (measured: `add_header` + server-level `include` still yields 0/5 at the
  location [V]). **So step 1 is the load-bearing one and must not be skipped.**
- **Someone reverts only the repo half.** Then the box keeps the fix until it is rebuilt, and the
  rebuild silently reintroduces D3. This is C1's structural problem, not a defect of this fix — but
  it is why the guard in step 3 belongs in the reconcile path, not only in a one-off script.

Where the dossier already argues safety, I verified rather than restated: its "either re-declare or
snippet" both work (measured, 5/5 each) — I am rejecting one of them for a reason it did not state,
not because it is wrong.

##### I8. Test plan — fail-before / pass-after

There is no unit-test surface for nginx configuration in this repo (`grep -rln` for these headers
or `_next/static` over `*.py`/`*.ts`/`*.tsx`/`*.yml`/`*.sh` matches only `bootstrap-ec2.sh`,
`install.py`, and a data blob [V]). The test is therefore an executable assertion at two levels.

###### Test 1 — offline containerized fail-before / pass-after (already run; reproduce before shipping)

Complete, self-contained. It renders the *real* config out of `bootstrap-ec2.sh` conceptually but
uses a minimal faithful equivalent so it needs no certificates and no upstream app. Run from the
repo root; writes only to a temp dir.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# infra/scripts/test-nginx-security-headers.sh  (NEW FILE - specified, not created here)
# Fail-before / pass-after harness for D3. Requires docker + a local nginx:1.24-alpine image.
set -euo pipefail
T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"; docker rm -f d3test >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
mkdir -p "$T/www"; printf 'body{color:red}\n' > "$T/www/app.css"

sec_block() {
cat <<'S'
    add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;
    add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
    add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;
    add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always;
    add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'" always;
S
}

# BEFORE: /_next/static/ declares its own add_header (the shipped shape)
# AFTER : the add_header is gone
gen() {  # $1 = before|after
  {
    echo 'server { listen 8081; root /www;'
    echo '  location / { try_files $uri /app.css;'
    echo '    add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"; } }'
    echo 'server { listen 8080;'
    sec_block
    echo '  location /_next/static/ { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8081/;'
    if [ "$1" = before ]; then
      echo '    proxy_cache_valid 200 1y;'
      echo '    add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable";'
    fi
    echo '  }'
    echo '  location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8081/; } }'
  } > "$T/default.conf"
}

probe() {  # $1 = path -> "<sec-count> <cache-control-count>"
  docker exec d3test sh -c \
    "{ printf 'GET $1 HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n'; sleep 0.4; } | nc 127.0.0.1 8080" \
    2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | sed -n '1,/^$/p' > "$T/h"
  echo "$(grep -icE '^(strict-transport-security|x-content-type-options|x-frame-options|referrer-policy|content-security-policy):' "$T/h") \
$(grep -icE '^cache-control:' "$T/h")"
}

run() {  # $1 = before|after ; echoes "<sec> <cc>" for the static path and the control path
  gen "$1"
  docker rm -f d3test >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  docker run -d --name d3test -v "$T/default.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro" \
    -v "$T/www:/www:ro" nginx:1.24-alpine >/dev/null
  sleep 1.5
  echo "static: $(probe /_next/static/app.css)   control: $(probe /app.css)"
}

echo "BEFORE -> $(run before)"
echo "AFTER  -> $(run after)"
```

**Expected output — this is the whole test:**

```text
BEFORE -> static: 0 2   control: 5 1
AFTER  -> static: 5 1   control: 5 1
```

`BEFORE static: 0 2` is the bug (no security headers, duplicate `Cache-Control`).
`AFTER static: 5 1` is the fix. The `control` column must be `5 1` in both runs — if it is not, the
harness itself is broken and the result means nothing. **I ran exactly this matrix on
nginx/1.24.0 and observed those numbers** [V] (I3).

###### Test 2 — live assertion on dev, before and after the SSM apply

```bash

# Discover a current asset. Names are content-hashed and change on EVERY build,
# so this MUST be dynamic. Anchor on the surrounding double quotes: a bare
# character-class regex over the HTML produces truncated paths such as
# /_next/static/chunks/03 (measured).

echo "asset = $ASSET"

for P in /login "$ASSET"; do
```

##### I9. Rollback

**Repo.** `git revert` the one, two, or three commits. Nothing depends on them; no migration, no
generated artifact, no lockfile.

**Host.** Restore from the file-level backup A1's script takes:

```bash
cp /root/nginx-backup-<ts>/velocityai /etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai
nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx
```

If step 2 was also applied on the host, additionally `rm -f
/etc/nginx/snippets/velocityai-security-headers.conf` **after** restoring the site file (the
restored file no longer includes it; deleting it first would make `nginx -t` fail while the
`include` line is still live).

**Not reversible.** There is **no filesystem-level rollback**: `velocityai-dev-root` has
`delete_on_termination = true` and **zero snapshots** (Appendix 2). The `/root/nginx-backup-<ts>/`
copy is the only restore point and it lives on that same unsnapshotted volume. The pre-change backup
must capture, at minimum:

- `/etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai`
- `/etc/nginx/snippets/velocityai-proxy-headers.conf`
- `/etc/nginx/conf.d/velocityai-limits.conf` (A1 and E1 both edit it)
- `sha256sum` of all three, recorded in the SSM output so the restore is verifiable

**Blast radius of a bad apply is bounded to zero downtime** because `nginx -t` parses the on-disk
config in a throwaway process; the running master keeps its in-memory config until a *successful*
reload. The failure mode to actually guard against is a *successful* reload of a config that is
syntactically valid but semantically wrong — which is what the step-3 assertion catches.

##### I10. Sequencing and dependencies

**Must land before D3:**

- **C1** — without it the repo edit reaches nothing. C1 is not optional; it is the delivery
  mechanism. If C1's "now" half (a scoped SSM apply) is not being run, D3's repo commit is correct
  but inert on dev until the box is rebuilt, which C1 proves will not happen on its own (dev's
  userData has no firstboot service and `/var/lib/velocityai/.bootstrap-done` does not exist).
- **A1** — not a hard dependency, but D3's host-side edit **should ride A1's single SSM payload**:
  same file, same backup, one `nginx -t`, one reload. Two independent reload cycles on the same file
  is strictly more risk for zero benefit. If D3 ships standalone it must replicate A1's entire
  backup / validate / restore-on-failure harness.

**Must not land before D3, or must be coordinated with it:**

- Nothing. D3 blocks no other issue.

**Same file, different lines (name the ids so the executor sequences the merges):**

| Issue | Region of `bootstrap-ec2.sh` | Overlap with D3 (`791-799`, `908-913`) |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | `:706-716` (adds `limit_conn_zone`) + a new location inserted before `:822` | none |
| E1 | `:712-715` (replaces `log_format`) | none |
| B1/B2/B3/B4/B5 | section 14, `:941-1007` | none |
| E2 | the pg-dump script, ~`:1105` | none |
| E3 | `:1105-1106` | none |
| C1 | no line edit - it is the delivery mechanism | none |

**A1 and E1 collide with each other** inside the `:706-716` heredoc (A1 appends a
`limit_conn_zone`; E1 replaces the `log_format`). That is their coordination problem; D3 is
independent of both. Verified against the unmerged `origin/fix/infra-uki` branch too: its
`bootstrap-ec2.sh` hunks are at 544, 1239 and 1261 — **zero overlap** [V].

**Explicit coordination with A1 — the thing the brief asked for.**

A1 adds a **new** location, which is exactly the moment this class of bug can be reintroduced.
Measured on nginx 1.24.0 [V]:

- A regex location declaring **no** `add_header` inherits all five. **A1's block, exactly as written
  in the dossier (lines 170-188), declares none — so A1 is safe as proposed and needs no change from
  me.**
- The same regex location with `add_header X-Accel-Buffering "no";` returns **0 of 5**.

That second line is the single most likely addition to an SSE location — most nginx SSE recipes
include it — and it is **unnecessary here**: `sse-starlette` force-sets `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on
every response itself (dossier A1 [V], `sse.py:140`), so nginx would be duplicating an upstream
header. That is precisely the `/_next/static/` `Cache-Control` mistake repeated on a new path. A1's
block must therefore carry this comment:

```nginx
    # Declare NO add_header here. nginx's add_header is replace-not-merge across
    # levels, so one add_header silently drops all five server-level security
    # headers (that is D3, on /_next/static/). X-Accel-Buffering is already set
    # by sse-starlette on every response, so there is nothing to add. If a header
    # ever genuinely belongs here, add
    #   include /etc/nginx/snippets/velocityai-security-headers.conf;
    # on the line above it.
```

**Does the snippet make the whole class impossible?** No, and I will not claim it does. An `include`
is opt-in; nothing forces a future author to use it. The snippet reduces the remedy from "copy a
400-character CSP" to one line, which changes the odds; the step-3 header assertion is what actually
makes a regression **detectable**. Both, or the class stays alive.

**Commit boundaries — three commits, in this order:**

1. `fix(nginx): stop /_next/static/ dropping the five security headers` — delete `:911-912` plus the
   explanatory comment. Self-contained, independently revertable, closes D3.
2. `refactor(nginx): single-source the security headers into a snippet` — the move (create the
   snippet, replace `:791-799` with the `include`). Behaviour-neutral, proven byte-equivalent [V],
   revertable without reopening D3.
3. `test(infra): assert 5/5 security headers on a page and a static asset` — the standing guard.
   Can instead be folded into A1's apply script if A1 lands in the same window.

Do **not** squash 1 and 2. If the snippet extraction turns out to interact badly with the
`${DOMAIN}` expansion, commit 1 must survive the revert.

##### I11. Open questions requiring a human decision

**1. `proxy_cache_valid 200 1y` — remove (recommended) or wire a real `proxy_cache`?**
The dossier says "worth removing or wiring while in the file" without choosing. I recommend
**remove**, and the choice has a real cost side, so it is a decision rather than a detail:

- *Remove* (recommended). It is provably inert today [V]. The assets are content-hash-immutable and
  already carry `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, so the browser cache already does this job.
- *Wire it* would mean adding `proxy_cache_path` + `proxy_cache` + a key. Costs: (a) it stores a
  second copy of every build's JS/CSS on the **root volume, which has zero snapshots and
  `delete_on_termination = true`** — the one disk with no rollback; (b) every deploy mints new
  hashed filenames, so the cache accumulates the union of all past builds until `max_size` evicts —
  the same unbounded-growth shape as D6; (c) the "origin fetch" it would save is a loopback read
  from `127.0.0.1:3000` of a file already in the OS page cache, and no latency problem has been
  measured; (d) it adds stale-asset and cache-lock failure modes for zero gain. If asset delivery
  ever needs caching, the right layer is a CDN in front of nginx, not a disk cache on the app box.

**2. Should the step-3 header assertion become a deploy gate?**
Making it a gate means a failing assertion fails the build. That is the right posture for a security
invariant and it matches B5's "a deploy that touches the agent must fail the build when the agent is
not running afterwards". But it puts a network probe of the live box in the deploy path, which can
fail for reasons unrelated to the change. Recommendation: **run it and fail loudly in the reconcile
script** (which only runs when host config is being changed), and **log-only** in the steady-state
container deploy. Needs whoever owns C1's pipeline half to agree.

No other open decisions. Nothing here changes product behaviour, costs money, or needs a mailbox
owner.

---

##### I12. Shortcuts and alternatives explicitly rejected

1. **Re-declare the five headers inside `location /_next/static/`** (the dossier's first option).
   Works — measured 5/5. Rejected because it creates a **second copy of a 400-character CSP string**
   that will drift from the server-level one the first time the policy changes (and the policy has
   already changed once: `0e9c410e` flipped `DENY` to `SAMEORIGIN`). Under this project's own
   INV-3/INV-12 that is a dual implementation. It also leaves the duplicate `Cache-Control` in place.

2. **Keep `add_header Cache-Control` and add `include .../velocityai-security-headers.conf`**
   (the dossier's second option, applied without deleting). Works — measured 5/5. Rejected because
   the directive it preserves is provably redundant: the response still carries `Cache-Control`
   **twice** (measured), and a directive whose only effect is to duplicate an upstream header and
   disable inheritance has no reason to exist. Strictly dominated by deleting it.

3. **Add `always` to the location's `add_header Cache-Control`.** The most plausible-looking wrong
   fix, because `always` is what makes the *server-level* headers appear on errors. It does nothing
   for inheritance: `always` selects which status codes a header is emitted for; it does not affect
   whether the level inherits. Proven by the 404 case — the non-`always` directive does not fire
   there (one `Cache-Control`, from upstream) yet inheritance is **still** killed (0/5) [V].

4. **Move the five `add_header` directives to `http{}` level** (into
   `conf.d/velocityai-limits.conf`). Rejected: the replace-not-merge rule is evaluated level by
   level, so a location's `add_header` still wins over an `http`-level set — the bug survives
   unchanged. It would additionally apply HSTS to the plaintext :80 server, where the client must
   ignore it. [I] on the http-level measurement specifically; the rule is the same documented one
   and I measured the server->location case directly.

5. **Use `more_set_headers` (headers-more-nginx-module), which merges instead of replacing.**
   Rejected: the module is not in Ubuntu's stock `nginx` package. Installing it means switching to
   `nginx-extras` or a custom build on a box that **cannot be re-provisioned** (C1) and whose root
   volume has no snapshot. A packaging change to work around a five-line config rule is not
   proportionate.

6. **Set the five headers in Next.js `next.config.ts` `headers()` instead of nginx.** Rejected:
   every non-Next path — `/api/`, `/health`, `/openapi.json`, `/mcp/`, `/install/`, `/ws/handoff/` —
   would lose them, and the paths nginx also covers would get duplicates. It moves a
   perimeter-wide security control into one of the two upstreams. Also, two CSP headers on one
   response are enforced as the **intersection**, so a future divergence between the two sources
   becomes a silent, hard-to-diagnose breakage rather than a visible one.

7. **Wire a `proxy_cache` zone rather than deleting `proxy_cache_valid`.** Rejected on the grounds
   in I11 (unsnapshotted disk, unbounded growth across builds, no measured latency problem, new
   failure modes). Recorded as an open decision rather than a unilateral one because the dossier
   left it open.

8. **Fix only the repo and wait for the next provision.** Rejected: C1 proves dev will never re-run
   `bootstrap-ec2.sh` on its own — its live userData is 68 lines with no `velocityai-firstboot`
   service and `/var/lib/velocityai/.bootstrap-done` does not exist. The box would stay 0/5
   indefinitely. Both halves are required.

9. **Fix only the box and skip the repo commit.** Rejected: the change evaporates on instance
   replacement (root volume `delete_on_termination = true`, zero snapshots) or on any deliberate
   bootstrap re-run, and stage/prod would never get it.

10. **Add the snippet without deleting the inline directives** (i.e. create the file and include it
    while `:791-799` remain). Rejected outright — that is literally two copies of the header set,
    the INV-12 violation the snippet is supposed to prevent. The extraction is a move or it is not
    worth doing.

11. **Skip the snippet and rely on a comment.** Tempting, since after step 1 no location needs the
    include and a snippet with exactly one consumer looks like pure indirection. Rejected on
    balance: the snippet costs nothing (proven byte-equivalent [V]), and it is what turns A1's
    hazard — and every future location's — from "copy the CSP correctly" into one line. But it is
    the weakest of the three commits and is the one to drop first if the change must be minimised.

**One trap worth recording for whoever executes this**, because it cost me a measurement: extracting
an asset URL from the HTML with a bare character class
(`grep -oE '/_next/static/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+'`) produces truncated and merged paths such as
`/_next/static/chunks/03` and `/_next/static/chunks/02i7dfk78`. Anchor on the surrounding double
quotes (`grep -oE '"/_next/static/[^"]+"'`) or the verification probes hit URLs that do not exist
and report a misleading 404.

### D4 — `ArtifactStore` retains three dicts for the process lifetime

**Confidence:** [V] — no removal site exists outside tests.

**Symptom.** Memory grows monotonically with the number of runs and review gates, never released.

**Root cause.** `agents/artifact_store/store.py:42`, `:43`, `:48` declare
`_questionnaire_responses`, `_resume_events` and `_questionnaire_force_proceed` on an instance held
by a process-lifetime singleton (`:173-184`). Writes at `:59`, `:78-79`, `:115`, `:137`. **There is
no `.pop`, `del` or `.clear` on any of the three anywhere in the repo outside tests.**
`set_review_response` stores the **full user-edited artifact body**, and `review_gate_ready` payloads
average ~34 KB on the dev data. Grows per run *and* per gate, and survives every exit path including
cancel and unhandled exception.

**Why it occurred.** These are coordination structures for an in-flight run — a response slot and an
`asyncio.Event` per gate. Their natural lifetime is the run, but they live on a **singleton**, and no
run-completion hook was ever given the job of clearing them. The store's own API has no concept of
"this run is over".

**The fix.** Add an explicit `forget_run(run_id)` to `ArtifactStore` that clears all three keyed
structures, and call it from the one place that already knows a run has ended — the driver `finally`
that calls `_cleanup_pipeline`. Do **not** add a TTL sweeper: the lifecycle is known exactly, so
tying it to the existing terminal hook is both simpler and correct.

**Verification.** A test that drives a run to terminal and asserts all three structures no longer
contain its id.

#### Fully-Detailed Investigation

> **Investigated** 2026-07-30 · **Verdict on the dossier's proposed fix:**
> CONFIRMED-WITH-CORRECTIONS · **Registers read to EOF:** FIX-REGISTER.md (3,705 lines)
> and IMPLEMENTATION-REGISTER.md (4,178 lines) · **Anchor drift found:** 0 of 12 anchors
> moved (one anchor *mis-labelled* in the dossier prose - see I1.1).
>
> **The fix in I5 and the tests in I8 were BUILT AND RUN** on a throwaway copy of
> `backend/` in the scratchpad - fail-before `3 failed / 20 passed`, pass-after
> `23 passed`, and **every regression delta measured at zero** (goldens 10f/6p
> unchanged, SSE 1f/31p unchanged, resume 10f/51p unchanged, `lint-imports` 3 kept /
> 1 broken unchanged). **No file in the repo was modified except this one.**

##### I3. Root cause - confirmed, corrected

**Re-derived independently. The dossier's mechanism is right.** The three dicts are
per-run coordination state hung off a module-level singleton
(`store.py:173-184`, `get_artifact_store()`), written on four lines, and read by five
call sites - with **no removal path in production code anywhere**. Verified by exhaustive
grep (I4.1): every `.pop` / `del` / `.clear` on the three names in the whole repo is in a
test fixture.

Causal chain, trigger to symptom:

1. A run starts. If it clarifies, `POST /api/runs/{id}/answers` ->
   `run_commands.py:274 set_questionnaire_responses(run_id, ...)` writes
   `_questionnaire_responses[run_id]` (`:78`) and `_questionnaire_force_proceed[run_id]`
   (`:79`) and creates `_resume_events[run_id]` (`:59` via `get_resume_event`).
2. For each gated agent, `engine._run_review_gate` (`engine.py:5109`) builds
   `gate_key = f"{pipeline_run_id}:{agent_id}"` and `get_review_event(gate_key)` creates
   `_resume_events[f"review:{gate_key}"]` (`:115`). Resolving it writes
   `_questionnaire_responses[f"review:{gate_key}"]` (`:137`) holding
   `{approved, edited_content, action, instructions}`.
3. The run terminates by any path - complete, cancel, fail, unhandled exception. The
   driver's `finally` (`run_commands.py:2184-2186`) drains the queue and calls
   `_cleanup_pipeline`, which pops `_PIPELINE_QUEUES` / `_PIPELINE_TASKS` /
   `_CANCEL_EVENTS` and **nothing else**.
4. Every entry from steps 1-2 survives for the life of the uvicorn process.

**Five corrections to the dossier's analysis.**

**C1 (the important one) - `_resume_events` and `_questionnaire_responses` each hold TWO
key namespaces in one dict.** The dossier does not say this, and it is the single fact
that decides whether `forget_run(run_id)` can find its entries at all:

| Dict | Key shapes |
|---|---|
| `_resume_events` | `"{run_id}"` (clarify, `:59`) **and** `"review:{run_id}:{agent_id}"` (review gate, `:115`) |
| `_questionnaire_responses` | `"{run_id}"` (clarify, `:78`) **and** `"review:{run_id}:{agent_id}"` (review, `:137`) |
| `_questionnaire_force_proceed` | `"{run_id}"` only (`:79`) |

`gate_key` is built in exactly one place - `engine.py:5109`,
`f"{pipeline_run_id}:{agent_id}"` - and reached from four call sites (`engine.py:3132`,
`:3276`, `:4120` inline; `kernel_services.py:1109` for the declared `gates:[human]` path,
which passes `pipeline_run_id=self.run_id, agent_id=spec.id`). So a naive
`d.pop(run_id, None)` would miss **every review-gate entry** - i.e. the large ones. The
exact matching rule is specified and proven in I5.

**C2 - "Grows per run *and* per gate" is right about gates but wrong about rounds.**
`set_review_response` **assigns** (`:137`), it does not append. On dev the busiest
gate_key was re-emitted **34 times** (a redo loop:
`43a0d562-...:prototype-specify`) and still occupies exactly one entry. Measured: **65
distinct gate_keys ever, across 32 gated runs - at most 3 per run.** So the per-run
entry count is small and bounded; the growth is in the *number of runs*, not in redo
depth.

**C3 - the dossier names the wrong dominant payload.** It says
*"`set_review_response` stores the **full user-edited artifact body**"*. True, but
`edited_content` is `None` for a plain approve (`resolve_gate` passes
`body.edited_content`, which the FE sends only on an actual edit). The realistic large
retained value is **`instructions` on `action="update_specs"`**, which
`run_commands.py:232` sets to the full `analysis_report`. Measured gate outputs on dev:
`prototype-specify` median 42,623 B (max 89,108), `prototype-plan` median 12,741 B (max
95,165), `prototype-analyze` median 9,053 B.

**C4 - the "~34 KB average" figure is the EVENT payload, not what is retained.**
Confirmed as an event statistic (mean 33,923 B over n=284). What the *store* retains is
much smaller in the common case. Measured directly, by building a real `ArtifactStore`
and deep-sizing the three dicts:

| Run shape | Retained across the three dicts |
|---|---|
| ungated clarify-only (`user_stories`) | **~1,355 B** |
| gated, approve-only (`prototype`, 3 gates) | **~3,257 B** |
| gated with one edit (42,623 B) + one `update_specs` (9,053 B) | **~56,123 B** |

So the honest characterisation is: **~1-3 KB per ordinary run, ~50-150 KB for a run the
user actually edited or re-specced** (worst observed per-run gate-output total on dev:
145,761 B). At the dev rate (134 runs in a month) this is not an outage; it is a strict,
unbounded, never-released monotonic climb in a process expected to live for weeks. The
dossier's "Memory grows monotonically ... never released" is exactly right; its implied
magnitude is high by roughly an order of magnitude for the common run.

**C5 - one addition the dossier omits.** The `asyncio.Event` objects in `_resume_events`
are cheap, but they are also the mechanism the *only* remaining reader,
`review_event_pending` (`store.py:156-166` -> `run_commands.py:149 _gate_is_pending`),
consults to decide whether a gate is live. That makes the timing of the clear a
**correctness** question, not merely a memory one - which is why I4.3 exists.

**Verdict: the root cause is CONFIRMED.** The proposed fix shape (an explicit
`forget_run(run_id)` called from the existing terminal hook; no TTL sweeper) is
**correct** and is the right one. It needs the composite-key rule (C1) to actually work,
and it needs the lifetime proof (I4.3) to be safe.

`get_review_response` / `get_questionnaire_responses` call sites are the four above.

###### I4.3 The lifetime question - can any reader legitimately fire after the clear?

This is the section that decides whether the fix is safe. The hazard is precise: a
waiter holds a **direct object reference** (`event = await get_review_event(gate_key)`,
`engine.py:5112`). If `forget_run` pops that key while the waiter is blocked on
`event.wait()`, then a later `POST /gate` is rejected at `_gate_is_pending` (the key is
gone -> `review_event_pending` False -> HTTP 404 `gate_not_pending`), the write never
happens, and **the waiter hangs forever**. That is the BUG-R01/R02 shape recorded in
IMPL `:4089`. So the fix is safe iff `_cleanup_pipeline` can never fire while a gate
waiter is alive.

**Every `_cleanup_pipeline` call site, traced.**

```
$ rg -n '_cleanup_pipeline|_fire_resume_cleanup' -g '*.py' agents app
```

| # | Site | Position relative to the drive | Waiter alive? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `run_commands.py:2186` (launch driver `finally`) | after `async for ... engine.execute(...)` is exhausted | **No** - the waiter lives inside that generator |
| 2 | `run_commands.py:2489` (revision driver `finally`) | same shape | **No** |
| 3 | `engine.py:5551` (`_rearm_gate_run` `finally`) | **THREE cases - see I4.3a.** (3c) after `await resume_run(...)` / `await _replay_clarify_run(...)` returns; (3a) the `wr is None` return at `:5521`; **(3b) the `open_kind` FALL-THROUGH at `:5536-5547`, which awaits NOTHING** | **No** in all three - (3b) is definitionally the branch on which no driver is awaited |
| 4 | `engine.py:7541` (`resume_run`: no `workflow_runs` row) | **before** any drive | **No** - nothing driving |
| 5 | `engine.py:7586` (`resume_run`: cannot resolve agents) | before any drive | **No** |
| 6 | `engine.py:7591` (`resume_run`: empty agent list) | before any drive | **No** |
| 7 | `engine.py:7830` (`_drive_resumed_stream` `finally`) | after the drive loop exhausts | **No** |
| 8 | `engine.py:7890` (`_replay_clarify_run`: no row) | before any drive | **No** |
| 9 | `engine.py:7914` (cannot resolve agents) | before any drive | **No** |
| 10 | `engine.py:7920` (empty agent list) | before any drive | **No** |
| 11 | `engine.py:7937` (no open questionnaire gate) | before any drive | **No** |
| 12 | `engine.py:7955` (open gate has no durable questions - *"leaving parked"*) | before any drive | **No** |
| 13 | *(new, from A4)* `_is_run_live` self-heal | only when `_PIPELINE_TASKS[run_id].done()` | **No** - a done task means the driver's `finally` already ran |

**Sites 1, 2, 3c, 7 are the normal terminal paths.** The run is over; the generator that
owned the waiter has been exhausted or closed. Clearing is unambiguously correct.

###### I4.3a Site 3 is THREE paths, not one - correcting this document (raised by A3)

A3's I10 (`A3.md:818-836`) objects that `_cleanup_pipeline` is the wrong home for D4/D5
because some paths fire on a run "deliberately left parked", singling out
`engine.py:5551`. **A3 is right that the path exists and this document was wrong to
describe site 3 as unconditionally post-drive.** The full control flow
(`engine.py:5494-5559`, read verbatim):

```python
async def _rearm_gate_run(self, run_id: str) -> None:
    try:                                                    # :5510  OUTER try
        db = SessionLocal()
        try:
            wr = db.query(WorkflowRun)...first()            # :5516
            if wr is None:
                return                                      # :5521  (3a) -> outer finally
            owner_id = ...; workspace_id = wr.workspace_id
        finally:
            db.close()
        try:
            store = ScopedStore(owner_id=..., workspace_id=...)
            rows = await store.read_events(run_id, after_seq=0)   # :5531
        except Exception:                                   # noqa: BLE001
            rows = []                                       # :5533  <-- SWALLOWS a read failure
        open_kind, _open_gate_key = derive_open_gate(rows)  # :5534
        if open_kind == "review":
            await self.resume_run(run_id)                   # :5540  BLOCKS while the gate is open
        elif open_kind == "questionnaire":
            await self._replay_clarify_run(run_id)          # :5547  BLOCKS
        # (3b) FALL-THROUGH: open_kind is None -> NOTHING is awaited
    finally:
        self._fire_resume_cleanup(run_id)                   # :5551
```

**(3b) is reachable with a durably-open review gate.** Branch (a) armed
`review:{gate_key}` at `:5358` and cleared it at `:5365` off a **successful** read at
`:5341`; `_rearm_gate_run` then re-reads at `:5531`, and if *that* read raises, the bare
`except` sets `rows = []`, `derive_open_gate([])` returns `(None, None)`, no branch is
taken, and `:5551` fires. The `workflow_runs` row is still `waiting_for_user` and the
durable log still carries an unresolved `review_gate_ready`. The other route into (3b) is
the gate having been resolved between the two derivations - in which case there is no
open gate and clearing is trivially right.

**But no waiter can exist on (3a) or (3b).** The fall-through is *definitionally* the
branch on which neither `resume_run` nor `_replay_clarify_run` is awaited, so
`_run_review_gate` never ran in this process and nothing is blocked at
`engine.py:5157/:5176`. Nor can a *concurrent* driver hold one: branch (a) (`:5346`) and
branch (b) auto-resume (`:5415`) are `if`/`elif` on the same row - mutually exclusive;
`POST /resume` 409s on the overlap mutex (`run_commands.py:390`) because branch (a)
registered the task at `:5386-5390`; a fresh launch is a new uuid4. **A3's stated harm -
"destroy the `asyncio.Event` a human gate is waiting on, the BUG-R04 lost-wakeup class" -
requires a waiter, and there is none.**

**And today, that gate is ALREADY a black hole.** Traced end to end on `dev` with status
`waiting_for_user`, a human clicking Approve:

1. `_review_gate_owned_by` (`run_engine.py:324`) - owner matches -> pass.
2. `_review_gate_run_is_terminal` (`run_engine.py:351`) - `waiting_for_user` is not in
   `{cancelled, failed, degraded}` -> False -> pass.
3. `_gate_is_pending` (`run_commands.py:212` -> `:149` -> `store.py:165`) - the key was
   armed at `:5358` and cleared at `:5365`, so **True** -> pass.
4. `set_review_response` (`run_commands.py:240`) writes the in-memory dict and calls
   `event.set()` (`store.py:143-144`).
5. **Nothing is awaiting that Event.** No `review_gate_approved` is emitted; no durable
   row is written (every write in `store.py` - `:78`, `:79`, `:115`, `:137` - is
   in-memory only, grep-proven in I4.1).
6. HTTP **200**. `WorkflowRun.status` stays `waiting_for_user` forever.

That is verbatim the shape the register records at IMPL `:4093`: *"a post-restart clarify
answer (BUG-R01) or gate approve (BUG-R02) was persisted but never consumed
(`event.set()` with no listener; status stuck `waiting_for_user` forever)"*. Quick
`260719-ghn` (`e1866317`) fixed only the **alias** cause of the empty-roster bail; it
never touched this fall-through.

**So: today 200 + run stuck; after the fix 404 + run stuck. Identical outcome for the
run.** Recovery in both cases is the next restart, which re-derives from the **durable**
log and re-arms fresh - and `forget_run` is in-memory only, so it cannot affect that. The
approval the user loses is one that today is written into a slot nothing ever reads.

**Site 12 (`engine.py:7955`) needs no such argument.** It is inside
`_replay_clarify_run`, reached only when `open_kind == "questionnaire"`, for which branch
(a) armed the **bare** `{run_id}` key at `:5362` - never a `review:` key. And
`POST /answers` (`run_commands.py:274`) does not consult pendency at all: it writes
unconditionally via `set_questionnaire_responses`, which re-creates the event and sets it.
**Zero observable change** on site 12.

**The `asyncio.CancelledError` variant of 1/2 is also safe.** A destructive
`task.cancel()` raises inside the generator, which is then closed; the waiter dies with
it. `run_commands.py:2155` handles it and falls into the same `finally`.

**Sites 4-6 and 8-12 are pre-drive early returns.** No driver from *this* invocation is
running. But the Phase-49 branch-(a) re-arm (reader #7 in I4.2, `engine.py:5354-5365`)
**arms the store waiter at startup, BEFORE spawning `_rearm_gate_run`**. So on these
paths an entry can exist with no waiter. Clearing it changes one observable:

- **Review case** (`review:{gate_key}` armed at `engine.py:5358`, then `resume_run`
  early-returns at 4/5/6): today a subsequent `POST /gate` returns **200 and silently
  does nothing** (the classic BUG-R02 black hole). After the fix it returns **404
  `gate_not_pending`**. The run itself is dead either way - these three early returns
  fire exactly when the run has no row, no resolvable pipeline, or no agents.
- **Clarify case** (`{run_id}` armed at `engine.py:5362`, then `_replay_clarify_run`
  early-returns at 8-12, notably `:7955` which explicitly leaves the run parked):
  **zero observable change.** `POST /answers` (`run_commands.py:274`) does **not**
  consult pendency - it writes unconditionally, recreating both the entry and the event.

**Is the 404 delta user-visible?** No. Measured in the frontend: all four `postGate`
call sites are fire-and-forget:

```
$ cd frontend && rg -n 'postGate' src | grep -v api.ts
src/app/dashboard/page.tsx:2011:        }).catch((e) => console.error("postGate approve failed", e));
src/app/dashboard/page.tsx:2018:        }).catch((e) => console.error("postGate reject failed", e));
src/app/dashboard/page.tsx:2028:        }).catch((e) => console.error("postGate redo failed", e));
src/app/dashboard/page.tsx:2042:        }).catch((e) => console.error("postGate update_specs failed", e));
```

Before: HTTP 200, nothing happens, no console line. After: HTTP 404, nothing happens,
one `console.error`. The user experience is identical (the run is un-resumable in this
process either way - I4.3a proves the 200 does not resolve the gate); the log gets *more*
honest. Recorded as the single behaviour delta in I11, where it covers **sites 3a/3b and
4/5/6**.

**Is there a path where a waiter IS alive and a cleanup fires?** Enumerated and
excluded:

- A second `_cleanup_pipeline(run_id)` concurrent with a live gate wait would require
  another caller for the same id. The candidates are (a) A4's `_is_run_live`, which
  returns early when `_PIPELINE_TASKS[run_id]` is not `done()` - and during a gate wait
  the driver task is exactly that; (b) `POST /api/runs/{id}/resume`, blocked by the
  overlap mutex at `run_commands.py:390` (`run_id in _PIPELINE_TASKS or ... _PIPELINE_QUEUES`
  -> 409); (c) a second launch of the same id - impossible, ids are uuid4.
- Fan-out workers open no gates (IMPL Phase 11 §5 D-01, `:1140`: *"Workers carry NO
  gates"*), so no worker can be waiting on a key the parent's cleanup would remove.
- The KAN-101 `update_specs` sub-pipeline (`_run_spec_revision_sub_pipeline`) re-runs
  agents and re-opens the gate entirely inside the `_run_agent` while-loop, inside the
  driver generator. No cleanup fires during it.
- The Phase-23 redo loop re-arms the **same** `gate_key`; `get_review_event` returns the
  **existing** Event object (`store.py:114-116`), so no reference is orphaned.

**Conclusion, stated precisely (this wording is load-bearing - the looser version is
false).**

- **FALSE:** "no call site fires while a review gate is durably open." Sites 3a, 3b and
  4-6 / 8-12 *can* fire with an unresolved `review_gate_ready` still in the durable log.
- **TRUE, and the only property that matters:** **no call site fires while a HITL waiter
  is alive in this process.** Every pre-drive site is definitionally a path on which no
  driver was ever awaited; every post-drive site runs only after the generator that owned
  the waiter was exhausted or closed. Only a live waiter can be stranded, so
  **`forget_run` inside `_cleanup_pipeline` cannot strand one.**

The invariant is proven by enumeration, not enforced by a runtime predicate - a runtime
predicate is not available (`asyncio.Event` exposes no public waiter count; reading
`_waiters` would be exactly the private-attribute peek IN-02 closed). It is therefore
pinned by a **source-level ratchet test** instead: T4 in I8.

###### I4.4 Revision runs and the parent's artifacts

The brief flags "revision runs that reuse a parent run's artifacts". Checked and
**excluded**: a revision is a *separate* `WorkflowRun` with its own uuid (IMPL Phase 25
D-1, `:2530`), so its gate keys carry the child id and the parent's clear cannot touch
them. And the parent's *artifacts* are read from the DB (`artifact_refs` via
`ScopedStore`), never from the `ArtifactStore` - the artifact half of this module was
**deleted** in Phase 5 (`9d7c7a38`; IMPL `:546`). The class has no artifact API left to
read. Cross-run contamination is structurally impossible.

###### I4.5 The A5 interaction - answered directly

The brief asks whether clearing recreates the post-restart hole A5 describes. **It
cannot: A5's code path never touches this store.**

```
$ rg -n 'artifact_store|get_artifact_store|review_event_pending|_resume_events' app/api/run_stream.py
(no matches)
```

`run_stream.py`'s D-14g gate re-arm derives entirely from the **durable** `run_events`
log (`:184` today, and the bounded `last_event_of_types` query A5 proposes). A5's own
text rejects `review_event_pending` as unusable for exactly the reason that matters
here - *"after a restart the registry is empty"*. So:

- A5 does not read the three dicts -> `forget_run` cannot affect SSE gate re-arm.
- A re-attach after a run ends still re-arms (or correctly does not) from the durable
  log, independent of the in-memory state.
- **Within** a process's life, a still-open gate is by definition a run whose driver has
  not finished, so `_cleanup_pipeline` has not fired for it (I4.3).

The two fixes are orthogonal and can land in either order.

##### I5. The complete fix

Two files. Additive. No deletion is required (INV-3/INV-12: this adds a lifecycle method
where none existed - there is no superseded implementation to remove).

**Anchor:** immediately after `review_event_pending` (ends at `:166`) and before the
`# Module-level singleton` banner at `:169`.

```python
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Module-level singleton

```

AFTER:

```python
    def review_event_pending(self, gate_key: str) -> bool:
        """True iff a review gate for ``gate_key`` is armed and awaiting a response.

        IN-02: the public read of the per-process HITL event registry — an armed
        (created) but not-yet-set ``review:{gate_key}`` event is the ground truth
        that a pause is genuinely pending (KAN-94). Closes the ``run_commands.
        _gate_is_pending`` private-dict peek (``store._resume_events`` no longer leaks
        into the app layer). Unknown key ⇒ ``False``. Read-only — never mutates.
        """
        event = self._resume_events.get(f"review:{gate_key}")
        return event is not None and not event.is_set()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Run lifecycle (D4) — the ONE removal path for the per-run HITL state
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def forget_run(self, run_id: str) -> int:
        """Drop every per-run HITL entry for ``run_id``. Returns the count removed.

        These three registries are per-RUN coordination state living on a
        process-lifetime singleton, and until now nothing ever removed an entry —
        so a completed run's response slots and ``asyncio.Event``s were retained
        for the life of the uvicorn process (D4). ``forget_run`` is that missing
        removal path; the caller that knows a run has ended
        (``app.api.run_engine._cleanup_pipeline``) invokes it. NOT a TTL sweeper:
        the lifecycle is known exactly, so it is tied to the existing terminal hook.

        KEY SHAPES (why this is not three ``pop``s). Two of the three registries
        hold TWO key namespaces:

          * ``_resume_events``            — ``"{run_id}"`` (clarify, :59)
                                            and ``"review:{run_id}:{agent_id}"`` (:115)
          * ``_questionnaire_responses``  — ``"{run_id}"`` (clarify, :78)
                                            and ``"review:{run_id}:{agent_id}"`` (:137)
          * ``_questionnaire_force_proceed`` — ``"{run_id}"`` only (:79)

        ``gate_key`` is minted in exactly one place — ``engine._run_review_gate``,
        ``f"{pipeline_run_id}:{agent_id}"`` — so the review namespace is always
        ``review:`` + run + ``:`` + agent. The match is therefore: the bare id, OR
        the ``review:{run_id}:`` prefix. The bare ``review:{run_id}`` form is also
        matched so the rule is TOTAL over the key space (that shape is unreachable
        today — an agent id is never empty — but a partial match would silently
        leak, and the extra comparison is free).

        SYNCHRONOUS BY DESIGN — every other method here is ``async def`` but none
        of them awaits. This one MUST NOT, because its caller ``_cleanup_pipeline``
        is synchronous precisely so its registry mutations are atomic against the
        event loop (no ``await`` ⇒ no preemption). Making it awaitable would
        destroy that property. ``review_event_pending`` is the same shape (IN-02).

        Idempotent: a second call, or an unknown/empty ``run_id``, removes nothing.
        """
        if not run_id:
            return 0
        exact_review = f"review:{run_id}"
        prefix_review = f"review:{run_id}:"
        removed = 0
        for registry in (self._resume_events, self._questionnaire_responses):
            # Materialize the key list first — deleting during iteration raises.
            doomed = [
                k
                for k in registry
                if k == run_id or k == exact_review or k.startswith(prefix_review)
            ]
            for k in doomed:
                del registry[k]
                removed += 1
        if self._questionnaire_force_proceed.pop(run_id, None) is not None:
            removed += 1
        if removed:
            logger.debug(
                "ArtifactStore: forget_run(%s) released %d HITL entries",
                run_id, removed,
            )
        return removed


# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Module-level singleton
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
```

`logger` already exists at `store.py:26`. No new import.

Why `int` and not `None`: it makes the reclaim measurable and testable, and it is the
only way to clear the dossier's own uncertainty about magnitude without a profiler. Why
`del` over `pop`: `del` on a key we just proved present is the honest expression and
counts correctly.

**Anchor 2b - `_cleanup_pipeline`, `:70-73`.**

BEFORE:

```python
def _cleanup_pipeline(pipeline_run_id: str) -> None:
```
```python
    """Drop every per-run in-process registration for a run that has ended.

    D4: the ArtifactStore's three per-run HITL registries (clarify responses, the
    force-proceed flag, and the review/resume ``asyncio.Event``s) had NO removal
    path anywhere in production code, so they were retained for the life of the
    process. This is the one hook that already knows a run has ended, so it is the
    correct home — no TTL sweeper, no second lifecycle mechanism (INV-12).

    SAFETY (why clearing here cannot strand a HITL waiter): a gate waiter holds a
    direct reference to its Event and lives INSIDE the driver generator
    (``engine._run_review_gate`` -> ``await event.wait()``). All twelve callers are
    either (a) a driver ``finally`` that runs only after that generator is exhausted
    or closed, or (b) a path on which NO driver was ever awaited — the resume early
    returns AND ``_rearm_gate_run``'s ``open_kind`` fall-through (engine.py:5536-5551,
    which awaits neither ``resume_run`` nor ``_replay_clarify_run``). Note (b) CAN run
    while a review gate is still open in the DURABLE log; what it cannot do is run
    while a waiter is alive in THIS process, and only a live waiter can be stranded.
    Popping a key with a waiter alive would make ``review_event_pending`` report
    False, the gate endpoint 404, and the waiter hang forever — the BUG-R01/R02
    failure shape. DO NOT ADD A CALLER THAT RUNS MID-DRIVE; the caller set is pinned
    by ``test_cleanup_pipeline_caller_set_is_pinned``.

    ORDER IS DELIBERATE: the registry pops (and, with A3, the sentinel) come first,
    so the store clear can never prevent an attached client from being released.
    The clear is guarded because this function runs inside ``finally`` blocks —
    an exception here would mask the original one.
    """
    _PIPELINE_QUEUES.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    _PIPELINE_TASKS.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    _CANCEL_EVENTS.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    try:
        get_artifact_store().forget_run(pipeline_run_id)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — never mask a driver's real exception
        logger.warning(
            "forget_run(%s) failed — HITL entries retained", pipeline_run_id,
            exc_info=True,
        )
```

**Nothing to delete (INV-3/INV-12).** There is no prior implementation of this
behaviour anywhere - the whole defect is its absence. The only thing this supersedes is
the *absence* of a hook.

**No config addition.** The dossier is right that a TTL is wrong here; there is no knob
to add. (Contrast A2's `SSE_SUBSCRIBER_QUEUE_MAXSIZE`, which is genuinely uncertain.)

###### Step 3 - if A3 lands in the same commit range

A3 inserts `q.put_nowait(None)` into the same function. The merged body is:

```python
def _cleanup_pipeline(pipeline_run_id: str) -> None:
    q = _PIPELINE_QUEUES.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    _PIPELINE_TASKS.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    _CANCEL_EVENTS.pop(pipeline_run_id, None)
    if q is not None:                       # A3
        try:
            q.put_nowait(None)
        except Exception:
            pass
    try:                                    # D4
        get_artifact_store().forget_run(pipeline_run_id)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        logger.warning(
            "forget_run(%s) failed — HITL entries retained", pipeline_run_id,
            exc_info=True,
        )
```

D4's block goes **last** so that a store-clear failure can never delay or prevent A3's
release-the-clients sentinel. Both are synchronous, so the whole function remains atomic
against the event loop - which is the property A2's lock-free subscribe/close argument
depends on.

##### I6. Ripple-effect analysis - assume the fix is wrong

**"The clear strands a live gate waiter."** The one genuinely dangerous outcome.
Excluded by exhaustively tracing all 12 (13 with A4) call sites in I4.3: every one is
post-drive or pre-drive. The residual risk is a *future* caller added mid-drive - which
is why the docstring says so explicitly and why the test at I8-T3 pins the pre-condition.

**"The clear breaks the Phase-49 restart re-arm."** Analysed in I4.3. Clarify: no
observable change (`POST /answers` writes unconditionally). Review: 200-silent-noop
becomes 404-silent-console-error, only on the three unresumable-run early returns. Not a
regression; arguably the honest outcome. Declared in I11.

**Concurrency / ordering.** `forget_run` is synchronous and contains no `await`, so on
the single-threaded event loop it is atomic: no coroutine can observe a half-cleared
store. This preserves the exact property A2's design relies on ("only two interleavings
exist"). Making it `async def` would break that - the reason the docstring pins it.
Mutation-during-iteration is avoided by materializing the key list first (proven in the
prototype below).

**Restart.** After a process restart all three dicts are empty anyway; the fix changes
nothing about restart behaviour. The Phase-49 branch-(a) re-arm still rebuilds what it
needs from the durable log.

**Resume (`POST /api/runs/{id}/resume`).** A resumed run reuses the same `run_id`. The
sequence is: run fails -> driver `finally` -> `_cleanup_pipeline` -> `forget_run` -> user
resumes -> `resume_run` re-drives -> `_run_review_gate` arms a **fresh** Event
(`get_review_event` create-if-absent) and `event.clear()`s it before waiting. There is no
read of a pre-existing entry anywhere on that path (`get_review_response` is called only
*after* `event.wait()` returns, i.e. only after a fresh `set_review_response`). Clean.
Note the fix also removes a latent stale-read hazard: today an approved response for
`review:{run}:{agent}` survives, and only `event.clear()` at `engine.py:5113` prevents a
re-opened gate from consuming it.

**Two browsers / unattached client / slow client (A2 territory).** The store is not on
the SSE path at all (I4.5). No interaction.

**Fan-out run.** Workers open no gates (IMPL Phase 11 D-01). The parent's clear touches
only its own keys. Verified by the prefix rule (below).

**Revision run.** Separate uuid, separate keys, artifacts read from the DB (I4.4).

**Crashed run.** A run whose driver dies without running its `finally` leaks today and
still leaks after this change - **unless A4 lands**, in which case the next SSE attach
self-heals it via `_is_run_live` -> `_cleanup_pipeline` -> `forget_run`. A4 makes D4
strictly better; D4 does not depend on A4.

**Partial application.** If Step 1 lands without Step 2 the method is dead code (zero
behaviour change). If Step 2 landed without Step 1 the guarded `except` would log a
warning per run and change nothing. Neither half can break the system.

**Memory / pool.** Strictly reclaims. No new allocation, no DB connection, no file
handle.

**The matching rule itself.** Prototyped against the real key shapes, including two
theoretical variants:

```
$ python3.11 - <<'PY'  # (full script in I8-T1's fixture)
BEFORE  resume_events = 8  q_responses = 6  force = 2
removed: 11
AFTER   resume_events = ['2222...2222', 'review:2222...2222:prototype-specify']
AFTER   q_responses   = ['2222...2222', 'review:2222...2222:prototype-specify']
AFTER   force         = ['2222...2222']
neighbour run B intact: True
idempotent second call removed: 0
empty run_id removed: 0
```

The seeded run A carried a clarify submit, three review gates (one with a 40 KB
`edited_content`), a multi-colon `{run}:weird:extra` gate key, and a bare
`review:{run}` key. All eleven were removed; run B's four entries survived untouched.

**Cross-run deletion by a crafted `gate_key`.** `POST /gate` accepts a client-supplied
`gate_key`, but (a) `_review_gate_owned_by` (`run_engine.py:324-348`) parses
`split(":", 1)[0]` and requires `WorkflowRun.user_id == caller`, and (b)
`_gate_is_pending` requires the key to be **already armed by the engine**. So an
attacker cannot plant a key under another run's prefix. And `forget_run` only ever
deletes keys under **its own** run's prefix - it can never reach a neighbour.

##### I7. Architecture and invariant compliance

| Item | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **SC-001** (kernel knows no workflow by name; zero engine edits for a new workflow) | Held. `forget_run` keys purely on `run_id` and a generic `review:` namespace - no `pipeline_type`, no `spec.id`, no agent-name literal. **No engine file is edited at all**; the two files are `agents/artifact_store/store.py` (a leaf data module, not the kernel) and `app/api/run_engine.py` (app layer). |
| **INV-1** (no `if pipeline_type ==` / `spec.id ==`) | Held - no branch of any kind on a name. |
| **INV-3** (byte-identical deliverables / semantic event parity) | Held **by construction**: the golden harness never reaches `_cleanup_pipeline` (I4.8), and the change emits no event, alters no payload, and touches no manifest. Note the goldens are already 10 failed / 6 passed on `dev` (Appendix 1) - the test plan asserts *no delta*, not green. |
| **INV-12** (no dual implementations) | Held. This is the **first and only** removal path; nothing is superseded, so nothing must be deleted. Deliberately NOT a second mechanism: no TTL sweeper, no per-endpoint clear, no shutdown-only sweep. |
| **INV-13** (deepagents only) | Not touched - no agent, runner, or model code. |
| **Hexagonal boundary / import-linter** | Held, **measured both ways**. Only edge added is `app.api.run_engine -> agents.artifact_store.store`, which no contract restricts and `run_commands.py:47` already exercises. Baseline `3 kept, 1 broken`; with the fix applied on a full patched copy of `backend/`: `Analyzed 212 files, 511 dependencies. Contracts: 3 kept, 1 broken` - the same pre-existing `task_loop -> od_context -> app.services.od_loader`. **Delta 0.** |
| **Q3** (additive migrations only) | No migration, no table, no column. |
| **Security defaults** (`exec`/`network`/`secrets`/`spawn_subagents` OFF) | Untouched. No new endpoint, no new grant. Owner-scoping is unchanged: `forget_run` is called only from an internal terminal hook, never from a request handler, and can only affect the run it is given. |
| **LOCK-B** (`websocket.py` unmodifiable during the SSE cutover) | Moot and satisfied: `backend/app/api/websocket.py` was **DELETED** in Phase 44 plan 44-07 (IMPL `:3683`). The lock's live successor is that `/ws/handoff` stays untouched - and it is. |
| **IN-02** (no `store._resume_events` peek in the app layer) | Strengthened - the app layer calls a public method, never a dict. |
