##### I10. Sequencing and dependencies

**Within E1, the order is format-then-filters and it is not arbitrary.**

Both orders leave a window where the format and the filters disagree. The two windows are not
equally bad:

- *Filters first:* `Nginx5xx` matches nothing; `nginx_5xx_spike` is `notBreaching`, so it stays OK
  and reports nothing. **Silent.**
- *Format first:* `Nginx5xx` matches nothing for the same reason, **but** `nginx-log-parse-stalled`
  is not yet deployed either, so it is equally silent — *unless* you deploy the format and the
  filters in one change window, which is the actual recommendation.

So: **apply the nginx format to the box and apply the Terraform in the same change window**, format
first so the log is already JSON when the filters go live. Both halves are in one commit; the
sequencing is operational, not repo-level.

**Commit boundaries — three commits, in this order:**

1. `fix(infra): structured JSON nginx access log with upstream fields` — `bootstrap-ec2.sh` only
   (both hunks: the format and the `:80` `access_log`). Independently reviewable and independently
   revertable; changes no AWS resource by itself.
2. `fix(infra): JSON metric filters + 429 accounting + log-ingestion canaries` —
   `modules/monitoring/main.tf` only.
3. `docs(infra): reconcile the access-log format and 5xx filter recipe` —
   `docs/SIMPLE_AWS_DEPLOYMENT.md` only.

They must land together on `dev` (one MR), but keeping them separate means a reviewer can reason
about the nginx change without reading Terraform, and a bad filter can be reverted without reverting
the format.

**Cross-issue ordering.**

| Issue | Relationship | Order |
|---|---|---|
| **C1** | Delivery mechanism. Without SSM, the format half never reaches the running dev box. | **Must be usable before E1's host half.** E1 does not depend on C1's *repo* work landing, only on the SSM procedure being available. |
| **A1** | **Same file, same heredoc.** A1 adds `limit_conn_zone velocityai_stream:10m;` to `/etc/nginx/conf.d/velocityai-limits.conf` — the exact block E1 rewrites (`bootstrap-ec2.sh:706-716`). **Textual conflict is certain if both are edited independently.** A1 also adds a `location` to the site file, which E1 touches at `:746-759`. | **Coordinate. One nginx-config change window, one `nginx -t`, one reload.** Whoever goes second rebases onto the other. My recommendation: **A1 first** (it fixes the reported outage), E1 immediately after in the same window. |
| **A1 (semantic)** | A1's `limit_conn` returns **503**, which `{ $.status >= 500 }` counts. Named in the `nginx_5xx` comment. | If A1 lands, consider adding a `{ $.status = 503 && $.upstream_addr = "-" }` companion. **That belongs to A1, not E1** — E1 supplies the format that makes it expressible. |
| **D3** | Same file (`bootstrap-ec2.sh:908-913`), disjoint lines, same reload. | Batch into the same nginx change window as A1+E1. Three edits, one reload. |
| **B1 + B2** | E1 is **observably inert** until both land — the log group has zero streams today. | E1 can ship **before** them (it is a no-op until then) but is **unverifiable end-to-end** until they land. T5 (`test-metric-filter`) is what substitutes. |
| **B3 + B4** | Touch the `collect_list` (`bootstrap-ec2.sh:988-995`) — a different section of the same file. Disjoint lines. | No conflict. Same file, so coordinate the commit. |
| **B6** | E1 adds **three alarms**, two of them `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`, which will fire immediately on a dev box that ships nothing. B6's own guidance is "fix B1 and B2 first, then subscribe" — E1 makes that ordering more important, not less. | **Confirm the SNS subscription LAST**, after B1+B2 have logs flowing and the new alarms have gone OK. Otherwise the first thing the newly-confirmed subscriber receives is three false pages. |
| **B6 (subscription filters)** | The brief asks about subscription ordering. **There are no subscription filters anywhere in the repo** (verified, I4 item 4). Nothing to order. | n/a |
| **D11** | Complementary; D11's text explicitly says "Pair this with E1". | **Independent, either order.** See the correlation-id note below. |
| **A2/A3/A4/A5** | Python only. | Fully independent. |
| **E2 / E3 / E4** | E2 and E3 touch `bootstrap-ec2.sh` (the pg-dump script and `:1105-1106`); E4 touches an IAM policy. All disjoint from `:706-716` / `:746-759`. | No conflict. E3 in particular is a **different section** of the same file. |

**Cross-issue constraint the dossier does not state:** A1's verification recipe includes a *pre-flight
config-drift check* (`sha256sum /etc/nginx/sites-available/velocityai` must equal the local render).
**E1 changes that render.** If E1's host half is applied first and A1's pre-flight is then run
unchanged, it will report drift and abort. Whoever goes second must re-baseline that hash. Name it in
whichever plan ships second.

###### `$request_id` end-to-end: what it does and does not buy

The dossier's format includes `"request_id":"$request_id"`. I checked what it can correlate with:

```
$ grep -rn "X-Request-ID\|x-request-id\|request_id\|correlation" backend/app backend/agents
backend/app/agents/types.py:85:    # correlation and ArtifactStore keying. Generated lazily if not supplied.
backend/agents/guardrails/mulesoft.md:33:- Log correlation IDs through all error paths ...
$ grep -rn "X-Request-Id\|request_id" infra/
(nothing)
```

**There is no correlation id anywhere.** The proxy-headers snippet (`bootstrap-ec2.sh:718-726`)
forwards `Host`, `X-Real-IP`, `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Proto` and sets
`proxy_http_version 1.1` — **it does not forward `X-Request-ID`**. And the backend's log format is
`"%(asctime)s | %(levelname)-8s | %(name)-25s | %(message)s"` (`backend/app/main.py:39`) — plain
pipe-delimited text with no request scope at all. So `$request_id` today is a per-line dedup key and
nothing more: you cannot join an nginx line to a backend line.

Making it a real correlation id needs three things, and **all three are outside E1**:

1. `proxy_set_header X-Request-ID $request_id;` in the proxy-headers snippet (one line,
   `bootstrap-ec2.sh:718-726` — same file, adjacent section);
2. FastAPI middleware putting that header into a `contextvar`;
3. the backend log format emitting it — which is **D11's territory**, since D11 already proposes
   switching `run_stream.py` to structured JSON logging.

**I am keeping `$request_id` in scope and steps 1-3 out of scope**, for one reason: emitting it costs
nothing (it is already generated per request whether logged or not), and it is the *prerequisite*
half — you cannot build the join later without it in the nginx log. Doing steps 1-3 inside E1 would
mean editing the proxy-headers snippet that A1 depends on and touching a Python file, and it would
make D11 and E1 mutually blocking. **Recommendation: log it now, and have D11 close the loop** by
adding the `proxy_set_header` line plus the backend side as one change. Flagged to D11 in I11.

##### I11. Open questions requiring a human decision

1. **Who owns `velocityai-dev-alerts@hexaware.com`?** E1 adds three alarms that page. Two are
   `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` and will be in ALARM the moment they are created, because the
   dev log groups are empty today (B1). If nobody owns that mailbox, the alarms are decoration.
   *This is B6's decision, but E1 raises the stakes* — the count of firing alarms goes from 41 to 44.
   **Recommendation:** create them anyway (they are the guard the incident argues for), and do not
   confirm the subscription until B1+B2 have logs flowing and all three read OK. If the mailbox
   cannot be owned, re-point `TF_VAR_alert_email` at a named human before confirming.

2. **The multi-environment consequence — accept, gate, or pre-empt?** The monitoring module is shared
   code and the boxes are not. A dev apply provably moves nothing in stage or prod (per-environment
   state keys `velocityai/<env>/app.tfstate`, per-environment resource names via
   `var.environment`/`var.name_prefix`, per-environment `for_each` over `local.log_groups`, and a
   separate CodeBuild project per branch that injects its own `ENVIRONMENT`) — verified in I4/I5 and
   provable with T7. But **the next stage or prod `app apply` will flip their filters to JSON while
   their nginx still emits space-delimited**, because their instances never re-run `bootstrap-ec2.sh`
   (C1) and only get the new script into their own S3 bucket on their own apply. The consequence:
   `Nginx5xx` on that environment silently returns zero and `nginx-5xx-spike`
   (`treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"`) sits OK forever. **Silent monitoring loss, not a page.**

   Today that is *latent*, because stage and prod also ship nothing (B1 affects all three — the
   dossier records zero streams in the stage and prod groups too). It becomes real the moment anyone
   fixes their agent without reconciling their nginx.

   **My recommendation, and this is the one that needs a decision:** ship the shared-module change
   **plus** the `nginx-log-parse-stalled` alarm (I5 step 3c), which turns the silent failure into a
   24-hour page in *every* environment that gets the module. Then make the promotion MR to
   stage/prod carry the SSM nginx reconcile as an explicit gate. Two alternatives I reject:
   gating the filters on `var.environment == "dev"` (creates two divergent monitoring behaviours in
   shared code — an infra dual implementation, and it just defers the same mismatch), and holding the
   whole change until stage/prod can be reconciled (leaves dev blind for the sake of environments
   that are equally blind already).

3. **`nginx-log-parse-stalled` and `app-log-ingestion-stalled` use a 24-hour window.** The dossier
   proposed 1 hour. I widened it because a dev box is legitimately idle overnight and
   `location = /health` sets `access_log off` (`bootstrap-ec2.sh:834`), so nothing keeps the group
   warm. 24 hours turns a month of blindness into a day. **Decision needed:** accept 24 hours, or
   fund a guaranteed heartbeat — a `systemd` timer writing one line every five minutes into a
   collected file would let the window drop to one hour. That timer belongs in `bootstrap-ec2.sh`
   §14 with B1/B4, not here. **Recommendation: accept 24 hours now, add the heartbeat with B4.**

4. **Should the four new thresholds be `variables.tf` knobs?** I hardcoded them, matching the
   in-file precedent (`nginx_5xx_spike` hardcodes `threshold = 10`). Making them variables is the
   more configurable choice but adds four knobs to a **shared** module that every environment then
   has to reason about, for a change whose scope is dev. **Recommendation: hardcode now; promote to
   variables if and when stage or prod needs a different value.**

5. **Log volume grows ~2.2x** (measured: +371 B/line). At any plausible dev volume that is under
   $1/month (I8). **No decision needed for dev.** Flagged only because prod volume is unknown and the
   same module change reaches it eventually.

##### I12. Shortcuts and alternatives explicitly rejected

1. **Keep the space-delimited format and just add `$upstream_addr` to the end.**
   Tempting because it is a two-word edit and the existing filter keeps working. **Why it is wrong:**
   the pattern `[ip, id, user, ts, request, status_code=5*, ...]` is *positional*. Appending a field
   is survivable (the trailing `...` absorbs it) but any future insertion silently shifts every
   field after it and the filter starts reading the wrong column — with no error, just wrong numbers.
   And a positional pattern cannot express `status = 429 AND upstream_addr = "-"` at all, because
   `upstream_addr` would be inside the unnamed `...` tail. The whole point of E1 is to make the
   discriminator *testable*, and positional patterns cannot test two fields at once.

2. **Set `run_as_user: root` / other B-cluster shortcuts.** Out of scope, and the dossier already
   rejects them for B1. Noted only so nobody folds them in while editing the same file.

3. **Keep the old space-delimited filter alongside the new JSON one "for the transition".**
   Superficially the safe move: neither environment loses coverage. **Why it is wrong:** it is a dual
   implementation with no removal trigger (INV-3/INV-12), and it produces double-counted metrics for
   whichever environment is emitting a format both can read — which is nobody, since a line is either
   JSON or space-delimited. So it costs the complexity of two filters and buys a metric that is
   correct in exactly one configuration. The **`nginx-log-parse-stalled` alarm is the correct answer
   to the same fear**: instead of covering the mismatch, it *detects* it, and it has a natural end
   state (it stays OK).

4. **`limit_conn_status 429` on A1's stream location so both limiters report the same code.**
   Would make `NginxLimitReject` a single clean number. **Why it is wrong:** A1 explicitly chose 503
   so that "429 means rate-limited (the bug), 503 means connection cap reached (working)" — and that
   distinction is worth more than a tidy metric. Not E1's decision to reverse.

5. **Emit `$request` instead of `$uri` "because a JSON access log should carry the full request
   line".** **Why it is wrong:** it re-introduces the query string, reversing the documented
   token-leakage mitigation (`docs/SIMPLE_AWS_DEPLOYMENT.md:821`, "$uri intentionally instead of
   $request"). This is the most likely well-intentioned regression in the whole change, which is why
   step 1 carries an explicit in-file comment forbidding it.

6. **Quote `$status` as a string and use `{ $.status = "5*" }`.** A legitimate alternative that also
   solves the `000` problem. **Why I did not pick it:** it trades an exact numeric comparison for a
   wildcard, and it silently changes the semantics of any future `>` / `<` predicate someone adds.
   The four-line `map` keeps the field numeric and I measured it as a pass-through on every real
   status.

7. **Filter empty strings directly: `{ $.status = 429 && $.upstream_addr = "" }`.** Would avoid the
   `map`. **Why I did not pick it:** empty-string equality is not a construct I can point to
   anywhere in this repo or verify without credentials, whereas `= "-"` is exactly the shape already
   in production at `main.tf:1520`. Guessing at a pattern that silently matches nothing is precisely
   the failure mode this issue exists to fix.

8. **Ship the dossier's `SseStreamSlow` as written.** **Why it is wrong:** `request_time` on a stream
   is the stream's lifetime, measured at 6.007s on a 6-second stream. `> 1` matches every stream, so
   an alarm on it would fire on normal operation and a human reading the metric name would draw the
   wrong conclusion. Renamed to `SseStreamClosed` and the predicate dropped.

9. **Add a `timestamp_format` to the `collect_list` while in the neighbourhood** so CloudWatch uses
   the log's `time` field instead of ingestion time. Genuinely useful and now possible. **Why not
   here:** it edits `bootstrap-ec2.sh:988-995`, which is B3's and B4's block, and it changes event
   timestamps — a behaviour change that deserves its own verification. Belongs with B3/B4.

10. **Fold in the `X-Request-ID` correlation chain** (proxy header + FastAPI middleware + backend log
    format). **Why not:** it would make E1 depend on D11 and touch the proxy-headers snippet A1 also
    depends on. Logging `$request_id` now is the free half; the join belongs to D11 (see I10).

11. **Do nothing until B1 and B2 land, since the filters are inert anyway.** **Why it is wrong:** the
    nginx format change has to be applied to the box by hand (C1), and there is exactly one
    nginx change window planned — the one A1 needs. Missing it means a second SSM run, a second
    `nginx -t`, a second reload, and a second chance to get it wrong on a box with no snapshots.

### E2 — The `PgDumpHeartbeat` alarm has no publisher

**Confidence:** [V]

**Symptom.** `velocityai-dev-pg-dump-heartbeat-stale` is permanently in ALARM, contributing to the
41 firing alarms in B6 and to alarm fatigue on the legacy topics.

**Root cause.** The alarm watches namespace `VelocityAI/Backups`
(`modules/monitoring/main.tf:733`). **That namespace does not exist** — nothing anywhere publishes to
it. Combined with `treat_missing_data = breaching`, it fires forever.

**Why it occurred.** The alarm was written against an intended heartbeat metric that the backup
script was supposed to emit. The script does the backup correctly (hourly `pg_dump` objects are
landing in S3, latest 2026-07-29T18:01 [V]) but never got the `put-metric-data` call. Alarm and
publisher were built by different changes, and `treat_missing_data = breaching` — correct for a real
heartbeat — turned the gap into a permanent false positive.

**The fix.** Either add a `aws cloudwatch put-metric-data --namespace VelocityAI/Backups` call to the
`velocityai-pg-dump` script on success, or delete the alarm. The former is right: a backup you are not
alerted about is not a backup. Note this alarm currently fires on **dev, stage and prod**, so a fix in
`bootstrap-ec2.sh` benefits all three whenever they are next rebuilt — but per the dev-only
constraint, only apply it to the dev box directly.

**Verification.** After one hour, the metric exists and the alarm transitions to OK.

#### Fully-Detailed Investigation

> **Investigated** 2026-07-30 · **Verdict on the dossier's proposed fix:** CONFIRMED-WITH-CORRECTIONS ·
> **Registers read to EOF:** FIX-REGISTER.md (3,705 lines) and IMPLEMENTATION-REGISTER.md (4,178 lines) ·
> **Anchor drift found:** 0 of 5 anchors moved.
>
> The dossier's diagnosis ("the alarm has no publisher") is exactly right. Its prescription
> ("add a `put-metric-data --namespace VelocityAI/Backups` call ... per the dev-only constraint,
> only apply it to the dev box") is **unsafe as written**: the alarm carries **no dimensions**
> and a namespace shared by all three environments, so a dev-only zero-dimension publisher would
> drive **stage's and prod's** heartbeat alarms to OK off dev's backup. That converts a false
> positive into a **false negative on production backup monitoring**. The fix must change either
> the namespace or the dimension set; a publisher-only change is not correct.

##### I3. Root cause — confirmed, corrected, or replaced

**CONFIRMED-WITH-CORRECTIONS.** The dossier's causal chain is right as far as it goes:

```
alarm  velocityai-dev-pg-dump-heartbeat-stale
  watches  VelocityAI/Backups :: PgDumpHeartbeat, statistic SampleCount, period 7200s, threshold 1
  with     treat_missing_data = "breaching"
nothing on the box, in the repo, or in the account ever calls put-metric-data into that namespace
  ->  every evaluation window has 0 samples
  ->  "missing" is treated as breaching
  ->  permanent ALARM  ->  one of the 41 in B6  ->  alarm fatigue
```

I re-derived every link independently:

- **Nothing publishes to `VelocityAI/Backups`.** `grep -rn "PgDumpHeartbeat\|VelocityAI/Backups" infra/`
  returns exactly four hits, all in the alarm and its comment (`monitoring/main.tf:717, 728, 732, 733`).
  There is exactly **one** `put-metric-data` call in the entire repo
  (`grep -rn "put-metric-data" infra/` -> `bootstrap-ec2.sh:1105`, which is E3's stuck-workflows probe
  and targets `VelocityAI/Prod`). No backend Python publishes CloudWatch metrics
  (`grep -rn "put_metric_data\|boto3.client(.cloudwatch" backend/app backend/agents` -> empty). [V]
- **The backup itself works.** `velocityai-pg-dump` (`:1062-1077`) does `pg_dump | gzip -9` then
  `aws s3 cp ... --sse aws:kms`, under `set -euo pipefail` (`:1064`). The dossier verified hourly
  objects landing in S3 (latest `2026-07-29T18:01`, `[V]` at dossier `:1879`). So the alarm is a pure
  false positive: the thing it watches is healthy and the signal was never wired.

**Correction 1 — the dossier's prescription is unsafe, and this is the material finding.**

The dossier says: *"add a `aws cloudwatch put-metric-data --namespace VelocityAI/Backups` call ...
per the dev-only constraint, only apply it to the dev box."* Applied literally that is a
**cross-environment false negative on production backups.** Here is the mechanism, from the alarm
definitions themselves.

I extracted `(namespace, metric_name, dimensions)` for every alarm in the module programmatically:

```
resource                               namespace                    metric                     dims
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
cpu_high                               var.cw_metric_namespace      "cpu_usage_user"           InstanceId = var.instance_id
mem_high                               var.cw_metric_namespace      "mem_used_percent"         InstanceId = var.instance_id
disk_root_high                         var.cw_metric_namespace      "disk_used_percent"        InstanceId | path = "/"
disk_data_high                         var.cw_metric_namespace      "disk_used_percent"        InstanceId | path = "/var/lib/postgresql"
nginx_5xx_spike                        var.cw_metric_namespace      "Nginx5xx"                 NONE
db_conn_error                          var.cw_metric_namespace      "DBConnError"              NONE
bedrock_throttles                      "AWS/Bedrock"                "InvocationThrottles"      ModelId
bedrock_server_errors                  "AWS/Bedrock"                "InvocationServerErrors"   ModelId
billing                                "AWS/Billing"                "EstimatedCharges"         Currency = "USD"
ws_disconnect_spike                    var.cw_metric_namespace      "WSDisconnect"             NONE
bedrock_tokens_daily                   "AWS/Bedrock"                "InputTokenCount"          ModelId
pg_dump_heartbeat                      "VelocityAI/Backups"         "PgDumpHeartbeat"          NONE     <-- E2
cert_renew_failure                     var.cw_metric_namespace      "CertRenewFailure"         NONE
cert_renew_heartbeat                   var.cw_metric_namespace      "CertRenewSuccess"         NONE
agent_error_high                       var.cw_metric_namespace      "AgentErrorCount"          NONE
stuck_workflows                        var.cw_metric_namespace      "StuckRunningWorkflows"    NONE     <-- E3
unexpected_secret_read                 var.cw_metric_namespace      "UnexpectedSecretRead"     NONE
unexpected_kms_decrypt                 var.cw_metric_namespace      "UnexpectedKmsDecrypt"     NONE
inode_low                              var.cw_metric_namespace      "disk_inodes_free"         InstanceId | path = each.key
```
[V]

`pg_dump_heartbeat` is the **only** alarm in the module with a hardcoded VelocityAI namespace, and it
has **no dimensions**. Every other custom-metric alarm derives its namespace from
`var.cw_metric_namespace`, which the app layer sets to `"VelocityAI/${title(var.environment)}"`
(`app/main.tf:173`) — i.e. `VelocityAI/Dev`, `VelocityAI/Stage`, `VelocityAI/Prod`. [V]

Therefore the three deployed heartbeat alarms —

| Alarm name | Namespace | Metric | Dimensions |
|---|---|---|---|
| `velocityai-dev-pg-dump-heartbeat-stale` | `VelocityAI/Backups` | `PgDumpHeartbeat` | `{}` |
| `velocityai-stage-pg-dump-heartbeat-stale` | `VelocityAI/Backups` | `PgDumpHeartbeat` | `{}` |
| `velocityai-pg-dump-heartbeat-stale` (prod) | `VelocityAI/Backups` | `PgDumpHeartbeat` | `{}` |

— differ **only in their name**. All three watch the **same single timeseries**: CloudWatch
identifies a metric by the triple *(namespace, metric name, exact dimension set)*, and all three
triples are identical. A zero-dimension datapoint published from the dev box lands in that one
timeseries and satisfies all three alarms. Prod's backup timer could be dead for a week and its
alarm would sit at OK, fed by dev.

That is strictly worse than the status quo. Today the alarm is a known-noisy false positive that
everyone ignores (B6). After a naive dev-only fix it becomes a **confidently green false negative on
the production RPO-1h control** — the failure mode the alarm exists to prevent. This is the
correction the dossier needs.

**Correction 2 — the dimension trap, checked explicitly (orchestrator point 3).**

CloudWatch alarm-to-metric matching is **exact on the full dimension set**; an alarm with dimension
set *D* matches only datapoints published with dimension set *D*, not a superset and not a subset.
A sibling agent found this class of defect in the same module for the CWAgent host alarms, and I
verified it independently:

- The agent config sets `append_dimensions: {"InstanceId": ..., "InstanceType": ...}`
  (`bootstrap-ec2.sh:979-982`), so **every** agent-emitted metric carries at least
  `{InstanceId, InstanceType}` (plus plugin dimensions: `cpu` for the cpu plugin with
  `"totalcpu": true`, and `path`/`device`/`fstype` for `disk`). [V]
- `cpu_high` and `mem_high` specify `dimensions = { InstanceId = ... }` only
  (`:376-378`, `:401-403`); `disk_*` and `inode_low` specify `{InstanceId, path}`
  (`:426-429`, `:452-455`, `:1643-1646`). [V]
- Those alarms therefore cannot match the agent's datapoints even once B1/B2 make the agent work.
  Not mine to fix — flagged for E1/B6 — but it is precisely the trap I must not repeat.

**My alarm's dimension set is `{}` (empty). My publisher must therefore emit `{}`, i.e. call
`put-metric-data` with NO `--dimensions` argument.** Stated explicitly, as required. The reference
implementation for this exact shape already exists in-tree and is provably self-consistent: E3's
`velocityai-stuck-workflows-check` (`:1105-1109`) publishes with no `--dimensions`, and its alarm
`stuck_workflows` (`:908-926`) declares no `dimensions`. That pair matches. I copy that shape.

**Correction 3 — E2 and E3 are not the same shape, and the dossier implies they are.**

- **E3:** alarm is already correct (`var.cw_metric_namespace`, no dimensions). Only the *publisher*
  is wrong. E3 is a **bootstrap-only** fix; it needs no Terraform change.
- **E2:** the *publisher* is missing **and** the alarm's namespace is not per-environment. E2 needs
  a bootstrap change **and** a one-line Terraform change.

They share the namespace-derivation mechanism, nothing else.

**Correction 4 — a latent shell hazard in the exact place the publisher must go.** Discovered by
running it, not by reading. `velocityai-pg-dump` installs `trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT` at `:1069`.
In bash, when a script aborts on a **parameter-expansion error** (`: "${VAR:?msg}"`) while an `EXIT`
trap is installed, the script's exit status becomes the status of the **last command in the trap** —
here `rm -rf`, which succeeds:

```
=== :? with EXIT trap whose last cmd succeeds ===
bash: NOPE: required
  rc=0                     <-- the failure is MASKED
=== :? with NO trap ===
  rc=1
=== set -e abort (failed simple command) WITH succeeding EXIT trap ===
  rc=1                     <-- NOT masked
```
[V] (measured on bash 3.2; the Ubuntu target is bash 5.x, so this specific status behaviour on the
box is `[I]` — which is exactly why the fix below avoids `:?` entirely rather than relying on it.)

The existing `: "${VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET:?...}"` guards at `:1065-1066` are unaffected because
they run **before** the trap is installed at `:1069`. Any guard added *after* `:1069` — i.e. mine —
would fail silently. The publisher therefore uses an explicit `if ...; then echo >&2; exit 1; fi`.
E3's script has **no** `EXIT` trap (`:1094-1110`), so `:?` is safe there; that asymmetry must be
communicated or E3 will copy the wrong idiom.

**(h) What a bootstrap edit can and cannot reach — the C1 dependency.** This is the most important
sequencing fact and the dossier does not state it.

`bootstrap-ec2.sh` runs once per instance (dossier "Why this happened" `:49-51`), and dev's live
userData has no firstboot service at all (dossier C1 `:1379-1384`, `[V]`). So the repo edit alone
changes nothing on the running dev box. C1's proposed `reconcile-host-config.sh` **does not help
either**: sibling C1's own analysis (`C1.md:1619`) records that `velocityai-pg-dump` is in **section
16**, outside C1's extracted section 13/14 range, and recommends widening to section 16 as a
**follow-up commit after C1 lands**. Independently confirmed from the source: section 13 is
`:703-938` (nginx), section 14 is `:941-1007` (agent), section 16 is `:1061-1111`. [V]

**Consequence:** E2 needs its own one-shot SSM payload for the host half now, and C1's widened
reconcile later. Both halves are specified in I5.

**(i) IAM — definitive answer.** The instance role **does** permit `cloudwatch:PutMetricData`, and
there is **no namespace condition** that could reject `VelocityAI/Backups` or `VelocityAI/Dev`.

```hcl
# infra/terraform/modules/iam/main.tf:157-174
data "aws_iam_policy_document" "cw_agent_describes" {
  statement {
    sid    = "CloudWatchAgentMetricPut"
    effect = "Allow"
    actions = [
      "cloudwatch:PutMetricData",
      "ec2:DescribeTags",
      "ec2:DescribeVolumes"
    ]
    resources = ["*"]

    condition {
      test     = "StringEquals"
      variable = "aws:RequestedRegion"
      values   = [var.region]
    }
  }
}
```

- The **only** condition is `aws:RequestedRegion == var.region`. CloudWatch supports a
  `cloudwatch:namespace` condition key; **it is not used here.** Any namespace is permitted. [V]
- The policy is attached (`aws_iam_role_policy "cw_agent"` `:176-180`) and is inside the sealed
  inline-policy list `aws_iam_role_policies_exclusive.instance` (`:236`), so it cannot be silently
  detached by drift. [V]
- **The region condition is load-bearing for my fix.** A `put-metric-data` that resolves a different
  region is `AccessDenied`. The `postgres` user the unit runs as has no `~/.aws/config`, so the call
  **must** pass `--region` explicitly. I use `--region "${VELOCITYAI_REGION:-eu-central-1}"`, the
  identical expression the `aws s3 cp` on `:1073` already uses in the same script.
- **Credential reachability from `User=postgres` is empirically proven**, not assumed: the same
  script already performs `aws s3 cp` as `postgres` and the dossier verified hourly objects landing
  in S3 (`:1879`, `[V]`). Instance-role credentials come from IMDS and are not user-scoped, so a
  second AWS API call from the same process tree authenticates identically.

**(j) Behaviour of the timer/alarm pair — no tuning change needed.** Timer `OnCalendar=hourly`,
`RandomizedDelaySec=120` (`:1159-1162`). Alarm `period = 7200` (2h), `statistic = "SampleCount"`,
`threshold = 1`, `comparison = LessThanThreshold`, `evaluation_periods = 1` (`:730-739`). Two runs
land per window, so a single failed run still leaves SampleCount 1 -> OK; two consecutive failures
-> 0 -> ALARM. That is exactly what `:735-737`'s comment claims. [V] No alarm-tuning edit required.

**(k) Application-layer surfaces: none.** No `backend/` or `frontend/` file is touched, so:
characterization goldens, `test_wire_parity`, the SSE suites, import-linter, Playwright and vitest
are all unaffected **by construction**. The Appendix-1 red baselines are not perturbed. [V]

##### I5. The complete fix

Four artefacts. **Artefact 1 is owned by E3** (see I10); E2 consumes it. Artefacts 2-4 are E2's.

###### Artefact 1 (E3 introduces, E2 consumes) — the ONE shared namespace mechanism

**File:** `infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh`, new sub-section immediately before the existing
`# -- 16. Backups: ...` header at `:1061`.

**Why a runtime helper and not a bake-in.** `ENV_TITLE` (`:82`) is an *install-time* bash variable
inside the bootstrap process. The publishers run hourly, in a different process, hours to months
after bootstrap exited. "Reuse `ENV_TITLE`" therefore has exactly two implementations: bake its
value into the emitted script at install time, or re-derive the same mapping at publish time. Baking
is **fail-open**: `ENVIRONMENT="${VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT:-prod}"` (`:79`) means a box whose
`bootstrap.env` lacked the variable would bake `VelocityAI/Prod` with no runtime signal — which is
the E3 defect, recreated. The orchestrator's binding constraint is fail-closed, so I re-derive at
publish time, **once**, in a shared helper.

**Why an explicit `case` and not a second `${x^}`.** `${x^}` is bash-4+ only, proven:

```
### interpreter: /bin/bash (GNU bash 3.2.57)
  ns-caret env=dev       rc=1  ${VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT^}: bad substitution
  ns-map   env=dev       rc=0  VelocityAI/Dev
  ns-map   env=stage     rc=0  VelocityAI/Stage
  ns-map   env=prod      rc=0  VelocityAI/Prod
  ns-map   env=pre-prod  rc=1  refusing unknown environment 'pre-prod'
  ns-map   env=<unset>   rc=1  VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT is required
```
[V] The Ubuntu target is bash 5.x so `:82` is fine where it is; the point is that `${x^}` and
Terraform's `title()` are **different functions** that merely coincide on the three values
`app/variables.tf:35` allows (`title("pre-prod")` -> `Pre-Prod`; `${x^}` -> `Pre-prod`). An explicit
three-way map is *provably* equal to the Terraform side for exactly the permitted set and refuses
everything else, so the two can never silently diverge.

```bash
# -- 16a. Shared CloudWatch metric namespace for on-host publishers --------
#
# ONE derivation site for the per-environment namespace used by every on-host
# `aws cloudwatch put-metric-data` caller (the pg-dump heartbeat in section 16 and
# the stuck-workflows probe in the same section). It must stay byte-equal to the
# Terraform monitoring module's
#     cw_metric_namespace = "VelocityAI/${title(var.environment)}"
#   (infra/terraform/app/main.tf:173)
# and to this script's own CloudWatch-agent namespace at section 14
#   ("namespace": "VelocityAI/${ENV_TITLE}", :970).
#
# FAIL-CLOSED by design. This script's ENVIRONMENT falls back to "prod" (:79) for
# its install-time needs; propagating that fallback into a metric namespace is
# exactly the defect E3 fixes (dev publishing into VelocityAI/Prod and corrupting
# prod's metric). A publisher that cannot resolve its environment must refuse to
# publish, loudly, rather than guess.
#
# The three-way map mirrors the Terraform variable validation
# (infra/terraform/app/variables.tf:34-37, environment in dev|stage|prod). It is
# used in preference to bash's ${VAR^} because ${VAR^} and Terraform's title()
# are different functions that only agree on those three values -- and because
# ${VAR^} needs bash 4+.
cat > /usr/local/bin/velocityai-cw-namespace <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Print the CloudWatch metric namespace for this environment, or fail.
# Reads VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT, which systemd supplies to every publisher unit
# via EnvironmentFile=/etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env (written by Terraform's
# compute module user_data, user_data.sh.tpl:52-53).
set -euo pipefail
if [[ -z "${VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT:-}" ]]; then
    echo "velocityai-cw-namespace: VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT is unset" \
         "(expected from /etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env) - refusing to guess" >&2
    exit 1
fi
case "$VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT" in
    dev)   _env_title=Dev   ;;
    stage) _env_title=Stage ;;
    prod)  _env_title=Prod  ;;
    *)
        echo "velocityai-cw-namespace: unknown environment" \
             "'${VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT}' - refusing to publish" >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
esac
printf 'VelocityAI/%s\n' "$_env_title"
EOF
chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/velocityai-cw-namespace
```

No systemd unit file changes are required: both publisher units already carry
`EnvironmentFile=/etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env` (`:1149` and `:1207`), so `VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT` is
in their environment already. This is a deliberate design goal — it keeps the host patch to plain
file writes with no `daemon-reload` and no timer restart.

**E3's consumption** (E3 owns this edit; recorded here only so the two agree):

```bash
# bootstrap-ec2.sh, inside the velocityai-stuck-workflows-check heredoc.
# BEFORE (:1105-1109):
aws cloudwatch put-metric-data \
    --namespace VelocityAI/Prod \
    --metric-name StuckRunningWorkflows \
    --value "$COUNT" \
    --region "$AWS_REGION"

# AFTER:
CW_NAMESPACE="$(/usr/local/bin/velocityai-cw-namespace)"
aws cloudwatch put-metric-data \
    --namespace "$CW_NAMESPACE" \
    --metric-name StuckRunningWorkflows \
    --value "$COUNT" \
    --region "$AWS_REGION"
```
That script has no `EXIT` trap, so `set -e` propagates the helper's non-zero status through the
command substitution normally and the unit fails loudly. (E2's script does have a trap — see below.)

###### Artefact 2 (E2) — the publisher

**File:** `infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh`, inside the **quoted** heredoc that emits
`/usr/local/bin/velocityai-pg-dump` (`:1062-1077`). Quoted (`<<'EOF'`) is correct and must stay
quoted: the body contains runtime variables (`$TMP`, `$DUMP`, `$VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET`) that must
survive to run time. Everything added below is likewise runtime-resolved, so the quoting is not a
constraint here — unlike E3, nothing needs install-time interpolation.

**BEFORE — `:1062-1078` verbatim:**

```bash
cat > /usr/local/bin/velocityai-pg-dump <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
: "${VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET:?VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET is required}"
: "${VELOCITYAI_KMS_KEY_ID:?VELOCITYAI_KMS_KEY_ID is required}"
TS=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
DUMP="$TMP/velocityai-${TS}.sql.gz"
pg_dump --format=plain --no-owner --no-acl velocityai | gzip -9 > "$DUMP"
aws s3 cp "$DUMP" "s3://${VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET}/postgres/${TS}/velocityai.sql.gz" \
    --region "${VELOCITYAI_REGION:-eu-central-1}" \
    --sse aws:kms \
    --sse-kms-key-id "$VELOCITYAI_KMS_KEY_ID"
echo "pg_dump complete: $(stat -c%s "$DUMP") bytes uploaded to S3"
EOF
chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/velocityai-pg-dump
```

**AFTER — full replacement text:**

```bash
cat > /usr/local/bin/velocityai-pg-dump <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
: "${VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET:?VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET is required}"
: "${VELOCITYAI_KMS_KEY_ID:?VELOCITYAI_KMS_KEY_ID is required}"
TS=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
DUMP="$TMP/velocityai-${TS}.sql.gz"
pg_dump --format=plain --no-owner --no-acl velocityai | gzip -9 > "$DUMP"
aws s3 cp "$DUMP" "s3://${VELOCITYAI_BACKUP_BUCKET}/postgres/${TS}/velocityai.sql.gz" \
    --region "${VELOCITYAI_REGION:-eu-central-1}" \
    --sse aws:kms \
    --sse-kms-key-id "$VELOCITYAI_KMS_KEY_ID"
DUMP_BYTES=$(stat -c%s "$DUMP")
echo "pg_dump complete: ${DUMP_BYTES} bytes uploaded to S3"

# --- Heartbeat (feeds <prefix>-pg-dump-heartbeat-stale) -------------------
# Reached ONLY when pg_dump AND the S3 upload both succeeded: `set -euo
# pipefail` aborts above on any failure, and `pipefail` catches a pg_dump that
# dies mid-pipe into gzip. Nothing is published for a failed or partial backup.
#
# NO --dimensions. The alarm (infra/terraform/modules/monitoring/main.tf:727-748)
# declares no `dimensions` block, and CloudWatch matches an alarm to a metric on
# the EXACT dimension set. A heartbeat published with any dimension would create
# a different timeseries and leave the alarm permanently breaching -- the same
# class of defect the CWAgent host alarms already have (they specify
# {InstanceId} while the agent appends {InstanceId, InstanceType}).
#
# --region is explicit and mandatory: the instance role's PutMetricData grant is
# conditioned on aws:RequestedRegion (infra/terraform/modules/iam/main.tf:168-172)
# and this unit runs as User=postgres with no ~/.aws/config. Same expression the
# `aws s3 cp` above uses.
#
# The guard below is an explicit `if`, NOT `: "${VAR:?...}"`. A :? abort while the
# `trap ... EXIT` above is installed exits with the TRAP's status (rm -rf, which
# succeeds), so the failure would be silently reported as success. The guards at
# the top of this script are safe only because they precede the trap.
if [[ -z "${VELOCITYAI_CW_NAMESPACE:-}" ]]; then
    CW_NAMESPACE="$(/usr/local/bin/velocityai-cw-namespace)" || {
        echo "velocityai-pg-dump: cannot resolve the CloudWatch namespace;" \
             "backup WAS uploaded but the heartbeat was NOT published" >&2
        exit 1
    }
else
    CW_NAMESPACE="$VELOCITYAI_CW_NAMESPACE"
fi

aws cloudwatch put-metric-data \
    --namespace "$CW_NAMESPACE" \
    --metric-name PgDumpHeartbeat \
    --value 1 \
    --region "${VELOCITYAI_REGION:-eu-central-1}"

# Companion gauge, same namespace, same empty dimension set. The heartbeat proves
# the pipeline RAN; this proves the artefact is not degenerate, so a dump that
# silently collapses (wrong database, empty schema) is detectable. No alarm is
# wired to it yet -- see I11.
aws cloudwatch put-metric-data \
    --namespace "$CW_NAMESPACE" \
    --metric-name PgDumpBytes \
    --value "$DUMP_BYTES" \
    --unit Bytes \
    --region "${VELOCITYAI_REGION:-eu-central-1}"
EOF
chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/velocityai-pg-dump
```

Two non-obvious choices, each with its reason:

- **`--value 1` with no `--unit` on the heartbeat.** The alarm's statistic is `SampleCount`, which
  counts datapoints and ignores the value, so `1` is conventional. `--unit` is omitted deliberately:
  the alarm declares no `unit`, so unit is not part of the match today, and adding one creates a
  second attribute that must stay in sync forever. It also keeps the call byte-shaped like E3's
  existing publisher. `PgDumpBytes` does carry `--unit Bytes` because no alarm watches it and the
  unit is genuinely informative.
- **`DUMP_BYTES` hoisted out of the `echo`.** `:1076` already computes `stat -c%s "$DUMP"` inline;
  hoisting it lets the gauge reuse the value instead of stat-ing a second time, and keeps the log
  line byte-identical.

###### Artefact 3 (E2) — the one-line alarm change

**File:** `infra/terraform/modules/monitoring/main.tf`. **Anchor:** the `namespace` attribute of
`resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "pg_dump_heartbeat"`, currently `:733`.

**BEFORE:**
```hcl
  namespace           = "VelocityAI/Backups"
```
**AFTER:**
```hcl
  namespace           = var.cw_metric_namespace
```

And the surrounding comment must be corrected in the same commit, because it currently documents the
namespace that is being removed and cites a stale IAM path:

**BEFORE — `:712-726`:**
```hcl
# 11. pg_dump heartbeat -- RPO 1h backstop.
#
# The `velocityai-pg-dump` systemd timer (docs/SIMPLE_AWS_DEPLOYMENT.md
# 11.2 / Appendix B.3) runs hourly and PUTs to s3://.../postgres/<TS>/
# under SSE-KMS. After a successful upload, the script publishes a
# CloudWatch custom metric `VelocityAI/Backups::PgDumpHeartbeat = 1` --
# absence of that metric for >2h means the timer is stuck or the host is
# unreachable, both of which jeopardise the documented RPO 1h.
#
# treat_missing_data = "breaching" is the *correct* setting here -- the
# whole point is that absence IS the alert signal.
#
# (The IAM instance role already grants cloudwatch:PutMetricData on
# Resource: "*" -- see infra/modules/iam/main.tf::cw_agent_describes --
# because that API doesn't support resource-level scoping.)
```
**AFTER:**
```hcl
# 11. pg_dump heartbeat -- RPO 1h backstop.
#
# The `velocityai-pg-dump` systemd timer (infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh
# section 16) runs hourly and PUTs to s3://.../postgres/<TS>/ under SSE-KMS.
# After a successful upload -- and only then -- the script publishes
# `PgDumpHeartbeat = 1` into this environment's namespace. Absence of that
# metric for >2h means the timer is stuck or the host is unreachable, both of
# which jeopardise the documented RPO 1h.
#
# NAMESPACE: per-environment (var.cw_metric_namespace, "VelocityAI/<Env>"),
# NOT a shared "VelocityAI/Backups". This alarm declares no dimensions, so a
# shared namespace would make dev's, stage's and prod's alarms watch one
# identical (namespace, metric, {}) timeseries -- and a healthy dev backup
# would hold prod's alarm at OK while prod's backups were dead. Per-environment
# namespacing is how every other custom-metric alarm in this module is scoped;
# the publisher derives the same string from VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT via
# /usr/local/bin/velocityai-cw-namespace (one derivation, shared with the
# stuck-workflows probe).
#
# DIMENSIONS: deliberately none. CloudWatch matches an alarm to a metric on the
# EXACT dimension set, so the publisher must call put-metric-data with no
# --dimensions. Do not add a dimension here without adding the identical one to
# the publisher in the same commit.
#
# treat_missing_data = "breaching" is the *correct* setting here -- the
# whole point is that absence IS the alert signal.
#
# (The IAM instance role already grants cloudwatch:PutMetricData on
# Resource: "*" -- see infra/terraform/modules/iam/main.tf::cw_agent_describes --
# because that API doesn't support resource-level scoping. The grant carries an
# aws:RequestedRegion condition, so the publisher must pass --region.)
```

**Nothing is deleted beyond the superseded literal** — the `VelocityAI/Backups` namespace ceases to
be referenced anywhere in the repo after this change, which is the INV-3 requirement satisfied
(grep must return 0 hits afterwards; see I8).

###### Artefact 4 — delivery. Two halves; both required.

**Half A — host, now (this is what actually fixes dev).** Scoped by instance id, never by tag
(dossier Appendix 2 `:2025-2027`: six tag values are byte-identical across dev/stage/prod). This is
the *durable* mechanism for the repo but **evaporates on instance replacement** — the root volume is

```bash
set -euo pipefail
DEV=i-092d5961f5aca87a6
NAME=$(aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids "$DEV" \
  --query 'Reservations[0].Instances[0].Tags[?Key==`Name`].Value|[0]' --output text)
[ "$NAME" = "velocityai-dev-app" ] || { echo "REFUSING: $DEV is '$NAME'"; exit 1; }

aws ssm send-command --instance-ids "$DEV" --document-name AWS-RunShellScript \
  --comment "E2 pg-dump heartbeat publisher (dev only)" \
  --parameters commands='[
"if [ -z \"${BASH_VERSION:-}\" ]; then exec bash \"$0\" \"$@\"; fi",
"set -euo pipefail",
"TS=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ); BK=/root/e2-backup-$TS; mkdir -p $BK",

"[ -f /usr/local/bin/velocityai-cw-namespace ] && cp -a /usr/local/bin/velocityai-cw-namespace $BK/ || true",
"echo BACKUP=$BK",
"# STEP 0 - hard pre-flight: the env must be resolvable and must be dev.",

"# STEP 1 - shared helper (idempotent; skip if E3 already installed it).",

"chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/velocityai-cw-namespace",
"test \"$(VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT=dev /usr/local/bin/velocityai-cw-namespace)\" = VelocityAI/Dev",
"# STEP 2 - consistency pin against the CloudWatch agent config (same env, same namespace).",
"AGENT_NS=$(python3 -c \"import json;print(json.load(open(chr(39)+chr(47)+chr(39)))[chr(39)+chr(39)])\" 2>/dev/null || true)",
"# STEP 3 - publisher: idempotent rewrite of the whole script from Artefact 2.",
"grep -q PgDumpHeartbeat /usr/local/bin/velocityai-pg-dump && echo ALREADY-PATCHED || { ...write Artefact 2 body...; }",
"chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/velocityai-pg-dump",
"bash -n /usr/local/bin/velocityai-pg-dump",
"# STEP 4 - prove it end-to-end now rather than waiting an hour.",
"systemctl start velocityai-pg-dump.service",
"systemctl is-failed velocityai-pg-dump.service && { cp -a $BK/velocityai-pg-dump /usr/local/bin/; echo ROLLED-BACK; exit 1; } || echo OK"
]'
```

Notes the executor must honour, each with a reason:

1. **The `exec bash` first line is mandatory.** `AWS-RunShellScript` runs `/bin/sh` (dash) on Ubuntu;
   the payload uses `[[ ]]` and `${VAR:-}`. `infra/buildspec.yml:236` already uses exactly this
   re-exec idiom for the same reason. [V]
2. **Step 0 is a hard gate, not a formality.** If `bootstrap.env` does not carry
   `VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT=dev`, the helper correctly refuses and the heartbeat never publishes.
   Evidence that it *is* present: bootstrap rendered the agent's log-group names as
   `/velocityai/dev/*` (dossier B1 `:1044-1045`, `[V]`) and the dossier looked for host metrics in
   `VelocityAI/Dev` (`:1020`). Both are `${ENVIRONMENT}`/`${ENV_TITLE}`-derived, and with `:-prod` as
   the fallback they could only read `dev` if the variable was set. That makes presence
   near-certain — but it is `[I]`, so it is gated rather than assumed. **Remedy if the gate fails:**
   append `VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT=dev` to `/etc/velocityai/bootstrap.env` in the same payload
   (idempotent `grep -q || echo >>`), and raise it with C1 as a userData-drift finding.
3. **Backup before write; restore on failure.** There is no filesystem rollback on dev
   (zero snapshots), so `/root/e2-backup-<ts>/` is the only restore point.
4. **`systemctl start` in step 4 runs a real backup.** That is intended and harmless — it is the
   same work the timer does hourly — and it collapses verification from ~70 minutes to ~1 minute.
5. **No `daemon-reload`, no unit edit, no timer restart.** The design deliberately avoids systemd
   churn (see Artefact 1).

**Half B — repo, same day (durable).** Commit Artefacts 1-3 to `dev`. This makes the change survive
an instance rebuild, because `infra/terraform/app/main.tf:79-94` declares
`aws_s3_object.bootstrap_script` with `source_hash = filemd5(...)` into the **per-environment**
bucket, and every dev push runs `$TF/app apply` for `ENVIRONMENT=dev`. So the commit re-uploads the
script to `s3://velocityai-dev-pg-dumps-577954642302/config/bootstrap-ec2.sh` **and nowhere else**
(dossier C1 `:1425-1430`, `[V]`). The Terraform alarm change lands on dev's alarm via the same
`$TF/app apply`; stage and prod alarms change only when someone applies those environments. That is
what keeps a module edit dev-scoped in effect.

**Half B does NOT get a reconcile path from C1 as currently scoped** — `velocityai-pg-dump` is in
section 16, outside C1's section-13/14 extraction (`C1.md:1619`, confirmed against source). C1's own
recommendation is to widen the reconcile to section 16's three `cat >`+`chmod` script emissions as a
**follow-up commit after C1 lands and is proven**. Take that; do not widen C1's own commit, which
would break its provable-no-op acceptance gate.

##### I6. Ripple-effect analysis — why nothing else breaks

Adversarial: assume the fix is wrong and hunt for the failure.

**"The Terraform edit changes stage and prod."** It does not, in effect. Terraform state is per
environment (`velocityai/<env>/app.tfstate`, Appendix 2 `:2014`) and the pipeline runs
`$TF/app apply` for the pushed environment only. Editing the shared module changes stage's and
prod's *plan*, so the next apply of those environments will move their alarms to
`VelocityAI/Stage` / `VelocityAI/Prod` — at which point they will be **breaching until those boxes
also get the publisher**. That is the correct, honest outcome (an unwatched backup should alarm), and
it is strictly better than the alternative, which is prod silently reading dev's heartbeat. It is
also **exactly the same posture E1 and E3 have**, so it does not introduce a new class of drift.
Flagged for the operator in I11.

**"The alarm will flap while the first datapoint lands."** It cannot flap; it can only improve.
Pre-change state is ALARM. Post-change, the alarm remains ALARM until the first datapoint lands in
the trailing 2h window, then transitions to OK. There is no state in which it is worse than today.
Manually starting the unit (Half A step 4) makes the first datapoint immediate.

**"A failed `put-metric-data` now fails the backup unit."** It fails the unit *after* the backup is
safely in S3. Verified by execution (see the matrix below): case E leaves `s3=1, heartbeat=0, rc=1`.
The dump is not lost. The unit is `Type=oneshot` with **no `Restart=`** (`:1145-1153`), so there is no
retry storm; the next hourly tick runs normally. And a single missed heartbeat does not fire the
alarm (SampleCount over a 2h window with two runs). The trade is: a transient CloudWatch blip marks
one unit run failed. I accept that, because the alternative — swallowing the publish failure with
`|| true` — recreates the silent-signal-loss bug that E2 exists to fix.

**"The `postgres` user cannot call CloudWatch."** It can. The same script already calls
`aws s3 cp` as `postgres` and the dossier verified the objects landing (`:1879`). IMDS credentials
are not user-scoped. The one real hazard is region resolution, closed by the explicit `--region`.

**"The helper is a new failure point in the backup path."** It is invoked *after* the upload, so it
cannot prevent a backup. On a box where it is missing or broken, the backup still completes and the
heartbeat is skipped with a loud message and a non-zero exit — which the alarm then reports after 2h.
Fail-closed, degrading in the safe direction.

**"E3 lands first and E2's helper write clobbers it."** Both writes are byte-identical `cat >` +
`chmod` of the same content, so the second is a no-op. The Half-A payload additionally guards with
`grep -q`/idempotence. If the two agents' texts ever diverged, that would be an INV-3 violation and
the I8 test (`cmp` the two rendered helpers) catches it.

**"Concurrency / ordering."** Nothing concurrent. Two systemd `oneshot` timers, hourly and every 15
minutes, each a short-lived process. `RandomizedDelaySec` prevents thundering-herd alignment. No
shared mutable state beyond the helper file, which is read-only at run time.

**"Startup / shutdown / restart."** No unit file changes, so no `daemon-reload`, no restart, no
interaction with `velocityai-app.service` or the deploy path. A reboot re-arms both timers from their
existing `[Install] WantedBy=timers.target`.

**"Partial application."** Enumerated, and every intermediate state is safe:

| Landed | Result |
|---|---|
| Helper only | Nothing publishes. Identical to today. |
| Helper + publisher, no Terraform | Heartbeat lands in `VelocityAI/Dev`; the alarm still watches `VelocityAI/Backups` and stays in ALARM. Same as today, plus a correct metric waiting. **No cross-env harm** — this is why publishing to the per-env namespace is safe to land first. |
| Terraform only, no publisher | Dev's alarm moves to `VelocityAI/Dev::PgDumpHeartbeat`, still absent, still ALARM. Same as today. |
| All three | Alarm goes OK within one timer tick. |
| **The dossier's literal fix** (publisher into `VelocityAI/Backups`, no Terraform) | Dev's alarm goes OK **and so do stage's and prod's**, off dev's data. **The only unsafe intermediate state, and it is the one the dossier prescribes.** |

**"Application-layer ripple."** None. Zero files under `backend/` or `frontend/`. No unattached
client, slow client, crashed run, restart, resume, fan-out run, revision run or two-browser scenario
is reachable from this change — those all live in cluster A. Memory and connection-pool effects: none;
the publisher is two short-lived `aws` CLI invocations per hour on the host, outside the container.

**Verifying the dossier's own safety argument rather than restating it.** The dossier asserts
(`:1885-1887`) that *"this alarm currently fires on dev, stage and prod, so a fix in
`bootstrap-ec2.sh` benefits all three whenever they are next rebuilt — but per the dev-only
constraint, only apply it to the dev box."* The first clause is true. The second clause is what
breaks: with a shared, dimensionless metric, applying the publisher to **one** box does not benefit
one alarm — it satisfies **all three**. The dossier treats the alarms as three independent things
because they have three names. They are not; they are one metric with three watchers.

##### I9. Rollback

**Repo half.** `git revert` the two commits (Terraform, then bootstrap) and push to `dev`. The next
`$TF/app apply` returns dev's alarm to `namespace = "VelocityAI/Backups"` and re-uploads the previous
`bootstrap-ec2.sh` to the per-env S3 config prefix. Fully reversible; no state migration, no
destroy/recreate — `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` namespace is an in-place update.

**Host half.** Restore from the pre-change backup the payload took:

```bash
aws ssm send-command --instance-ids i-092d5961f5aca87a6 --document-name AWS-RunShellScript \
  --parameters commands='[
"set -euo pipefail",
"BK=$(ls -1dt /root/e2-backup-* | head -1); echo restoring from $BK",
"cp -a $BK/velocityai-pg-dump /usr/local/bin/velocityai-pg-dump",
"chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/velocityai-pg-dump",
"bash -n /usr/local/bin/velocityai-pg-dump",
"rm -f /usr/local/bin/velocityai-cw-namespace   # only if E3 has NOT landed",
"systemctl start velocityai-pg-dump.service && systemctl is-failed velocityai-pg-dump.service || echo restored"
]'
```

**What is NOT reversible, and what the backup must therefore capture.** There are **no EBS snapshots
of any root volume in any environment**, and all carry `delete_on_termination = true` (dossier
`:2033-2034`). The `/root/e2-backup-<ts>/` file copy is the **only** restore point for
`/usr/local/bin/velocityai-pg-dump`. It must be taken **before** the first write, and it must include
`velocityai-cw-namespace` if that file already exists (i.e. if E3 landed first) so a rollback of E2
cannot delete E3's helper out from under it. The payload in I5 does both.

**Irreversible side effects of the change itself: none.** CloudWatch datapoints already published
cannot be deleted, but they expire on the standard retention schedule and are inert. No data is
mutated, no S3 object is removed, no IAM is changed, no systemd unit is altered.

**Rollback of the last resort — deleting the alarm.** If the fix cannot be made to work at all, the
alarm can be removed rather than left as noise (`terraform state rm` is *not* the way; delete the
resource block and apply). I argue against it in I12, but it is a clean exit.

##### I10. Sequencing and dependencies

**Must land BEFORE E2:**

- **E3** — introduces the shared `/usr/local/bin/velocityai-cw-namespace` helper. E2 consumes it.
  This is a **hard dependency for the repo half** and a soft one for the host half (the SSM payload
  writes the helper idempotently if it is absent).
  **Rationale for E3 owning it:** E3's entire defect *is* the namespace, so the mechanism is the
  substance of its fix; E3 is publisher-only (no Terraform), so it has the smaller blast radius and
  can land first; and E3's bug is actively corrupting prod's `StuckRunningWorkflows` metric today,
  which makes it the more urgent of the two.
  **If E3 slips:** E2 introduces the helper instead and E3 consumes it. Never both — two copies is an
  INV-3 violation and the T4 grep is the gate.
- **B1 + B2** — not a hard dependency, but strongly preferred. Until the CloudWatch agent works, a
  `systemctl` failure on the pg-dump unit is invisible from outside the box. E2's failure signal is
  the alarm itself, which does work, so E2 is not *blocked*; it is just less observable.

**Must land AFTER E2 (and after B1/B2):**

- **B6** — confirming the `velocityai-dev-alerts` SNS subscription. The dossier is explicit
  (`:1326`, `:1340`): fix the sources of the noise first, then subscribe. `PgDumpHeartbeat` is
  named there as one of the "two dead signals to fix while here". **Do not subscribe before E2, E3
  and B1/B2 land**, or the first human on that mailbox is buried in 41 self-resolving alarms.

**Same-file collisions — name the issue ids:**

- `infra/terraform/modules/monitoring/main.tf` is edited by **E2** (`:712-733`), **E1** (log-format
  metric filters at `:466-490` plus new `Nginx429` / `NginxLimit429` / `SseStreamSlow` /

  resources whose insertion point is unconstrained. **Merge instruction:** E1 should append its new

- `infra/scripts/bootstrap-ec2.sh` is edited by **A1** (nginx, section 13), **B1/B2/B3/B4/B5**

##### I11. Open questions requiring a human decision

1. **Stage and prod will start alarming honestly once their environments are next applied.**
   After commit 3 (the module change), a `$TF/app apply` for stage or prod moves that alarm to
   `VelocityAI/Stage` / `VelocityAI/Prod`, where nothing publishes until those boxes get the
   publisher — which, per C1, requires an instance rebuild or a separate SSM run per box.
   - **(a)** Accept it: prod's backup monitoring is honestly red until someone fixes prod. Prod is
     already in the 41-firing set with no confirmed subscriber, so nothing gets worse today.
   - **(b)** Run the same SSM payload against stage and prod at the same time.
   - **(c)** Hold commit 3 until stage/prod can be patched together.
   **Recommendation: (a).** It is the only option that keeps the dev-only fence and it makes the real
   state visible. (b) breaches the stated scope. (c) leaves dev unfixed for an unbounded time.
   This is a genuine product/ops decision because it changes what prod's monitoring says.

2. **Does anyone want a cross-environment "backup health" view?** Moving to a per-env namespace makes
   "all three environments' backup health in one query" require metric math across three namespaces
   rather than one. Nobody has asked for it and no dashboard exists (I4(e)), but the `VelocityAI/Backups`
   namespace suggests someone once intended it. If that view is wanted, the alternative is Option B in
   I12 (keep the shared namespace, add an `Environment` dimension to both alarm and publisher).
   **Recommendation: per-env namespace.** It is consistent with the other 16 alarms and it is the
   option in which a mistake fails safe.

3. **Should `PgDumpBytes` get an alarm?** The gauge is published but unwatched. A "dump size dropped
   below X% of its 7-day median" alarm is the cheapest available approximation of "the backup is
   still meaningful", and it is what would catch a dump that silently collapses. It needs a
   threshold someone is willing to own and a week of baseline data first.
   **Recommendation: publish the gauge now, decide the alarm after a week.** Do not fold an
   unvalidated threshold into this change.

4. **`ENVIRONMENT="${VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT:-prod}"` (`bootstrap-ec2.sh:79`) defaults to prod for the
   whole script**, including the CloudWatch agent's namespace and every log-group name. My fix
   routes around it (the publisher never consults `ENVIRONMENT`), but the default itself is a
   footgun that would silently mis-namespace an entire host. Changing it to `:?` is a one-line
   fail-closed hardening that touches B1's territory.
   **Recommendation: raise it with whoever owns B1/C1; do not change it in E2's commits.**

##### I12. Shortcuts and alternatives explicitly rejected

**1. The dossier's literal prescription: publish to `VelocityAI/Backups`, dev only, no Terraform
change.** Rejected. The alarm has no dimensions and the namespace is shared, so one zero-dimension
datapoint satisfies all three environments' alarms. Prod's backup timer could be dead and prod's
alarm would read OK. **The specific failure: a false negative on the production RPO-1h control.**
This is the correction that motivates the whole plan.

**2. Publish with an `Environment` dimension into `VelocityAI/Backups`** (and add
`dimensions = { Environment = var.environment }` to the alarm). Rejected, though it is *defensible*
and would work. Three reasons: it still requires the same monitoring-module edit, so it buys nothing
in blast radius; it introduces a **new** dimension key that must match exactly between publisher and
alarm forever — the precise trap that already broke the CWAgent host alarms in this very file; and it
leaves `VelocityAI/Backups` as a second namespace scheme alongside `var.cw_metric_namespace`, which
is the INV-3 duplication the project forbids. **The specific failure it risks:** someone later adds a
second dimension on one side only, and the alarm silently returns to permanent ALARM with no error
anywhere.

**3. Delete the alarm** (the dossier's stated alternative). Rejected — and it deserves a real
argument, not a slogan.

The case *for* deleting is not weak. An alarm nobody is subscribed to (B6: zero confirmed subscribers
on every current-stack topic) that has been in ALARM since the day it was created is not monitoring;
it is one of the 41 entries generating the alarm fatigue that is itself a documented finding. Deleting
it would reduce noise immediately, at zero risk, with one line of Terraform.

The case *against* is decisive: `pg_dump` to S3 is one of only two backup mechanisms
(`docs/SIMPLE_AWS_DEPLOYMENT.md:28`: EBS snapshot nightly plus `pg_dump` hourly, "RPO 1 hour, RTO 30
min"), and it is the one that carries the hourly RPO. It runs on a `Type=oneshot` unit with **no
`Restart=`** (`:1145-1153`), driven by a timer, on a box whose root volume has **zero snapshots**. If
that timer dies, the RPO silently degrades from 1 hour to 24 hours and **nothing else in the system
would notice** — there is no other watcher on the backup path. The dossier's line, *"a backup you are
not alerted about is not a backup"*, is correct. The alarm is also cheap and already written; the only
thing missing is four lines of shell.

**Deleting is therefore rejected — but with a precondition:** it is only true monitoring once someone
is subscribed (B6). Landing E2 without B6 converts a noisy false positive into a quiet true negative
that still pages nobody. **E2 and B6 are complements; ship both.**

**What "good" actually looks like, and the gap this fix does NOT close.** The brief asks whether the
heartbeat proves the dump is RESTORABLE or only that a file was written. **Only that a file was
written**, and I will not claim otherwise. Precisely:

- It proves `pg_dump` exited 0 through a `pipefail` pipeline into `gzip -9` (so a mid-pipe `pg_dump`
  failure *is* caught — verified, T1 case B), and that `aws s3 cp` to the KMS-encrypted prefix
  returned 0 (T1 case C).
- It does **not** prove the object is readable, that it decompresses, that it parses as SQL, that it
  restores into an empty Postgres, or that the restored database is complete. **Nothing in this
  system has ever read a dump back.** The DR path is documented (`SIMPLE_AWS_DEPLOYMENT.md:1649`) and
  deliberately uses a *different* identity — the instance role is write-only under `postgres/` — so
  the box that writes the backups structurally cannot verify them.
- It does not detect a *degenerate* dump: `pg_dump` against an empty or wrong database exits 0 and
  produces a small valid file. `PgDumpBytes` (Artefact 2) is the cheap partial mitigation and is why
  I included it, but with no alarm wired it is currently only forensic.

**The honest statement to carry forward:** after this fix the system alerts on *"the backup pipeline
stopped running"*. It still does **not** alert on *"the backups are not restorable"*. Closing that
needs a periodic restore drill from the DR identity into a scratch database, publishing its own
heartbeat — a separate, larger piece of work that must not be smuggled into this change. Name it in
the backlog rather than let the green alarm imply a guarantee it does not make.

**4. Alarm on S3 `PutObject` activity instead of a custom metric** (the `docs/INFRA_AUDIT.md:93`
suggestion: *"alarm on 'no PutObject under `s3://.../postgres/` for >2h'"*). Rejected. S3 request
metrics are a paid per-bucket feature and are filterable by prefix only with a configured metrics
filter; the CloudTrail-data-event route needs a trail with S3 data events, which the account
deliberately does not have (Appendix 2, and `monitoring/main.tf:928-935` notes data events are
management-events-only here). It would also be a **weaker** signal: an object landing proves less
than a script reaching the end of its own success path, because a partial or degenerate upload still
produces an object.

**5. Bake the namespace into the script at install time from `${ENV_TITLE}`** via the unquoted-prelude
technique E3's dossier entry proposes. Rejected for **E2** specifically. It is fail-**open**: `:79`
defaults `ENVIRONMENT` to `prod`, so a box whose `bootstrap.env` lacked `VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT` bakes
`VelocityAI/Prod` permanently, with no runtime signal and no way to detect it short of reading the
file on the box. **The specific failure: dev silently publishing into prod's namespace — the exact E3
defect, recreated by the fix for it.** The orchestrator's fail-closed constraint rules it out.
(The technique itself is sound and remains the right answer for values that genuinely must be fixed
at install time.)

**6. Carry the namespace in a new `EnvironmentFile` (`/etc/velocityai/cw-namespace.env`).**
Rejected — a near-miss. It reuses `ENV_TITLE` most literally, but it requires editing **two systemd
unit files** plus `daemon-reload` on the host, and it inherits the same `:-prod` fail-open unless a
separate guard is added at the derivation site. With `EnvironmentFile=` unprefixed, a missing file
makes the unit fail — which would break the **backup**, not just the heartbeat. With `EnvironmentFile=-`
it degrades silently, which is the bug. The runtime helper achieves the same single-derivation
property with **zero systemd churn** and an unambiguous failure mode.

**7. Append the namespace to `/etc/velocityai/app.env`.** Rejected on evidence:
`velocityai-load-secrets` **regenerates that file wholesale** on every
`velocityai-app.service` start — it writes a `mktemp` file and `mv`s it over `$OUT`
(`bootstrap-ec2.sh:617-701`). Anything appended is destroyed on the next deploy. [V]

**8. Swallow publish failures with `|| true`.** Rejected. It makes the heartbeat unreliable in exactly
the way that produces the bug being fixed: a run that "succeeded" while the signal was lost. The
alarm's 2h/SampleCount window already absorbs a single transient failure, so there is nothing to gain.

**9. Bound the fix to the host and skip the repo commit.** Rejected. Root volumes are
`delete_on_termination = true` with zero snapshots; the host change dies with the instance. The repo
half is what makes it survive a rebuild, and it costs one commit that the existing
`aws_s3_object.bootstrap_script` + per-env `$TF/app apply` already delivers with no new pipeline step.

**10. Use `${VELOCITYAI_ENVIRONMENT^}` in the helper** rather than the explicit three-way map.
Rejected on measurement: `${x^}` is bash-4+ only (proven to fail on bash 3.2), and more importantly
it is a *different function* from Terraform's `title()`. They agree on `dev|stage|prod` and diverge on
anything hyphenated. The explicit map is provably equal to the Terraform side for exactly the
permitted set and refuses everything else, so the two sides cannot silently drift apart if the
`environment` validation is ever widened.

**11. Target the SSM command by tag.** Rejected — dossier Appendix 2 `:2025-2027`: `Project`, `Owner`,
`CostCenter`, `Repo`, `ManagedBy` and `Component` are **byte-identical** across dev, stage and prod.
A tag-targeted command would patch production. `--instance-ids` plus the `Name` assertion is the only
safe form.

subscription state, S3 object timestamps) is either the dossier's own `[V]` — explicitly attributed —
or marked `[I]`. Everything I tag `[V]` myself is a repo file I read, a command I ran, or a script I

in the session scratchpad.

### E3 — The stuck-workflows check hardcodes the prod namespace

**Confidence:** [V]

**Symptom.** `StuckRunningWorkflows` alarms on dev and stage sit permanently in
`INSUFFICIENT_DATA`, while **dev's data lands in prod's namespace**, corrupting prod's metric.

**Root cause.** `bootstrap-ec2.sh:1105-1106` passes `--namespace VelocityAI/Prod` as a literal,
inside a **quoted** heredoc — so the `${ENVIRONMENT}` interpolation that the rest of the script relies
on does not apply, and every environment publishes to `VelocityAI/Prod`.

**Why it occurred.** The quoted-heredoc boundary is the trap. Elsewhere in the same file, unquoted
heredocs are used deliberately so `$DOMAIN` and `${ENVIRONMENT}` expand at install time (see
`:728-731`, which comments on exactly this). This block is quoted — correctly, because it contains
runtime shell variables that must survive — and the namespace literal was written inside it without
noticing that it therefore could not be templated.

**The fix.** Pass the environment into the script's execution context rather than trying to
interpolate inside the quoted heredoc — e.g. write `ENVIRONMENT=<value>` as a line *before* the
quoted heredoc body (the same technique `infra/buildspec.yml` already uses at `:228-232` for
`BUCKET`/`REGISTRY`/`REGION`), and reference `$ENVIRONMENT` inside. Then derive the namespace as
`VelocityAI/${ENV_TITLE}`.

**Verification.** Confirm `VelocityAI/Dev` gains a `StuckRunningWorkflows` metric and the dev alarm
leaves `INSUFFICIENT_DATA`; confirm prod's metric no longer receives dev's data points.

> and IMPLEMENTATION-REGISTER.md (4,178 lines) · **Anchor drift found:** 2 of 6 anchors moved.
